name: AI Agents in Biology
description: A curated, weekly updated collection of LLM-driven AI agents for biological and biomedical research, tagged by the five-dimension taxonomy of Qi et al., Briefings in Bioinformatics 2026.

cite.title: Artificial Intelligence agents for biological research: a survey

papers.title: Real PMIDs, Wrong Papers: Harness Design for Biomedical Claim-Verification Agents
papers.summary: The study evaluates different harness designs for biomedical claim verification agents, finding that models formulating their own PubMed queries significantly improve accuracy compared to naive retrieval methods. The research highlights the importance of effective retrieval over reasoning in enhancing model performance and underscores the need for better safeguards against irrelevant citations.

papers.title: An Evidence-Driven Multi-Agent Compound AI System for Head and Neck Proton Radiotherapy Planning
papers.summary: A reinforcement learning policy first generates candidate proton therapy plans, then LLM planning, chat and evaluation agents let physicians refine them conversationally with evidence from the reference plans. The planning agent justifies each recommended adjustment and the evaluation agent checks clinical metrics and constraint violations.

papers.title: Agentic artificial intelligence for code status extraction from clinical notes: a cross-model comparison of single agent, reflective agent, and multiagent extractor-reviewer system
papers.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
papers.summary: The paper evaluates different AI architectures for extracting clinical code status from discharge summaries, finding that single-agent systems perform comparably or better than more complex multiagent and reflective agent designs in capable models. The study highlights the importance of matching architectural complexity to model capability.

papers.title: Workflow Topology-Guided Skill Loading for Agentic AI in Clinical Trial Data Pipelines: Sequential Exploratory Evaluation
papers.summary: The paper presents a method for guiding skill loading in AI agents using workflow topology to improve the quality of clinical trial data pipeline artifacts. The study shows that topology-guided context improves artifact quality compared to prompt-only approaches, especially when tasks require evidence not easily retrievable through lexical means.

papers.name: Pathways
papers.title: An Auditable AI Pipeline for Long-Tail Healthcare Resource Discovery and Directory Maintenance
papers.summary: The Pathways system uses an auditable pipeline to discover and maintain community healthcare directories by expanding queries across multiple dimensions and verifying extracted information. It demonstrates high accuracy in interpreting requests and restoring missing data, but emphasizes the need for further validation and clinical evaluation.

papers.name: ColonyAgent
papers.title: Knowledge-Guided Skills Agent for Microbial Colony Detection in Automated Laboratory Testing
papers.venue: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: Assesses image quality, retrieves reusable preprocessing skills and past experiences, plans a workflow with an LLM and refines it from label-free feedback, leaving deployed microbial colony detectors untouched. It raised mean detection mAP by 0.08 to 0.17 across three detector architectures on AGAR and an in-house dataset.

papers.name: NeuroPilot
papers.title: NeuroPilot: Longitudinal intravital neural imaging across scales and modalities through an agentic platform
papers.summary: NeuroPilot is an agentic framework that uses a multimodal large language model and computational imaging modules to analyze longitudinal neural recordings, improving signal recovery and tracking in challenging conditions. It demonstrated the ability to decode behavioral states from neural population activity across different experimental settings.

papers.title: The accessible human surfaceome
papers.summary: The paper describes an agentic LLM pipeline that curates the accessible human surfaceome from literature, outperforming existing databases in accuracy and breadth. The system uses a manually curated benchmark to assess its performance and provides detailed annotations for each protein record.

papers.name: EchoMed Agent
papers.title: EchoMed Agent: A Foundation Model–Based Agentic Framework for Echocardiographic Left Ventricular Segmentation and Functional Assessment
papers.summary: A constrained GPT-5.2 natural-language interface routes prompts to an adapted video segmentation foundation model and an axis-regression module to segment the left ventricle and estimate ejection fraction. With 20 labeled site-specific studies it reached a Dice of 0.940 and median ejection fraction error of 4.33 points on an independent Mayo Clinic cohort.

papers.name: PigGPA
papers.title: PigGPA: A Domain-Constrained Agent for Porcine Genomic Breeding with Verifiable Tool Execution
papers.summary: PigGPA is an agent for porcine genomic breeding analyses that combines domain-constrained skills with hashed execution contracts checking that run parameters match declared ones. The authors showed that general agents were inconsistent across sessions and that skills improved scores from 73.44 to 89.06 out of 100.

papers.name: MedMCP
papers.title: MedMCP: An Open Agentic Ecosystem for Medical Imaging Workflows
papers.summary: MedMCP is an agentic framework designed to make advanced medical image analysis tools accessible to non-technical users through natural language interaction. It demonstrates the potential for routine adoption of these methods by clinicians and researchers, enabling reproducible analyses with human oversight.

papers.name: Magnolia
papers.title: Magnolia: A Persistent-Memory Agent Framework for Computational Chemistry
papers.summary: Magnolia is an agent framework for computational chemistry with a three-tier memory that distils session observations into project entries and human-validated cross-project rules. Across four case studies, including protein-peptide docking and modified-DNA simulations, it tracked 317 runs and memory-enabled replays passed configuration checks that memory-free runs failed.

papers.name: CS1
papers.title: A general-purpose System One decision model for clinical records
papers.summary: CS1 is a 4-billion-parameter model that answers many typed questions about a patient record in one pass with calibrated probabilities, deployed inside two agentic harnesses alongside a generalist model. On 963,408 held-out patients it beat larger open decision models on 13 of 14 tasks and generalized across 21 external datasets.

papers.title: Does Multi-Agent Collaboration Reduce Hallucination in Clinical Tasks?
papers.summary: The paper evaluates the impact of multi-agent collaboration on reducing hallucination in clinical tasks, finding that while collaboration improves task performance, it does not consistently reduce hallucination. The effectiveness varies by model rather than topology or number of agents.

papers.name: LeakBench
papers.title: LeakBench: Auditing Reward Hacking through Prediction-Time Leakage in Clinical Modeling Agents
papers.summary: LeakBench is a framework designed to audit clinical modeling agents for prediction-time leakage and other critical issues, using synthetic tasks and real-world datasets. It demonstrates that even advanced models can fail in specific conditions without proper constraints or oversight, highlighting the need for robust auditing mechanisms.

papers.name: PRAXIS-MD
papers.title: PRAXIS-MD: a long-term brain-enhanced agent framework for end-to-end molecular dynamics research
papers.summary: PRAXIS-MD is a long-term brain-enhanced agent framework that converts natural-language biological questions into auditable molecular dynamics workflows, using case memory and reusable skills. The system demonstrated improved reproducibility and interpretability in MD research when evaluated against benchmark tasks.

papers.title: Aptamers as a sandbox for lab-in-the-loop agentic molecular discovery
papers.summary: The paper describes an AI-driven pipeline for designing protein-binding aptamers that iterates between computational design and wet-lab testing. The system showed significant improvement in binding affinity and specificity of the designed aptamers over successive rounds, demonstrating the value of integrating empirical lab data into iterative molecular discovery processes.

papers.name: CADS
papers.title: CADS: Measuring the Incremental Contribution of LLM Proposers in Sequential Biological Screens
papers.summary: CADS is a framework designed to measure the incremental contribution of large language models in guiding sequential biological screens, providing an error-controlled evaluation that separates the model's value from underlying algorithmic capabilities. The study reveals that while LLMs can contribute positively to discovery rates, their impact diminishes over time and may be overstated without proper control mechanisms.

papers.name: EGIP
papers.title: EGIP: An Evidence-Grounded Interaction Protocol for Clinical Agents
papers.summary: EGIP is an interaction protocol designed to enhance the performance of clinical agents by enforcing structured evidence acquisition and decision-making processes. The system improves diagnostic accuracy across various datasets and language models, with clinician reviews indicating a significant increase in evidence-supported correct responses.

papers.name: MedPAO-Assist
papers.title: MedPAO-Assist: Edge-Deployable, Modality-Aware Agentic AI for Radiology Report Structuring
papers.summary: MedPAO-Assist structures radiology reports from dictation on a laptop CPU using an extract-ground-generate pipeline with SNOMED-CT grounding and a 0.6B-parameter model. It covers four imaging modalities with about 3.3 GB peak memory and roughly 31 seconds end-to-end latency.

papers.name: ReTRACE
papers.title: ReTRACE: Feedback-Guided LLM Agent in a Chemistry Harness for Retrosynthesis Planning
papers.summary: Places an LLM among molecular tools, single-step prediction engines, a purchasable materials library, route memory and a multi-criterion evaluator, learning from feedback to backtrack and revise weak routes. With Claude Opus 4.8 a top-10 route passed audit for 86.7 to 95 percent of targets, and two routes were executed in the wet lab after expert revision.

papers.name: CucurbitAgent
papers.title: CucurbitAgent: An AI agent for exploring cucurbit multi-omics resources
papers.summary: CucurbitAgent is an AI research agent designed for functional genomics in cucurbits, integrating extensive multi-omics data and literature. It demonstrated superior performance compared to general-purpose LLMs on a benchmark curated by domain experts, showcasing its ability to provide accurate, complete, relevant, and traceable responses.

papers.name: BioMINTREL
papers.title: BioMINTREL expands biological problem solving through cross-disciplinary representations
papers.summary: BioMINTREL is an AI agent designed to discover and apply methods from various disciplines to biological data, enabling the exploration of new research questions. It outperforms existing models in a comprehensive benchmark by improving agreement with human experts and expanding coverage of potential applications.

papers.name: DrugHarness
papers.title: DrugHarness: An Evolvable Agent Harness for Computational Drug Discovery
papers.summary: Couples over 80 scientific operations with induction of conditional skills from execution trajectories, which a separate review agent verifies before they guide later tasks. It beat reported MolClaw results on MolBench, and a compound designed in a prospective HPK1 study reached a cellular IC50 of 14.19 nM.

papers.name: FusionRare
papers.title: Unified Multiparadigm Fusion Intelligence for Rare Disease Diagnosis
papers.summary: FusionRare is a unified framework that integrates multiple AI paradigms to diagnose rare diseases, achieving superior diagnostic performance compared to existing methods. It demonstrates significant improvements in clinical decision-making by enhancing physician confidence and reducing diagnosis time.

papers.name: inClinico Agent
papers.title: inClinico Agent for clinical trial endpoint prediction and prospective evaluation
papers.summary: The inClinico Agent is a machine-learning system that predicts the success of clinical trials based on registration-time features, providing a continuous Predictive Trial Index (PTI) for efficacy and safety/toxicity endpoints. The paper demonstrates high predictive accuracy with an AUROC of 0.828 for efficacy predictions and 0.809 for safety/toxicity predictions.

papers.name: ExpertTwins
papers.title: ExpertTwins: Auditable Long Horizon Scientific Panels through Grounded Expertise
papers.summary: ExpertTwins builds multi-agent scientific panels in which each seat retrieves evidence under an explicit policy and deliberation is checked with quotation verification and peer source review. In a nine-seat neuroblastoma panel, 438 of 439 claims passed quotation checks and seats defended or withdrew positions when challenged.

papers.name: Brieflow-auto
papers.title: Harness-Driven Agentic Operation of Optical Pooled Screen Analysis
papers.summary: Brieflow-auto is an automated pipeline for optical pooled screening data analysis, utilizing a large language model to interactively tune parameters and validate configurations. It demonstrated improved accuracy in gene assignment compared to manual analyses and enhanced the reliability of the underlying codebase.

papers.name: AutoOnboarder
papers.title: AutoOnboarder: Autonomously Onboarding LLM Agents
papers.summary: AutoOnboarder is a system that autonomously adapts large language model agents to perform specific tasks, such as submitting genomic sequencing prior authorization forms. It demonstrates the ability of these adapted agents to match or exceed baseline performance at significantly lower costs but highlights the variability in final agent performance.

papers.title: Auditing Escalation Reliability in Healthcare LLM Agents: A Perturbation-Controlled Benchmark of Workflow-State Failures
papers.summary: The paper evaluates the reliability of large language models in healthcare decision-making under uncertain conditions, using a synthetic benchmark with controlled perturbations. It highlights that while models perform well on clean data, their ability to escalate decisions when evidence is ambiguous or conflicting is significantly weaker.

papers.title: The Model Knows Better: Defending Medical Multi-Agent Systems Against Prompt Injection
papers.summary: The paper investigates the vulnerability of medical multi-agent systems to prompt injection attacks, where an attacker manipulates LLMs into incorrect decisions. It proposes a training-free defense mechanism that separates patient findings from clinical judgments and verifies each judgment against the findings alone, effectively reducing attack success rates while maintaining system accuracy.

papers.name: TIR-EC
papers.title: Incentivizing Tool-Use Reinforcement Learning for Post-Arrival Emergency Care Prediction
papers.summary: TIR-EC is a reinforcement learning framework that integrates tools into large language models to improve their performance in emergency care prediction tasks. It demonstrates superior macro F1 scores compared to conventional ML methods and larger LLMs, while also showing more efficient use of clinical evidence.

papers.name: TRACER
papers.title: TRACER: A Multimodal Harness for Patient Care in Hospitals
papers.summary: TRACER is a multimodal system that integrates video and clinical records to provide minute-level action reports for patient care in hospitals. It demonstrates the ability to accurately detect patient actions and answer clinician questions, showing potential for supporting clinical decision-making without training on protected health data.

papers.title: Towards guideline-grounded clinical decision-making: a multi-scale study of retrieval augmented generation based large language model agents
papers.summary: Evaluates retrieval-augmented agent configurations on 2,400 real MIMIC-CDM patient pathways across information gathering, diagnosis, treatment and guideline retrieval, with eight LLMs from 1B to 70B. Retrieval raised mean diagnostic accuracy from 55.6 to 64.3 percent, and autonomous query rewriting mattered most for retrieval fidelity.

papers.title: Skill-guided agentic reasoning enables longitudinal synthesis of myeloma records at expert-level concordance
papers.summary: An agent guided by an indexed clinical skill library synthesized longitudinal records of 811 myeloma patients and was compared against single-pass RAG, iterative RAG and full-context input. It reached 80.1% concordance with expert answers, above the roughly 76% ceiling of the alternatives, with larger gains on complex tasks.

papers.name: ReproBAIT
papers.title: ReproBAIT: Can coding agents build their own biological AI tools?
papers.summary: ReproBAIT evaluates the ability of coding agents to design, implement, and train biological AI tools from limited descriptions. The study finds that some tools can be substantially reproduced by these agents, but complex ones are harder to recreate, suggesting caution in publicly releasing tool information.

papers.name: HEM-Med
papers.title: HEM-Med: A Hierarchical Agentic Memory Framework for Safe Multi-Center Medication Recommendation
papers.summary: HEM-Med is a hierarchical agentic memory framework designed for multi-center medication recommendation, addressing the challenge of transferring knowledge across hospitals while ensuring safety constraints. The system demonstrates improved performance in terms of both accuracy and safety compared to existing methods on real-world data.

papers.name: PRISMATIC
papers.title: PRISMATIC : Prescription Risk Inspection System for Multi-Agent Treatment Interaction in Clinical Decision-Making
papers.summary: PRISMATIC has specialty agents build and revise drug regimens for multimorbid patients on a blackboard, with agent influence weights adapted from past case outcomes and short-term discrepancy feedback. It targets prescribing errors that come from fragmented decisions across specialties.

papers.name: MolHop
papers.title: MolHop: Scaffold-Hopping Molecular Design with Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Organizes about 1.6 million commercial scaffolds into a coarse-to-fine action space so an agent can jump to new scaffold regions and then edit candidates, keeping trajectory memory for long searches. Trained with agentic reinforcement learning, MolHop-9B beat large generative baselines on cross-scaffold success while producing more distinct scaffolds.

papers.name: BioAgent-RAG
papers.title: BioAgent-RAG: A Knowledge-Graph-Augmented Multi-Agent LLM Framework with Self-Reflective Verification for Explainable Drug Repurposing
papers.summary: BioAgent-RAG is a multi-agent framework designed for drug repurposing that integrates knowledge graphs to enhance biological plausibility and reduce reasoning errors. The system demonstrates superior performance on various benchmarks, indicating its potential as an explainable computational tool for prioritizing drug candidates.

papers.title: Verification Turns Capability Gaps into Routing Decisions: Small Language Models for Clinical Documentation
papers.summary: This study fixes a four-evaluator verification stack and refinement policy for clinical note generation and swaps only the generator between a 4B on-device model and a frontier baseline. The small model reached 0.984 claim-level factual entailment against 0.992, with its remaining weakness in section arrangement turned into an explicit escalation decision.

papers.name: TrialPD-Bench
papers.title: The Last Mile of Coding Agents for Long-Document Tasks: An Empirical Study on Clinical Trial Protocol Digitization
papers.summary: TrialPD-Bench is an expert-annotated benchmark of 150 clinical trial protocol PDFs across four task categories for coding agents that select tools, run code and revise their approach. Across nine models in five harnesses, agents usually found the right evidence but failed at transcribing it into accurate structured output.

papers.name: CLARA
papers.title: CLARA: Compound Library Active Learning with Reasoning Agents
papers.summary: CLARA uses a language model to guide batch active learning for ligand discovery, making strategic decisions about chemical compound selection. It outperformed random sampling in most scenarios and showed promising results in terms of recall rates across different protein targets, demonstrating the feasibility of using AI agents for molecular drug design.

papers.name: HACE
papers.title: Heterogeneous Agentic Coevolution
papers.summary: Heterogeneous Agentic Coevolution (HACE) is a framework that evolves specialized foundation models and large language model agents through reciprocal learning, improving their performance in various domains including protein function prediction. HACE demonstrates superior performance compared to existing self-improving methods across multiple challenging tasks.

papers.name: MADDIE
papers.title: MADDIE: Multi-Agent Drug Discovery Engine
papers.summary: MADDIE is a multi-agent system designed for drug discovery that includes specialized agents for different stages of the process, such as hit identification and lead optimization. It demonstrates superior performance compared to existing systems by efficiently generating molecules with desired properties and synthesis routes across 50 protein targets.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning In Partially Verifiable Environments for Colon Cancer Treatment Planning
papers.summary: Oncology treatment planning is cast as an interactive reinforcement learning problem under partial observability, with process-aware rewards built from decision sequences in real colon cancer records. The agent must decide what information to gather before committing to a treatment, a setting where several trajectories can be defensible.

papers.name: UMCR
papers.title: UMCR: Universal Medical Concept Recognition through Guideline Integration and Agentic Linking
papers.summary: UMCR is a pipeline designed to extract and link medical concepts from various text types to any target ontology, addressing the challenge of adapting to different ontologies without retraining. The system demonstrates strong performance on the MedPath benchmark, showcasing its ability to enhance interoperability in healthcare by aligning diverse medical standards.

papers.name: ProCARE
papers.title: ProCARE: Real-World Study Automation via Profile-Grounded Evidence Contracts
papers.summary: ProCARE is a framework that automates real-world studies by converting data profiles into Evidence Contracts and compiling study objectives into an intermediate representation, ensuring semantic consistency and traceability. It outperforms existing large language model agents in code executability and conclusion traceability on benchmark tasks, with validation through automated checks and expert review.

papers.title: Autonomous AI agents discover reverse transcriptases with tandem repeat arrays
papers.summary: Claude Code instances in an autonomous harness surveyed reverse transcriptase loci across 1.9 billion protein clusters. They surfaced array-associated RTs, a new jumbo-phage RT family with repeat arrays that are expressed during Staphylococcus phage infection.

papers.name: GNQA
papers.title: An Expert-Curated Benchmark for Frontier and Local LLMs Querying a Biomedical Knowledge Graph
papers.summary: The GNQA system uses a combination of retrieval-augmented generation and querying a biomedical knowledge graph to answer expert-curated questions, demonstrating significant improvements in performance when using more advanced language models compared to local models.

papers.name: LangPoli
papers.title: SciCurateBench: Curating Experimental Data from Heterogeneous Scientific Literature with Verbal-Action Agents
papers.summary: LangPoli is a system designed to curate experimental data from scientific literature by using a policy agent that generates natural language action guidelines and actor agents that convert these into executable tools. The system demonstrated strong performance in paper classification and structured information retrieval, outperforming plain LLMs and other existing systems.

papers.name: DRYLAB-Bench
papers.title: DRYLAB-Bench: Benchmarking the Biosecurity Risk of Agentic LLM Mutation Design
papers.summary: DRYLAB-Bench is a benchmark designed to evaluate the biosecurity risks posed by large language models (LLMs) in designing hazardous biological mutations. It assesses LLMs' capabilities in orchestrating specialized biological design tools to iteratively refine mutation designs, scoring them against empirical wet-lab measurements for risk quantification.

papers.name: KGR-MAS
papers.title: KGR-MAS: Knowledge Graph-Enhanced Multi-Agent LLM Framework for Evidence-Based Medical Diagnosis and Clinical Decision Support
papers.venue: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: KGR-MAS is a multi-agent framework that uses knowledge graphs to enhance the reasoning and decision-making capabilities of large language models in medical settings. It demonstrates improved accuracy on clinical diagnostic tasks compared to larger, less specialized models.

papers.title: Evaluating Autonomous LLM Agents Across Molecular Prediction and Optimization Benchmarks
papers.summary: The paper evaluates the performance of autonomous large language model (LLM) agents in molecular prediction and optimization tasks, showing that these agents can develop methods competitive with human-developed approaches across various drug discovery benchmarks. The study demonstrates the capability of LLMs to autonomously create high-performing models for ADMET property prediction, activity prediction, and practical molecular optimization.

papers.name: LongCAF
papers.title: LongCAF: A longitudinal context-constructive agentic framework for LLM-supported hypertension self-management
papers.summary: LongCAF is a longitudinal context-constructive agentic framework designed to support hypertension self-management by integrating patient-specific context and interaction coordination. The system was evaluated in a real-world deployment over six months, demonstrating improved context completeness and high precision in safety escalation.

papers.name: PaleoRigor
papers.title: PaleoRigor: a bounded research agent with a reproducible evidence trail for paleomicrobiome data processing
papers.summary: PaleoRigor is a bounded research agent that uses a language model to plan data analysis for paleomicrobiome studies, ensuring reproducibility and adherence to predefined constraints. The system demonstrated high accuracy in processing ancient microbial evidence while maintaining the integrity of the data through rigorous validation steps.

papers.name: ARGUS
papers.title: Unlocking the Regulatory Genome by ARGUS: An Evidence-Constrained Agentic Framework for Interpreting Single Nucleotide Variants
papers.summary: ARGUS is an evidence-constrained agentic framework that uses large language models and biological computation to interpret single nucleotide variants in noncoding regulatory regions. It demonstrates the ability to navigate complex genomic data, making decisions based on real experimental evidence to determine the functional impact of genetic variations.

papers.name: ActiveMedAgent
papers.title: ActiveMedAgent: Cost-Aware Trajectory Learning for Multimodal Medical Diagnosis
papers.summary: ActiveMedAgent is a framework that uses a cost-aware sequential logic to guide the acquisition of medical evidence, aiming to minimize costs while maximizing diagnostic accuracy. The system demonstrates its effectiveness by outperforming full-modality baselines in several benchmarks, highlighting its ability to identify when less information can lead to correct diagnoses.

papers.name: CircuitATLAS
papers.title: CircuitATLAS: Agentic reasoning over a systems neuroscience knowledge graph for target discovery in circuitopathies
papers.summary: CircuitATLAS is a knowledge graph and agentic framework for discovering therapeutic targets in neurological diseases by reasoning through neural circuits to molecular interventions. It successfully identified ATP1A3 as a control point on cortical excitability, which was validated through experimental studies.

papers.name: DrugTargetWorld
papers.title: DrugTargetWorld: A Synthetic Biobank for Training and Benchmarking AI Scientists
papers.summary: DrugTargetWorld is a synthetic biobank framework that generates simulated worlds to train and evaluate AI agents for drug target discovery. The system evaluates nine agents across multiple episodes, revealing limitations in distinguishing causal from non-causal proteins despite high composite scores.

papers.title: Omics data discovery agents: Agent-supported retrieval, reanalysis, and synthesis of published omics data
papers.summary: LLM agents with MCP-exposed tools locate published omics datasets, extract metadata, download data, run containerized quantification pipelines and synthesize results across studies. The system catalogued dataset references across thousands of PubMed Central articles and completed five end-to-end proteomics and RNA-seq reanalyses.

papers.name: MAGI
papers.title: From Benchmark to Bench: Can Agents Survive Real-World Drug Discovery?
papers.summary: MAGI is an open modular agent designed to coordinate molecular design tools for drug discovery, capable of generating molecules either directly or by delegating tasks. The study shows that MAGI's effectiveness in real-world projects is limited more by the accuracy and applicability domain of predictive models than by its own orchestration capabilities.

papers.name: Enrich.AI
papers.title: Enrich.AI: An Agentic AI Platform for Interactive Gene Set Enrichment Analysis and Biological Interpretation
papers.summary: Enrich.AI is an AI platform that integrates statistical gene set enrichment analysis with automated biological interpretation, using a conversational interface to guide users through the process. The system was validated in a study involving 50 gene sets, demonstrating its ability to provide accurate and relevant biological interpretations.

papers.name: MedZERO
papers.title: MedZERO: Self-Evolving Agents for Open-Ended Medical Reasoning Through Controlled Knowledge Accumulation
papers.summary: MedZERO is a self-evolving framework designed for medical reasoning that combines an Examiner and a Reasoner to generate and solve complex medical questions, respectively. The system demonstrates significant improvements in accuracy on public medical reasoning benchmarks compared to existing methods.

papers.title: Planner-Executor Style Multimodal Agentic System to Answer Patient Questions in Lung Cancer Screening CT
papers.summary: The system uses a multi-agent architecture to answer patient questions about lung cancer screening CT results, demonstrating high accuracy in tool invocation and self-regulation. It was evaluated by physicians for clinical quality and patient understandability.

papers.title: An agentic AI- and n8n automation-powered maternal care framework with predictive pregnancy monitoring and continuous learning
papers.summary: The Agentic AI Maternal Triage Framework uses predictive models and a retrieval-augmented generation-powered LLM to provide real-time risk stratification for maternal care, reducing alert fatigue in clinicians. The framework demonstrated high accuracy in simulation-based evaluations but requires further clinical validation before deployment.

papers.name: EASER
papers.title: Bridging the Evidence-to-Execution Gap:A Reflective Agent for Multi-Objective Peptide Design
papers.summary: EASER is a reflective agent designed to bridge the gap between scientific reasoning and sequence manipulation in peptide design, using evidence-aware strategies. It demonstrates superior multi-objective performance in designing antimicrobial peptides by integrating literature evidence with iterative feedback mechanisms.

papers.name: PsyCIDRA
papers.title: PsyCIDRA: A Dual-Agent Framework for Psychiatric Interviewing and Diagnostic Reasoning
papers.summary: PsyCIDRA pairs an interviewer agent that keeps working notes, loads expert skills and consults ICD-11 with a reasoning agent that reports hypotheses plus supporting, conflicting and missing evidence. It agreed with psychologists on whether to offer a hypothesis in 79.6% of blinded cases against 65.4% for direct prompting.

papers.name: MedPrune
papers.title: MedPrune: Topology-Efficient Multimodal Multi-Agent Communication Evolution for Medical VQA Tasks
papers.summary: MedPrune treats medical visual question answering as a communication graph of department specialist agents and learns to prune both irrelevant agents and low-value connections. The sparsification is meant to improve reasoning while cutting the token cost of redundant agent chatter.

papers.name: MedicalHarness
papers.title: MedicalHarness: A Controlled Evaluation of LLMs and Agent Harnesses on Medical Tasks
papers.summary: MedicalHarness evaluates the performance of large language models on medical tasks using different agent harnesses, revealing that the choice of harness significantly impacts outcomes. The study also identifies specific mechanisms within these harnesses that contribute to model performance.

papers.name: LifeLong Digital Twin
papers.title: LifeLong Digital Twin: A Unified Modeling Paradigm and Agent Harness for Event-Driven Lifelong Health State Trajectories
papers.summary: The LifeLong Digital Twin system models a person's lifelong health trajectory by integrating various types of data into daily health states and lifelong health contexts. It demonstrates significant improvements in predicting disease trajectories and outcomes compared to existing methods, highlighting its potential for personalized healthcare.

papers.name: AgentDiscover
papers.title: AgentDiscover: Autonomous Discovery with Minimal Search Scaffolding
papers.summary: AgentDiscover is an autonomous discovery framework that uses a large language model to plan and execute scientific searches, storing all attempts in a database for iterative improvement. The system demonstrates superior cost-efficiency compared to existing frameworks across various domains including biology, outperforming human competitors in past contests.

papers.title: Are We Measuring Scientific Intelligence? Rethinking the Evaluation of AI Scientists
papers.summary: The paper evaluates AI agents' ability to perform scientific analyses by assessing their reliance on provided data versus prior knowledge. It introduces a method to test evidence grounding, revealing that many agents can answer correctly without using the given dataset.

papers.name: TEMPLAR
papers.title: templar: agentic induction and evolution of standardized radiology reporting templates from large-scale clinical corpora
papers.summary: TEMPLAR is an AI system that uses multi-agents and neuro-symbolic architecture to induce and evolve standardized radiology reporting templates from large clinical datasets. It outperforms existing methods in terms of coverage, information fidelity, and diagnostic accuracy.

papers.name: BioGAIP
papers.title: BioGAIP: a scalable and robust LLM-powered multi-agent system for automated bioinformatics tasks
papers.venue: Journal of genetics and genomics = Yi chuan xue bao
papers.summary: BioGAIP is an LLM-powered multi-agent system for automating bioinformatics tasks. No abstract was available, so details of its evaluation are not summarized here.

papers.title: Toward a Locally Deployable Agentic Co-Scientist: Small-Model Planning for Early-Stage Drug Discovery
papers.summary: The paper introduces a lightweight framework where a compact language model coordinates 18 scientific tools for early-stage drug discovery, demonstrating its ability to generate parseable and schema-compliant plans. The evaluation shows high performance in tool selection and argument matching but highlights the challenge of compositional generalization.

papers.name: ARISE
papers.title: ARISE: Adaptive Agentic Reasoning with Image-grounded Self-Evaluation for Interpretable IBD Assessment
papers.summary: ARISE is an autonomous planning framework designed to improve the interpretability and diagnostic performance of medical image analysis in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). It demonstrates consistent improvement over baseline vision-language models by providing a transparent, step-by-step workflow that enhances clinical decision support.

papers.name: PaaP+GRA
papers.title: Prompt-as-a-Protocol with Agentic Research Automation: A Validated Methodology for AI-Native Biomedical Data Science Producing Peer-Reviewed Findings Across Genomics and Biosensor Domains
papers.summary: Prompt-as-a-Protocol (PaaP) converts natural-language research questions into executable analytical protocols, which are then executed by an agentic Generative Research Automation layer. This system autonomously identified significant biological findings in single-cell transcriptomics and biosensor analytics, demonstrating its capability to produce novel peer-reviewed results across different biomedical domains.

papers.name: ddkg.skill
papers.title: ddkg.skill: A Compositional Agent Skill for Translating Biomedical and Bioinformatics Questions into Cypher for the Data Distillery Knowledge Graph
papers.summary: ddkg.skill is an agent skill with a controller, references, validated query patterns and a routing table that helps LLMs write correct Cypher queries for the Data Distillery Knowledge Graph. In a nine-test evaluation against a live instance, five of seven tests on unseen sources returned correct results, and failures were documented.

papers.title: Development and Validation of Human-AI Collaborative Workflow in SNOMED CT Mapping of Bilingual Clinical Text
papers.summary: The paper describes a human-AI collaborative workflow for mapping bilingual clinical text to SNOMED CT concepts, using an agent system with translation, abbreviation expansion, and vector-based retrieval modules. The study shows that the AI-assisted approach improves mapping accuracy and reduces time by about half compared to human-only or AI-only methods.

papers.title: Auditing Pairwise Equivalence Judgments: Self-Critique Effects and Diversity Measurement in Multi-Agent Hypothesis Generation
papers.summary: The paper evaluates multi-agent systems in scientific hypothesis generation, focusing on the impact of self-critique rounds and equivalence rules used to measure diversity. It shows that increasing critique rounds significantly diversifies hypotheses initially but has diminishing returns thereafter, and different equivalence rules yield vastly different assessments of mechanism similarity.

papers.name: ELMS
papers.title: Evaluator-in-the-Loop Monte Carlo Tree Search via LLM Agents for Motif Scaffolding in Protein Design
papers.summary: ELMS is a multi-agent system that uses evaluator-in-the-loop Monte Carlo Tree Search to guide motif scaffolding in protein design, improving the generate-then-filter paradigm by incorporating structural evaluation feedback into iterative design processes. The system demonstrates superior performance compared to existing methods on standard benchmarks for single and paired-motif tasks.

papers.name: GAMA
papers.title: A Guideline-Augmented Multi-Agent Framework for Schema-as-Code Biomedical Named Entity Recognition
papers.venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Bioinformatics and Biomedicine (BIBM), 2026
papers.summary: GAMA is a multi-agent framework designed to enhance biomedical named entity recognition by inducing and verifying annotation rules from labeled data, generating schema-constrained entities, and refining predictions. The system demonstrates superior performance compared to existing LLM-based methods across multiple datasets.

papers.name: Sentinel
papers.title: Trajectory-Derived Confidence for Reliable, Resource-Aware Clinical Text-to-SQL Agents
papers.summary: Sentinel is a confidence layer that reads a clinical text-to-SQL agent's reasoning, code and database outputs to refuse unanswerable questions, abort failing trajectories and withhold untrustworthy answers. On EHRSQL it raised the reliability score from +0.08 to +0.24 and delivered-answer accuracy from 54% to 69% as coverage fell.

papers.name: RadOnc-Agent
papers.title: RadOnc-Agent: An LLM-Orchestrated Framework for AI Workflows Across the Radiotherapy Care Pathway
papers.summary: An LLM controller maps clinical intent to 26 schema-constrained function calls across four radiotherapy phases while keeping patient and workflow state. It chose the intended function in 98.8 percent of 7,800 single-function executions and completed about 96.5 percent of cross-stage and real-patient workflows, with longitudinal state removal cutting completion to 84 percent.

papers.name: Orchestrator
papers.title: Orchestrator multi-agent clinical decision support system for secondary headache diagnosis in primary care
papers.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
papers.summary: The Orchestrator system uses a multi-agent architecture to assist in the diagnosis of secondary headaches by breaking down clinical reasoning into specialized agents, each focusing on specific red flag domains. The study demonstrated that this approach enhances diagnostic accuracy and transparency compared to single large language model methods.

papers.name: PMxAgent
papers.title: PMxAgent: An Agentic Platform for Pharmacometrics
papers.summary: PMxAgent is an open-source platform that automates pharmacometric analyses by integrating various tools into a Docker-based API server, enabling AI agents to perform tasks like non-compartmental analysis and exposure-response modeling. The system was benchmarked against other AI agents for accuracy and reproducibility in NCA workflows, demonstrating superior performance and deterministic results.

papers.name: MR-MAS
papers.title: MR-MAS: an end-to-end multi-agent system for autonomous Mendelian randomization analysis
papers.summary: MR-MAS is a multi-agent LLM system that runs Mendelian randomization end to end, from data acquisition and causal estimation to interpretation and manuscript drafting, backed by an MR knowledge base for code repair. In test scenarios it executed workflows stably, reproduced literature-supported causal signals and gave consistent estimates across repeated runs.

papers.name: StrokeAgent
papers.title: An auditable multimodal agentic system for sequential decision-making across the acute stroke pathway
papers.summary: StrokeAgent is a multimodal agentic system designed to support decision-making in acute stroke care by integrating clinical records, laboratory results, ECG waveforms, and CT images. The system demonstrated high concordance with expert decisions and was rated highly for clinical utility and reasoning quality compared to large language models and neurologists.

papers.title: From seven combination hypotheses to one testable interaction: a gated agentic AI–QSP workflow applied to healthy-ageing interventions
papers.summary: The paper describes a workflow that uses an AI agent to generate hypotheses for combination therapies and constructs quantitative systems pharmacology models to evaluate them. The system identified one testable interaction from seven generated hypotheses, highlighting the importance of strict evaluation criteria in filtering out unsupported hypotheses.

papers.title: End-to-End PET/CT Interpretation and Quantification with an LLM-Orchestrated AI Agent: A Real-World Pilot Study
papers.venue: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
papers.summary: The system uses a large language model to orchestrate an end-to-end workflow for PET/CT image interpretation and report generation, demonstrating high sensitivity in primary tumor detection but lower specificity in nodal involvement and distant metastasis assessment.

papers.name: CXRAgent
papers.title: CXRAgent: Director-Orchestrated Multi-Stage Reasoning for Chest X-Ray Interpretation
papers.summary: CXRAgent has a central director that orchestrates chest X-ray analysis tools, validates their outputs against visual evidence, plans the next diagnostic step and reasons over collected findings. It is built to adapt to new diagnostic tasks and to weigh how reliable each tool is.

papers.title: Audiologist-Guided Multimodal AI for Pure-Tone Audiometry and Tympanometry Interpretation and Reporting
papers.summary: The paper describes a multimodal AI system that assists audiologists in interpreting and reporting pure-tone audiometry and tympanometry results. The study evaluates the accuracy of the AI's performance in different modules, showing improvements in agreement rates for hearing loss types and acoustic reflexes when guided by specific skills or prompts.

papers.name: CoTI
papers.title: Automated Health Care Thematic Analysis Using a Multiagent Large Language Model: Algorithm Development and Evaluation Study
papers.summary: Collaborative Theme Identification Agents (CoTI) is a multiagent system designed to automate thematic analysis in qualitative research, generating supporting excerpts and themes for human review. The study showed that CoTI's outputs were more aligned with those of senior investigators compared to junior researchers or baseline models, indicating its potential as an efficient tool for scalable qualitative research.

papers.name: CGEx
papers.title: Let Me Cypher That for You: A Multi-Graph Agent for Deciphering Biomedical Knowledge
papers.summary: CGEx is a system that translates natural-language questions into Cypher queries to retrieve and explain information from multiple heterogeneous biomedical knowledge graphs. The evaluation showed significant improvements in query accuracy with user feedback, demonstrating the utility of CGEx for uncovering meaningful insights across diverse data sources without requiring users to learn Cypher.

papers.name: EHR-RobustGym
papers.title: EHR-RobustGym: Benchmarking and Training Agents for Robust Clinical Reasoning
papers.summary: EHR-RobustGym is a scalable and interactive environment designed to evaluate and train clinical agents on noisy electronic health records, aiming to improve their robustness in real-world scenarios. The system reveals significant performance drops when agents are exposed to noise, indicating the need for more robust training methods.

papers.name: OSWorld-Science
papers.title: OSWorld-Science: A Benchmark of Computer Use Agents for Learning and Using Scientific Software
papers.summary: OSWorld-Science is a benchmark designed to evaluate visual language models (VLMs) on their ability to perform scientific tasks using specialized software interfaces. The paper demonstrates that while current VLMs are proficient in certain areas, they still struggle with complex scientific workflows and require further development.

papers.title: Design and implementation of an intelligent ICD coding system using large language model
papers.summary: The paper describes an automated ICD coding system that uses a large language model and a multi-agent framework to assign diagnostic and procedural codes accurately. The system was evaluated using real-world medical records, demonstrating high precision and recall rates for both diagnosis and procedure codes.

papers.name: PhenoAIR
papers.title: From Retrieval to Reasoning: Agentic Mechanism Prediction from Cell Painting Profiles
papers.summary: PhenoAIR is a reliability-aware multi-agent framework designed to predict mechanisms of action from Cell Painting profiles by reasoning over uncertain evidence. It outperforms existing methods in various MOA prediction settings, demonstrating its capability to handle noisy and misleading data.

papers.name: STAM
papers.title: Personalized State-Transition-Aware Memory for Clinical Agents
papers.summary: STAM is a memory framework for clinical agents that tracks patient state transitions while preserving historical context. It demonstrated improved performance in downstream tasks and diagnostics compared to baseline methods across four longitudinal clinical benchmarks.

papers.name: KlinikeBench
papers.title: KlinikeBench: Evaluating Language Models Beyond Diagnostic Accuracy
papers.summary: KlinikeBench evaluates language models in clinical settings beyond diagnostic accuracy by simulating full patient interactions, including history gathering and examination requests. The benchmark reveals a significant gap between diagnosis accuracy and interactive performance, with professional clinicians rating model-generated dialogues higher than real conversations.

papers.name: PrivMeSA
papers.title: PrivMeSA: Privacy-Aware Self-Evolving Multi-Agent System for Medicine via Local-Remote LLM Collaboration
papers.summary: PrivMeSA is a privacy-aware multi-agent system designed to manage medical consultations while minimizing patient data exposure. It uses reinforcement learning to balance task accuracy with privacy risks, demonstrating significant improvements in both clinical decision-making and privacy protection compared to direct remote consultation methods.

papers.name: gemot
papers.title: GEMOT: Towards Mechanistic World Models for Biology
papers.summary: gemot is an agentic framework that proposes explicit mechanistic models of biological systems and scores them against data through an MCP evaluation layer that keeps hypotheses auditable. On 18 published problems in molecular biology, epidemiology and immune differentiation its models matched or exceeded reference models in fit and parsimony.

papers.title: A Multi-Agent Framework for Explainable Brain Tumour Instance Segmentation and Clinical Report Generation Using ASIO-Optimised YOLO Architectures
papers.summary: The paper presents a multi-agent framework for brain tumor instance segmentation and clinical report generation using YOLO architectures optimized with ASIO. The system demonstrates improved diagnostic precision and rapid inference latency, outperforming baseline methods in terms of mean Average Precision.

papers.name: M3OS
papers.title: M3OS: A Monte Carlo Graph Search-Orchestrated Multi-Agent LLM System for Evidence-Traced Molecular Optimization
papers.summary: M3OS is a multi-agent system that uses large language models and Monte Carlo graph search to optimize small molecules for drug design, maintaining evidence-traced optimization histories. It demonstrates higher success rates in molecular optimization benchmarks compared to baseline methods.

papers.name: BIABench
papers.title: BIABench: Evaluating AI agents on real-world bioimage analysis tasks
papers.summary: BIABench is a benchmark designed to evaluate AI agents' ability to perform real-world bioimage analysis tasks end-to-end, including handling various imaging modalities and dimensions. The evaluation reveals that while agents can handle routine 2D tasks well, they struggle with more complex analyses involving 3D volumes or time-lapse sequences.

papers.title: Unknown is not normal: separating language-model extraction from rule-based decision logic for clinical risk scores
papers.summary: An LLM marks each finding present, absent or unknown while deterministic code computes score bounds and asks only the questions that could change the risk category, across six clinical calculators. On 1,200 synthetic emergency cases it matched asking everything with half the questions, while treating missing as normal under-triaged 8.5 percent of patients and an end-to-end agent asked irrelevant questions.

papers.name: CLEAR-Med
papers.title: Large Language Models for Structured Clinical Data Analysis: Dual-Agent Grounding and Validation
papers.summary: CLEAR-Med splits natural-language analysis of structured clinical data into an invocation agent that writes and runs SQL and a separate cross-provider validation agent that accepts, requests one repair, or abstains. On a 21-site neonatal encephalopathy table of 532 infants, the invocation agent answered 66.4% of benchmark queries correctly versus 12.0% ungrounded.

papers.title: LLM sequential decision making under uncertainty in biochemical domains
papers.summary: The paper evaluates large language models' decision-making processes in biochemical domains using Bayesian Optimization, revealing that while LLMs show a sincere intent to explore new data, they often overreact and fail to effectively balance exploration with exploitation. The study highlights the need for decoupling priors from incoming data to improve LLM-driven scientific discovery.

papers.name: ECG-Scroll
papers.title: ECG-Scroll: A Long-Horizon, Streaming Benchmark and Agent Environment for Interpretation of Ambulatory Electrocardiograms
papers.summary: ECG-Scroll streams long ambulatory ECG recordings to an agent chunk by chunk so it must decide what to measure, store evidence as it passes and flag paroxysmal events without seeing the future signal. Because the signal is kept, answers are checked against objective ground truth with rule-based rewards.

papers.title: Multi-agent LLM diagnostic teams improve differential recall on curated cases and reverse on real emergency notes: a label-level reversal without a clinician-judged safety difference
papers.summary: Compares a single LLM call, five personas in one context and five blinded specialist agents merged by a moderator on curated case collections and 364 real emergency notes. The moderated team improved top-3 recall on curated cases but lowered it on real emergency notes, with blinded physicians finding no difference in error danger.

papers.name: BioLitBench
papers.title: What Can a Leaderboard Certify? Compositional Controllability for Fair Evaluation and Training of Biomedical Literature-Review Agents
papers.summary: Introduces a stage-wise admissibility test that refuses comparisons between literature-review agents given unequal evidence or budgets, plus a benchmark of 2,042 biomedical articles as claim graphs. It refused 11 of 21 comparisons that conventional statistics would have decided, and a stage-reward-trained agent earned a certified top rank interval.

papers.name: AnewDDE
papers.title: AnewDDE: An Agentic Drug Discovery Engine for Biomolecular Interaction Modelling and Closed-Loop Design
papers.summary: AnewDDE is an integrated drug discovery engine that combines various AI capabilities for biomolecular interaction modeling and design, including structure prediction, affinity estimation, molecular design, and experimental decision-making. The system demonstrates superior performance in identifying high-affinity binders and provides scientific reasoning and ADMET predictions, validated through internal benchmarks designed by pharmaceutical experts.

papers.name: BioDyad
papers.title: BioDyad: Synchronize Biomedical Discovery and Machine Learning Engineering
papers.summary: BioDyad is a system that integrates biomedical discovery and machine learning engineering through two hierarchies within Monte Carlo graph search, enabling the iterative construction, execution, and validation of candidate programs. It demonstrated superior performance on the BioXArena benchmark compared to other agent methods and one-shot baselines.

papers.name: MACBT
papers.title: MACBT: A Multi-Agent Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Decision Support System with Longitudinal Memory
papers.summary: MACBT is a multi-agent system designed to support cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) for depression, aiding clinicians in session preparation and documentation. The system includes a longitudinal memory module that tracks patient progress over time, demonstrating improved professionalism and clinical authenticity compared to existing systems.

papers.name: Genome Skeptic
papers.title: AI Models Excel at Orchestration but Falter at Biological Judgment: Findings from an Agentic Gene Annotation Study
papers.summary: The Genome Skeptic framework evaluates the performance of AI models in orchestrating biological analyses and making judgments based on those analyses. The study found that while GPT-5.6 Sol excelled at efficiently directing follow-up analyses, it faltered when tasked with interpreting evidence to make accurate gene annotation decisions.

papers.name: PFArena
papers.title: PFArena: Benchmarking Language Models for Protein Modification
papers.summary: PFArena is a benchmark designed to evaluate the performance of various AI models in protein modification tasks, including single-mutant generation and multi-mutant ranking. The evaluation reveals that different model types excel under varying conditions but all face challenges as task complexity increases.

papers.name: SkinAgent AI
papers.title: SkinAgent AI: A Safety-Grounded Multimodal Agentic Framework for Non-Diagnostic Skincare Support
papers.summary: SkinAgent AI is a multimodal framework that uses visual evidence and product information to provide skincare support, ensuring safety and privacy. The system demonstrated high accuracy in skin condition routing and skin-type estimation but showed limitations in tool selection and task completion.

papers.name: T-REX
papers.title: Agentic campaign control for high-throughput de novo binder design
papers.summary: T-REX is an agentic framework that orchestrates multiple protein design tools to efficiently allocate computational resources and generate structurally distinct binder designs. It demonstrates adaptive orchestration's potential in complementing powerful protein design models by achieving higher throughput compared to baseline methods.

papers.name: BaseCamp
papers.title: BaseCamp --- An Agentic AI Framework for Automating DNA Sequencing Data Pipelines
papers.summary: BaseCamp assigns six specialized agents to the judgment layer of DNA sequencing pipelines, choosing thresholds, configuring established tools, adjudicating borderline variants and flagging cases for review while the tools do the analysis. Evaluation found agent configurations concordant with expert practice and cross-stage checks that surfaced anomalies normal monitoring misses.

papers.name: LabFactory
papers.title: LabFactory: Building and Evaluating Executable AI Labs
papers.summary: LabFactory is a framework that enables the creation of task-specific AI labs for various scientific tasks, integrating models, knowledge resources, and tools. The system demonstrated its effectiveness by successfully executing 10 constructed labs across different domains, surpassing reference values in all subtests under independent evaluation.

papers.name: DrGait
papers.title: DrGait: Biomechanically Grounded Visual Reasoning for Interpretable Clinical Gait Analysis
papers.summary: DrGait is a training-free framework that uses Vision-Language Models to analyze gait videos for clinical applications, ensuring interpretability and accuracy by decoupling semantic reasoning from geometric perception through a structured workflow. It demonstrates the ability to generate transparent and audit-ready clinical reports while maintaining competitive diagnostic accuracy.

papers.name: MolDesignBench
papers.title: MolDesignBench: Evaluating LLM-based Agent for Scenario-grounded Molecular Design
papers.summary: Contains 2,000 molecule generation and optimization tasks with implicit design narratives, explicit property constraints and infeasible cases, solved through 17 chemistry tools. The best frontier LLM succeeded on only about 43 percent, failing mainly on implicit constraints and infeasibility detection.

papers.name: FiberPro 1.0
papers.title: FiberPro 1.0: Multiagent AI-Guided Design for High-Throughput Production and Conformal Deposition of Functional Protein Micro/Nanofibers
papers.summary: FiberPro 1.0 is a multiagent AI framework that guides the high-throughput production and conformal deposition of functional protein micro/nanofibers using focused rotary jet spinning, demonstrating its ability to optimize formulations within two iterations on average. It successfully designed an antibacterial zein-based active packaging system for food matrices, showcasing real-world applicability in extending shelf life.

papers.name: ChatT2
papers.title: ChatT2: An Adaptive Framework for Developing a Large Language Model-Based Agent for Natural Product Domain Research
papers.summary: ChatT2 is a mentor-executor-evaluator agent system for research on bacterial type II polyketides that combines retrieval with bioinformatics and cheminformatics tools. The mentor clarifies user intent, the executor runs the tools and the evaluator checks outputs before they are returned.

papers.name: Llemy
papers.title: User-driven development and evaluation of an agentic framework for analysis of large pathway diagrams
papers.summary: Llemy is an LLM-based system designed to assist users in navigating and understanding complex molecular interaction maps. The paper details a user-driven development process involving domain experts, highlighting the system's ability to summarize pathways and its potential for future enhancements based on user feedback.

papers.title: Silent Failures in Agent-Tool Interaction: An Audit of ToolUniverse
papers.summary: This audit examined how agents interact with 15 scientific tools in the ToolUniverse environment and catalogued cases where a call looks successful but returns incomplete data. Of 91 validated silent failures, most arose in the API or wrapper layer and could propagate into apparently valid scientific outputs.

papers.name: Eli5a v2.0
papers.title: Comparative Evaluation of a New Autonomous AI Agent Versus Frontier LLMs for AI-Generated Patient Information Sheets on Pediatric Pathologies
papers.summary: Eli5a v2.0 is an autonomous AI agent designed to generate patient information sheets for pediatric oral pathologies and rare head and neck tumors. The study found that Eli5a excelled in understandability, reading grade level, and actionability compared to other LLMs, highlighting its potential in creating accessible educational materials for complex medical conditions.

papers.name: CReaTe-LM
papers.title: CReaTe-LM: A large language model for stepwise, heuristic clinical reasoning instruction
papers.summary: Three cooperating agents simulate teaching dynamics to build a Chinese dataset of 6,400 clinical reasoning tutoring dialogues, used to fine-tune and reinforcement-train an instructing model. It beat eight baselines, exceeding GPT-4.1 by 10 to 15 points under LLM, expert and NLP evaluation, and was tested in a classroom.

papers.name: TRACEDD
papers.title: TRACEDD: A Tool-grounded Reasoning and Agentic Coordination for Explainable Drug Design
papers.summary: TRACEDD is a multi-agent drug design framework in which LLM agents orchestrate tools for target validation, structure prediction, pocket finding, molecular generation, ADMET and retrosynthesis in a reason-act-observe loop. A JAK2 case study showed the workflow running end to end, including falling back to AlphaFold when no structure existed.

papers.name: OASIS
papers.title: OASIS, a self-evolving AI scientist that integrates omics data and literature knowledge for plant stress research
papers.summary: Six agents for planning, hybrid retrieval, evidence distillation, data interrogation, review and synthesis link literature with omics data, and a module distills past trajectories into reusable rules. It scored 84 of 100 on a plant stress benchmark, well above baseline LLMs, and a prioritized rice gene, OsPP2a, showed salt-response phenotypes when disrupted.

papers.name: SpecOpt
papers.title: SpecOpt: Contact-Diff Reasoning for Agentic Molecule Optimization Toward Binding Specificity
papers.summary: SpecOpt docks a compound against its intended target and known off-targets, compares residue-level contact differences and has an LLM propose structural edits that improve selectivity while keeping the scaffold. The authors built a ChEMBL-derived benchmark of intended and off-target activities to evaluate this.

papers.name: TrialAtlas
papers.title: TrialAtlas: Multi-Agent Research Organization for Clinical Trial Design and Optimization
papers.summary: TrialAtlas is a multi-agent system designed to assist in clinical trial design and optimization by synthesizing literature, analyzing regulatory precedents, and providing integrated reasoning. It demonstrated superior performance compared to baselines in predicting the success of clinical trials and detecting deficiencies, as validated through both automated benchmarks and expert evaluations.

papers.title: A Modular Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework Guided by Large Language Models: Improving Quality and Efficiency of Treatment Planning in Lung Radiation Therapy
papers.venue: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics
papers.summary: A two-level framework uses LLM planner, evaluator and supervisor agents to coordinate reinforcement-learning agents that adjust doses in lung IMRT treatment planning. On 62 retrospective lung cancer cases it improved plan constraint compliance and efficiency relative to knowledge-based planning.

papers.name: SAFE-AI
papers.title: A medically grounded LLM agent-based tool to detect patient safety events in medical records
papers.summary: SAFE-AI is a tool that uses an ontology-driven model to minimize hallucinations in large language models (LLMs) for detecting patient safety events, specifically medication errors, in medical records. The system demonstrated high accuracy and reliability in identifying epinephrine overdoses and delays in administration compared to human experts, showcasing its potential as a trustworthy clinical decision support tool.

papers.title: From Prompt to Pipeline: A Comparative Evaluation of Large Language Model Coding Agents for Reproducible Bioinformatics Pipeline Construction
papers.summary: The paper evaluates Biomni and two other agentic coding systems on constructing a bioinformatics pipeline for CUT&Tag data analysis. While the generated pipelines appeared plausible, they did not fully satisfy the requested analysis requirements, highlighting the need for expert review in complex workflow construction.

papers.name: CellForge
papers.title: AI Scientists for Building Virtual-Cell Models
papers.summary: Agents survey literature, parse data, choose baselines, debate a model design with a critic, then write and run training code to return a trained perturbation predictor. On six transcriptomic, epigenomic and proteomic datasets its models were competitive with hand-built state of the art, and blinded raters preferred its research plans.

papers.title: Large Language Model Agents for Evidence Based Genetic Disease Severity Classification
papers.summary: The Genetic Severity Classifier is an AI agent that uses a ReAct-RAG architecture to classify the severity of genetic diseases based on ACMG and ACOG guidelines. It achieved high accuracy in classifying disease severity at both phenotype and gene levels, demonstrating its potential for standardized panel design in genomic screening.

papers.name: MAESSCR
papers.title: Early evidence for a multi-agent AI simulator for clinical reasoning practice: performance, consistency, and challenges
papers.summary: MAESSCR is a medical education simulator in which several LLM agents play the patient, physical exam and diagnostic testing roles in text-based clinical encounters. In transcripts from 175 second-year students, clinician-educators found it followed scripted case details in most encounters but sometimes leaked diagnosis-changing information.

papers.name: CDTD-Agent
papers.title: CDTD-Agent: a retrieval-augmented multi-agent digital health framework for integrated diabetes care: a single-case expert-rated pilot study
papers.summary: CTD-Agent is a retrieval-augmented multi-agent framework designed for integrated diabetes care, combining Western medicine, traditional Chinese medicine, and lifestyle management. In a single-case expert-rated pilot study, CTD-Agent received favorable ratings compared to general-purpose LLMs across several clinically important dimensions.

papers.name: scACORN
papers.title: scACORN: Context-engineered agent orchestration of specialized small language models for single-cell transcriptomic interpretation
papers.summary: scACORN is a system that uses specialized small language models and an orchestrating agent to interpret single-cell transcriptomic data, addressing the challenge of heterogeneous tasks in single-cell analysis. The system demonstrates improved performance metrics such as macro-F1 scores and recall rates, while reducing unsupported gene citations.

papers.name: SpineAgent
papers.title: A multi-agent system for spine MRI report generation from multi-sequence imaging
papers.summary: SpineAgent is a multi-agent system designed to generate spine MRI reports by integrating information from multiple imaging sequences. It demonstrates superior performance in spinal condition prediction and pathology localization, achieving state-of-the-art results through automated metrics and expert evaluation.

papers.name: GeneResolver
papers.title: GeneResolver: A Traceable Hybrid Multi-Agent Pipeline for Etiology-Aware Gene Prioritization
papers.summary: GeneResolver is a hybrid multi-agent pipeline that classifies rare disease cases based on their etiology and then prioritizes genes accordingly. It demonstrated improved accuracy in gene prioritization compared to existing tools, particularly when combining phenotype and genomic variant data.

papers.name: WetRobo
papers.title: WetRobo: A Reproducible Robot Kit for Coding Agents in Biological Laboratories
papers.summary: WetRobo is a robot kit designed for biological laboratories that enables coding agents to perform tasks without the need for local teleoperation training data or neural network retraining. The system demonstrated successful task execution across different laboratory environments, showcasing its adaptability and practicality in real-world settings.

papers.title: On-premise medical AI agents for reliable clinical decision-making
papers.summary: The paper describes the development of an on-premise clinical AI agent that can perform diagnostic workflows autonomously, achieving high accuracy in disease diagnosis tasks. The system also includes a reliability framework to estimate uncertainty at decision time, which helps identify cases suitable for autonomous handling with high diagnostic accuracy.

papers.name: CPS-Net
papers.title: CPS-Net (Collaborating Physicians in Silico Network): A Decentralized Multi-Agent Transformer Framework for Specialty-Aware Disease Prediction
papers.summary: Language model agents in primary care, specialty and subspecialty tiers consult 41 cohort-specific transformers trained on EHRs and make referral decisions through shared case memory without central control. On 3,000 test cases it reached 48.8 percent top-1 accuracy versus 19.2 percent for a single transformer and 12.7 percent for a single agent.

papers.name: HypoEvolve
papers.title: HypoEvolve: Genetic Algorithms Enable Multi-Agent LLMs to Discover Scientific Hypotheses
papers.summary: HypoEvolve is a system that uses genetic algorithms to coordinate specialized large language model agents for scientific hypothesis discovery. It demonstrates superior performance in drug repurposing tasks across 34 cancer types, outperforming baseline methods by generating more selective and evidence-supported hypotheses.

papers.name: EMR
papers.title: EMR: Self-Evolving Medical Multi-Agent System via Experience Mining and Reuse
papers.summary: EMR is a self-evolving medical multi-agent system that uses experience mining and reuse to improve clinical decision-making. It demonstrates superior performance on medical reasoning benchmarks compared to existing systems, showing its ability to generalize across different specialties and LLM backbones.

papers.name: ClinAgent
papers.title: ClinAgent: A ReAct-Based Agent for Conversational Access to Clinical Trial Information
papers.summary: ClinAgent is a conversational system that uses an agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) model to enable clinicians and researchers to query clinical trial information using natural language. The system integrates various tools such as ClinicalTrials.gov search, PubMed module, and a Python-based analyzer for efficient multi-turn interactions, demonstrating improved accessibility and synthesis of clinical trial data compared to manual methods.

papers.title: Evaluating Safety-Critical Communication Behavior of Large Language Models Using Workflow-Embedded Multi-Agent Clinical Simulation
papers.summary: A role-locked multi-agent LLM simulation of nurses, registrars and nurse managers was used to test how LLMs escalate deteriorating ward patients with and without ISBAR handover. Structured handover reduced hallucinations and shortened dialogues but did not reduce safety-critical omissions, with automated audits checked against ICU nurses.

papers.title: Same Patient, Different Order: Action-Level Reliability of Clinical LLM Agents Under Repeated Runs
papers.summary: Replays MedAgentBench tasks with all inputs fixed and compares the orders an agent actually files rather than its score, using six reliability metrics over 1,000 runs. Nearly all ordering groups produced different order sets across identical runs, often while the benchmark recorded the same verdict.

papers.name: Asclepius
papers.title: Asclepius: An Adaptive Harness for Long-Horizon Clinical Agents
papers.summary: Uses a simulator of full emergency-department shifts to show agents diagnose well but miss timely critical actions, then adds a harness that rewrites its operating manual between shifts, a clinical skills library and three subagents splitting the patient queue. On held-out batches it improved critical-action correctness by 22 percent while keeping diagnostic accuracy.

papers.name: MedRoundsQA
papers.title: MedRoundsQA: A Persona and Difficulty Aware Evaluation for Multi-Turn Medical Consultations
papers.summary: MedRoundsQA is a benchmark for evaluating AI agents in multi-turn medical consultations, converting board-exam cases into structured dialogues. It demonstrates that moving from single-turn to multi-turn interactions significantly degrades diagnostic accuracy and highlights equity risks associated with patient personas.

papers.name: AAD-Agent
papers.title: An LLM-enhanced AI agent for rapid diagnosis of acute aortic dissection in multi-center settings
papers.summary: AAD-Agent is an AI agent designed to assist in the rapid diagnosis of acute aortic dissection before imaging confirmation, using large language models for enhanced diagnostic accuracy. The system demonstrated consistent performance across different LLMs and settings, showing promise as a low-cost triage tool but with limitations on confirmatory diagnosis.

papers.name: AI-SP
papers.title: Evaluating Scaffolding-Oriented Multi-Agent Large Language Model System for Clinical Interview Training
papers.summary: This platform combines a simulated patient agent, a tutor agent giving Socratic prompts without revealing the diagnosis and a turn-level evaluator agent for clinical interview training. In a randomized study with 100 medical students, the multi-agent condition improved final OSCE-based scores though not diagnostic accuracy.

papers.title: AI agents’ system for automatic ICD predication
papers.summary: The paper introduces a multi-agent AI system for automatic ICD code generation in medical claims, which includes agents for input extraction, coding with enhanced GPT-2 XL model, and report compilation. The system was evaluated on real-world data achieving 95% accuracy, demonstrating its potential to streamline clinical decision support and reduce human error.

papers.title: Skill-File-Guided Virtual Screening: A Single-Target Formyl Peptide Receptor 2 Case Study of Large-Language-Model-Coordinated Physics and Diffusion Docking
papers.summary: A Claude Code agent prepared ligand libraries and ran Uni-Dock and DiffDock virtual screens on formyl peptide receptor 2 with either default choices or a Markdown skill file encoding expert protocol decisions. The skill-guided protocol raised Uni-Dock ROC AUC from 0.701 to 0.733.

papers.name: BRACED
papers.title: Bridge-Aware Reinforced Compositional Exploration and Decomposition for Biomedical Multi-Hop Answering
papers.summary: BRACED is a system designed to improve multi-hop reasoning in biomedical question answering by using reinforcement learning to optimize the decomposition of complex queries into simpler sub-queries. It demonstrates significant improvements over existing methods on the BioHopR benchmark, highlighting its effectiveness in retrieving accurate and verifiable answers.

papers.name: QuickFold
papers.title: Agent-driven Model Development for RNA 3D Structure Prediction
papers.summary: The paper describes the use of a large language model agent to iteratively develop an RNA 3D structure prediction model, QuickFold. The model was developed through a feedback-driven process where the agent proposed and implemented changes over multiple iterations, eventually matching leading open-source baselines in performance.

papers.title: Performance, Failures, and Oversight of a Large Language Model Agent for Clinical Data Analysis: Evaluation Study
papers.summary: The study evaluates an LLM agent's performance in clinical data analysis across five stages, using a dataset of patients with neovascular age-related macular degeneration. The agent reliably generates research questions and statistical analysis plans but requires expert oversight for code execution accuracy.

papers.title: From Clinical Free Text to Auditable Concepts: An Agentic Framework for Interpretable Prediction
papers.summary: The paper introduces an agentic workflow that converts unstructured clinical free text into interpretable features for predictive tasks, using large language models (LLMs) and local extractors. The framework improves prediction accuracy while reducing computational costs compared to direct LLM processing of full corpora.

papers.title: Real Science Is Harder Than Benchmarks: Evaluating Advanced AI Frameworks on Published Studies. II. Antibody Properties, Lipid-RNA Interactions
papers.summary: Runs Kosmos, K-Dense, ToolUniverse, BioAgents and AI Scientist-v2 on reproducing antibody developability prediction and lipid-RNA molecular dynamics studies from industry. The frameworks caught some methodological issues but none matched the scope of the originals, and several hallucinated or failed badly.

papers.name: MErlin
papers.title: From code to natural language: MErlin – a multi-omics toolkit for bacterial epigenomics delivered as Claude agent skill
papers.summary: MErlin is a 17-module bacterial epigenomics toolkit also delivered as an agent skill that lets an LLM assistant select and run the audited modules with preflight checks and human-input rules. It was validated on synthetic data with planted signals and demonstrated on a Pseudoalteromonas methylome-transcriptome comparison.

papers.name: ABLE
papers.title: Agentic BAIM-LLM Evaluation (ABLE): Benchmarking LLM Use of Protein Design Tools
papers.summary: ABLE benchmarks how well LLM agents use protein design tools such as ProteinMPNN and AlphaFold3 across structure retrieval, sequence generation and design validation.
