Of 15 frontier models, seven refused all tasks and the rest varied widely, with the best still inconsistent at planning compared with an expert baseline.

papers.name: MedCP
papers.title: An agentic AI framework connecting language models to electronic health records and a biomedical knowledge graph for real-world evidence
papers.summary: MedCP is an agentic AI framework that integrates large language models with electronic health records and a biomedical knowledge graph, enabling interactive human supervision for multi-step reasoning. It demonstrated improved performance in clinical research tasks and factual accuracy questions, while also facilitating the rapid replication of observational studies.

papers.name: Karenina
papers.title: Turning Domain Expertise into Multi-Dimensional Evaluation of Biomedical AI with Karenina
papers.summary: Karenina is an open-source framework that evaluates biomedical AI systems by incorporating expert knowledge across multiple dimensions, going beyond simple scoring to ensure trustworthy decision-making. The system illustrates its utility in evaluating question-answer pairs, multi-turn conversations, and autonomous data analysis tasks.

papers.title: BIT.UA at BioASQ 14B: Modular Retrieval with pg_textsearch and Qdrant, and Agent-Based Answer Generation
papers.venue: CLEF 2026 Working Notes, 21 - 24 September 2026, Jena, Germany
papers.summary: This BioASQ submission pairs modular BM25 and dense retrieval with an agent quorum in which several differently prompted LLM agents debate and converge on a consensus biomedical answer. It also uses an LLM-as-a-judge step and adaptive document retention for answer generation.

papers.title: A Structured Debate-Mixture-of-Agents Framework for Complex Clinical Diagnostic Decision Support
papers.summary: The Debate-Mixture-of-Agents (DMoA) framework uses a structured multi-agent approach to improve iterative diagnostic reasoning in complex clinical settings. It demonstrated significant improvements in diagnosis accuracy and safety rate compared to single-model approaches, highlighting the potential of multi-agent systems for clinical decision support.

papers.name: Bioinfoysis
papers.title: Bioinfoysis Technical Report
papers.summary: Bioinfoysis treats each bioinformatics request as a persistent analysis run where a planner keeps an executable checklist and replans from structured handoffs after each worker step. A controlled runtime validates generated scripts, tables and figures before they are reused, binding conclusions to the evidence that produced them.

papers.name: VERGE
papers.title: VERGE: Verification-Enhanced Refinement for Grounded Extraction of Early-Onset Colorectal Cancer Symptoms in Clinical Notes
papers.summary: VERGE is an agentic workflow designed to extract early-onset colorectal cancer symptoms and family history risk status from clinical notes. It uses a verification-refinement cycle to enhance accuracy, reducing false positives while maintaining detection of true cases.

papers.name: VERDICT
papers.title: Accountable AI with Grounded, Faithful, Consistent, Actionable Rationales: A Case Study in Clinical Trial Matching with VERDICT
papers.summary: VERDICT is an AI system designed for clinical trial matching that uses SMT solvers to ensure consistent application of decision policies and generation of accountable rationales. It outperforms other systems in terms of decision accuracy, policy consistency, and the quality of generated rationales as preferred by clinicians.

papers.title: A Multi-Agent Clinical Decision Support System with Patient Similarity Retrieval on MIMIC-IV
papers.summary: The system uses a multi-agent architecture to support clinical decision-making by retrieving patient similarity data from an electronic health record database and using large language models for analysis. It demonstrates the ability to generate temporally-aware clinical analyses through a case study, showcasing its potential in real-time clinical reasoning.

papers.name: FairMedAgent
papers.title: Instability Floors: Separating Bias from Noise in Fairness Audits of Clinical LLM Agents with FairMedAgent
papers.summary: FairMedAgent measures how often a clinical LLM agent changes its action on identical repeated inputs, establishing an instability floor against which counterfactual fairness flip rates must be read. Across six models the floor ranged from 2.5% to 23.7%, and majority voting over five draws removed about 39% of it.

papers.title: Let large language models judge each other: multi-agent peer-reviewed reasoning for medical question answering
papers.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
papers.summary: The paper introduces a multi-agent peer-reviewed reasoning method for medical question answering, where large language models independently generate and evaluate each other's chain-of-thought reasoning to produce final answers. This approach outperforms single-model and majority voting methods in terms of accuracy on benchmark datasets.

papers.name: MetaboAnnotate
papers.title: MetaboAnnotate: An AI-powered Multiagent Framework for Integrating Annotation Tools for Untargeted Metabolomics
papers.summary: MetaboAnnotate is a web-based framework that uses a large language model to integrate and orchestrate multiple metabolite annotation tools for untargeted metabolomics, enabling users to submit MS/MS spectra without local installation or programming expertise. The system demonstrates improved accuracy in metabolite identification through consensus among integrated tools on benchmark datasets.

papers.name: PlanningCopilot
papers.title: PlanningCopilot: An agentic framework integrating ESAPI modules for autonomous treatment planning in lung radiotherapy
papers.summary: PlanningCopilot is an agentic system that integrates large language models and a validated Eclipse Scripting API module to autonomously generate treatment plans for lung radiotherapy. The study demonstrates its ability to produce clinically acceptable plans, meeting dosimetric requirements and improving optimization efficiency through self-learning.

papers.name: DDA
papers.title: DDA: a traceable multi-agent framework for automated structure-based drug design
papers.summary: The Drug Discovery Agent (DDA) is a multi-agent framework designed for automated structure-based drug design, integrating various bioinformatics and molecular modeling tools. It was evaluated on the CrossDocked2020 benchmark, demonstrating superior performance with a higher screen-pass rate compared to specialized baselines.

papers.name: CyChat
papers.title: CyChat: a conversational Cytoscape app for no-code, reproducible network analysis
papers.summary: CyChat is a Cytoscape app that integrates a chat interface with an AI agent to facilitate no-code, reproducible network analysis. It was evaluated across various workflows and LLM providers, demonstrating high accuracy and efficiency compared to manual GUI workflows.

papers.name: SAGE
papers.title: Local large language model-guided optimization for prostate radiotherapy planning
papers.summary: The SAGE system uses a locally deployed large language model to autonomously optimize radiotherapy plans for prostate cancer patients, demonstrating its ability to generate clinically acceptable treatment plans. The study found that incorporating intra-case memory significantly improved sparing of the penile bulb while maintaining target coverage.

papers.name: ELISA
papers.title: ELISA (Embedding-Linked Interactive Single-cell Agent): an interpretable hybrid generative Artificial Intelligence agent for expression-grounded discovery in single-cell genomics
papers.summary: ELISA is a hybrid AI agent designed for single-cell genomics that integrates expression embeddings with semantic retrieval and large language model interpretation to facilitate interactive discovery. It outperforms existing methods in cell type retrieval tasks and can generate biologically plausible hypotheses, bridging the gap between transcriptomic data exploration and mechanistic biological understanding.

papers.name: PlanningCopilot
papers.title: Improving portability of knowledge-based planning using an LLM-driven plan refinement framework in lung radiotherapy
papers.summary: The Planning Copilot is an LLM-driven framework that refines radiotherapy treatment plans generated by knowledge-based planning models, improving their clinical goal achievement and portability across different institutions. It demonstrates significant improvements in plan quality metrics without the need for model-specific tuning or retraining.

papers.name: Living-OEP
papers.title: Development and validation of a human-supervised AI-augmented living oncology evidence platform: a breast cancer pilot study
papers.venue: ESMO real world data and digital oncology
papers.summary: An agentic system following a human annotation manual decomposes systematic review tasks, self-debugs and validates its outputs over tens of thousands of trial abstracts, linking structured results to guideline treatment pathways. Review accuracy was 95.1 to 97.2 percent against human annotations and the platform gave more comprehensive evidence than general AI search tools.

papers.title: Reference Composition Biases Automated Cell Annotation and Obscures Biological Signals in Xenotransplantation Single-cell Atlases
papers.summary: The paper evaluates the impact of reference composition biases on automated cell annotation in xenotransplantation single-cell atlases using Biomni, a biomedical agent. It reveals that biased references can lead to widespread mislabeling and obscure biological signals, highlighting the need for auditing reference compositions when interpreting AI-assisted annotations.

papers.name: EvoSCM
papers.title: EvoSCM: Scientific Belief Revision Through Causal Model Evolution and Experimentation
papers.summary: EvoSCM keeps a population of structural causal model hypotheses, uses them to pick discriminating experiments, and distils contradictions into correction rules that revise the models. Evaluated on physics, chemistry and biology tasks, it explained and predicted better than baseline agents while using experimental budget more efficiently.

papers.name: ClinTraceBench
papers.title: ClinTraceBench: Source-Verifiable Longitudinal Clinical Reasoning over EHR-Derived Dialogues
papers.summary: ClinTraceBench provides 385 MIMIC-IV-derived verified dialogues with event-level provenance and nine task types to test whether compressed patient histories preserve longitudinal signal. Comparing eight history strategies, including two agentic memory systems, across four models it found compression loses relational facts that the agents fail to recover.

papers.name: SPROUT
papers.title: A Multi-Agent Large Language Model Reasoning Engine for Early Detection of Pediatric Growth Disorders
papers.summary: A specific LLM screener flags concerning growth trajectories in pediatric records, then an orchestrator runs a panel of agents, corrected by a trainer-injected learner agent, to rank differential diagnoses. In walk-forward simulation the screener reached 98 percent specificity a year before diagnosis, and expert review confirmed suspicion in a third of flagged controls.

papers.title: CPT/HCPCS Code Recommendation from Clinical Notes: A Comparative Evaluation of AI Methods
papers.summary: The paper evaluates various AI methods for recommending CPT and HCPCS codes from clinical notes, focusing on recall within a fixed number of recommendations. It finds that zero-shot GPT-5.6-Sol achieves the highest recall among tested models.

papers.title: An Agentic Retrobiosynthesis Framework with Learned Frontier Selection
papers.summary: The Agentic Retrobiosynthesis Framework uses large language models to select which molecules to expand next in a deterministic biochemical search, demonstrating that policy-based frontier selection can enhance the efficiency of retrosynthetic pathway discovery. The framework's performance was evaluated using various benchmarks, showing improvements over traditional methods like MCTS and direct prompting.

papers.title: Toward Workflow-Aware Benchmarking for Healthcare NLP Agents
papers.summary: This work defines an episode-level evaluation protocol for healthcare agents that scores state continuity, evidence traceability and escalation decisions rather than one-shot answers. It is instantiated as four task templates covering documentation updates, evidence retrieval, patient messaging and triage handoff, with cost-sensitive treatment of escalation errors.

papers.name: DIASENTINEL
papers.title: DIASENTINEL: An Auditable Multi-Agent System for Guideline-Grounded Diabetes Risk Screening
papers.summary: DIASENTINEL is a multi-agent system designed for diabetes risk screening that integrates guideline-based recommendations with real-time patient data, ensuring reliable and auditable clinical decision support. The system demonstrates the capability to generate detailed reports grounded in ADA guidelines while maintaining patient privacy.

papers.name: MASGR
papers.title: Evidence, Logic, and Compliance: Multi-Agent Structured Graph Reasoning with Expert Arbitration for Medical Referral
papers.summary: MASGR is a multi-agent system designed to improve medical referral decisions by constructing structured graphs that integrate evidence from various patient data sources. It demonstrates superior performance in handling complex cases compared to existing models, highlighting its capability to balance chronic disease management with emergency interventions.

papers.name: GPAgentBench-2K
papers.title: GPAgentBench-2K: Benchmarking Large Language Model Agents in Complex Clinical Action Space
papers.summary: GPAgentBench-2K is a benchmark designed to evaluate large language model agents in complex clinical decision-making scenarios, using real-world GP encounter data. The system reveals significant performance degradation and safety issues among leading models when dealing with more realistic action spaces.

papers.title: Agentic AI uncovers conserved cross-tissue protein co-abundance programs inaccessible to single-dataset analysis
papers.summary: An LLM agent framework builds tissue-specific protein co-abundance networks, derives consensus clusters for tissue pairs and grounds them in atlases, interaction databases, pathways, disease catalogues and literature. Run over all 820 pairs of 41 human tissues and fluids it found 1,833 conserved clusters across 406 pairs.

papers.name: FedEHR-Agents
papers.title: FedEHR-Agents: Federated Agentic Optimization for Automated EHR Modeling
papers.summary: FedEHR-Agents is a federated learning framework that enables autonomous clinical agents to collaboratively model electronic health records while preserving patient data privacy. It demonstrates improved performance in diverse clinical prediction tasks compared to local and federated baselines, highlighting the potential of federated autonomous clinical intelligence.

papers.name: CaRDI
papers.title: Beyond Uncertainty Reduction: Calibrated Planning for Interactive Diagnosis
papers.summary: CaRDI is a planning framework for interactive medical diagnosis that selects questions based on clinical risk rather than uncertainty reduction, aiming to minimize diagnostic errors and severe omissions. Experiments demonstrate that CaRDI improves accuracy while requiring fewer questions compared to existing methods.

papers.name: NMRAgent
papers.title: Towards Generalizable and Evidential Nuclear Magnetic Resonance-Based Molecular Structure Elucidation via Large Language Model Agent
papers.summary: NMRAgent is a large language model-based agent designed to interpret complex NMR spectra for molecular structure elucidation, combining database retrieval and de novo generation with evidential reasoning. It demonstrated superior accuracy and transparency compared to existing methods on benchmarks involving novel scaffolds and real-world applications.

papers.name: DynaMate
papers.title: DynaMate: An Autonomous Agent for Protein-Ligand Molecular Dynamics Simulations
papers.summary: DynaMate is an autonomous multi-agent system designed to automate protein-ligand molecular dynamics simulations, reducing setup time and improving efficiency. It successfully executed MD simulations on a diverse dataset of systems, demonstrating its adaptability and robustness in biomolecular modeling.

papers.name: Co-Scientist
papers.title: Accelerating Scientific Research with Gemini in the Real-World
papers.summary: This work extends the Gemini-based Co-Scientist from in silico hypothesis generation to closed-loop work with real instruments across materials science, biology and computer science. In biology it predicted emergent behaviors and ran lab-in-the-loop cycles, alongside reactor-driven materials syntheses.

papers.name: AgentFold
papers.title: AgentFold: Closed-Loop Agentic Search for Protein Folding Model Design
papers.summary: Agents propose hypotheses, edit and debug code in an ESMFold codebase, train and evaluate variants, and store successful and failed interventions in memory under a tree-search resource policy. Exploring about 80 variants with roughly 5,000 GPU-hours it improved best lDDT by 7.5 percent over independent proposals and random search.

papers.name: GraphRAG
papers.title: A multi-agent GraphRAG framework for pharmacotherapy safety verification in clinical decision support systems
papers.summary: The GraphRAG framework integrates large language models with a pharmacotherapy knowledge graph to enhance the safety verification of clinical decision support systems. The system was evaluated on benchmark cases and showed improved accuracy in answering clinical safety questions compared to traditional retrieval augmentation approaches.

papers.name: BixBench3
papers.title: BixBench3: Benchmarking AI agents on research-study-scale computational biology tasks
papers.summary: BixBench3 is a benchmark designed to evaluate AI agents' ability to perform computational biology tasks at the scale of complete research studies, from raw data processing to generating scientific results. The study reveals that leading large language models (LLMs) vary significantly in their capacity to handle sequential analysis steps and manage large datasets across different biological domains.

papers.title: Interoperable Web Platform Based on Large Language Models for Medical Data Analysis: A Protocol for Clinical Decision Support
papers.summary: The paper describes an interoperable web platform that integrates clinical data using FHIR and LLMs to support medical data analysis and decision-making. The system demonstrates improved semantic interoperability and contextual reasoning, evaluated through both quantitative metrics and qualitative assessments.

papers.name: MARLA
papers.title: MARLA: An Autonomous Agent for Medical AI Research and Development
papers.summary: MARLA is an autonomous agent designed to facilitate medical AI research by translating high-level clinical goals into executable research loops, coordinating specialized code agents, and refining strategies based on feedback. It demonstrates the capability to autonomously conduct complex medical AI tasks with reduced reliance on AI expertise.

papers.title: Federation Is Nearly Free, Reasoning Is Not: Tradeoffs for AI Co-Scientists in Protein Characterization Workflows
papers.summary: The paper evaluates the performance of autonomous agents in protein characterization tasks, finding that while language models like Opus provide high accuracy, cheaper deterministic policies can achieve near-frontier accuracy with better reproducibility. Federation across institutional boundaries imposes a negligible penalty on performance.

papers.name: MTDiag
papers.title: MTDiag: A Multi-Turn Diagnostic Dataset Towards Clinically Meaningful LLM Evaluation
papers.venue: Chouayfati, Pia, et al. "MTDiag: A Multi-Turn Diagnostic Dataset Towards Clinically Meaningful LLM Evaluation." Proceedings of the 27th Annual Meeting of the Special Interest Group on Discourse and Dialogue. 2026
papers.summary: MTDiag is a physician-validated multi-turn diagnostic dialogue dataset built from DDXPlus, MIMIC-IV and case reports, normalized to UMLS and ICD-10, with a patient utterance generator. It adds knowledge-grounded metrics for judging models as interactive diagnostic agents rather than static answerers.

papers.name: EviDx
papers.title: EviDx: Evidence-Aware Active Diagnosis with Scaffolded LLM Agents
papers.summary: EviDx builds interactive diagnostic environments from raw clinical cases and runs role-specialized agents with evidence tools and an observer harness that decides when enough evidence has been gathered to stop. A three-level evaluation covers execution robustness, reasoning dynamics and diagnostic outcome.

papers.name: FrontierChallenge
papers.title: FrontierChallenge: Evaluating Scientific Workflow Completion
papers.summary: FrontierChallenge is a benchmark for evaluating scientific workflow completion across various domains, assessing models' ability to produce complete research artifacts. The study reveals that high partial scores and confident claims of task completion do not reliably indicate full delivery, underscoring the need for comprehensive evaluation of end-to-end workflows.

papers.name: BioCheck Agent
papers.title: Generating Biomedical Fact-Checking Reports with RL-Enhanced Agentic Search
papers.summary: BioCheck Agent fact-checks biomedical claims by issuing Boolean PubMed searches, appraising the retrieved literature and writing a structured report rather than a bare label. Reinforcement learning is used to improve its search and reasoning for public health claim verification.

papers.name: MediSkill-Evo
papers.title: MediSkill-Evo: Process-Constrained Self-Evolution for Evidence-Grounded Clinical Interaction
papers.summary: MediSkill-Evo is an interactive clinical agent that self-evolves its process knowledge to improve evidence-grounded decision-making in medical scenarios. It demonstrates significant improvements in diagnosis accuracy and treatment intent coverage compared to existing agents, while also reducing critical failures under stress conditions.

papers.name: TrialCode Agent
papers.title: TrialCode Agent: LLM-Assisted Clinical Code-Set Construction for Trial Emulation
papers.summary: TrialCode Agent is a hybrid-large language model system designed to translate free-text clinical trial criteria into computable code sets, supporting various medical terminologies. The study demonstrated that while retrieval and broad family expansion can improve performance in specific cases, deterministic verification significantly enhances the validity and readiness of generated code sets for database use.

papers.name: KMGen
papers.title: KMGen: A Skill-based Approach for Synthetic Individual Patient Data Generation
papers.summary: KMGen is an automated framework that extracts Kaplan-Meier curves and generates synthetic individual patient data, including adverse event trajectories. It demonstrates high accuracy in curve extraction and effective generation of realistic patient data across various clinical trial conditions.

papers.name: DeepSAGE
papers.title: DeepSAGE: Stage-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Structured CBT Counseling Dialogue
papers.summary: DeepSAGE represents a first cognitive behavioral therapy session as eleven stages, with a controller judging stage completion and a reinforcement learning policy choosing therapeutic intentions that steer LLM responses. Against six alternatives it gave higher simulated client engagement and the best balance of stage-goal completion and efficiency, with expert review of the transcripts.

papers.title: Role-Specialized Mixture-of-Agents with Open-Weight LLMs for Clinical Prediction
papers.summary: Combines medical knowledge retrieval and similar-patient reasoning across specialised analyst agents feeding a smaller integrator agent, varying roles while holding retrieval fixed. For in-hospital mortality it matched closed-model prompting on F1 while flagging more true high-risk patients, with smaller gains for readmission.

papers.name: BioMed-Agent-RL
papers.title: BioMed-Agent-RL: A Meta Learning, All You Need for Biomedical Applications
papers.summary: BioMed-Agent-RL orchestrates clinical grounding, lesion segmentation and reasoning expert models through a policy trained with preference optimization and group relative policy optimization. It is aimed at multimodal clinical cases where static agent pipelines mishandle noise and modality mismatch.

papers.name: FRAC-MAS
papers.title: FRAC-MAS: A Safe and Explainable Multi-Agent System for Fracture Diagnosis
papers.summary: FRAC-MAS is a multi-agent system designed for automated and explainable bone fracture diagnosis, integrating deep vision models with conformal prediction to ensure statistical reliability. The system demonstrates improved clinical interpretability and safety by triaging cases into high-confidence and uncertain categories, outperforming single-agent systems in patient preference studies.

papers.name: HiMA-MDD
papers.title: HiMA-MDD: A Hierarchical Multi-Agent Harness for Interpretable Multimodal Depression Detection in Clinical Interviews
papers.summary: HiMA-MDD is a hierarchical multi-agent system designed to interpret multimodal clinical interviews for depression detection, breaking down the task into three layers of agents that handle evidence collection, symptom scoring, and profile verification. The paper shows that HiMA-MDD outperforms existing methods on the E-DAIC dataset.

papers.name: MSM-Mem
papers.title: MSM-Mem: A Universal Medical Structured Multimodal Memory Framework for Medical AI Agents
papers.summary: MSM-Mem is a memory framework for medical AI agents that enables them to retain and utilize clinical experiences over time, improving their decision-making abilities. Evaluations show consistent performance improvements as the agent accumulates more experience.

papers.name: ATHENA
papers.title: Agentic neural architecture search for clinical prediction from electronic health records: Cross-hospital knowledge transfer and computational efficiency
papers.summary: ATHENA is a framework that uses neural architecture search to optimize Transformer-based models for clinical prediction from EHRs, enabling efficient and effective model selection across different hospitals. It demonstrates superior performance compared to baseline methods in various clinical tasks, showcasing its capability to transfer knowledge and maintain computational efficiency.

papers.name: DDx-Finder
papers.title: A Human-in-the-Loop Large Language Model System Based on the Model Context Protocol for Differential Diagnosis from Electronic Medical Records and Literature
papers.summary: DDx-Finder is an open-source framework that uses large language models and the Model Context Protocol to extract clinical state information from electronic medical records and literature, aiding in differential diagnosis. The system demonstrates its potential for providing accessible and systematic diagnostic support by addressing operational challenges such as resource constraints and privacy concerns.

papers.name: ChatInvent
papers.title: Designing a Robust LLM-Based Evaluation System for Agentic AI in Drug Discovery Through Human Alignment
papers.summary: The paper introduces an evaluation framework for ChatInvent, a drug discovery assistant using large language models (LLMs), focusing on human alignment and output quality dimensions. It validates the LLM's performance as a judge through expert annotations and demonstrates improvements in aligning with human judgments.

papers.title: Benchmarking System Configurations for Rubric-Constrained Personalized Exercise Planning
papers.summary: Compares a plain LLM, single-agent, multi-agent and ReAct configurations that turn wearable data into daily workout plans on 50 matched user-days, scored by four blinded LLM judges on eight rubric criteria. Deterministic preprocessing before the LLM drove the gains, while differences among the scaffolded configurations were not significant.

papers.name: LabBridge
papers.title: Clinical Laboratory Terminology Standardization for Semantic Interoperability Using a Large Language Model-Based Agent: Methodological Study
papers.summary: LabBridge is a large language model-based framework that standardizes laboratory test terminologies to the LOINC standard, enhancing semantic interoperability across different languages and institutions. The system demonstrated high accuracy in mapping laboratory tests from both Chinese and English datasets, outperforming baseline methods.

papers.name: GEOMeta
papers.title: Automating scientific annotations for open transcriptomic profiles via multi-stage agents
papers.summary: GEOMeta is a multi-stage pipeline of task-specific LLM agents that retrieves, extracts, standardizes, ontology-maps and quality-checks GEO metadata. It annotated about 600,000 human bulk RNA-seq samples, and a comparison of 22 LLMs showed cheaper open models matching leading reasoning models.

papers.name: Biomni
papers.title: Autonomous biomedical research with an artificial intelligence agent
papers.summary: Biomni is a general biomedical agent whose environment was built by mining tools, databases and protocols from publications across 25 domains, combined with retrieval-augmented planning and code execution. It generalized across tasks such as gene prioritization, drug repurposing, rare disease diagnosis and cloning, and was shown in case studies running analyses and lab protocols.

papers.name: AGVF
papers.title: Agentic Governance and Adversarial Verification for Policy-Constrained LLM Healthcare Appeal Generation
papers.summary: AGVF generates medical-necessity appeals through five agents for policy formalization, evidence retrieval, gap analysis, adversarial critique and gated synthesis, with a citation gate blocking unsupported claims. The authors prove the refinement loop terminates and validate the implementation on 1,000 synthetic appeal cases.

papers.title: A knowledge-guided agentic framework for mitigating patient-context ambiguity in health queries
papers.summary: This framework sits between a patient and an unchanged downstream model, using a knowledge graph to build plausible hypotheses for an underspecified health question, find the missing patient details and ask targeted follow-ups. It was tested with five language models on two controlled ambiguity benchmarks including symptom-based diagnosis retrieval.

papers.title: A Multidisciplinary Team-Based Large Language Model Framework for Predicting Postoperative Neurological Complications in Acute Type A Aortic Dissection: Model Development and Validation Study
papers.summary: Compares single-agent and multidisciplinary-team LLM settings, with and without cohort summary statistics in context, for predicting neurological complications after acute type A aortic dissection surgery. Validated on 763 retrospective and 120 prospective patients against machine learning models such as random forest.

papers.name: ED-Triage-Agent (ETA)
papers.title: ED-triage-agent: a multi-agent framework for human-in-the-loop emergency triage
papers.summary: ED-Triage-Agent is a multi-agent framework designed to assist in emergency department triage by providing provisional acuity assessments based on symptom data alone and refining these assessments once vital signs are available. The system demonstrated high accuracy and sensitivity in prioritizing patient care, with performance comparable to existing benchmarks.

papers.name: HistAgent
papers.title: HistAgent: an evidence-grounded agent for spatial molecular reasoning from routine histology
papers.summary: HistAgent couples a visual-omics model trained on 2.23 million H&E-spatial transcriptomics spots with an agentic module that organizes inferred readouts into evidence cards for multi-turn analysis. It recovered literature-defined spatial findings and reproduced five standard spatial analyses at lower cost than conventional workflows.

papers.title: Multi-Agent AI System for Radiology Report Structuring and Quality Assurance with Independent Radiologist Evaluation
papers.summary: A locally deployed pipeline of rule-based and LLM agents restructures CT reports into anatomical sections and flags findings-impression mismatches, gender-anatomy conflicts and undocumented critical results. It flagged 14.1 percent of 638 reports, and two radiologists rated QA good or excellent in 84 percent of reviewed reports with no fabricated content.

papers.name: ICD-Deepresearch
papers.title: Foundation Agents Meet Agentic Deep Research: Evidence-Grounded Clinical Code Forecasting
papers.summary: ICD-Deepresearch is a clinical decision support system that forecasts future diagnosis codes for patients using a combination of predictive models and medical search tools. It demonstrates improved precision and recall compared to standalone systems, with higher usefulness ratings from physicians for the evidence it retrieves.

papers.name: The Little Scientist
papers.title: The Little Scientist: LLM Agent-Driven Discovery via the Scientific Method
papers.summary: The Little Scientist is an LLM-based agent that follows the scientific method to discover new algorithms and ensemble strategies. It demonstrated its capability by outperforming existing methods in protein fitness prediction and DNA motif discovery.

papers.name: BioFirewall
papers.title: BioFirewall: A genome-writing-native governance layer for design-stage biosecurity screening of agentic AI
papers.summary: BioFirewall is a middleware system designed to screen genome-writing plans for biosecurity risks, operating between the foundation model and DNA synthesizer stages. It demonstrated high accuracy in detecting hazardous sequences while maintaining low false-refusal rates, showcasing its potential as an effective governance tool during the design stage of agentic AI systems.

papers.name: ACCREDIT
papers.title: ACCREDIT: A Quality-Aware Agentic Engine for Cell-resolved Cross-modal Image Registration with Dynamic Iterative Tuning
papers.summary: ACCREDIT registers spatial omics images to H&E sections with deterministic pipelines, scores registration quality without a reference, and calls an LLM rescue agent to diagnose failures and pick recovery strategies. It treats registration as an iterative decision process that rejects plausible but incorrect alignments.

papers.name: PHA
papers.title: Grounding Health AI: Architecture and Evaluation of a Domain-Expert Metabolic Health Agent
papers.summary: The PHA is a specialized metabolic health agent that generates accurate and trustworthy clinical reports by grounding its generation in four layers: HPP cohort data, domain-expert tools, declarative skills, and automated evaluations. It demonstrates significant improvements in structural completeness, numerical accuracy, and compliance with clinical language standards compared to general-purpose models.

papers.name: ASTA
papers.title: Autonomous Spatial Transcriptomics Analysis (ASTA): Demonstrating Performance Improvements through Clustering, Biological Annotation, and AI-Driven Discovery
papers.summary: ASTA combines ensemble clustering, marker-based cell annotation and a GPT-4o-mini agent for autonomous spatial transcriptomics analysis. Clustering improved silhouette scores over single methods and the agent produced three biological hypotheses with validations on ovarian tissue.

papers.name: DeLiriuMAgents
papers.title: A large language model-driven multidisciplinary AI agent system predicts delirium in emergency critically ill patients
papers.summary: DeLiriuMAgents combines a machine learning risk model, LLM specialist agents for emergency medicine, neurology and psychiatry, and retrieved evidence to predict delirium in emergency critically ill patients. It was validated on MIMIC-IV, a two-hospital Peking University cohort and eICU, with accuracy between 0.67 and 0.75, and clinicians reviewed its reasoning.

papers.name: Union-then-Filter Framework
papers.title: From Computational Prediction to In Vivo Experimental Validation: A Translational AI Pipeline for Anthracycline-Induced Cardiotoxicity
papers.summary: The system uses a 'Union-then-Filter' framework to prioritize cardioprotective drugs for anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity by combining predictions from multiple graph learning models and filtering with evidence synthesis from PubMed abstracts. It successfully identified novel drug candidates that were validated in zebrafish models, demonstrating the pipeline's potential for translational research.

papers.name: MARC v1
papers.title: MARC v1: An Open-Source Multi-Agent Framework for Clinical AI Reasoning and Coordination
papers.summary: MARC v1 is a multi-agent framework for clinical AI reasoning that replaces monolithic large language model prompting with specialized agents for extraction, reasoning, answer generation, and evaluation. The system demonstrates the ability to coordinate these tasks deterministically, making it interpretable and accessible even to non-programmers.

papers.title: Virtual-cell verification enables self-auditing AI discovery for immune rejuvenation
papers.summary: The paper introduces a verification framework for AI-driven drug discovery in immune rejuvenation, featuring verifiers like PACE and CellQ to ensure predictions align with biological data. The system demonstrates self-correction capabilities by refining its scoring logic based on experimental results.

papers.name: SABLE
papers.title: A Modular Agentic Framework for Synthetically Constrained Multi-Objective Hit-to-Lead Optimization
papers.summary: SABLE is a modular framework that uses an LLM to interpret user-defined goals and route tasks for hit-to-lead optimization in drug discovery. It enriches candidate sets by evaluating only a subset of the enumerated search space, demonstrating its effectiveness in prioritizing synthetically constrained analogs.

papers.name: GatorOnco
papers.title: An Agentic Generative Large Language Model for Treatment Planning of Colorectal Cancer
papers.summary: GatorOnco is an agentic large language model designed for colorectal cancer treatment planning, which integrates time-sensitive clinical guidelines through a retrieval-augmented generation approach. In a randomized evaluation by oncologists, GatorOnco demonstrated expert-level performance in treatment planning and received higher ratings for readability and completeness compared to human experts.

papers.name: AMIE
papers.title: Towards Expert-level Medical AI for Real-time Video Consultations
papers.summary: AMIE was extended to real-time video consultations as a Gemini-based multi-agent system combining low-latency dialogue, clinical reasoning and audio-visual perception. In a randomized OSCE with 30 primary care physicians, 15 patient actors and 100 scenarios, evaluators rated the video configuration against physicians and the text-only version.

papers.name: ATLAS
papers.title: Coupled Graph--Policy Distillation for Personalized Medication Safety in Older Adults with Multimorbidity
papers.summary: ATLAS is a framework that uses a coupled graph-policy distillation approach to personalize medication safety for older adults with multiple conditions. It structures guideline evidence into a medication-safety graph and updates this based on patient-specific information, achieving superior performance in decision-making benchmarks compared to existing systems.

papers.title: Agentic AI-driven Immersive Simulation: A Knowledge-Aware Virtual Training Platform for High Dose Rate (HDR) Brachytherapy
papers.summary: The paper introduces an agentic AI-driven immersive simulation for training in HDR brachytherapy, using VR and mobile computing to create a risk-free learning environment. The system integrates a knowledge-aware assistant that provides real-time guidance based on clinical guidelines, validated through prototype deployment with promising results.

papers.name: GrEBI
papers.title: AI semantics for biomedical data integration
papers.summary: The GrEBI system uses a multi-agent architecture to integrate and query multimodal biomedical data across different scales and organisms, grounded in biological knowledge from ontologies. It demonstrates the capability of large language model agents to perform cross-cutting queries on complex, heterogeneous datasets when provided with scientifically accurate grounding.

papers.title: Conversational Large Language Models for Vestibular Diagnosis in Outpatient Clinics: Prospective Multicenter Diagnostic Accuracy Study
papers.summary: The paper evaluates DeepSeek-R1, a conversational large language model deployed in outpatient vertigo clinics to assist with vestibular diagnosis. The system showed high diagnostic concordance rates (around 80%) compared to specialist diagnoses, particularly for benign paroxysmal positional vertigo and Ménière disease.

papers.name: Fisher-R1
papers.title: Fisher-R1: Training LLM Agents for Reliable Hypothesis Testing
papers.summary: P-Bench holds 425 open-ended hypothesis-testing tasks from economics, biology and medicine where an agent must choose a method, compute a p-value and conclude, and Fisher-R1 is an open-weight agent trained with reinforcement learning for this. Fisher-R1-14B improved substantially over its backbone and beat strong baselines, exposing inferential errors that benchmarks scoring only execution miss.

papers.name: CliniCARE-Bench
papers.title: CliniCARE-Bench: Clinical Calibrated Audit of Medical Reasoning in EHR
papers.summary: CliniCARE-Bench has agents audit 750 MIMIC-IV-derived cases from 25 clinician-validated scenarios through a logged tool environment, returning yes, no or one of two kinds of indeterminate verdict. It scores evidence and policy grounding, process adherence, calibrated abstention and efficiency against independently adjudicated references.

papers.name: ResidencyRL
papers.title: ResidencyRL: Reinforcement Learning in Simulated Clinical Environments
papers.summary: ResidencyRL trains a clinical agent through simulated multi-turn encounters of up to 60 turns and 8 tool calls against rewards for diagnosis, management, communication, documentation and safety. On held-out evaluations it raised diagnostic accuracy under adversarial simulated patients from 81.0% to 88.0% and cut missed red flags by 31%.

papers.name: Research Assistant
papers.title: Research Assistant: AstraZeneca's Agentic System for R&D
papers.summary: Research Assistant is an internal large language model-based system at AstraZeneca designed to assist scientists and clinicians in exploring biomedical questions across various data sources. The system provides a chat-style interface that supports both direct question answering and multi-step research tasks, demonstrating its utility in supporting day-to-day R&D workflows.

papers.name: nMAS
papers.title: Tracing the Heart: An Evidence-Linked Pipeline for Heart-Failure Feature Engineering
papers.summary: The Nimblemind Multi-Agent System (nMAS) is an automated pipeline for heart-failure feature engineering from electronic health records, using a multi-agent architecture to integrate fragmented data and clinical guidelines. It demonstrated improved predictive performance in phenotyping heart failure subtypes and achieved high scores on rubric assessments of evidence support and methodological soundness.

papers.name: QuanTiMedAI
papers.title: QuanTiMedAI: Quantum-Enhanced Time-Series Model guided by Agentic AI for Cardiac Arrest Mortality Prediction
papers.summary: QuanTiMedAI is a quantum-enhanced time-series model guided by an agentic AI for predicting mortality in cardiac arrest patients. It uses a large language model to discover clinically relevant features and a compact quantum recurrent network for temporal prediction, demonstrating superior performance with fewer parameters compared to existing methods.

papers.name: ECHO
papers.title: ECHO: A Locally-Deployable Agentic Health Assistant with Temporal Memory, Safety Guardrails, and Speech Assessment
papers.summary: ECHO is a locally-deployable conversational health assistant designed for chronic care management, integrating an agentic chatbot with clinical tools and safety layers. It demonstrates high accuracy in tool execution and safety classification, as well as effective multimodal speech assessment.

papers.title: Towards Accessible Radiological Image Analysis via Local Agentic Framework: Validation in Mammography
papers.summary: The paper introduces an LLM-driven agentic framework that can reconstruct, optimize, and customize deep-learning models for radiological image analysis on a consumer-grade PC. The system demonstrated improved performance in mammography analysis across multiple datasets and outperformed radiologists in a reader study.

papers.name: OntoCodex
papers.title: OntoCodex: a multi-agent biomedical ontology enrichment framework
papers.summary: OntoCodex is a multi-agent framework that uses large language models and ontologies to semi-automatically enrich biomedical knowledge bases, improving precision, recall, and F1 scores in concept extraction across various chronic diseases. The system demonstrated enhanced accuracy in standardized terminology mapping for medications but showed lower performance in laboratory test mapping.

papers.name: AgentEYE
papers.title: An autonomous multimodal AI agent for evidence-grounded ophthalmic diagnosis
papers.summary: AgentEYE is an autonomous multimodal AI agent designed to integrate ocular imaging data and medical evidence for ophthalmic diagnosis. It demonstrated higher diagnostic correctness, completeness, and safety compared to large language model baselines in both internal benchmarks and blinded evaluations by ophthalmologists.

papers.name: MTS-Bench
papers.title: MTS-Bench: A Manchester Triage System Benchmark for Language Model Triage Safety
papers.summary: DR. INFO is an agentic AI clinical assistant that retrieves from a curated clinical knowledge base, with an additional MTS-specific retrieval configuration. The study shows that DR. INFO significantly reduces undertriage rates compared to general-purpose language models like GPT-5.1 when used for emergency triage.

papers.name: DRAgent
papers.title: An agentic multidisciplinary framework for diabetic retinopathy treatment planning
papers.summary: DRAgent is a multi-agent system designed for diabetic retinopathy treatment planning, integrating ophthalmology and endocrinology expertise. The system demonstrates improved performance over standalone large language models in generating individualized patient plans, as validated through both automated metrics and human evaluations.

papers.name: CASCADE
papers.title: CASCADE: An Agentic Regulatory Network Framework for Patient-Data-Validated Downstream Perturbation Prediction
papers.summary: CASCADE is an agentic framework that predicts downstream transcriptional effects of gene perturbations using precomputed regulatory networks. It demonstrates strong concordance with real patient data for MYC knockdown predictions, outperforming baseline methods and existing knowledge.

papers.name: CANOE
papers.title: Adaptive Arena-based Contestable Argumentative Network-of-Experts for Open-Ended Care Plan Coordination
papers.summary: CANOE is a multi-agent neuro-symbolic framework designed for care plan coordination in healthcare, using an arena-based argumentation system to resolve conflicts and generate acceptable intervention plans. The evaluation demonstrates that CANOE provides clinically correct and safe recommendations while also offering transparent explanations through its argumentative structure.

papers.name: DoctorAgents
papers.title: DoctorAgents: an agentic framework to iteratively refine AutoML pipeline for small clinical temporal data
papers.summary: DoctorAgents builds and optimizes machine learning pipelines for small temporal clinical datasets using generation, validation and refinement agents that pass natural-language feedback as textual gradients. Across several clinical tasks it beat established AutoML baselines while yielding more interpretable task-specific representations.

papers.name: ANCHOR-RE
papers.title: ANCHOR-RE: An Agentic Biomedical Relation Extraction Framework with Retrieval Augmentation and Error-Driven Verification
papers.summary: ANCHOR-RE is an agentic framework for biomedical relation extraction that uses retrieval augmentation and error-driven verification to enhance the reliability of knowledge graph construction and hypothesis generation. The system demonstrated improved performance across various benchmarks, showing its capability to generalize well even with newly published literature.

papers.title: Agents Catching Agents: Shortcut Cascades and Benchmark Gaming in Clinical Multi-Agent Systems
papers.summary: This study tested whether committees of Gemini agents deliberating on clinical cases can be gamed by cues a clinician would ignore, across seven cohorts of text, imaging and ICU tabular data. Individual agents resisted the cues, but when two peers asserted the same wrong answer the agent under test adopted it 38% of the time, and only one of three oversight agents detected this reliably.

papers.title: Learning Clinical-Trial Strategy: Offline Policy Training for Decision Agents
papers.summary: Frames oncology clinical development as an offline decision task where an agent predicts a drug program's next trial portfolio from date-gated public records, and compares offline-trained policies with frontier LLM agents using a shared retrieval scaffold. Reward-weighted behavioral cloning beat the best tool-using LLM agent on indication-level and strict F1.

papers.name: Agentic OODA Framework
papers.title: An Agentic OODA Framework for Transparent End to End Clinical Decision Support
papers.summary: The Agentic OODA Framework is a multi-agent system designed for clinical decision support that breaks down the decision-making process into modular, stateful agents. It was evaluated in stroke care and showed significantly higher reliability and consistency compared to general LLM models.

papers.title: Architectural Safety Mechanisms for Multi-Agent Clinical LLM Systems Under Knowledge Base Distribution Shift
papers.summary: The paper evaluates multi-agent LLM architectures for maintaining guideline compliance in clinical decision support systems under knowledge base distribution shifts. It shows that a stateful graph architecture with an independent safety floor mechanism can maintain high compliance even when the retrieval quality degrades, though it introduces additional latency.

papers.name: Gemma curation agent
papers.title: Detailed curation of biological samples and experimental designs for genomics using LLM-supported agentic workflows
papers.summary: The Gemma curation agent is an automated software tool that uses large language models and traditional methods to curate biological sample data for genomics studies, achieving near-human performance at a fraction of the cost and time. The system's evaluation includes benchmarking against human-curated datasets and preliminary error triage methods to identify potential inaccuracies.

papers.title: A Privacy-Preserving Zero-Code Conversational Statistical Analysis System for Clinical Research Using Agentic AI and Local R Execution
papers.summary: The system translates natural-language clinical research requests into executable R workflows, ensuring privacy by retaining patient data locally. It was validated in a study on metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, demonstrating its capability to execute complex statistical analyses without manual coding.

papers.name: MedSR-Copilot
papers.title: A PRISMA-Aligned Agentic Framework for Medical Systematic Reviews and Evidence Synthesis
papers.summary: MedSR-Copilot is a multi-agent system designed to automate medical systematic reviews under the PRISMA workflow, covering literature retrieval, screening, data extraction, and evidence synthesis. It demonstrates significant improvements in efficiency and accuracy when used as a copilot in human-AI collaboration studies.

papers.title: Reference-Free large language model agents for physician-guided radiotherapy treatment planning
papers.summary: The paper presents a large language model agent that assists in radiotherapy treatment planning for head-and-neck cancer patients, demonstrating its ability to generate plans comparable to those made by certified dosimetrists. The study highlights the potential of using reference-free LLMs to streamline clinical workflows and reduce variability in treatment planning.

papers.name: RelAgent
papers.title: RelAgent: a multi-agent solution for molecular relationship grounding
papers.summary: RelAgent is a multi-agent system designed to bridge the semantic-structural gap in molecular relationship grounding, improving tasks like patent interpretation and structural analysis. It demonstrates substantial improvements over existing models on the MolGround benchmark, showcasing its effectiveness in entity extraction, substructure localization, and ontology-guided relationship reasoning.

papers.name: HS-MIND
papers.title: [Development of a multidisciplinary intelligent nexus for decision support in digestive malignancies and its application to comprehensive perioperative management in older patients]
papers.venue: Zhonghua wei chang wai ke za zhi = Chinese journal of gastrointestinal surgery
papers.summary: An on-premises system layers data and knowledge, retrieval and tool-augmented reasoning, multi-agent collaboration and clinical application with safety governance for digestive malignancy management. Used before multidisciplinary discussions for 25 older patients, its conflict-detection module fired in five cases involving cardiovascular risk or antithrombotic therapy.

papers.name: CORA
papers.title: Large language models improve physician accuracy but lead to false reliance
papers.summary: CORA is a retrieval-augmented large language model designed to provide source-linked clinical support for physicians, improving their decision-making accuracy. The study revealed that while CORA enhances physician accuracy and adoption of correct advice when supported by citations, it also reduces resistance to incorrect advice when such advice appears citation-supported.

papers.name: C-Mind
papers.title: A Neuro-Symbolic Knowledge Graph and Large Language Model Hybrid Architecture for Multi-Modality Mental Health Counseling
papers.summary: A clinical knowledge graph routes therapeutic decisions for an LLM across eight psychotherapy modalities, tested with guideline vignettes and progressively disclosing simulated patient agents. It routed 116 of 117 vignettes appropriately, detected 96.7 percent of adversarial crisis probes and 98.5 percent of external suicidal-ideation dialogues, with fully auditable decisions.

papers.name: MDArena
papers.title: MDArena: Evaluating Coding Agents on Realistic Molecular Dynamics Workflows
papers.summary: MDArena evaluates the performance of coding agents on realistic molecular dynamics tasks, finding that while some configurations show promise with partial successes, significant challenges remain for complex and detailed scientific workflows. The benchmark provides a platform to track progress in automating biomolecular simulation research.

papers.title: A Multiagent Large Language Model Framework for Emergency Treatment Recommendation in Acute Ischemic Stroke: Development and Validation Study
papers.summary: The paper presents a multiagent large language model framework for recommending emergency treatments in acute ischemic stroke, which integrates clinical data and imaging information to provide accurate treatment suggestions. The system was validated using real-world cases and showed improved accuracy and safety compared to single-agent models, with potential to enhance decision-making among less-experienced physicians.

papers.name: EMBL AI Librarian
papers.title: EMBL AI Librarian: Life-Sciences Knowledge Layer for AI Agents
papers.summary: EMBL AI Librarian is a knowledge layer designed to enhance the Europe PMC interface for AI agents, enabling them to query in natural language and receive precise evidence. It demonstrates improved performance across various benchmarks, including literature synthesis and claim verification tasks.

papers.name: CyberNeuro
papers.title: CyberNeuro: A Privacy-Preserving Agentic Workbench for Cohort-Scale Neuroimage and Clinical Data Analysis
papers.summary: CyberNeuro is an AI-driven workbench designed to automate and streamline neuroimaging data analysis, reducing the need for manual intervention. It demonstrated significant improvements in accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods while maintaining clinical-grade privacy.

papers.name: MA-RAG
papers.title: MA-RAG: Multi-Agent Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Query-Driven Summarization of Longitudinal Parkinson's Disease Assessments
papers.summary: MA-RAG is a multi-agent framework designed to generate accurate and temporally consistent summaries of longitudinal Parkinson's disease assessments. It improves factual correctness and reduces hallucinations compared to baseline methods, as validated by clinical experts.

papers.name: CIViC MCP
papers.title: CIViC MCP: integrating large language models with the Clinical Interpretations of Variants in Cancer
papers.summary: The authors built a Model Context Protocol server that lets LLM clients query the CIViC cancer variant knowledgebase through its API in natural language. In a benchmark it improved retrieval of clinical significance and ran much faster than GPT-5 Agent Mode browsing the web.

papers.title: A Large Language Model-Driven System for Advance Care Planning Training Among Health Care Providers in the Chinese Context: Development and Technical Evaluation
papers.summary: The paper describes the development and evaluation of a multi-agent system using large language models for advance care planning training in Chinese healthcare. The system, which includes an assistant, vignette, and evaluator agent, was evaluated through both automated metrics and human assessments, showing significant improvements over baseline models.

papers.name: Swin-Qwen3
papers.title: Swin-Qwen3: a three-stage vision-language framework for automated radiology report generation with multi-agent verification
papers.summary: Swin-Qwen3 is a vision-language framework designed to generate accurate radiology reports from chest X-rays, incorporating a three-stage process for drafting, verification, and refinement. The system demonstrates modest improvements in clinical accuracy and factual consistency compared to simpler models but still requires further validation before clinical deployment.

papers.name: ClinLens
papers.title: ClinLens: Towards Long-Horizon LLM Agents for Longitudinal Multimodal Clinical Data Science
papers.summary: ClinLens is a benchmark designed to evaluate large language model agents on longitudinal clinical data science tasks, focusing on patient-centric workflows. The system assesses the ability of these agents to maintain context and integrate multimodal evidence over time, revealing that while some agents perform well in execution success rates, they struggle with strict pass rates due to issues like incorrect patient episode grounding.

papers.name: GuideSkill
papers.title: GuideSkill: Evolving Executable LLM Agent Skills for Guideline-Grounded Clinical Reasoning
papers.summary: GuideSkill is a system that compiles clinical practice guidelines into executable functions to assist in differential diagnosis, improving diagnostic accuracy. It demonstrates significant performance gains over existing methods and receives positive expert evaluations for its clinically sound and reliable rules.

papers.name: PatientAgentBench
papers.title: PatientAgentBench: A Benchmark Framework for Evaluating Patient-Facing Health AI Agents
papers.summary: PatientAgentBench is a benchmark framework that evaluates AI agents designed to interact with patients in healthcare settings, assessing their ability to converse, reason about health records, and act on behalf of the patient. The system revealed significant clinical gaps among various models, particularly in triage quality, clinical safety, and workflow accuracy, highlighting the need for more comprehensive evaluation standards beyond static benchmarks.

papers.name: Cardiologent
papers.title: Cardiologent: Multi-Agent Clinical Decision Support for Patient-Level Arrhythmia Assessment, Urgency, and Management
papers.summary: Per-signal agents read ECG and PPG windows using measured features, assemble a patient rhythm profile and reason over retrieved guidelines, with a critic agent checking each conclusion against its cited guideline. It ranked first on diagnosis, significance and management tasks under both cardiologist and LLM-judge scoring.

papers.name: GraphRareBench
papers.title: GraphRareBench: An Auditable Graph-Evidence Benchmark for Phenotype-Driven Rare-Disease Diagnosis
papers.summary: GraphRareBench is a benchmark of 2,365 ontology-derived rare disease cases with fixed candidate pools, graph-defined hard confounders and source-linked evidence records. Tool-using agents reached MRRs around 0.72-0.75, close to supervised rankers, but differed greatly in how much of the supporting evidence they actually examined.

papers.name: TCellAlign
papers.title: TCellAlign: Cross-study T-cell Populations Alignment with Nomenclature-Guided Multi-Agent Workflow
papers.summary: TCellAlign aligns study-specific T-cell population labels to standardized nomenclature using agents for literature retrieval, information extraction, nomenclature-guided alignment and evidence-based adjudication. The authors built a manually validated benchmark linking study labels, CZ CELLxGENE annotations and standard T-cell names across 44 curated studies.

papers.name: Plato-Bio
papers.title: Plato-Bio: verification-first biological novelty screening with temporal rediscovery and structural benchmarks
papers.summary: Plato-Bio extends the Plato/Denario research agent architecture for biology with explicit workflow states, provenance records, citation checks, claim-to-evidence links and publication gates. A source audit fixed three evaluation defects, and in a frozen pre-1986 rediscovery task it ranked the later-confirmed fish oil and Raynaud link first.

papers.name: Pathology-CoT
papers.title: Pathology-CoT: learning visual chain-of-thought agents from expert whole-slide image diagnosis behaviour
papers.summary: Pathology-CoT is an AI framework that captures and learns from the interactive diagnostic behavior of expert pathologists to navigate whole-slide images, propose regions of interest, and provide explainable diagnoses. The system demonstrated superior performance in detecting gastrointestinal lymph node metastasis compared to existing vision-language models.

papers.name: MetaClaw
papers.title: MetaClaw: an auditable AI agent for end-to-end, multi-directional metagenomic and multi-omics analysis
papers.summary: MetaClaw maps a user request to registered metagenomic and multi-omics workflows, runs standardized upstream processing and study-specific downstream analyses in isolated containers, and records parameters and outputs per job. Across four published cohorts with 769 profiles it recovered most of the originally reported marker groups.

papers.title: Enhancing Psychiatry Training Using an Agentic AI Simulated Consultation Tool: Prospective Cohort Study
papers.summary: The STACER Agentic System uses AI agents to simulate psychiatric consultations and provide structured feedback, demonstrating technical feasibility in supporting psychiatry residents' consultation skills. The system showed high behavioral fidelity and medical faithfulness but had limitations in facilitating rapport building.

papers.name: BioSecBench-Surveillance
papers.title: BioSecBench-Surveillance: A Verifiable Benchmark for AI Agents in Pathogen Genomic Surveillance
papers.summary: One hundred evaluations give agents only the raw sequencing data and context a human analyst would have, across seven task categories and several sequencing technologies, and grade structured answers deterministically. The best of sixteen model-harness pairs cleared only about half, with errors coming from choices of references, thresholds and normalization.

papers.name: PULSE
papers.title: A knowledge-enhanced domain-aware large language model agent for atrial fibrillation management
papers.summary: PULSE is a knowledge-enhanced, domain-aware large language model agent designed to improve atrial fibrillation patient self-management. It integrates multimodal inputs and clinical knowledge bases to enhance the accuracy, integrity, utility, safety, empathy, and clarity of medical outputs compared to leading base LLMs.

papers.title: Generating guideline-concordant and safe recommendations for diabetic kidney disease management via a hierarchical retrieval-augmented large language model
papers.summary: A hierarchical multi-agent system combines a local guideline retrieval module with a cloud reasoning model to produce management recommendations for diabetic kidney disease. Twelve physicians rated its outputs on 267 multi-center cases as more accurate and safer than unaugmented LLMs, especially for renal-stage medication contraindications.

papers.name: CardioAgent
papers.title: CardioAgent: A Traceable Agentic and Retrieval-Augmented Architecture for Cardiovascular Clinical Decision Support
papers.summary: CardioAgent is a clinical decision support system that integrates an LLM with deterministic tools and guideline retrieval to enhance cardiovascular diagnosis accuracy. In evaluations, CardioAgent demonstrated improved accuracy over generic models by incorporating structured workflows and traceability features.

papers.title: Safety-aware AI for NSCLC trial pre-screening: a comparative proof-of-concept study of rule-based, single-agent, and multi-agent approaches
papers.summary: This proof-of-concept compared rule-based, single-agent and multi-agent LLM configurations, with a safety agent for abstention, for pre-screening patients for NSCLC trials. On 90 held-out synthetic patient-trial pairs, the study focused on which setups reduced false inclusion of ineligible patients.

papers.name: SHARE
papers.title: A framework for human-artificial intelligence co-learning for disease activity labeling using electronic health records
papers.summary: The SHARE system uses a human-AI co-learning framework to accurately label disease activity from electronic health records, improving the quality of gold-standard labels and identifying ambiguous cases for further review. It demonstrates scalability in labeling large datasets while maintaining accuracy through efficient resource allocation.

papers.name: TCGA-Agent
papers.title: A ReAct Agentic AI System for Natural Language Querying and Statistical Analysis of The Cancer Genome Atlas Clinical Data
papers.summary: The TCGA-Agent is an agentic system that uses a large language model to query and analyze The Cancer Genome Atlas clinical data, providing natural language responses with statistical analysis. It outperforms other methods in accuracy and completeness, especially for fields not covered by the curated CDR.

papers.name: EnzGFM-Agent
papers.title: An enzyme-specific protein language model for catalytic property prediction
papers.summary: EnzGFM-Agent is a protein language model specifically designed for enzymes, which uses hierarchical pre-training to predict catalytic properties from amino acid sequences. The system demonstrates improved performance and efficiency in predicting enzyme properties compared to general-purpose models, with experimental validation showing its potential in reducing the need for extensive wet-lab screening.

papers.title: Agentic Calibration of Grey-Box Simulation Models: An LLM-Driven Alternative
papers.summary: The paper introduces an agentic calibration method using a large language model to optimize grey-box simulation models, showing it achieves lower error rates with fewer evaluations compared to traditional methods under unconstrained conditions. Under constrained conditions, the method performs comparably while being more efficient and offering explainability through textual rationale.

papers.title: Multi-Agent Dynamic Refinement Outperforms Static RAG in Clinical Reasoning for Complex Nephrology Cases
papers.summary: The Multi-Stage Iterative Clinical Reasoning Agent framework uses a multi-agent architecture to improve clinical reasoning in complex nephrology cases by iteratively refining its responses. The system outperformed both baseline large language models and static retrieval-augmented generation methods, demonstrating the importance of dynamic refinement for longitudinal medical reasoning.

papers.name: ReCo
papers.title: ReCo: a self-configuring and self-extending agentic framework for biomedical research
papers.summary: ReCo is a self-configuring and self-extending agentic framework for biomedical research that uses a large language model to interact with various computing tools and servers. It successfully operationalized five heterogeneous systems, demonstrating its capability in configuring, documenting, and integrating diverse biomedical frameworks.

papers.name: BioPathfinder
papers.title: BioPathfinder: Evidence-guided multi-agent platform enables hypothesis discovery for CAR-T engineering
papers.summary: BioPathfinder links publications with patient single-cell data in a provenance-aware knowledge resource and uses role-specialized LLM agents to generate, review and prioritize mechanistic hypotheses. Applied to CAR-T studies, it nominated NKG2A, and blocking it improved CAR-T antitumor activity in vivo.

papers.name: RadFabric
papers.title: Interpretable agentic AI system with localized reasoning for radiology
papers.summary: RadFabric is an agentic AI system that integrates multiple CXR analytics models and VLMs to provide explainable diagnoses. It demonstrated superior performance in detecting various lesion types, especially uncommon ones, compared to existing state-of-the-art models.

papers.title: Autonomous radiotherapy planning via agentic orchestration using a multimodal TPS-integrated compound AI platform
papers.summary: The paper describes a compound AI platform for autonomous radiotherapy treatment planning that integrates multi-agent large language models and dose prediction tools. The system was evaluated on 60 retrospective cases, demonstrating its ability to achieve dosimetric criteria comparable to clinical reference plans.

papers.name: MEDA
papers.title: Automatic Ordinary Differential Equations Discovery For Biological Systems Using Large Language Model Powered Agentic System
papers.summary: Retrieves background knowledge, fixes admissible variables and mechanistic constraints, proposes candidate differential equations for biological dynamical systems, then fits and evaluates them. It recovered correct state variables and structures in retrieval and extrapolation tasks, with ablations showing the knowledge-based constraints were essential.

papers.title: Evaluating Frontier AI Agents as Autonomous Clinical Security Auditors
papers.summary: Defines a containerized task in which frontier agents, using only a bash shell, implement four attacks and compute a security score for clinical prediction models on breast cancer and MIMIC-IV data. Claude Sonnet 4.6 and GPT-4.1 completed all runs correctly, while GPT-4o finished 61 percent.

papers.name: PAUSE-Agents
papers.title: PAUSE-Agents: A Clinician-in-the-Loop Multi-Agent AI Pipeline for ICU-to-Ward Handoff Briefs
papers.summary: PAUSE-Agents is a clinician-in-the-loop multi-agent AI system designed to draft structured handoff briefs for ICU-to-ward transfers, using role-specialized agents and safety checks. The system was evaluated by physicians who reviewed 100 drafts, showing high accuracy with minimal errors and omissions.

papers.title: Autonomous Agents for Auditable Cardiovascular Artificial Intelligence Development
papers.summary: The paper introduces two autonomous agents, Iteration and Evolution, which optimize AI-enhanced electrocardiography models for structural heart disease by proposing and evaluating code changes. These agents improved the model's performance in external evaluations without requiring new data or human intervention.

papers.name: EcoXAI
papers.title: EcoXAI: Autonomous Agentic Ecosystem for Explainable Artificial Intelligence and Biomedical Discovery
papers.summary: EcoXAI is a containerized multi-agent system with bioinformatics agents and explicit knowledge graph integration that runs staged analyses and produces grounded explanations. In an Alzheimer's drug repurposing case it evaluated 103 candidates and flagged 79 novel ones, including maraviroc, with later literature support.

papers.name: JADE-Plus
papers.title: JADE-Plus: A Multimodal Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation Large Language Framework for Diagnostic Support in Jawbone Lesions: Development and Technical Validation Study
papers.venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
papers.summary: JADE-Plus is a multimodal, agentic retrieval-augmented generation framework designed to assist in the diagnosis of jawbone lesions. It integrates vision-language models and an agentic verification loop for improved diagnostic accuracy and stability, outperforming other systems in clinical decision support tasks.

papers.title: A Controlled Comparison of Human and AI-Assisted Automated Revision of Delphi Statements on RNA-Based Medicines: Parallel, 2-Arm Study
papers.summary: The paper evaluates an AI-assisted pipeline for revising Delphi statements on RNA-based medicines, comparing its performance to human reviewers. The AI system, comprising multiple agents for citation detection and summarization, achieved comparable consensus rates with human oversight, demonstrating potential for accelerating expert consensus while maintaining methodological rigor.

papers.title: Agentic systems for breast cancer treatment recommendations
papers.summary: The paper evaluates agentic large language model systems for breast cancer treatment recommendations using real clinical cases and rubrics. The best system, Claude Opus 4.8 with D&C+SA pipeline, showed mixed performance improvements depending on the tool use and agent autonomy, highlighting persistent clinically relevant errors despite generating some clinically relevant recommendations.

papers.name: OCellus
papers.title: OCellus: A Language-Model Framework for Single-Cell, Spatial, and Perturbation Biology with Natural-Language Reasoning
papers.summary: OCellus is a nine-billion-parameter language model fine-tuned on various biological tasks, enabling it to perform spatial reasoning, perturbation prediction, and multi-task queries without specialized architectural modifications. It demonstrates superior performance across multiple benchmarks compared to existing models, showcasing its capability in natural-language explanations of predictions.

papers.title: Information-seeking failures of large language models in agentic clinical reasoning
papers.summary: The paper evaluates large language models' ability to engage in clinical reasoning by developing an agentic evaluation framework for hematologic oncology, finding that the best-performing model achieved only 68% accuracy. It highlights a failure of information-seeking under uncertainty as the primary limitation rather than medical knowledge deficits.

papers.name: CellPilot
papers.title: CellPilot: an agentic framework that pilots small language models through autonomous single-cell annotation
papers.summary: Guides a locally deployed small language model through single-cell analysis from raw counts to cluster annotation, planning steps, running standard tools, inspecting intermediate results and revising decisions. On GTEx it lifted an 8B model from 0.39 to 0.89 accuracy, near GPT-4o, and beat reference-, marker- and LLM-based annotators on three atlases.

papers.name: RadGuide AI
papers.title: RadGuide AI: Development and Technical Evaluation of a General Nuclear Medicine Agent for Traceable Radiopharmaceutical Decision Support
papers.summary: RadGuide AI is a nuclear medicine agent that integrates QA items, literature, and clinical trial data to provide traceable decision support for radiopharmaceutical development. The system demonstrated high accuracy in technical evaluations compared to other models, showing promise for clinical use after further validation.

papers.name: PathFound
papers.title: PathFound: An agentic multimodal model activating evidence-seeking pathological diagnosis
papers.summary: PathFound is an agentic multimodal pathology model that makes an initial diagnosis, actively seeks more slide evidence and then refines its decision, using RL-trained reasoning models. Adding this evidence-seeking strategy improved diagnostic accuracy across several multimodal models.

papers.name: SAGEAgent
papers.title: SAGEAgent: A Self-Evolving Agent for Cost-Aware Modality Acquisition in Multimodal Survival Prediction
papers.summary: SAGEAgent decides sequentially which diagnostic modalities to acquire for a cancer patient, weighing predictive gain against invasiveness, using tools that verbalize predictions plus episodic and semantic memory. It treats multimodal survival prediction as an acquisition decision problem rather than assuming all data are present.

papers.name: LongMedBench
papers.title: LongMedBench: Benchmarking Medical Agents for Long-Horizon Clinical Decision-Making
papers.summary: LongMedBench is a benchmark for evaluating medical agents in long-horizon clinical decision-making using real-world EHR data. It assesses how well these agents can aggregate and use patient information over time, revealing that while they perform well with explicit timestamps, implicit temporal reasoning remains challenging.

papers.name: MedicalAgentsBench
papers.title: MedicalAgentsBench for complex medical reasoning: Comparing internalized reasoning models versus externalized agent-based frameworks
papers.summary: MedicalAgentsBench is a benchmark designed to evaluate complex medical reasoning tasks using both internalized and externalized agent-based approaches. The study demonstrates that combining these methods can significantly improve performance in clinical decision support, with the best results achieved by integrating multi-agent systems onto an advanced single-agent model.

papers.name: Ensemble QSP
papers.title: A hierarchical memory architecture overcomes context limits in long-horizon multi-agent computational modeling
papers.summary: Ensemble QSP is a multi-agent framework with hierarchical memory architecture designed for long-horizon computational modeling tasks in biology and biomedicine. It demonstrated improved parameter recovery, robust prompt interpretation, and independence from proprietary LLMs across various scientific domains.

papers.name: SpaCellAgent
papers.title: SpaCellAgent: A Self-Evolving LLM-Based Multi-Agent Framework for Trajectory Analysis
papers.summary: SpaCellAgent is a self-evolving multi-agent framework that automates trajectory inference analysis in computational biology, reducing manual intervention and improving analytical efficiency.
