It demonstrates significant performance gains over existing methods on diverse datasets, showcasing its potential to democratize advanced spatiotemporal modeling.

papers.name: BioMaster
papers.title: BioMaster: Multi-agent system for automated bioinformatics analysis workflow
papers.summary: BioMaster is a multi-agent system designed to automate complex bioinformatics workflows, integrating planning, execution, error recovery, and validation. It demonstrated superior performance in completing more complex workflows compared to existing automated systems across various tasks.

papers.name: Octopus
papers.title: Autonomous computational prioritisation of colorectal cancer vulnerabilities via multi-scale AI swarms
papers.summary: Octopus is a neuro-symbolic framework that uses multi-agent swarms to autonomously generate and test therapeutic hypotheses in colorectal cancer. It successfully identified Insulin-like Growth Factor 2 (IGF2) as a predictive biomarker for 5-Fluorouracil sensitivity, with the discovery validated through rigorous statistical analysis and independent mouse model experiments.

papers.title: A multimodal multi-agent LLM framework for identifying key drivers of sleep disorders
papers.summary: The paper presents a multi-agent framework using large language models to analyze sleep disorders by integrating various lifestyle, behavioral, and physiological factors. The system identifies key drivers of sleep disorders through an interpretable approach that enhances evidence-based reasoning in clinical research.

papers.name: MOSAIC
papers.title: Multi-Large Language Model Orchestrated Severity Assessment of Clinical Records (MOSAIC)
papers.summary: Agents build and then apply a severity rubric for type 2 diabetes from electronic records, covering domains such as glycaemic staging, beta-cell function and social determinants. On a synthetic cohort its open-weight version matched the proprietary pipeline, agreed moderately with algorithmic severity indices and separated mortality risk, differing from deterministic execution of the same rubric.

papers.name: EEG-SpikeAgent
papers.title: EEG-SpikeAgent: Agentic Closed-Loop Program Synthesis for Automated EEG Spike Detection
papers.summary: An LLM agent repeatedly writes EEG feature-extraction code, runs it, scores a tabular classifier and uses the diagnostics to refine the next feature module for interictal spike detection. On the VEPISET dataset the generated features reached an AUROC of 0.935, and artifact-aware search improved balanced accuracy.

papers.name: ClawBench
papers.title: Benchmarking large language models for ACMG/AMP variant interpretation and variant calling
papers.summary: ClawBench is a framework for evaluating large language models in the context of ACMG/AMP variant interpretation and calling, focusing on validity, safety, provenance, and reproducibility rather than just accuracy. It demonstrates that different types of errors arise from distinct architectural layers within the genomic workflow.

papers.name: Prompt-to-Paper
papers.title: Prompt-to-Paper: Agentic AI System for Bioinformatics
papers.summary: Prompt-to-Paper is a multi-agent system that grounds manuscript claims in a retrieved corpus, runs real computational biology experiments through a coding agent, and scores drafts on eight quality dimensions. It is aimed at making generated bioinformatics papers verifiable rather than fabricated.

papers.name: Sofiya
papers.title: Conversational artificial intelligence for pre-procedural patient preparation: implementation, validation and patient satisfaction
papers.summary: Sofiya is an LLM voice agent that phones patients before cardiac catheterization to give instructions, collect clinical data, answer questions and hand off to nurses. Across 1,606 calls to 1,431 patients it completed about 87% of calls in routine nurse-led use.

papers.name: MedCalc-Pro
papers.title: MedCalc-Pro: Solving Complex Medical Calculations with LLM Agents
papers.summary: Introduces a benchmark of 2,268 clinical cases requiring single, multiple or nested medical calculators, and an agent framework that selects and chains calculator tools with structured validation of parameters. The framework scored best across all three settings compared with open, closed and medical LLMs.

papers.name: KGRD
papers.title: KGRD: a knowledge-graph-augmented automated reasoning framework for diagnosis and counselling of paediatric rare genetic disorders
papers.summary: KGRD is a diagnostic support framework for pediatric rare genetic disorders that uses knowledge-driven and data-driven inference over patient-level genomic and phenotypic data. It demonstrated improved diagnostic accuracy in a validation benchmark, increasing the mean Bond score of top-ranked diagnoses and raising correct identification efficiency.

papers.name: GeneGenie
papers.title: GeneGenie: enhancing biomedical question-answering with agentic graphs
papers.summary: GeneGenie is a multi-agent framework that enhances biomedical question-answering by orchestrating query planning, retrieval from curated databases, and execution of bioinformatics tools. The system demonstrates superior performance compared to standalone large language models in terms of accuracy, completeness, and factual grounding.

papers.name: TRUST
papers.title: TRUST: an large language model-based dialogue system for trauma understanding and structured assessments
papers.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
papers.summary: TRUST is a dialogue system powered by large language models designed to conduct structured diagnostic interviews for PTSD, replicating clinician behavior. The study demonstrates that TRUST performs comparably to human clinicians in terms of clinical quality.

papers.name: Doctor Xiao Yi
papers.title: Real-World Analysis of Organ Transplantation-Specific Agent Based on Large Language Model in Post-Transplant Self-Management During Off-Hours: A Mixed-Methods Study
papers.summary: Doctor Xiao Yi is a specialized AI agent designed to provide post-transplant medical and psychological support during off-hours, addressing the limitations of general large language models. The study demonstrated that Doctor Xiao Yi effectively bridges the gap in care for transplant recipients by remaining active and responsive during non-working hours.

papers.name: Agentomics
papers.title: Agentomics: an agentic system that autonomously develops novel state-of-the-art solutions for biomedical machine learning tasks
papers.summary: Agentomics is an autonomous system that uses large language models to develop machine learning solutions for biomedical datasets, implementing various modeling strategies and validation checkpoints. It demonstrated superior performance compared to other agentic systems and generated state-of-the-art models for several benchmark datasets.

papers.title: Agentic AI integrated with scientific knowledge: laboratory validation in systems biology
papers.venue: Journal of the Royal Society, Interface
papers.summary: The paper describes an AI-driven framework that integrates large language models with laboratory automation to validate and refine scientific hypotheses in systems biology. The system identified novel biological interactions, such as the effect of glutamate on cell growth under specific conditions, demonstrating its potential for reliable machine-driven discovery.

papers.name: NOVA
papers.title: Local LLMs as cooperative agents for low-cost surgical navigation support
papers.venue: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery
papers.summary: NOVA is a set of locally run LLM agents for knowledge questions, user interface actions and delegation that acts as a hands-free interface for a low-cost surgical navigation system. Agents were tested on two semisynthetic benchmarks and integrated into a working prototype.

papers.name: ReclAIm
papers.title: ReclAIm: A Multiagent Framework for Monitoring and Correcting Performance Decline in Medical Imaging AI
papers.summary: ReclAIm is a multiagent framework designed to monitor and correct performance decline in medical imaging AI models through automated evaluation and fine-tuning. The system successfully detected performance discrepancies and restored model accuracy, demonstrating its potential for continuous improvement of AI systems in clinical settings.

papers.name: RESCUE
papers.title: RESCUE: An end-to-end multi-agent LLM system for proactive rare-disease patient screening in the EHR
papers.summary: RESCUE is a multi-agent system that uses machine learning to screen electronic health records for patients who may benefit from rare disease diagnostic testing. It demonstrated strong performance in identifying appropriate candidates, with high precision and likelihood of subsequent genomic assessments.

papers.name: MARCH
papers.title: MARCH: Multi-Agent Radiology Clinical Hierarchy for CT Report Generation
papers.venue: Proceedings of the conference. Association for Computational Linguistics. Meeting
papers.summary: MARCH is a multi-agent system designed to generate 3D radiology reports for CT scans, emulating the hierarchical structure of radiology departments. It showed significant improvement in clinical fidelity and linguistic accuracy compared to existing models on the RadGenome-ChestCT dataset.

papers.name: BAISBench
papers.title: Benchmarking AI scientists for omics data-driven biological discovery
papers.summary: Tests AI scientist systems on cell type annotation across 15 expert-labeled datasets and on 193 discovery questions drawn from 41 published single-cell studies, with bioinformaticians as a human baseline. Current systems fell short of autonomous discovery but showed useful support for data-driven research.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence agent for delirium screening among patients in oncology and cardiac intensive care units: a proof-of-concept study
papers.summary: The Delirium Screening AI Agent uses a knowledge graph derived from clinical guidelines to autonomously select appropriate delirium assessment tools and generate guideline-aligned care recommendations. The agent demonstrated high accuracy in tool selection and conclusion generation, outperforming baseline models, with human experts validating its outputs for coherence and relevance.

papers.name: FaithMed
papers.title: FaithMed: Training LLMs For Faithful Evidence-Based Medical Reasoning
papers.summary: Trains LLMs that actively search for evidence using clinician-designed, automatically refined rubrics as step-level process rewards in reinforcement learning. Across seven medical benchmarks it beat agentic-search baselines by 9 percent on average and raised evidence-based medicine rubric scores.

papers.name: AgentODE
papers.title: LLM-Guided ODE Discovery and Parameter Inference from Small-Cohort Aggregate Data
papers.summary: AgentODE is a framework that uses an LLM to propose ODE structures and iteratively refines parameter distributions using population-level summary statistics. It demonstrates the ability to recover functionally consistent ODE structures in sparse, noisy data settings for rare diseases like RDEB.

papers.name: HemaGuide
papers.title: Clinical decision support in hematological malignancies using a case-grounded AI agent
papers.summary: HemaGuide is a locally deployable LLM agent that structures clinical documents, routes cases to guideline, advanced or molecular decision modes, and grounds advice in guideline flowcharts and over 2,000 past tumor board cases. In blinded evaluation on 45 complex hematologic cases it improved concordance with tumor board decisions across six LLMs.

papers.name: GeneBench-Pro
papers.title: GeneBench-Pro: Evaluating Multistage Statistical Reasoning in Genomics, Quantitative Biology, and Translational Biomedicine
papers.summary: GeneBench-Pro is a benchmark designed to evaluate AI agents' ability to perform multi-stage reasoning in genomics and translational biomedicine. It includes complex, real-world problems reviewed by domain experts and demonstrates that current models like GPT-5.6 Sol struggle with long-horizon biological reasoning.

papers.name: DDIAgents
papers.title: DDIAgents: Mechanism-Conditioned Context Flow for Drug-Drug Interaction Prediction
papers.summary: DDIAgents is a multi-agent framework designed to predict drug-drug interactions by dynamically routing relevant knowledge sources and orchestrating specialized expert agents. The system demonstrates superior performance on realistic DDI prediction benchmarks compared to existing methods, showcasing its ability to organize heterogeneous scientific data for adaptive reasoning.

papers.name: HealthAgentBench
papers.title: HealthAgentBench: A Unified Benchmark Suite of Realistic Agentic Healthcare Environments for Challenging Frontier AI Agents
papers.summary: HealthAgentBench is a benchmark suite for evaluating AI agents in complex, long-horizon healthcare tasks. It assesses the ability of agents to navigate real-world clinical workflows and reveals that even advanced models like Codex GPT-5.5 struggle with certain task categories.

papers.name: PHO-Agents
papers.title: PHO-Agents: A Large Language Model–Powered Multi-Agent System for Predicting Health Outcomes
papers.summary: PHO-Agents is a multi-agent system that uses large language models to predict health outcomes from electronic health records, improving prediction accuracy and interpretability. The system outperformed single-agent baselines in predicting mortality for acute kidney injury patients, onset of AKI in chronic kidney disease patients, and immune-related adverse events in cancer patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors.

papers.name: PhenoAgent
papers.title: PhenoAgent: agentic LLM framework for phenotyping electronic health records via structured query decomposition and self-correction
papers.summary: PhenoAgent is a large language model framework designed to extract clinical phenotypes from free-text electronic health records by decomposing queries into structured formats and using self-correction loops. The system demonstrated high accuracy in phenotype retrieval, achieving macro-F1 scores comparable to physician evaluations and outperforming traditional baseline methods.

papers.name: Clair3-Connect
papers.title: Client-server interfaces enable efficient agent-driven variant calling
papers.summary: The paper presents Clair3-Connect, a client-server rearchitecting of the variant caller Clair3 to enable efficient agent-driven analysis. It demonstrates that this design reduces token usage and improves reliability compared to traditional shell-driven methods.

papers.name: Octopus
papers.title: Autonomous mechanistic discovery of colorectal cancer vulnerabilities via multi-scale AI swarms
papers.summary: Octopus couples local LLM agent swarms with deterministic modeling engines to generate therapeutic hypotheses from CRISPR dependency data, trace causal cascades and test them against in vivo and survival data. An unsupervised sweep of colorectal cancer transcriptomes nominated IGF2 in 5-fluorouracil resistance, which held up statistically and in an independent mouse cohort.

papers.name: ATHENA-R1
papers.title: An AI agent for treatment reasoning over a biomedical tool universe
papers.summary: ATHENA-R1 is a treatment reasoning agent trained by reinforcement learning over 212 biomedical tools that at each step finds missing information, runs tools and folds in the evidence. Trained without human traces using self-generated trajectories, it beat language models across five benchmarks covering 3,168 drug reasoning tasks and 456 patient cases.

papers.name: GNPS2 Agentic AI
papers.title: Agentic AI for Structural Elucidation and Discovery of Drug Metabolites from Mass Spectrometry Data
papers.summary: The GNPS2 Agentic AI system uses large language models to generate structural hypotheses for unknown drug metabolites from mass spectrometry data, integrating spectral alignment and machine learning-based spectrum prediction. The system successfully predicted and experimentally confirmed several novel metabolite structures, demonstrating its capability in generating testable hypotheses for previously uncharacterized compounds.

papers.name: VST
papers.title: Virtual Speech Therapist: A Clinician-in-the-Loop AI Speech Therapy Agent for Personalized and Supervised Therapy
papers.summary: Virtual Speech Therapist classifies stuttering from speech samples and then uses LLM agents that generate, critique and refine individualized therapy plans before clinician review. Expert speech therapists judged the resulting plans to be consistent and clinically appropriate.

papers.name: MARTP
papers.title: MARTP: a multi-agent simulation framework for automated radiation therapy planning based on LLMs
papers.summary: Five agents handle data analysis, objective weight adjustment, plan optimization, plan evaluation and reporting, with fine-tuning on expert weight adjustments, retrieval of similar cases and reinforcement learning from expert preferences. Dosimetric metrics of its plans did not differ significantly from expert clinical plans while planning was much faster.

papers.name: ABCD
papers.title: Preclinical Dialogue Simulation: Evaluating Response Accessibility in Conversational Artificial Intelligence for Aphasia Therapy
papers.venue: Journal of speech, language, and hearing research : JSLHR
papers.summary: The Agent-Based Conversational Dialogue method simulates multi-turn therapy sessions between an LLM clinician and an LLM-simulated aphasic patient. Comparing Claude, GPT and Gemini under different prompting and reasoning settings, it found distinct readability profiles, with few-shot prompting and advanced reasoning producing more accessible language.

papers.name: MedGuards
papers.title: MedGuards: Multi-Agent System for Reliable Medical Error Detection and Correction
papers.summary: MedGuards is a multi-agent system designed to detect and correct errors in medical text, enhancing patient safety by ensuring the accuracy of clinical notes. The system demonstrates significant improvements over existing methods across various metrics and datasets, highlighting its potential for safer deployment in real-world healthcare settings.

papers.name: Healink
papers.title: Bridging the Post-discharge Gap: A Traceable Multi-agent Framework for Safe and Continuous Care
papers.summary: Combines triage routing, a database-backed patient memory and constraint-based retrieval to answer post-discharge follow-up questions grounded in prescriptions while checking cross-department drug conflicts. On 485 real follow-up cases, blinded clinical experts rated it above physician baselines for authority and safety.

papers.title: Agentic Autodiscovery of Diastolic Dysfunction Phenotypes from Surface Electrocardiogram
papers.summary: The paper describes an agentic auto-discovery framework that uses AI to identify diastolic dysfunction phenotypes from surface ECGs, demonstrating its effectiveness in classifying LVDD severity with high accuracy. The system combines transfer learning and autonomous architecture optimization, achieving robust external validation across large datasets.

papers.name: DeepBD
papers.title: DeepBD: A Grounded Agentic Workflow for Variant Prioritization and Diagnosis of Genetic Birth Defects
papers.summary: DeepBD is a grounded agentic workflow designed to prioritize genetic variants and assist in the diagnosis of birth defects. It integrates various types of evidence, including rule-based knowledge and biological context, to improve variant prioritization accuracy compared to existing methods.

papers.name: KnowMol
papers.title: KnowMol: A Knowledge-Guided Multi-Agent Framework for Interpretable Drug–Target Interaction Prediction, Validated in PRMT3-Targeted NAFLD Therapy
papers.summary: KnowMol couples LLM agents that generate knowledge-guided hypotheses about drug and protein features with machine learning validation in a closed loop to predict drug-target interactions. It outperformed prior methods on three interaction benchmarks and eight property datasets and was applied to PRMT3 inhibitors for NAFLD.

papers.title: Agentic Artificial Intelligence for Hospital Readmission Review: A Single-Center Blinded Evaluation and Exploratory Qualitative Analysis
papers.summary: An LLM agent queried a clinical database of notes, encounters, procedures and labs to complete the structured 30-day readmission review rubric used by physicians. Blinded physicians rated its reviews of 20 readmissions against those of two physicians each, and it was then applied to 100 more cases.

papers.name: EHR-Complex
papers.title: EHR-Complex: Benchmarking Medical Agents for Complex Clinical Reasoning
papers.summary: EHR-Complex is a benchmark designed to evaluate the performance of clinical agents in handling complex electronic health record (EHR) data through interactive database reasoning. The benchmark highlights significant challenges and limitations in current models' ability to accurately perform longitudinal multi-table aggregation and compositional reasoning, indicating a need for more robust clinical decision support systems.

papers.name: VFB-MCP
papers.title: VFB-MCP: Natural-Language Access to Drosophila Neuroscience Grounded by an Expert-Curated Ontology-Led Knowledgebase
papers.summary: Exposes the Virtual Fly Brain knowledgebase of Drosophila neuroanatomy, connectome and molecular data to LLMs through Model Context Protocol tools. On 30 neuroscience tasks the MCP-equipped LLM gave precise, verifiable answers on 25, versus 14 with web search and 2 for a bare LLM.

papers.name: BioBrain
papers.title: BioBrain: A Multi-Agent Framework for Natural Language Driven Quantitative Microscopy Data Analysis
papers.summary: BioBrain is a multi-agent framework that turns natural-language goals into microscopy analysis pipelines assembled from validated methods and lab scripts, reporting every method and parameter. It reproduced expert results on TIRF and lattice light-sheet benchmarks, while frontier LLMs writing code made large quantitative errors.

papers.title: Knowledge-Graph Grounding Helps LLMs Only for Out-of-Training Knowledge: A Controlled Study on Clinical Question Answering
papers.summary: This controlled study tested whether knowledge graph grounding, including an agentic natural-language-to-Cypher loop over PrimeKG, improves clinical question answering. Grounding did not help on MedQA across model sizes but did raise accuracy on counterfactual and novel-fact benchmarks, locating its benefit outside training knowledge.

papers.name: VISTA Architect
papers.title: VISTA Architect: A graph database-oriented health AI system demonstrated in multidisciplinary tumor boards
papers.summary: VISTA Architect is a database-oriented AI system that integrates large language models with electronic health records to create a persistent, provenance-linked knowledge graph. It demonstrated high accuracy in reconstructing patient histories for multidisciplinary tumor boards and reduced preparation time without sacrificing precision.

papers.name: Dementia-Agents
papers.title: Dementia-Agents: A Multi-Modal Multi-Agent System for Dementia Staging and Phenotyping
papers.summary: A data agent converts structured clinical records to text and routes them to five fine-tuned domain expert agents, whose outputs a coordinator agent aggregates into staging and phenotype calls. On 1,066 patients from two neurology services it outperformed single multimodal LLMs and earlier medical multi-agent systems.

papers.title: A Multi-Agent Audit Framework for High-Stakes Reasoning: Evaluation and Interpretability in Clinical Mental Health Screening
papers.summary: A LangChain workflow chains perception, retrieval, clinical reasoning and an audit agent that verifies the reasoning before predicting PHQ-8 depression severity from interview transcripts. On DAIC-WOZ it lowered mean absolute error from 5.35 to 5.02 relative to a single-agent baseline.

papers.name: MedRLM
papers.title: MedRLM: Recursive Multimodal Health Intelligence for Long-Context Clinical Reasoning, Sensor-Guided Screening, Evidence-Grounded Decision Support, and Community-to-Tertiary Referral Optimization
papers.summary: MedRLM is a framework that uses specialized agents to recursively inspect and synthesize patient information for clinical decision support, incorporating multimodal data like EHRs, medical images, and sensor signals. It demonstrates the potential of recursive reasoning in handling long-context clinical scenarios by integrating evidence from various sources into a Clinical Evidence Graph Memory.

papers.title: Process-Reward Tactic Evolution for Long-Horizon Bioinformatics Workflows
papers.summary: The Process-Reward Tactic Evolution framework trains an agent to execute complex bioinformatics workflows in Galaxy, a platform for managing and executing such workflows. The system demonstrates improved completion rates, biological correctness, and execution efficiency compared to baseline methods.

papers.title: Dual-Agent Framework for Cross-Model Verified Translation of Natural-Language Protocols into Robotic Laboratory Platform
papers.summary: The paper introduces a dual-agent framework for translating natural-language biological experiment protocols into executable commands for robotic laboratory platforms, addressing the semantic gap between human-readable instructions and machine-executable code. The system was evaluated through automated benchmarks involving various parsers and validators, demonstrating its effectiveness in accurately converting ELISA protocols and enabling autonomous execution of protein quantification assays.

papers.name: MIRA
papers.title: Towards autonomous medical artificial intelligence agents
papers.summary: MIRA is an autonomous agent in a sandboxed EHR that gathers histories, orders and interprets tests, generates differential diagnoses and writes treatment plans. In simulations on real patient cases it outperformed physicians in diagnostic accuracy.

papers.name: AMIE
papers.title: Towards conversational artificial intelligence for disease management
papers.summary: AMIE was extended with an agentic system for multivisit disease management that grounds its reasoning in clinical guidelines and drug formularies using long-context retrieval. In a blinded virtual OSCE with 100 scenarios, it was non-inferior to 21 primary care physicians on management reasoning.

papers.name: MedAgent
papers.title: MedAgent: A Retrieval-Augmented Clinical Decision Support Agent with Verifiable Evidence Grounding for Evidence-Based Medicine
papers.summary: MedAgent is an evidence-based medicine agent trained with supervised fine-tuning, reward modeling and GRPO to run a workflow of question parsing, PICO extraction, evidence retrieval and grounded answering. It is designed to cite traceable evidence and respect evidence hierarchies in clinical answers.

papers.name: TxBench-PP
papers.title: TxBench-PP: Analyzing AI Agent Performance on Small-Molecule Preclinical Pharmacology
papers.summary: TxBench-PP is a benchmark designed to evaluate AI agents' ability to make accurate decisions in small-molecule preclinical pharmacology by analyzing real-world assay data. The study found that no system could reliably recover preclinical pharmacology decisions, with the best performing configuration achieving only 59.3% accuracy.

papers.name: EmoPatient
papers.title: EmoPatient: An Emotion-Directed Patient Simulator for Realistic Palliative Care Communication Training
papers.summary: EmoPatient is an emotion-directed patient simulator designed to train clinicians in palliative care communication by generating realistic emotional responses. The system demonstrates improved emotional realism and robustness across different conversational scenarios, enhancing the training experience for healthcare professionals.

papers.name: PhysAssistBench
papers.title: Are LLMs Ready to Assist Physicians? PhysAssistBench for Interactive Doctor-Patient-EHR Assistance
papers.summary: PhysAssistBench is a benchmark designed to evaluate the interactive assistance capabilities of large language models in clinical settings, focusing on their ability to coordinate knowledge, communication, and system interaction. The evaluation shows that current LLMs are unreliable for such tasks due to their inability to reliably integrate these diverse skills.

papers.name: IAN
papers.title: IAN, an intelligent system for omics data analysis and discovery
papers.summary: IAN is an R package that runs pathway, regulatory and protein interaction enrichment analyses and has multiple LLM agents summarize and integrate the results into interpretations. It was demonstrated on human transcriptomic data, tested for robustness to LLM choice, and rated by human experts for clarity and relevance.

papers.name: FlowBench
papers.title: FlowBench: separating planning, fault recovery and interpretation in agentic bioinformatics
papers.summary: FlowAgent is a modular, provider-agnostic framework for evaluating agentic bioinformatics systems by separating planning, fault recovery, and biological interpretation. The study reveals that while models excel at generating valid workflow plans from named toolchains, they struggle with inferring appropriate toolchains from biological intent alone and handling data-grounded interpretation.

papers.name: scIsoAgent
papers.title: scIsoAgent enables autonomous isoform-resolved characterization and sequence-informed interpretation of long-read single-cell transcriptomes
papers.summary: An LLM agent plans and executes isoform-resolved long-read single-cell RNA-seq workflows with stage-aware planning and persistent computational context. It recovered major published findings on real data and extended a differential transcript usage event into a sequence-based functional hypothesis.

papers.name: Orion
papers.title: Orion: Towards Lab Automation with Computer-Using Agents
papers.summary: Orion is an AI agent designed for biomedical image analysis and interpretation, capable of automating computational workflows in laboratory settings. It demonstrated the ability to generate research reports from experimental imaging data and produce biologically plausible hypotheses that were prioritized by human scientists.

papers.name: RubricsTree
papers.title: RubricsTree: Scalable and Evolving Open-Ended Evaluation of Personal Health Agents across Health Memory and Medical Skills
papers.summary: RubricsTree is an evaluation framework for personal health agents that uses a hierarchical taxonomy of clinically-verifiable rubrics to assess the performance of AI systems in healthcare. It demonstrates superior alignment with expert evaluations and can significantly improve model performance when used as structured instructions or training rewards.

papers.name: WEQA
papers.title: WEQA: Wearable hEalth Question Answering with Query-Adaptive Agentic Reasoning
papers.summary: WEQA is a query-adaptive agent framework that uses an LLM controller to synthesize execution plans and route queries to specialized wearable analytical tools, demonstrating significant improvements in accuracy over existing methods through expert review and user studies.

papers.title: Agentic AI-based Framework for Mitigating Premature Diagnostic Handoff and Silent Hallucination in Healthcare Applications
papers.summary: The Agentic AI-based Framework uses a multi-agent system to mitigate premature diagnostic handoff and silent hallucinations in healthcare applications, ensuring thorough patient data collection before making diagnoses. The framework demonstrates improved diagnostic precision through deterministic orchestration constraints and epistemic uncertainty quantification mechanisms.

papers.name: ProvenanceGuard
papers.title: ProvenanceGuard: Source-Aware Factuality Verification for MCP-Based LLM Agents
papers.summary: ProvenanceGuard is a source-aware factuality verification system designed to ensure that claims made by large language model agents are correctly attributed to their sources. It evaluates the provenance of answers generated through the Model Context Protocol, demonstrating high accuracy in detecting and correcting cross-source conflation errors.

papers.title: An Agentic LLM Framework for Autonomous Surgical Continuum Monitoring: ReAct-Driven Tool-Use Agents for Presurgical, Intraoperative, and Postsurgical Cardiopulmonary Care
papers.summary: The paper specifies six ReAct tool-use agents with Reflexion self-correction and confidence-gated human review for monitoring patients across presurgical, intraoperative and postsurgical cardiopulmonary care. It replaces a rule-based multi-agent digital twin with LLM-mediated coordination and formally defines agent tool registries and escalation logic.

papers.title: Intelligent tool orchestration for rapid mechanistic model prototyping: MCP servers as AI-biology interfaces
papers.summary: The paper presents Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers that enable AI agents to rapidly prototype multicellular mechanistic models through natural language interactions with bioinformatics tools. The system demonstrated the ability to construct a multiscale cancer cell fate model using three different tools, showcasing its potential for accelerating biological research and hypothesis exploration.

papers.title: Trustworthy agentic genomics through versioned skill libraries
papers.summary: The paper evaluates the use of large language models in pharmacogenomics, finding that direct reasoning by these models is unreliable and unsafe. It proposes a trustworthy agentic genomics architecture where validated decision logic is encoded as versioned skills executed as code, ensuring deterministic and auditable clinical mappings across diverse populations.

papers.name: DeepRoot
papers.title: DeepRoot: A KG-Coordinated Multi-Agent System for Therapeutic Reasoning over Historical Medical Texts
papers.venue: ICML 2026 GenBio; ACM CAIS 2026 Workshop AI Agents for Discovery in the Wild
papers.summary: DeepRoot is a multi-agent system that uses historical medical texts to discover potential drug treatments by building and utilizing a verified knowledge graph. It outperforms other systems in recovering known compound-disease pairs and maintaining reasoning coherence without hallucination.

papers.name: Pepti-Agent
papers.title: Pepti-Agent: An AI Agent for Peptide Design and Optimization
papers.summary: Pepti-Agent is an AI agent designed for the iterative design and optimization of therapeutic peptides, addressing multiple constraints such as solubility, hemolytic activity, and non-fouling properties. It demonstrates improved peptide candidate refinement through a closed-loop framework that integrates generation, property prediction, and mutation operations, offering a reproducible method for benchmarking and experimental validation.

papers.name: AutoMedic
papers.title: AutoMedic: An Automated Evaluation Framework for Clinical Conversational Agents with Medical Dataset Grounding
papers.venue: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: AutoMedic is a multi-agent simulation framework designed to evaluate large language models as clinical conversational agents by transforming static QA datasets into virtual patient profiles for realistic dialogue simulations. The system demonstrates its effectiveness in providing a comprehensive evaluation of LLMs' performance in clinical settings, validated by human experts.

papers.name: DeepTCM1.0
papers.title: DeepTCM1.0: A Multi-Expert AI Agent for Deciphering Mechanisms of Chinese Herbal Formulae Based on General Large Language Models
papers.summary: DeepTCM1.0 is a multi-expert AI agent framework that integrates classical TCM theory with modern scientific research to analyze the mechanisms of Chinese herbal formulae, demonstrating robust reliability and validity in its evaluation through multiple independent assessments.

papers.title: An autonomous AI agent for knowledge and data cooperation in ED clinical decision support
papers.summary: The Autonomous AI Agent integrates medical knowledge graphs with dynamic clinical data to enhance decision-making in emergency departments. It demonstrates superior performance across various tasks, including triage and drug interaction detection, compared to existing methods.

papers.name: PathLab
papers.title: Democratizing and accelerating AI-driven pathology research through agentic intelligence
papers.summary: PathLab is an autonomous framework that translates natural-language research objectives into executable computational pathology workflows, reducing the need for programming expertise. It demonstrated non-inferior performance compared to expert implementations across various tasks and significantly reduced the time required for designing and executing computational pathology studies.

papers.name: Trust but Verify
papers.title: Trust but Verify: Mitigating Medical Hallucinations via Post-Hoc Adversarial Auditing and Multi-Agent Feedback Loops
papers.summary: Five agents sharing one LLM backbone draft, check and audit answers to clinical questions against current regulatory data on withdrawn drugs. On 103 adversarial questions the agentic setup cut the rate of recommending banned drugs by about 53 percent across model families.

papers.name: ClinAgent
papers.title: ClinAgent: AI-assisted methodology for clinical trial data processing and statistical programming
papers.summary: ClinAgent is an AI-assisted system designed to enhance clinical trial data processing and statistical programming, addressing the bottleneck in pharmaceutical research. It demonstrates its capability by successfully validating nine skills on a Phase 2 cardiovascular study dataset, though it highlights the need for expert review in complex domains due to varying accuracy levels.

papers.name: AIMAH
papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Medical Assessment Hospital (AIMAH): An AI-Native Virtual Hospital Platform for Clinical Simulation and Medical Education
papers.summary: AIMAH is an AI-driven virtual hospital platform for medical education that simulates patient interactions and provides structured assessment feedback. The system was validated through a study with medical trainees, demonstrating high realism, educational usefulness, and learner engagement.

papers.name: LatentDx
papers.title: LatentDx: Latent Multi-Agent Communication for Cross-Hospital Rare-Disease Diagnosis
papers.summary: Hospital agents keep patient records and retrieved cases local and send compressed latent KV blocks to a host agent that makes the rare-disease diagnosis. On a self-built cross-hospital benchmark it improved diagnosis while leaking less reconstructable clinical text than raw latent exchange.

papers.name: ArogyaSutra
papers.title: ArogyaSutra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Multimodal Medical Reasoning in Indic Languages
papers.venue: Proceedings of the Thirty-Fifth International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI-26), pages 7183-7191, 2026
papers.summary: ArogyaSutra is a multi-agent framework designed for multimodal medical reasoning in Indic languages, addressing the limitations of existing English-centric models. The system improves accuracy in multilingual medical reasoning and decision support by integrating tool grounding with dual-memory mechanisms.

papers.name: GovernAgent
papers.title: An Efficient and Reliable Agent-Based System for Clinical Data Governance
papers.venue: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: GovernAgent is an LLM-driven framework designed to address data quality issues in clinical records by employing hierarchical governance mechanisms and constrained action planning. It improves the accuracy, efficiency, and reliability of clinical data governance while minimizing hallucinations.

papers.name: OpenClaw
papers.title: Skill-Augmented AI Agents for Medical Research Analysis: An Exploratory Multi-Model Human Evaluation in an NSCLC Transcriptomic Biomarker Task
papers.summary: The paper evaluates OpenClaw, an AI agent augmented with medical research skills, in a non-small cell lung cancer biomarker task. It shows that skill-augmented outputs are directionally higher in quality compared to native AI models but the difference is not statistically significant due to high variability and noise.

papers.name: M3A
papers.title: Evaluating agentic AI for biological discovery in autonomous and copilot settings
papers.summary: The M3A framework lets LLM agents reason over persistent multimodal single-cell multi-omic data states in autonomous and human copilot modes. Using datasets from 11 cancer types, the authors assessed what current agents can and cannot do in open-ended biological discovery.

papers.name: ABC-Bench
papers.title: ABC-Bench: An Agentic Bio-Capabilities Benchmark for Biosecurity
papers.summary: ABC-Bench is a benchmark suite designed to evaluate the biosecurity-relevant capabilities of large language model agents in biological research tasks. The system demonstrated that LLM agents can outperform human experts on various biology and software tasks, including scripting for liquid handling robots and designing DNA fragments, with some limitations in novel bioinformatics reasoning.

papers.name: PATHFinder Agent
papers.title: PATHFinder Agent for Tailored Prenatal Care
papers.summary: The PATHFinder Agent is a conversational AI system designed to gather patient information and create personalized prenatal care plans aligned with ACOG's PATH guidelines. The study shows that GPT-5.2 performs well in generating tailored healthcare plans, though it still has gaps in antenatal testing recommendations.

papers.name: mLLMCelltype
papers.title: Large language model consensus substantially improves the cell type annotation accuracy for scRNA-seq data
papers.summary: mLLMCelltype has several LLMs annotate single-cell clusters and then deliberate iteratively to reach a consensus label with a confidence score. Across 49 datasets it reached 77.2% mean accuracy, 15.7 points above the best single LLM.

papers.title: From raw audio to structure: an agent-based pipeline that boosts medical LLM performance
papers.summary: The paper introduces an agent-based pipeline that converts raw, noisy audio recordings of doctor-patient conversations into structured transcriptions suitable for training large language models. The system demonstrated high accuracy in noise removal and dialogue structuring tasks compared to manual processing and other methods, leading to improved performance when used to fine-tune a medical LLM.

papers.name: XMedFusion
papers.title: XMedFusion: A Knowledge-Guided Multimodal Perception and Reasoning Framework for Autonomous Medical Systems
papers.venue: 2026 International Conference on Robotics and Automation in Industry (ICRAI), pp. 1-6, May 2026
papers.summary: XMedFusion is a modular AI framework that uses multiple agents to interpret medical images and generate radiology reports, improving the reliability of automated diagnostic systems. The system demonstrates significant improvements in various evaluation metrics over existing vision-language models, showcasing its effectiveness in enhancing robustness and transparency in intelligent medical imaging.

papers.name: PACT
papers.title: PACT: Learning Diverse Diagnostic Strategies via Privileged Synthesis and Branch Consensus
papers.summary: Uses doctor, patient and supervisor agents to synthesize consultation dialogues under four diagnostic reasoning styles, then trains paradigm-specific LoRA branches merged into a shared model for an interactive doctor agent. On a new dynamic Chinese consultation benchmark it outperformed proprietary and medical baselines on diagnosis and process metrics.

papers.name: My Chemical Harness
papers.title: My Chemical Harness: Evolutionary Molecular Design over Synthetic Pathways with Large Language Model Agents
papers.summary: Evolves populations of executable synthetic routes from purchasable building blocks, with an LLM choosing high-level search strategy while deterministic chemistry code builds, validates and scores routes. On a soluble epoxide hydrolase proxy task it beat single-pass LLM and deterministic controllers on binding score, synthesizability and route success.

papers.name: PAG-Agent
papers.title: PAG-Agent: a biologist-oriented research assistant for context-aware pathway-level analysis and interpretation
papers.summary: PAG-Agent runs preprocessing, differential expression and pathway analyses on bulk and single-cell data, then interprets pathways in light of experimental context with literature support and writing help. In Alzheimer's disease case studies it consistently recovered neurodegeneration pathways and it beat six LLMs at citation retrieval.

papers.name: gSage
papers.title: Optimizing genomics-aware clinical agents in precision oncology
papers.summary: The paper introduces gSage, a workflow-orchestrated agent designed for precision oncology clinical decision support. It demonstrates that restricting the agent to a curated set of tools and knowledge sources enhances its reliability and safety compared to broader access approaches.

papers.name: Multimodal Anonymizer
papers.title: A locally deployable agentic framework for clinical data deidentification
papers.summary: The Multimodal Anonymizer is a locally deployable framework designed to deidentify identifiers across various formats in clinical data. It demonstrated high sensitivity and critical clinical preservation in automated and manual evaluations, supporting its feasibility for patient-level data anonymization.

papers.title: A Large Language Model-Powered Multiagent Framework Emulating Standardized Patients in Clinical Communication Skills Training: Development and Evaluation Study
papers.summary: Five subagents modeled on brain functional regions, with retrieval and character reasoning, jointly simulate standardized patients for medical students' communication practice. It outperformed single-LLM virtual patients on response quality, role-play, efficiency and perceived educational value.

papers.name: gget virus
papers.title: Deterministic access to global viral sequence data enables robust agentic scientific discovery
papers.summary: The paper evaluates the performance of Biomni and other AI systems in retrieving viral genome data from NCBI's Virus database, finding significant variability in accuracy. It introduces gget virus, a deterministic query framework that enhances retrieval accuracy and stability for these systems.

papers.name: AMREC
papers.title: Agentic Molecular Recovery via Molecule-Aware Exploration
papers.summary: AMREC is an AI system designed to recover the chemical validity of molecular structures generated by language models while preserving their structural identity. It demonstrates superior performance in recovering valid SMILES strings from invalid drafts compared to existing methods, as measured by various structural and exact-match metrics.

papers.title: Use of AI agents to assess preoperative frailty in cancer patients
papers.summary: The paper evaluates an agentic large language model system for assessing preoperative frailty in cancer patients, showing it outperforms a single LLM system in both binary classification and score generation tasks. The findings suggest that an agentic workflow can enhance the accuracy of automated frailty assessments from EHR data.

papers.title: Agentic Authoring of OMOP Concept Sets from Natural Language
papers.summary: The system automatically generates OMOP concept sets from natural language descriptions, combining various vocabulary tools and ontologies. It demonstrated high precision and recall in cohort-level validation against EHR data and outperformed unrestricted SQL access and PHOEBE 2.0 on a benchmark of AD/ADRD studies.

papers.title: Agentic Chart Review from Longitudinal Clinical Notes: a Lung Cancer Guideline Concordance Use Case
papers.summary: The paper evaluates a large language model agent for chart review in lung cancer guideline concordance, showing that the search-enabled agent achieves higher accuracy and reduces errors compared to sequential note review. The study suggests that tool-augmented LLM agents can effectively support scalable information extraction from longitudinal clinical documentation.

papers.name: SymptomAI
papers.title: SymptomAI: Toward a Conversational AI Agent for Everyday Symptom Assessment
papers.summary: SymptomAI is a conversational AI agent designed for patient symptom assessment and differential diagnosis, deployed in a study involving 13,917 participants. The system demonstrated significant accuracy in diagnosing illnesses like influenza compared to clinician-provided diagnoses.

papers.name: CodeCytos
papers.title: CodeCytos: AI-assisted spatial molecular imaging analysis via code-augmented agent action space
papers.summary: CodeCytos is an AI-assisted framework that uses code-driven automation to analyze spatial molecular imaging data, enabling dynamic and customizable interaction with tissue images. The system demonstrates improved efficiency and flexibility in exploring custom spatial cellular features across various tissue types through case studies and evaluations by bioscientists.

papers.name: PSEBench
papers.title: PSEBench: A Controllable and Verifiable Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs in Patient Safety Event Triage
papers.summary: PSEBench is a benchmark designed to evaluate large language models in the context of patient safety event triage, focusing on their ability to interpret and apply jurisdiction-specific policies. The system demonstrates the capability trends of various LLMs and highlights areas for improvement in using AI for clinical decision support.

papers.name: MedSP1000
papers.title: Evaluating Large Language Models in Dynamic Clinical Decision-Making with Standardized Patient Cases
papers.summary: MedSP1000 is an interactive benchmark for evaluating clinical agents using standardized patient cases, which assesses their performance in dynamic decision-making scenarios. The system reveals that current large language models, even those specialized for medical use, are not yet reliable enough to be integrated into actual clinical practice.

papers.name: CP-Agent
papers.title: CP-Agent: Context-Aware Multimodal Reasoning for Cellular Morphological Profiling under Chemical Perturbations
papers.summary: CP-Agent is a context-aware multimodal large language model designed to interpret cellular morphological changes under chemical perturbations, generating human-interpretable rationales for mechanism-of-action inference. It demonstrates high accuracy in distinguishing treatment effects and mechanisms with an F1-score of up to 0.896.

papers.name: D2MDT
papers.title: D2MDT: Department-aware Multidisciplinary Team Consultation with Deliberation for Efficient Clinical Prediction
papers.summary: Assigns department-specific doctor agents to each patient, retrieves complementary EHR evidence for them and updates only unresolved points across deliberation rounds before fusing the consensus with structured features. It improved mortality prediction while reducing consultation cost.

papers.name: MeDxAgent
papers.title: MeDxAgent: Multi-Agent Consultation for Interactive Medical Diagnosis
papers.summary: Builds a 4,421-case interactive diagnosis benchmark and a multi-agent consultation system that gathers demographics, questions the patient and refines candidate diagnoses over turns. It gained 10.3 percent accuracy over the baseline, closing about half the gap to a full-information oracle.

papers.name: ClinicalMC
papers.title: ClinicalMC: A Benchmark for Multi-Course Clinical Decision-Making with Large Language Models
papers.summary: ClinicalMC is a benchmark designed to evaluate large language models' performance in multi-course clinical decision-making scenarios, covering patient care from admission to discharge. The system includes a multi-agent evaluation framework and assesses various LLMs across different settings, demonstrating the complexity and evolving nature of medical decision-making processes.

papers.name: WMLLM
papers.title: WMLLM: Self-Evolving Optimization Agents via Predict-Then-Act World Modeling
papers.summary: WMLLM is a self-evolving optimization agent that uses predict-then-act world modeling to improve the efficiency of black-box molecular optimization tasks. It demonstrates state-of-the-art performance in multi-objective molecular optimization under limited evaluation budgets.

papers.title: From Idea to Data: An Agentic Architecture for the Clinical Trial Life Cycle
papers.venue: Studies in health technology and informatics
papers.summary: The paper describes a multi-agent system that uses large language models to support researchers throughout the clinical trial life cycle, from preparation to translation. The system demonstrates how an agentic AI approach can manage and streamline complex clinical research workflows with human oversight.

papers.title: Performance comparison of a neuro-symbolic large language model system versus conventional AI models and human experts in cholangitis management
papers.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
papers.summary: The paper presents a genetic neuro-symbolic LLM system that integrates multiple AI agents for managing cholangitis, demonstrating superior accuracy compared to conventional AI models and human experts in a multi-center study. The results suggest potential for advanced AI architectures in clinical decision support for complex medical conditions.

papers.name: DynamiCare
papers.title: DynamiCare: A Dynamic Multi-Agent Framework for Interactive and Open-Ended Medical Decision-Making
papers.venue: AMIA Joint Summits on Translational Science proceedings. AMIA Joint Summits on Translational Science
papers.summary: DynamiCare is a dynamic multi-agent framework designed to simulate interactive and iterative clinical decision-making processes, using MIMIC-Patient dataset for patient-level simulations. The system demonstrates the feasibility of modeling complex medical scenarios through iterative queries and adaptive strategies by specialist agents.

papers.name: MAP
papers.title: MAP: evaluation and multi-agent enhancement of large language models for inpatient pathways
papers.summary: The MAP framework uses specialized clinical agents to support decision-making for patient admission, diagnosis, and treatment planning in inpatient settings. Experiments showed that MAP outperforms existing large language models in aligning with operational protocols.

papers.name: Med.ai ASK
papers.title: Med.ai ASK: an agentic system for biomedical question answering
papers.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
papers.summary: A ReAct-style agent selects among biomedical knowledge bases, vector retrieval over 44 million documents, external APIs and NER tools to answer scientists' questions. It led on long-form accuracy and faithfulness, was competitive on short-form questions, and serves over 1,600 users in production.

papers.name: ClinNoteAgents
papers.title: ClinNoteAgents: An LLM Multi-Agent System for Predicting and Interpreting Heart Failure 30-Day Readmission from Clinical Notes
papers.venue: AMIA Joint Summits on Translational Science proceedings. AMIA Joint Summits on Translational Science
papers.summary: ClinNoteAgents is an LLM-based multi-agent system designed to predict heart failure 30-day readmission risk from clinical notes, transforming free-text into structured representations and clinician-style abstractions. The system demonstrates high extraction fidelity for clinical variables and key risk factor identification while preserving predictive signal with significant text reduction.

papers.name: AgentPLM
papers.title: AgentPLM: Agentic Protein Language Models with Reasoning-Augmented Decoding for Protein Sequence Design
papers.venue: Workshop on Generative and Agentic AI for Biology, 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2026)
papers.summary: Equips a pretrained protein language model with decoding that interleaves sequence generation with calls to structure prediction, stability and docking tools, trained by a trajectory-level preference method. Across enzyme design, antibody optimisation, thermostability and interface design tasks it improved on passive baselines, notably antibody top-10 percent hit rate.

papers.name: ClinEnv
papers.title: ClinEnv: An Interactive Multi-Stage Long Horizon EHR Environment for Agents
papers.summary: ClinEnv is an interactive benchmark that evaluates large language models as attending physicians in real inpatient admissions, focusing on their decision-making process and information gathering. The system reveals significant gaps between the quality of discharge diagnoses and management actions made by these models.

papers.name: DrugClaw
papers.title: DrugClaw and DrugAudit: A Primary-Source-Grounded Agent and Authority-Aware Benchmark for Drug-Information Question Answering
papers.summary: DrugClaw is a multi-agent system designed to answer drug information questions by querying a registry of drug and pharmacovigilance skills, ensuring answers are grounded in primary regulatory or peer-reviewed sources. It outperforms other systems on the DrugAudit benchmark, demonstrating high accuracy and faithfulness in its responses.

papers.name: PROBE
papers.title: Probe Before You Edit: Probing-Guided Molecular Optimization for LLM Agents in Structure-Based Drug Design
papers.summary: The PROBE system uses an iterative multi-agent framework to optimize molecular structures for drug design, addressing the challenge of balancing binding affinity and druggability. It introduces diagnostic metrics that reveal common failure modes in existing LLM-based optimization pipelines and demonstrates improved performance on a benchmark dataset.

papers.name: BIOGEN
papers.title: BIOGEN: evidence-grounded multi-agent reasoning framework for transcriptomic interpretation in antimicrobial resistance
papers.summary: BIOGEN is a multi-agent framework designed to interpret RNA-seq data in the context of antimicrobial resistance, integrating biomedical retrieval and structured interpretation. It demonstrated strong biological coherence and evidence-grounded reasoning across multiple datasets compared to LLM-only baselines.

papers.title: Agentic Authoring of Interactive Multiview Visualizations in Genomics
papers.summary: The paper explores the use of large language models and agentic systems for creating interactive multiview visualizations in genomics, addressing challenges such as data heterogeneity and complexity. It evaluates different configurations of these systems and finds that agentic iteration significantly improves visualization quality compared to baseline methods.

papers.title: Clinical agents fail silently on patient identity
papers.summary: The study evaluates the ability of clinical agents to detect and handle patient identity inconsistencies in electronic health records. It finds that these agents often fail to identify subtle changes in patient identity, highlighting a critical risk for misbinding during routine clinical workflows.

papers.name: SURGENT
papers.title: SURGENT: A Surgical Multi-Agent Assistance System Across the Perioperative Workflow
papers.summary: SURGENT is a surgical multi-agent assistant with a tree-of-thought planner, department-specific agents, guideline and literature retrieval, and separate long-term and working memory over patient histories. It was evaluated on five perioperative tasks including case analysis, plan simulation, safety monitoring, risk assessment and rehabilitation.

papers.title: Counterfactual Evaluation Reveals Hidden Capability Profiles in Clinical LLMs and Agents
papers.summary: The paper introduces the Causal Sensitivity Score (CSS) to evaluate how clinical AI systems adjust their recommendations based on changes in patient inputs, revealing differences not captured by traditional coverage-based metrics. It highlights a universal safety blind spot where all models fail to update recommendations when surgery status changes.

papers.name: HetMedAgent
papers.title: Why Specialist Models Still Matter: A Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Paradigm for Medical Artificial Intelligence
papers.summary: HetMedAgent is a multi-agent framework that integrates generalist large language models and domain-specific specialist models to enhance clinical decision-making. The system demonstrates improved performance in real-world tasks by leveraging the strengths of both types of models, highlighting the continued importance of specialist models for precise analysis.

papers.name: GRASP
papers.title: GRASP: Gated Regression-Aware Skill Proposer for Self-Improving LLM Agents
papers.summary: Treats agent improvement as edits to a bounded library of procedural skills, admitting a candidate only if it nets improvement on a held-out probe under a hard regression budget. On FHIR-based MedAgentBench it lifted gpt-oss-120b from 40.6 to 88.8 percent and beat the best of five self-improvement baselines by 21 points.

papers.name: MediHive
papers.title: MediHive: A Decentralized Agent Collective for Medical Reasoning
papers.summary: MediHive is a decentralized multi-agent system designed for medical reasoning tasks, utilizing large language models to collaboratively analyze and resolve complex medical questions. The system demonstrates superior performance compared to single-LLM and centralized MAS approaches on standard medical QA datasets.

papers.name: Viral Sentry AI
papers.title: Viral Sentry AI-Automated zoonotic surveillance and drug repurposing agent
papers.summary: Continuously scans NCBI submissions, parses host information with an LLM, predicts human infectivity with a fine-tuned long-context genome model, and then scores viral proteins against approved drugs for repurposing candidates. It was cross-validated on a curated set of over 33,000 complete viral genomes.

papers.title: Automated de-identification of linguistically-diverse clinical narratives: a retrospective, multi-agent AI framework development and validation study in a global health surveillance network
papers.summary: The paper presents a multi-agent AI framework for de-identifying clinical narratives from low- and middle-income countries, addressing the lack of tools that can handle diverse linguistic characteristics. The system uses a hybrid approach combining LLMs with rule-based modules to detect and substitute personally identifiable information, achieving high F1-scores across various document types.

papers.title: Trajectory-Level Stability of Agentic Clinical Reasoning in Sepsis: A Longitudinal Evaluation Framework Using MIMIC-IV
papers.summary: Runs repeated stochastic rollouts of an LLM reasoning over 550 MIMIC-IV sepsis trajectories across six timesteps and measures divergence, entropy and temporal consistency. Individual outputs looked plausible, but intervention agreement across runs was near zero and instability grew over time.

papers.name: PKFM
papers.title: An AI-agent-orchestrated grey-box Transformer framework for sparse pharmacokinetic curve reconstruction and pharmacometric model initialization
papers.summary: The PKFM is a grey-box Transformer framework that reconstructs sparse pharmacokinetic curves and initializes pharmacometric models, improving accuracy and stability in drug exposure inference. The system outperformed general-purpose programming tools on standard benchmarks but requires human confirmation for downstream use.

papers.name: SpatialBench-Long
papers.title: Verifiable Benchmarking of Long-Horizon Spatial Biology
papers.summary: SpatialBench-Long asks agents to recover biological claims from raw spatial measurements without prescribed methods, with 24 evaluations across pancreatic cancer, glioblastoma organoids, lineage-traced lung tumors and aging optic nerve across many platforms. Claims were hardened by reproduction and scientist review and are graded deterministically.

papers.name: MolLingo
papers.title: MolLingo: Molecule-Native Representations for LLM-Powered Scientific Agents
papers.summary: MolLingo is a multi-agent system that uses chemically meaningful representations to automate molecular design, outperforming existing LLMs and specialized methods in optimizing drug properties and target binding. It demonstrates the potential of LLMs as molecular design assistants when guided by biologically grounded structural context.

papers.name: AutoScientists
papers.title: AutoScientists: Self-Organizing Agent Teams for Long-Running Scientific Experimentation
papers.summary: AutoScientists is a decentralized team of agents that self-organize around hypotheses, critique proposals before spending compute and share failures across long-running computational experiments. On BioML-Bench it reached a 74.4% mean leaderboard percentile across 24 tasks and found an ACE2-Spike fitness prediction method 12.5% better than the prior best.

papers.name: SafeRx-Agent
papers.title: SafeRx-Agent: A Knowledge-Grounded Multi-Agent Framework for Safe and Explainable Medication Recommendation
papers.summary: Agents combine patient context with external drug knowledge and a safety verification step to recommend medication sets at the fourth ATC level. On MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV it improved fine-grained accuracy while limiting interactions, contraindications and set size.

papers.name: SpatialClaw
papers.title: SpatialClaw: A Memory-Augmented Autonomous Ecosystem for Spatial Omics Analysis
papers.summary: SpatialClaw is a memory-augmented autonomous ecosystem designed for spatial omics analysis, integrating 30 specialized skills to handle various aspects of data processing and analysis. It demonstrates superior performance in complex biological scenarios compared to standard large language models, showcasing its utility in dissecting intricate tumor microenvironments.

papers.name: FetUSAgents
papers.title: Towards Reliable Fetal Ultrasound Interpretation with Multi-Agent Collaboration
papers.summary: LLM agents decompose fetal ultrasound queries into plane recognition, segmentation and measurement subtasks run by visual tools, and an arbitration step reconciles LLM reasoning with tool evidence stored in a retrieval bank. On a new 3,205-question fetal ultrasound VQA benchmark it beat the strongest MLLM baseline by more than 25 percent.

papers.name: LipoAgent
papers.title: LipoAgent: Coordinating Fine-Tuned LLM Agents for Safer Lipid Design
papers.summary: LipoAgent coordinates fine-tuned LLM agents for lipid nanoparticle design, predicting toxicity first and treating it as a precondition for efficiency prediction, with multi-agent verification and human review on disagreement. It improved mRNA transfection efficiency prediction by about 32% on average and its virtual screening rankings held up in wet-lab tests.

papers.title: Automated Detection and Classification of Delusion-related Content in Naturalistic Audio Diaries Using Multi-Agent Language Models
papers.summary: The system uses a multi-agent language model pipeline to detect and classify delusion-related content in naturalistic audio diaries, demonstrating the effectiveness of detailed diagnostic prompts and majority voting for accurate classification. The study highlights the importance of careful prompt design and evaluation methods in automated mental health diagnosis.

papers.name: MDIA
papers.title: MDIA: A Multi-Agent Diagnostic Intelligence Pipeline on HealthBench Professional
papers.summary: MDIA is a multi-agent system designed for clinical reasoning tasks, implemented as a 7-node specialty-routed graph that significantly outperforms ChatGPT on the HealthBench Professional benchmark. The study highlights how architectural design and context preservation can enhance performance in clinical decision support systems.

papers.name: PRAXIS
papers.title: PRAXIS: Case-distilled and code-verified AI agents for biological research
papers.summary: PRAXIS is a framework for biological research agents that uses literature learning and case distillation to create structured long-term memory, enabling it to support various biocomputational tasks. The system demonstrates improved method selection, error suppression, and workflow organization in complex biological research through object validation and public benchmarks.

papers.name: PathNavigate
papers.title: PathNavigate: A Training-Free Pathology Agent with Surprise-Guided Scan and Shared Slide Memory for Whole-Slide Image VQA
papers.summary: PathNavigate is a training-free pathology agent designed to address whole-slide image visual question answering (WSI-VQA) by navigating gigapixel slides efficiently. It uses a surprise-guided scan and shared slide memory to locate sparse, high-resolution evidence, improving answer accuracy and interpretability.

papers.name: VDSS
papers.title: Human-in-the-Loop Multi-Agent Ventilator Decision Support with Contextual Bandit Preference Learning
papers.summary: The Ventilator Decision Support System (VDSS) is a human-in-the-loop multi-agent system designed to assist clinicians in making ventilator decisions by adapting to individual clinician preferences using contextual bandit learning. Retrospective evaluations with expert review indicate that VDSS improves the acceptability of recommendations and reduces interaction rounds compared to traditional methods.

papers.name: MARRVEL-MCP
papers.title: MARRVEL-MCP: An agentic interface for Mendelian disease discovery via tool-augmented context engineering
papers.summary: Gives LLMs 44 tools covering gene and variant utilities, pathogenicity and phenotype databases, expression atlases, orthologs and literature, with the model inferring which to call and in what order. On 100 expert-curated questions a 20B model reached a 94 percent pass rate with the tools versus 41 percent without.

papers.name: NanoCortex
papers.title: NanoCortex: A Unified Agentic System for Nanopore Sequencing Analysis
papers.summary: NanoCortex is a unified agentic system for nanopore sequencing analysis that bridges the gap between raw signal basecalling and biological interpretation, using a multi-agent architecture. The system demonstrates significantly higher usability compared to general-purpose large language models in complex analytical tasks.

papers.name: TRACE
papers.title: Molecular Lead Optimization via Agentic Tool Planning
papers.summary: TRACE is an AI agent designed for molecular lead optimization in drug discovery, which uses trajectory-aware decision-making to select and sequence molecular optimization tools. The system demonstrated superior performance in optimizing ADMET properties compared to baseline models.

papers.name: MARICL
papers.title: From Residuals to Reasons: LLM-Guided Mechanism Inference from Tabular Data
papers.summary: MARICL is a framework that uses LLM agents to analyze residuals from base models and iteratively refine explanations for scientific data, particularly in biomedical contexts. The system demonstrates its ability to generalize beyond batch-specific noise by successfully applying learned formulas across different experimental conditions.

papers.title: Standalone LLM and a Pre-specified Agentic Pipeline for Explaining ICU Mortality Predictions: a Feasibility Study on the eICU Demo Dataset
papers.summary: Contrasts a single LLM with a four-step pipeline separating data interpretation, guideline checking and explanation when narrating XGBoost ICU mortality predictions on the eICU demo set. The pipeline avoided outcome leakage and grounded explanations in guidelines better, while the standalone LLM aligned more closely with SHAP attributions.

papers.name: SMDD-Bench
papers.title: SMDD-Bench: Can LLMs Solve Real-World Small Molecule Drug Design Tasks?
papers.summary: SMDD-Bench is a multi-turn benchmark of 502 solvable small-molecule drug design tasks across five task types and 102 protein targets, with a limited oracle call budget. Seven frontier LLM agents were tested, showing how far current planning and tool use fall short on real design problems.

papers.name: MedExpMem
papers.title: MedExpMem: Adapting Experience Memory for Differential Diagnosis
papers.summary: VLM diagnostic agents record pairwise differential-diagnosis notes from their own failures and reflective re-diagnosis, then retrieve these notes when reading new radiology cases. Across 11 radiology subspecialties it raised accuracy by up to 7 points over several models.

papers.name: ClinSeekAgent
papers.title: ClinSeekAgent: Automating Multimodal Evidence Seeking for Agentic Clinical Reasoning
papers.summary: ClinSeekAgent is an automated framework that enables clinical agents to actively seek and integrate multimodal evidence from patient records for better decision support. It demonstrates significant improvements in performance over models using curated inputs, showing the effectiveness of its dynamic evidence acquisition approach.

papers.name: DeepLens Diagnosis Agent
papers.title: DeepLens Diagnosis Agent: Agentic Workflow Design Lets a Small Reasoning Model Compete with Frontier LLMs
papers.summary: The DeepLens Diagnosis Agent is a structured pipeline that enhances diagnostic accuracy by guiding a small medical reasoning model through five stages of clinical extraction, retrieval, generation, triangulation, and decision-making. It demonstrates significant performance gains over the same model without the pipeline on the DiagnosisArena benchmark, highlighting the importance of workflow design in complex tasks like medical diagnosis.

papers.title: Evaluating open LLMs for agentic analysis orchestration in a typical biomedical lab
papers.summary: Claude Opus wrote variant-calling plans of increasing detail and six open-weight LLMs executed them as agents on desktop GPUs. qwen3.6:27b matched frontier accuracy on all plans and on an error-injection matrix, running on hardware under $2,000.

papers.name: StructAgent
papers.title: StructAgent: Orchestrating Cryo-EM Model Building and Refinement with a Multi-Agent LLM System
papers.summary: StructAgent pairs a literature-grounded structural reasoning agent with an execution agent that runs local cryo-EM software, tracks state and recovers from failures, with expert approval gates for major changes. Case studies covered refitting a 64-chain proteasome, auditing 530 ribosomal metal sites and fitting an ambiguous ligand.

papers.name: Memisis
papers.title: Memisis: Orchestrating and Evaluating Synthetic Data for Tabular Health Datasets
papers.summary: A tool in which an LLM agent takes natural-language goals and calls existing tabular synthesizers and privacy, utility and fairness metrics to build synthetic health datasets. The demo runs six synthesizers on a schizophrenia dataset with a locally hosted LLM orchestrating the workflow.

papers.name: SEMA-RAG
papers.title: SEMA-RAG: A Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework for Medical Reasoning
papers.summary: Splits medical question answering among an interpreter agent, an explorer agent that keeps retrieving until evidence is sufficient, and an arbiter agent that adjudicates the answer. Across five benchmarks and five backbones it beat the strongest baseline by 6.46 accuracy points on average.

papers.title: Simulating population compliance with pandemic interventions using large language models
papers.summary: The paper explores the use of large language models to simulate individualized behavioral responses to pandemic interventions, demonstrating their ability to generate mobility changes in different venues without fitting to observed data. The study highlights the potential and limitations of LLM-based agents for modeling population compliance with non-pharmaceutical interventions during a pandemic.

papers.name: EchoAgent
papers.title: EchoAgent: guideline-centric reasoning agent for echocardiography measurement and interpretation
papers.venue: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery
papers.summary: EchoAgent is a framework that uses large language models to control specialized vision tools for echocardiography, enabling structured and interpretable automation. It outperforms existing medical visual-language models in video-level reasoning tasks by accurately measuring anatomical structures and providing clinically grounded interpretations.

papers.name: S2F-Agent
papers.title: S2F-Agent: Harnessing sequence-to-function models for verifiable genome interpretation
papers.summary: S2F-Agent is a human-in-the-loop framework that orchestrates sequence-to-function models for genome interpretation, translating biological requests into reliable execution and rigorous downstream analysis. It demonstrated superior performance in various genomic analyses compared to general-purpose language models, showcasing its reliability and scalability.

papers.name: EOS AI Agent
papers.title: From Prompts to Protocols: An AI Agent for Laboratory Automation
papers.summary: The EOS AI Agent integrates large language models with laboratory orchestration to enable scientists to create and monitor automated lab protocols using natural language. It was evaluated in three simulated labs, achieving high success rates in protocol generation and significantly reducing interface actions.

papers.name: MethylCurate
papers.title: MethylCurate: Tool for Dataset Curation and Epigenetic Aging Clock Evaluation
papers.summary: MethylCurate combines deterministic GEO retrieval, quality control and clock evaluation modules with LLM agents for metadata extraction, harmonization and data parsing in a dialogue-driven workflow. It turns user-specified DNA methylation datasets into standardized inputs for benchmarking epigenetic aging clocks.

papers.name: BiomniBench
papers.title: BiomniBench: Process-level Evaluation of LLM Agents for Real-world Biomedical Research
papers.summary: BiomniBench is a process-level evaluation framework for large language model agents in biomedical research, scoring their full trajectory against expert-designed rubrics. It reveals that while models can reliably ground claims in real sources, they struggle with method selection and scientific reasoning.

papers.name: DrugSAGE
papers.title: DrugSAGE:Self-evolving Agent Experience for Efficient State-of-the-Art Drug Discovery
papers.summary: DrugSAGE keeps a cross-task memory of verified skills, evidence about effective strategies and recurring errors so that it can reuse past searches when building drug discovery models. It ranked first among nine agents on 33 molecular property prediction tasks and scored 0.935 on 17 held-out tasks using accumulated memory without new search.

papers.name: SepsisAgent
papers.title: Agentifying Patient Dynamics within LLMs through Interacting with Clinical World Model
papers.summary: SepsisAgent is a large language model augmented with a clinical world model to simulate patient responses and recommend sepsis treatment decisions. The system demonstrates superior performance in value-based decision-making while maintaining safety compared to traditional reinforcement learning and LLM-based methods.

papers.name: MechAInistic
papers.title: MechAInistic: A Reviewer-Supervised Multi-Agent LLM System for Auditable Mechanistic Drug-Hypothesis Generation
papers.summary: MechAInistic is a multi-agent system that generates auditable mechanistic drug hypotheses by grounding language model outputs in computational evidence.
