It demonstrated the ability to identify specific metabolic pathways and drugs for therapeutic hypothesis generation in immune-cell diseases, outperforming general-purpose LLM systems in terms of auditability.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning for Tool-Calling Agents in Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR)
papers.summary: The paper introduces a reinforcement learning (RL) post-training approach for an agent to improve multi-turn reasoning and answer clinically meaningful questions over FHIR data. The RL-trained agent significantly enhances the accuracy of responses while adhering to data integrity constraints, demonstrating superior performance compared to prompt-based methods.

papers.name: ProtoMedAgent
papers.title: ProtoMedAgent: Multimodal Clinical Interpretability via Privacy-Aware Agentic Workflows
papers.summary: ProtoMedAgent is a framework that uses iterative, zero-gradient optimization to generate clinically interpretable reports from multimodal data while maintaining patient privacy. It outperforms standard retrieval-augmented generation methods in terms of faithfulness and reduces the risk of membership inference attacks.

papers.name: RealICU
papers.title: RealICU: Do LLM Agents Understand Long-Context ICU Data? A Benchmark Beyond Behavior Imitation
papers.summary: RealICU is a benchmark designed to evaluate large language models' ability to understand and reason about long-context ICU data, using hindsight annotations from senior physicians. The study reveals that existing LLMs struggle with clinical decision-making in realistic ICU conditions, highlighting issues like recall-safety tradeoffs and anchoring bias.

papers.title: An Agentic LLM-Based Framework for Population-Scale Mental Health Screening
papers.summary: Wraps each stage of a retrieval-based screening pipeline as a policy-governed agent that is tuned against proxy metrics and locked or rolled back, coordinated by an orchestrator agent. A transcript-based depression detection proof of concept converged to stable configurations while avoiding regressions.

papers.name: GxP-Agent
papers.title: GxP-Agent: Process-DAG Topology for Reliable Clinical Trial Programming with LLM Agents
papers.summary: Encodes the regulatory order of clinical trial dataset derivation as a directed graph whose nodes are run by worker agents with pharmaverse context, validation gates and retries. On a benchmark built from the FDA CDISCPilot01 submission it matched all 49 ADSL variables in every run, where single-agent and flat multi-agent setups scored zero.

papers.name: ClaroAI-Bench
papers.title: ClaroAI-Bench: Evaluating Agentic Scientific Reproducibility on Real Biomedical Papers
papers.summary: ClaroAI-Bench is an evaluation suite designed to measure AI agents' ability to reproduce computational findings from real biomedical research papers. It demonstrates that full-capability agents can achieve a 60.6% success rate in reproducing results, highlighting the importance of accessible data and code for successful reproduction.

papers.name: ToolMol
papers.title: ToolMol: Evolutionary Agentic Framework for Multi-objective Drug Discovery
papers.summary: ToolMol is an evolutionary agentic framework that uses a multi-objective genetic algorithm and an LLM operator to iteratively generate drug-like molecules. It demonstrates superior performance in discovering ligands with higher predicted binding affinity and better Absolute Binding Free Energy scores compared to existing methods.

papers.title: Beyond Manual Curation: Augmenting Targeted Protein Degradation Databases via Agentic Literature Extraction Workflows
papers.summary: The paper presents an expert-in-the-loop LLM workflow for extracting data from literature on targeted protein degradation, achieving high accuracy in expanding molecular glue and PROTAC databases. The system demonstrates the potential of AI-assisted scientific curation to enhance predictive models by providing essential experimental context.

papers.name: AssayBench
papers.title: AssayBench: An Assay-Level Virtual Cell Benchmark for LLMs and Agents
papers.summary: AssayBench is a benchmark for predicting phenotypic screen outcomes using large language models and agentic systems, formulated as gene rank prediction tasks. It demonstrates that zero-shot generalist LLMs outperform specialized biology-focused models in this task.

papers.name: AgentRx
papers.title: AgentRx: A Benchmark Study of LLM Agents for Multimodal Clinical Prediction Tasks
papers.summary: Evaluates LLM agents on clinical risk prediction from EHR time series, images, radiology reports and notes, in unimodal and multimodal settings and in single versus multi-agent configurations. Single agents outperformed naive multi-agent systems, handled multimodal inputs better and were better calibrated.

papers.title: UTS at PsyDefDetect: Multi-Agent Councils and Absence-Based Reasoning for Defense Mechanism Classification
papers.summary: A deliberative council of Gemini agents, with class-specific advocates scoring evidence under clinical rules, labels defense mechanisms in emotional-support dialogues, and a builder-critic-guard agent team selects overrides from fine-tuned models. The system placed second of 64 teams in the shared task, though the council was often wrong on minority classes.

papers.name: DeepTumorVQA
papers.title: DeepTumorVQA: A Hierarchical 3D CT Benchmark for Stage-Wise Evaluation of Medical VLMs and Tool-Augmented Agents
papers.summary: DeepTumorVQA is a hierarchical benchmark for evaluating medical vision-language models and AI agents on tumor diagnosis tasks using 3D CT scans. It decomposes the diagnostic process into stages, identifies measurement as a critical bottleneck, and demonstrates that tool augmentation can significantly improve performance.

papers.name: CodeClinic
papers.title: CodeClinic: Evaluating Automation of Coding Skills for Clinical Reasoning Agents
papers.summary: CodeClinic is a benchmark designed to evaluate the ability of large language model agents to automate clinical reasoning tasks, such as ICU monitoring and patient state tracking. It demonstrates that these agents can synthesize reusable clinical skills more effectively than zero-shot code generation methods, improving consistency while reducing computational costs.

papers.name: AI co-clinician
papers.title: Towards Conversational Medical AI with Eyes, Ears and a Voice
papers.summary: The AI co-clinician is a conversational medical AI system that uses audio-visual data to assist in real-time clinical decision-making during telemedicine consultations. It demonstrated performance comparable to primary care physicians and significantly better than text-only approaches, highlighting the importance of multimodal input for effective medical consultation.

papers.name: VibeProteinBench
papers.title: VibeProteinBench: An Evaluation Benchmark for Language-interfaced Vibe Protein Design
papers.summary: VibeProteinBench is a benchmark designed to evaluate the performance of language-interfaced models in protein design tasks, including recognition, engineering, and generation stages. The benchmark reveals that no current model excels across all three stages simultaneously, highlighting recurring failure patterns and the importance of tool integration for effective protein design.

papers.title: Human-in-the-Loop Large Language Model Framework for Identification of Cutaneous Immune-Related Adverse Events
papers.summary: The study presents a human-in-the-loop framework using multi-agent large language models to identify cutaneous immune-related adverse events from clinical notes, showing improved accuracy and inter-rater agreement compared to manual review alone.

papers.title: Agentic GPT-5.0 system outperforms standard large language models and human experts in critical care clinical decision-making: a simulation study
papers.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
papers.summary: The study evaluates an agentic system combining GPT-5.0 and Gemini 2.0 Flash in critical care clinical decision-making, showing superior performance compared to standard LLMs and human experts in acid-base disorder interpretation and sepsis management using text-based vignettes.

papers.name: PromptBio-Bench
papers.title: PromptBio-Bench: Benchmarking LLM-based Bioinformatics Agents for End-to-End Data Analysis
papers.summary: Provides 244 expert-curated bioinformatics and data science tasks with reference answer files and structured file comparison for scoring agents. Biomni and ToolsGenie performed comparably, and all agents degraded sharply as task difficulty rose.

papers.name: BioDesignBench
papers.title: Benchmarking and behavioral characterization of LLM agents for protein design
papers.summary: BioDesignBench is a benchmark for evaluating large language model agents in protein design tasks, using expert-curated workflows and metrics. The study reveals that while the agents can select appropriate tools, their performance is limited by premature termination of candidate evaluation and lack of comprehensive metric coverage.

papers.name: WoundScribeAI
papers.title: Responsible AI for Personalized Patient Education and Engagement Across Medical Conditions: Leveraging Multi-Agent LLMs, Ambient Technology, and NotebookLM-A Case Study in Diabetes Education and Limb Preservation
papers.venue: Journal of the American Podiatric Medical Association
papers.summary: WoundScribeAI's Scribe AI uses a multi-agent system to transcribe and generate educational content for patients, enhancing communication in clinical settings. The study demonstrated the model's ability to produce accurate SOAP notes, visit summaries, and engaging patient education materials without hallucinations.

papers.title: Automated Extraction of Patient Demographics from Clinical Vignettes Using a Multi-Agent Large Language Model Framework
papers.summary: The paper presents a multi-agent framework using large language models to automatically extract demographic information from clinical vignettes in medical education materials. The system demonstrates high accuracy and reliability, with improvements through autonomous error correction.

papers.name: Open-Rosalind
papers.title: Open-Rosalind: Tool-First Biomedical LLM Agents with Process-Aware Benchmarking
papers.summary: Open-Rosalind is a biomedical agent system that emphasizes evidence-grounded outputs and tool-mediated execution, designed to enhance accountability in scientific research. The study demonstrates the importance of structured workflows and explicit tool usage for improving accuracy and reliability, though it also highlights challenges in external validity.

papers.name: MechAInistic
papers.title: MechAInistic: An LLM-guided Multi-Agent System for Reasoning over Genome-Scale Constraint-Based Metabolic Models
papers.summary: MechAInistic is a multi-agent system that uses large language models to convert natural-language biological questions into executable workflows for metabolic model analysis. It demonstrated its utility in generating therapeutic hypotheses by identifying potential drug targets and repurposing candidates from paired immune-cell metabolic models.

papers.name: BioProVLA-Agent
papers.title: BioProVLA-Agent: An Affordable, Protocol-Driven, Vision-Enhanced VLA-Enabled Embodied Multi-Agent System with Closed-Loop-Capable Reasoning for Biological Laboratory Manipulation
papers.summary: BioProVLA-Agent is a multi-agent system designed for biological laboratory manipulation, using protocols as the task interface and integrating visual state verification with embodied execution. The system demonstrates improved robustness in executing complex tasks under challenging visual conditions compared to existing methods.

papers.name: MedExAgent
papers.title: MedExAgent: Training LLM Agents to Ask, Examine, and Diagnose in Noisy Clinical Environments
papers.summary: MedExAgent is a trained large language model agent designed to perform clinical diagnosis by interacting with patients and ordering medical exams, formalized as a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP). The system demonstrates comparable diagnostic accuracy to larger models while maintaining cost-efficient examination strategies through extensive experiments.

papers.name: BioResearcher
papers.title: BioResearcher: Scenario-Guided Multi-Agent for Translational Medicine
papers.summary: Ingenix BioResearcher is a scenario-guided multi-agent system designed for translational medicine, which integrates over 30 specialized tools and machine-learning endpoints to perform evidence synthesis from heterogeneous biomedical sources. The system demonstrates superior performance in unit-level capabilities, open-ended biomedical reasoning, and end-to-end clinical discovery benchmarks compared to existing baselines.

papers.name: Starling
papers.title: Self-Driving Datasets: From 20 Million Papers to Nuanced Biomedical Knowledge at Scale
papers.summary: Starling is a multi-agent system that autonomously extracts nuanced biomedical knowledge from PubMed, producing large-scale datasets with high precision and recall. It demonstrates the potential of AI-driven therapeutic design by outperforming existing curated databases in terms of accuracy and scale.

papers.name: TheraAgent
papers.title: TheraAgent: Self-Improving Therapeutic Agent for Precise and Comprehensive Treatment Planning
papers.summary: TheraAgent is a self-improving therapeutic agent that iteratively generates, judges, and refines treatment plans to ensure they are precise and comprehensive. It outperforms existing methods on the HealthBench dataset and achieves an 86% win rate against physicians in expert evaluations.

papers.name: EvoSyn
papers.title: Bridging LLM Reasoning and Chemical Knowledge via an Evolutionary Multi-Agent Framework for Molecular Synthesis
papers.summary: EvoSyn is a multi-agent framework that integrates large language model reasoning with domain expert knowledge to design molecules, addressing the challenge of hallucinations and chemical logic errors. The system demonstrates significant improvement over existing methods in generating bioactive and synthetically feasible molecules through extensive benchmark evaluations.

papers.name: SPARROW
papers.title: SPARROW: subtyping Parkinson's disease with agentic reasoning and robust omics workflow
papers.summary: SPARROW is a multimodal framework that integrates genomic, imaging, clinical and cognitive data for Parkinson's disease subtyping. It uses chain-of-thought reasoning to provide transparent subtype decisions, highlighting contributions from each data source, and demonstrated superior classification performance on the PPMI dataset.

papers.name: STAT
papers.title: STAT: A multi-agent framework for integrated and interactive spatial transcriptomics analysis
papers.summary: STAT is a multi-agent framework for conversational spatial transcriptomics analysis with a persistent session, an interactive tissue viewer and a staged skill-aware pipeline. Across eleven task categories on three platforms it outperformed a plain LLM and existing autonomous spatial analysis agents.

papers.name: AgenticPosesRanker
papers.title: AgenticPosesRanker: An Agentic AI Framework for Physically Grounded Ranking of Protein-Ligand Docking Poses
papers.summary: AgenticPosesRanker has GPT-5 reason over six deterministic structural analysis tools to rank protein-ligand docking poses. On a balanced benchmark of ten systems and 162 poses it matched the Smina scoring function at 50% best-pose accuracy, far above random, recovering some systems Smina failed on.

papers.name: CuraView
papers.title: CuraView: A Multi-Agent Framework for Medical Hallucination Detection with GraphRAG-Enhanced Knowledge Verification
papers.summary: CuraView is a multi-agent framework designed to detect and explain faithfulness hallucinations in discharge summaries generated by large language models, using a GraphRAG-based knowledge graph for evidence retrieval. The system demonstrates improved factual reliability of clinical documentation with an F1 score of 0.831 on the safety-critical E4 metric.

papers.name: ADAPTS
papers.title: ADAPTS: Agentic Decomposition for Automated Protocol-agnostic Tracking of Symptoms
papers.summary: ADAPTS is a framework that uses a mixture-of-agents LLM architecture to automate the rating of depression and anxiety severity from clinical interviews. It decomposes long-form interviews into symptom-specific tasks, providing auditable justifications while maintaining temporal alignment. The system demonstrated improved accuracy compared to human ratings on high-discrepancy interviews.

papers.name: PhysicianBench
papers.title: PhysicianBench: Evaluating LLM Agents in Real-World EHR Environments
papers.summary: One hundred physician-reviewed tasks drawn from real consultations run inside an EHR environment accessed through commercial-style APIs, each needing about 27 tool calls and graded against 670 execution-verified checkpoints. The best of 13 agents passed only 46 percent of tasks and open models at most 19 percent.

papers.name: MediCARE
papers.title: MediCARE: Medical Collaborative Agents REasoning over Interpretable Heterogeneous Graphs
papers.summary: MediCARE trains a graph neural network on patient graphs for medication recommendation, explains it with XAI methods, and has collaborating LLM agents discuss and revise reports of the predictions. On MIMIC-III it produced accurate reports and improved prediction precision.

papers.name: SciResearcher
papers.title: SciResearcher: Scaling Deep Research Agents for Frontier Scientific Reasoning
papers.summary: SciResearcher is an automated framework that constructs data for frontier scientific reasoning by synthesizing diverse tasks and eliciting sophisticated computational and reasoning capabilities. It demonstrates superior performance on benchmarks like HLE-Bio/Chem-Gold, SuperGPQA-Hard-Biology, and TRQA-Literature compared to larger proprietary agents.

papers.name: ALEX
papers.title: ALEX: Automatic Language Explanations for Interpreting Treatment Effects via Multi-Agents
papers.summary: ALEX is a multi-agent framework that uses machine learning to identify important subgroup treatment effects from clinical trials and then employs large language models to generate natural-language explanations for these effects. The system was evaluated by specialist physicians who found the generated explanations clinically relevant, indicating its potential in enhancing precision medicine.

papers.title: Skill-Augmented Frontier Agents Nearly Saturate BixBench-Verified-50
papers.summary: The paper evaluates the performance of advanced language model agents on a curated bioinformatics benchmark, demonstrating near saturation accuracy with skill augmentation. It highlights that access to high-quality scientific skills and external resources significantly improves agent performance.

papers.title: Automated Symptom Identification from Clinical Interview Transcripts in Diagnosed Schizophrenia: A Multi-Agent LLM Framework
papers.venue: Studies in health technology and informatics
papers.summary: Seven specialized LLM agents with DSM-5/ICD-11 retrieval extract symptoms, match criteria, consider differentials, check timing, reason counterfactually, vote and arbitrate on schizophrenia interview transcripts. On 71 diagnosed cases it reached 95.8% positive agreement, above single-agent baselines with and without retrieval.

papers.name: MedAgentBrief
papers.title: Physician-Reported Safety Outcomes of AI-Generated Hospital Course Summaries
papers.summary: MedAgentBrief is an AI system that generates hospital course summaries using a large language model, which was evaluated in a clinical setting for safety and utility. The study found that the system was frequently used by physicians with minimal risk of harm and associated with reduced physician burnout.

papers.name: AERO
papers.title: AERO: An AI Agent for Adaptive Eligibility Refinement and Optimization of Clinical Trial Criteria in Real-World Trial Emulation
papers.summary: AERO is an AI agent designed to refine and optimize clinical trial eligibility criteria for better real-world applicability. It demonstrated the importance of systematic refinement in generating accurate real-world evidence by emulating a specific clinical trial with Mayo Clinic data.

papers.title: Federated Multi-Agent Architecture for Harmonizing Public Health Datasets into OMOP and FHIR Standards
papers.venue: Studies in health technology and informatics
papers.summary: The system uses a federated multi-agent architecture to harmonize public health datasets into OMOP and FHIR standards, enabling interoperable data integration. It demonstrated high mapping accuracy in integrating MIMIC-IV, ELSA, and synthetic datasets, showing the feasibility of scalable clinical decision-making support.

papers.title: Virtual Speech Therapist: A Clinician-in-the-Loop AI Agent for Speech Therapy Planning
papers.summary: The Virtual Speech Therapist (VST) is an AI-driven system that supports clinicians in assessing stuttering and creating personalized therapy plans. It integrates deep learning for stutter detection with large language models to generate, critique, and refine therapy plans iteratively, ensuring clinical interpretability and feasibility.

papers.name: NEURA
papers.title: NEURA: A proof-carrying framework for hallucination-resistant neuroimaging automation
papers.summary: NEURA is a framework that automates neuroimaging research workflows by converting free-text questions and datasets into executable analysis plans, validated outputs, and structured reports. It demonstrates improved accuracy in planning tasks compared to direct LLM queries and effectively detects hallucinations without false positives.

papers.title: Modeling Clinical Concern Trajectories in Language Model Agents
papers.summary: The paper presents a lightweight agent architecture that integrates a memoryless clinical risk encoder over time to produce continuous concern trajectories, enabling early detection of rising risks in clinical settings. The study demonstrates that second-order dynamics can reveal gradual increases in concern before critical thresholds are reached, enhancing the transparency and usability of LLM agents for human monitoring.

papers.title: Detecting Clinical Discrepancies in Health Coaching Agents: A Dual-Stream Memory and Reconciliation Architecture
papers.summary: The paper presents a Dual-Stream Memory Architecture for health coaching agents that separates patient narratives from structured clinical records to detect discrepancies, ensuring safe and accurate longitudinal healthcare management. The system was evaluated on real-world data, demonstrating its capability to identify 84.4% of designed clinical discrepancies with high safety-critical recall.

papers.name: BioAgent
papers.title: BioAgent: An Auditable Multi-Agent Framework for Reproducible Translational Bioinformatics
papers.summary: BioAgent is a LangGraph multi-agent workflow with a shared research state that coordinates literature retrieval, planning, data download from nine repositories, analysis, reporting and review with checkpointing and retry logic. It was evaluated on BRAF V600E melanoma, TP53 pan-cancer and PBMC single-cell case studies.

papers.name: SCOPE
papers.title: SCOPE:Planning for Hybrid Querying over Clinical Trial Data
papers.summary: SCOPE is a multi-LLM planner-based framework designed to reason over clinical trial data, breaking down tasks into row selection, structured planning, and execution phases. It demonstrates improved accuracy for reasoning-based questions compared to direct prompting or heavier agentic baselines.

papers.name: AgentClinic
papers.title: AgentClinic: a multimodal benchmark for tool-using clinical AI agents
papers.summary: AgentClinic is a multimodal benchmark designed to evaluate large language models in simulated clinical environments, focusing on sequential decision-making and tool usage. The system demonstrates that existing LLMs struggle with complex clinical tasks when evaluated under realistic conditions, highlighting the need for further development in their ability to use tools effectively.

papers.name: NS-MAS
papers.title: Neurosymbolic Multi-Agent Large Language Model System Versus Specialist Physicians in COPD and Asthma Management: A Comparative Performance Evaluation Using Guideline-Based Clinical Vignettes
papers.summary: A neurosymbolic multi-agent system with a LangGraph orchestrator and eight specialized agents answered 30 guideline-based COPD and asthma vignettes. Its accuracy was compared against 30 board-certified pulmonologists, allergists and emergency physicians.

papers.name: BenchGuard
papers.title: Who Guards the Benchmarks? Automated Auditing of LLM Agent Benchmarks
papers.summary: BenchGuard uses frontier LLMs to cross-audit the artifacts of execution-based agent benchmarks, optionally using agent solutions and traces as evidence. It found 12 author-confirmed issues in ScienceAgentBench and matched 83.3% of expert-identified problems on a BixBench subset for under USD 15 per 50-task audit.

papers.title: Case-Specific Rubrics for Clinical AI Evaluation: Methodology, Validation, and LLM-Clinician Agreement Across 823 Encounters
papers.summary: The paper introduces a method for evaluating clinical AI systems using case-specific rubrics authored by clinicians, validated through automated scoring by large language models (LLMs). It demonstrates that LLM-generated rubrics can approximate clinician agreement in ranking the quality of AI outputs, enabling more efficient and cost-effective evaluation compared to traditional expert review methods.

papers.name: FastOMOP
papers.title: FastOMOP: A Foundational Architecture for Reliable Agentic Real-World Evidence Generation on OMOP CDM data
papers.summary: Separates governance, observability and orchestration layers from pluggable agent teams for phenotyping, study design and analysis over OMOP CDM databases, enforcing deterministic validation outside agent reasoning. A natural-language-to-SQL agent team on Synthea, MIMIC-IV and an NHS dataset reached reliability scores of 0.84 to 0.94 and blocked all adversarial queries.

papers.title: Agentic clinical reasoning over longitudinal myeloma records: a retrospective evaluation against expert consensus
papers.summary: An agentic system navigates tens of thousands of clinical documents and lab values from 811 myeloma patients to answer treatment-history questions, compared with single-pass RAG, iterative RAG and full-context input. It reached 79.6 percent concordance with oncologist labels, above both baselines, though more of its errors were clinically significant than expert disagreements.

papers.name: EndoGov
papers.title: EndoGov: A knowledge-governed multi-agent expert system for endometrial cancer risk stratification
papers.summary: Pathology, molecular and clinical agents produce schema-constrained evidence reports, and a governance agent applies executable guideline rules from a knowledge graph, with hard overrides such as POLE status. On TCGA-UCEC it reached 0.943 accuracy with under 1 percent logic violations, and 0.842 on CPTAC versus under 0.31 for neural baselines.

papers.name: DxChain
papers.title: Thinking Like a Clinician: A Cognitive AI Agent for Clinical Diagnosis via Panoramic Profiling and Adversarial Debate
papers.summary: DxChain is a clinical reasoning framework that uses large language models to assist in diagnosing diseases by emulating the cognitive process of clinicians. It demonstrates improved diagnostic accuracy and logical consistency compared to existing methods on real-world benchmarks.

papers.name: MSAgent
papers.title: MSAgent: An Evidence Grounded Agentic Framework for LLM-driven Scientific Exploration in Mass Spectrometry-based Metabolomics
papers.summary: MSAgent is an autonomous framework that uses large language models to integrate over 50 mass spectrometry tools, enabling automated and evidence-grounded molecular identification from raw data. It demonstrated significant improvements in retrieval performance and reliability across various benchmarks compared to existing methods.

papers.title: Investigating the application of a generative artificial intelligence-based virtual patient agent in dental medicine for enhancing doctor-patient communication training: a randomised controlled trial
papers.summary: The paper describes the development and evaluation of a DeepSeek AI agent for dental communication training, which uses contextually adaptive dialogue generation to enhance doctor-patient interaction skills. The study found that students trained with the AI agent showed significantly higher scores in simulated patient consultations compared to those using traditional peer-to-peer role-play practice.

papers.name: DxDirector-7B
papers.title: DxDirector: an agentic large language model driving the full-process clinical diagnosis
papers.summary: DxDirector-7B is an autonomous large language model designed to guide the entire clinical diagnostic process, from initial ambiguous patient complaints to final diagnosis. It demonstrates superior diagnostic accuracy and efficiency compared to existing models while significantly reducing physician involvement in routine tasks.

papers.name: ROSIE
papers.title: Autonomous multimodal agents enable transparent, spatiotemporal reconstruction of immune dynamics in pancreatic cancer progression
papers.summary: ROSIE combines deep-learning prediction of multiplex immunofluorescence from H&E slides with LLM agent logic that orchestrates biomarker inference and spatiotemporal reasoning. Applied to pancreatic neoplasia in transgenic mice, it profiled 10.44 million cells and identified three ordered immune-stromal states.

papers.title: An autonomous LLM-agent platform for computational binder design and conjugation-aware prioritization of antibody–drug conjugates
papers.summary: Open Intelligence Hub (OIH) is an autonomous platform that uses large language models to plan and execute multi-step workflows for designing protein binders and prioritizing antibody-drug conjugates. The system demonstrated high accuracy in classifying oncology targets and generating binders with improved scores compared to alternative methods, suggesting its potential utility in computational drug design.

papers.name: GeneBench
papers.title: GeneBench: Assessing AI Agents for Multi-Stage Inference Problems in Genomics and Quantitative Biology
papers.summary: GeneBench is a benchmark designed to assess AI agents' performance in multi-stage scientific data analysis tasks relevant to genomics and quantitative biology. It evaluates the ability of these systems to handle complex, real-world challenges such as data cleaning, exploratory analysis, model selection, and producing actionable conclusions.

papers.name: CAES
papers.title: Using a large language model artificial intelligence agent to improve the efficiency of clinical quality measure evidence evaluation: a case study
papers.summary: Extracts claims and citations from a submitted pneumonia quality measure, retrieves further PubMed evidence and rates the strength and agreement of evidence for each claim with justifications. It judged 64 claims and 355 claim-evidence pairs in about five hours, agreeing with a subject matter expert on 69 percent of claims.

papers.name: RepurAgent
papers.title: Human-supervised Agentic AI for Hypothesis Generation and Experimental Assistance in Drug Repurposing
papers.summary: RepurAgent is a hierarchical multi-agent system with supervisor, planning, research, prediction, data and report agents, episodic memory and human oversight, built on drug repurposing tools and procedures. In acute myeloid leukemia, blinded experts judged its candidates more novel and mechanistically credible than a plain LLM's, and it was also applied to experiment design and assay analysis.

papers.title: Agentic AI for Personalized Physiotherapy: A Multi-Agent Framework for Generative Video Training and Real-Time Pose Correction
papers.summary: The paper introduces a multi-agent system for personalized physiotherapy that uses generative AI and computer vision to create patient-specific exercise videos and provide real-time pose correction. The system aims to improve at-home physiotherapy compliance by offering dynamic, tailored feedback.

papers.title: Benchmarking Agentic Large Language Models for Complex Protein-Set Functional Annotation
papers.summary: The study evaluates the reliability of large language model agents in annotating protein sets using a controlled task, finding that while coverage is complete, reproducibility and biological correctness vary. The research highlights the need for deterministic evidence tables and expert review to ensure high-quality annotations.

papers.name: SIMBA
papers.title: SIMBA: an agentic AI platform for single-molecule multi-dimensional imaging
papers.summary: SIMBA is an AI-driven platform that integrates single-molecule localization, spectral processing, and deep learning-based denoising into a unified framework. It demonstrates the ability to support standard imaging workflows while enabling advanced analysis of multi-dimensional imaging data through user-guided interactions.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Gated Glaucoma Screening: Combining Semi-Supervised Classification with Multi-Agent Large Language Model Deliberation
papers.summary: The system uses a two-tier approach for glaucoma screening, combining a semi-supervised classifier with a multi-agent deliberation system. It demonstrates improved diagnostic accuracy on ambiguous cases by routing uncertain predictions to agents for further analysis.

papers.title: First, Do No Harm (With LLMs): Mitigating Racial Bias via Agentic Workflows
papers.summary: DeepSeek V3 is a large language model used for clinical tasks, particularly in generating synthetic patient cases and ranking differential diagnoses. The study shows that when embedded within an agentic workflow, DeepSeek V3 can reduce explicit bias in diagnostic tasks compared to its standalone version.

papers.title: Neuro-Symbolic Resolution of Recommendation Conflicts in Multimorbidity Clinical Guidelines
papers.summary: Agents translate clinical guideline recommendations into symbolic logic that a SAT solver checks for redundancies and conflicts arising in patients with multiple conditions. On 12 SGLT2 inhibitor guidelines it found most conflicts were comorbidity-specific and detected them with an F1 of 0.861, where plain LLMs failed.

papers.name: PKGPT
papers.title: PKGPT: Expert-Orchestrated Recursive LLM Agent for Automated NONMEM PopPK Modeling with Human Benchmarking
papers.summary: PKGPT is a recursive large language model agent designed to automate the development of NONMEM-based population pharmacokinetic models. It showed promise in producing executable and converging models, but still requires human oversight for physiological plausibility and clinical interpretability.

papers.name: ProtoCycle
papers.title: ProtoCycle: Reflective Tool-Augmented Planning for Text-Guided Protein Design
papers.summary: ProtoCycle uses an LLM planner that calls protein design tools, reflects on their feedback and revises its plan over multiple rounds, trained with supervised trajectories and reinforcement learning. It improved alignment to natural-language functional requirements while keeping foldability, and ablations showed reflection drove much of the gain.

papers.name: StoryMI
papers.title: StoryMI: Steerable Multi-Agent Therapeutic Dialogue Generation
papers.summary: StoryMI is a multi-agent framework that generates therapeutic dialogues using large language models, with situational context and dynamic strategy control. The system demonstrates improved adherence to motivational interviewing standards and clinical plausibility through structured dialogue generation.

papers.name: ORION
papers.title: ORION: An agentic reasoning construct for the analysis of complex human immune profiling
papers.summary: ORION is a multi-agent framework that combines statistics, machine learning and automated literature review to interpret PhIP-seq immune profiling data. On an APS-1 dataset it recovered the known autoantibody signature in about two hours, compared with one to two months of manual work.

papers.name: RadAgent
papers.title: RadAgent: A tool-using AI agent for stepwise interpretation of chest computed tomography
papers.summary: RadAgent is a tool-using AI agent designed to generate stepwise and interpretable chest CT reports, providing clinicians with an inspectable trace of the reasoning process. The system demonstrates improved clinical accuracy, robustness under adversarial conditions, and introduces a new metric called faithfulness compared to its 3D VLM counterpart.

papers.title: An agentic AI system for automated pharmacogenomic recommendation generation
papers.summary: The paper presents an agentic AI system that automates the generation of pharmacogenomic recommendations using large language models and structured evidence from biomedical literature. The system was evaluated by experts who found it to outperform other LLMs in clinical clarity and guideline concordance.

papers.name: MetaMuse
papers.title: MetaMuse: A Multi-Agent AI System for Biomedical Metadata Curation and Harmonization
papers.summary: MetaMuse is a multi-agent AI system that autonomously curates and harmonizes unstructured biomedical metadata from public repositories like GEO. It demonstrated high accuracy in curation tasks, achieving over 95% across key fields on a gold-standard dataset.

papers.name: U-Probe
papers.title: Universal agentic probe design for imaging-based spatial-omics
papers.summary: U-Probe is a universal probe design platform for spatial-omics that uses AI agents to facilitate natural language-based workflows and supports diverse probe architectures. It was validated in various scenarios, demonstrating its capability to drive MiP-seq panel design, genome tiling DNA-FISH, and novel RCA-based ligation probes.

papers.name: Evo-MedAgent
papers.title: Evo-MedAgent: Beyond One-Shot Diagnosis with Agents That Remember, Reflect, and Improve
papers.summary: Adds a memory of past case episodes, reflection-updated diagnostic rules and per-tool reliability tracking to a tool-orchestrating chest X-ray agent, letting it learn across cases at test time without training. On ChestAgentBench it raised accuracy from 0.68 to 0.79 with GPT-5-mini and from 0.76 to 0.87 with Gemini-3 Flash.

papers.title: Beyond Arrow's Impossibility: Fairness as an Emergent Property of Multi-Agent Collaboration
papers.summary: The paper explores fairness in a multi-agent system within a hospital triage scenario, where two agents negotiate patient allocation based on ethical frameworks and demographic biases. It demonstrates that fairness emerges through the interaction of these agents, leading to more equitable outcomes than those achieved by individual agents alone.

papers.name: OphAgent
papers.title: OphAgent: A Generalisable Ophthalmic Agentic System for Global Eye Care
papers.summary: Agents plan the diagnostic workup, consult a knowledge base and interpret multimodal eye images through structured debate across four modalities and 11 datasets. It averaged 85 percent retinal diagnosis accuracy, above leading multimodal LLMs, and improved accuracy by up to 20 percent for 311 ophthalmologists in a global reader study.

papers.name: GPCR-Nexus
papers.title: GPCR-Nexus: Multi-Agent Orchestration for Knowledge Retrieval
papers.summary: GPCR-Nexus combines a GPCR-ligand knowledge graph with literature retrieval and a multi-agent architecture for query planning, evidence retrieval, validation and synthesis. It returns citation-backed answers about receptor interactions, mechanisms and disease links, shown through example queries.

papers.name: CARIS
papers.title: Coding-Free and Privacy-Preserving Agentic Framework for Data-Driven Clinical Research
papers.summary: The Clinical Agentic Research Intelligence System (CARIS) automates clinical research workflows, including planning and documentation, using large language models and modular tools. It was evaluated on three datasets with high completeness scores in both automated and human evaluations.

papers.name: VCR-Agent
papers.title: Towards Autonomous Mechanistic Reasoning in Virtual Cells
papers.summary: VCR-Agent is a multi-agent framework that integrates biologically grounded knowledge retrieval and verification to generate and validate mechanistic reasoning in virtual cells. The system demonstrates improved factual precision and effectiveness in gene expression prediction when trained with verified explanations from the VC-TRACES dataset.

papers.name: Pipette
papers.title: Pipette: Encoding scientific literature into an executable Skill Graph for multi-agent bioinformatics
papers.summary: Pipette is a multi-agent AI framework that uses a literature-derived Skill Graph to guide the execution of bioinformatics workflows through natural language interaction. It was benchmarked across various biological domains and showed superior performance in generating coherent, biologically valid workflows compared to LLMs without such constraints.

papers.name: CARE-ECG
papers.title: CARE-ECG: Causal Agent-based Reasoning for Explainable and Counterfactual ECG Interpretation
papers.summary: CARE-ECG is a causally structured framework that uses large language models to interpret ECGs and provide clinical decision support. It improves diagnostic accuracy and explanation faithfulness by encoding multi-lead ECGs into latent biomarkers, performing causal graph inference, and supporting counterfactual analysis.

papers.name: TrajOnco
papers.title: TrajOnco: a multi-agent framework for temporal reasoning over longitudinal EHR for multi-cancer early detection
papers.summary: TrajOnco is a multi-agent framework that uses temporal reasoning over longitudinal EHR data to predict cancer risk and generate patient-level summaries. It demonstrated comparable performance to supervised machine learning methods in predicting lung cancer, with the added benefit of better interpretability and scalability.

papers.title: Neurosymbolic Multi-Agent Artificial Intelligence versus General-Purpose Large Language Models for Clinical Decision Support in Ileus and Volvulus
papers.summary: The paper evaluates a neurosymbolic multi-agent system designed for clinical decision support in diagnosing and managing ileus and volvulus. The system, comprising specialized agents for perception, synthesis, and verification, outperforms general-purpose LLMs in diagnostic accuracy and reduces hallucinations and critical safety errors.

papers.name: CACM
papers.title: Constraint-Aware Corrective Memory for Language-Based Drug Discovery Agents
papers.summary: CACM is a drug discovery framework that uses precise set-level diagnosis and memory write-back to correct protocol violations, improving the success rate of language-based drug discovery agents. It demonstrates that reliable autonomous drug discovery benefits from more accurate failure localization and efficient planning context management.

papers.name: HealthAdminBench
papers.title: HealthAdminBench: Evaluating Computer-Use Agents on Healthcare Administration Tasks
papers.summary: Provides simulated EHR, payer portal and fax environments with 135 expert-defined prior authorization, appeals and equipment order tasks for computer-use agents. The best agent completed only 36.3 percent of tasks end to end despite high subtask success.

papers.name: G-Health
papers.title: Clinically grounded multi-agent artificial intelligence for preventive health management
papers.summary: G-Health turns routine health examination reports into preventive actions using aligned LLMs, 20 quantitative risk models and guideline retrieval in a multi-agent framework. Its models ranked best on 13 benchmarks, and 79 blinded medical assessors preferred its reports to those of other LLMs and senior physicians.

papers.name: STAnalyzer
papers.title: STAnalyzer: Transparent Spatial Transcriptomics Analysis via an Agentic Architecture
papers.summary: STAnalyzer is an intelligent multi-agent framework designed to automate the analysis of spatial transcriptomics data, from raw data processing to hypothesis generation. It demonstrated its capability in dynamically translating natural language queries into bioinformatics workflows and ensuring analytical robustness through multimodal feedback and cross-validation with biological knowledge.

papers.name: CompBioBench
papers.title: Agentic systems are adept at solving well-scoped, verifiable problems in computational biology
papers.summary: One hundred expert-curated tasks across genomics, transcriptomics, epigenomics, single-cell analysis, human genetics and machine learning workflows, built with scrambled metadata and synthetic data so each has one ground-truth answer. Leading coding agents reached 78 to 83 percent overall and 49 to 69 percent on the hardest questions from a bare environment.

papers.name: MedConceal
papers.title: MedConceal: A Benchmark for Clinical Hidden-Concern Reasoning Under Partial Observability
papers.summary: Builds 300 cases with an interactive patient simulator that withholds concerns and tracks whether a dialogue agent elicits and addresses them over multiple turns. No model dominated across metrics, and human clinicians remained stronger on several aspects of the interaction.

papers.name: ASDAgent
papers.title: From Synthesis to Clinical Assistance: A Strategy-Aware Agent Framework for Autism Intervention based on Real Clinical Dataset
papers.summary: ASDAgent is a framework that includes DoctorAgent and ChildAgent to provide high-fidelity dialogue synthesis and clinical decision support for Autism Spectrum Disorder intervention. It demonstrates strategic consistency with human experts in real autism interventions and enhances the therapeutic capabilities of small language models through synthetic data generation.

papers.title: Deep learning for microscopy without machine learning expertise
papers.summary: The paper introduces a framework where researchers can describe their microscopy problems to an LLM agent, which then autonomously designs and trains deep learning models without further human intervention. The system was validated across various microscopy modalities, demonstrating its ability to achieve high accuracy in tasks such as nuclear segmentation and histopathology classification.

papers.name: SEA
papers.title: Joint Optimization of Reasoning and Dual-Memory for Self-Learning Diagnostic Agent
papers.summary: SEA is a self-learning diagnostic agent designed to improve clinical decision support by integrating a dual-memory module and reinforcement learning for reasoning and memory management. The system demonstrates superior performance in standard evaluation metrics and long-horizon tasks, with expert evaluations confirming its clinical correctness and practical usefulness.

papers.name: GraphDx
papers.title: GraphDx: A Cost-Aware Knowledge-Enhanced Multi-Agent Framework for Sequential Diagnosis
papers.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2026, pages 21721-21736, 2026
papers.summary: GraphDx is a multi-agent framework designed for sequential diagnosis that integrates medical knowledge into a structured graph to enhance diagnostic accuracy while minimizing costs. The system demonstrates significant improvements in diagnostic success rates and cost reduction compared to existing large language model approaches.

papers.name: CCD-CBT
papers.title: CCD-CBT: Multi-Agent Therapeutic Interaction for CBT Guided by Cognitive Conceptualization Diagram
papers.summary: CCD-CBT is a multi-agent framework designed to simulate Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) more accurately by dynamically reconstructing the Cognitive Conceptualization Diagram and implementing information-asymmetric interactions. The system demonstrates improved counseling fidelity and positive-affect enhancement compared to existing methods, as validated by clinical scales and expert therapists.

papers.name: OncoAgents
papers.title: Transforming oncology clinical trial matching through neuro-symbolic, multi-agent AI and an oncology-specific knowledge graph: a prospective evaluation in 3804 patients
papers.venue: ESMO real world data and digital oncology
papers.summary: LLM extraction and reasoning agents work with an oncology knowledge graph, a recommendation engine and human review to screen patients for trials over 157,367 clinical pages. In a prospective evaluation of 3,804 patients it achieved an F1 of 0.82 against dual-oncologist labels, above GPT-4 prompting baselines.

papers.name: MAT-Cell
papers.title: MAT-Cell: A Multi-Agent Tree-Structured Reasoning Framework for Batch-Level Single-Cell Annotation
papers.summary: Builds candidate-specific premises from tissue context and marker genes, then verifier agents turn them into reasoning trees and debate over bounded rounds before reaching a cell type label. With a local Qwen3-30B model it averaged 75.5 percent accuracy across five datasets, above chain-of-thought and scPilot baselines.

papers.title: Epistemic Blinding: An Inference-Time Protocol for Auditing Prior Contamination in LLM-Assisted Analysis
papers.summary: Describes an agentic system that reasons across biological datasets for drug target prioritisation, with LLM-guided evolutionary optimisation of scoring functions, plus an inference-time protocol that replaces gene names with codes to measure reliance on memorised knowledge. Blinding changed 16 percent of top-20 oncology targets while recovering the same validated targets.

papers.name: DosimeTron
papers.title: DosimeTron: Automating Personalized Monte Carlo Radiation Dosimetry in PET/CT with Agentic AI
papers.summary: A GPT-5.2 agent calls 23 tools over Model Context Protocol servers to extract DICOM metadata, preprocess images, run Monte Carlo simulation, segment organs and write dosimetry reports. On 597 PSMA-PET/CT studies it ran without failures and agreed closely with OpenDose3D organ doses.

papers.name: CareGuardAI
papers.title: CareGuardAI: Context-Aware Multi-Agent Guardrails for Clinical Safety & Hallucination Mitigation in Patient-Facing LLMs
papers.summary: A controller agent routes patient questions through safety-constrained generation and separate clinical-safety and hallucination risk assessments, refining answers until both risk scores fall below a threshold. It outperformed baseline models on PatientSafeBench, MedSafetyBench and MedHallu.

papers.name: OGA-AID
papers.title: OGA-AID: Clinician-in-the-loop AI Report Drafting Assistant for Multimodal Observational Gait Analysis in Post-Stroke Rehabilitation
papers.summary: OGA-AID is a clinician-in-the-loop system that uses multiple specialized agents to draft structured reports for post-stroke rehabilitation based on multimodal gait analysis data. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of OGA-AID in reducing errors compared to baseline methods and highlights its potential as an AI-assisted tool complementing human clinical judgment.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Guided Latent Diagnostic Trajectory Learning for Sequential Clinical Diagnosis
papers.summary: The paper introduces a Latent Diagnostic Trajectory Learning (LDTL) framework for sequential clinical diagnosis, using two LLM agents to model the acquisition of diagnostic evidence under uncertainty. The system demonstrates improved diagnostic accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods on the MIMIC-CDM dataset.

papers.name: Med-ICE
papers.title: Med-ICE: Enhancing Factual Accuracy in Medical AI through Autonomous Multi-Agent Consensus
papers.summary: Med-ICE has several peer LLM agents generate and review answers over repeated rounds until a semantic consensus monitor detects agreement, without an external arbiter. It outperformed single-model generation and self-refinement on medical question-answering benchmarks.

papers.name: MedResearchBench
papers.title: Citation Hallucination Determines Success: An Empirical Comparison of Six Medical AI Research Systems
papers.summary: MedResearchBench evaluates six AI research systems on clinical epidemiology tasks using NHANES data, revealing that citation accuracy is crucial for system reliability. The study also demonstrates the effectiveness of a multi-agent pipeline in improving citation integrity and overall performance.

papers.title: A neural-symbolic AI agent system for biomedical concept mapping
papers.summary: The Medical Concept Mapping (MCM) system uses language models to rephrase ambiguous biomedical text into standardized descriptions before linking them to concepts in terminologies and ontologies. This approach improves the accuracy of concept mapping, especially for underrepresented or abbreviated terms, outperforming existing methods on multiple benchmarks.

papers.name: DrugAgent
papers.title: DrugAgent: A multi-agent digital biosensor framework for interpretable virtual drug screening
papers.summary: DrugAgent is a multi-agent framework designed for virtual drug screening that ingests raw physicochemical property signals and performs closed-loop sensing and decision-making. It demonstrates superior performance in accuracy, interpretability, and robustness compared to existing models under various evaluation metrics.

papers.name: OMICX-Agent
papers.title: OMICX: An AI-powered web platform for integrative analysis of multi-condition single-cell transcriptomics data
papers.summary: OMICX-Agent is an AI-powered web platform that enables users to perform integrative analysis of multi-condition single-cell transcriptomics data through natural language interactions. The system demonstrates its utility in real-world case studies, showcasing its ability to integrate single-cell RNA-seq with bulk RNA-seq and GWAS summary statistics.

papers.name: ESL-Bench
papers.title: ESL-Bench: An Event-Driven Synthetic Longitudinal Benchmark for Health Agents
papers.summary: Simulates 100 users with multi-year device streams, exam records and life events with known per-event effects, and asks 100 queries each about lookup, trend, comparison, anomaly and explanation. Database-native agents scored 48 to 58 percent against 30 to 38 percent for memory-augmented retrieval, with the gap on multi-hop attribution questions.

papers.title: Benchmarking Agentic Bioinformatics Systems for Complex Protein-Set Retrieval: A Coccolithophore Calcification Case Study
papers.summary: The paper evaluates three AI agents (Codex, Biomni Lab online, DeerFlow 2) on their ability to retrieve coccolithophore calcification-related proteins from UniProt. Codex showed the best balance between sensitivity and specificity, while also demonstrating high repeatability across runs.

papers.name: DILIConsult
papers.title: DILIConsult: A Multi-Agent Large Language Model Framework for Evaluating Drug-Induced Liver Injury in ICU Settings
papers.summary: DILIConsult is a multi-agent large language model framework designed to evaluate drug-induced liver injury (DILI) in ICU settings by intelligently parsing clinical and drug information. The system demonstrated improved performance in extracting DILI characteristics and analyzing suspected cases compared to conventional approaches, with evaluations conducted by clinician panels.

papers.name: BloClaw
papers.title: BloClaw: An Omniscient, Multi-Modal Agentic Workspace for Next-Generation Scientific Discovery
papers.summary: BloClaw is an agentic workspace for life-science research with a dual-track tool-call protocol, a sandbox that captures plots at runtime and a dynamic viewport interface. It was benchmarked on cheminformatics, ESMFold protein folding, docking and retrieval tasks, with far fewer serialization failures than JSON tool calling.

papers.name: CARE
papers.title: CARE: Privacy-Compliant Agentic Reasoning with Evidence Discordance
papers.summary: A proprietary LLM generates structured categories and transitions without seeing patient data, and a local LLM uses them to gather evidence and decide, on ICU cases where symptoms contradict signs. On the derived MIMIC-DOS dataset it outperformed single-pass LLMs and other agentic workflows while keeping data local.

papers.name: VIBEMed
papers.title: Toward Vibe Medicine: A Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Framework for Clinical Decision Support
papers.summary: VIBEMed is a self-evolving multi-agent framework designed for clinical decision support, integrating specialized agents for diagnosis and treatment planning. It demonstrates superior performance in complex clinical cases through its ability to learn from patient outcomes over time.

papers.title: Emergent Misinformation Genesis in Multi-Agent LLM Clinical Pipelines
papers.summary: This study ran 4,800 trials of multi-agent LLM clinical pipelines across four model families and found they generate clinical assertions that no single agent produced. Between 30% and 56% of network assertions were emergent and judges rated most of them as clinically dangerous.

papers.name: PDT
papers.title: Pre-diagnosis Diagnosis Treatment (PDT): A Novel Architecture for Diagnosis and Treatment-option Generation in Rare Castleman Diseases based on GPT4o
papers.summary: PDT screens patients for possible Castleman disease and then uses knowledge-enriched GPT-4o diagnostic and treatment agents to produce diagnoses and treatment plans. It was tested on 10 Castleman and 10 non-Castleman patients with results reviewed by clinicians.

papers.name: Cirrina
papers.title: Cirrina : LLM-driven pharmacological reasoning agent enables preclinical CNS drug evaluation
papers.summary: Cirrina is an AI agent that uses large language models and pharmacology tools to evaluate preclinical CNS drug candidates, providing reasoning traces for decision-making. It demonstrated higher accuracy in identifying failure-prone drug candidates compared to traditional deterministic methods.

papers.name: AcmGENTIC
papers.title: Large Language Models for Variant-Centric Functional Evidence Mining
papers.summary: Benchmarks reasoning and non-reasoning LLMs on screening abstracts and extracting functional evidence for genomic variants from ClinGen curations, then builds an end-to-end pipeline that expands identifiers, retrieves literature, filters, fetches PDFs and drafts evidence reports. The reasoning model classified full-text evidence with 96 percent accuracy and much higher specificity.

papers.name: CAMP
papers.title: One Panel Does Not Fit All: Case-Adaptive Multi-Agent Deliberation for Clinical Prediction
papers.summary: CAMP is a multi-agent system designed for clinical prediction that dynamically assembles a specialist panel based on the complexity of each case. It demonstrates improved performance and decision transparency compared to existing single-agent and fixed-role multi-agent approaches.

papers.name: MDCrow
papers.title: MDCrow: automating molecular dynamics workflows with large language models
papers.summary: MDCrow is an agentic large language model assistant designed to automate molecular dynamics workflows for proteins, using a chain-of-thought approach with expert-designed tools. The system demonstrates robust performance across various tasks and complexity levels, showing the potential of LLMs in automating complex scientific processes.

papers.name: BioMedAgent
papers.title: Empowering AI data scientists using a multi-agent LLM framework with self-evolving capabilities for autonomous, tool-aware biomedical data analyses
papers.summary: BioMedAgent is a self-evolving multi-agent LLM framework that learns to chain bioinformatics tools into executable workflows through exploration and memory retrieval. It reached a 77% success rate on the new 327-task BioMed-AQA benchmark and generalized to BixBench.

papers.name: VaaS
papers.title: VaaS is a Multi-Layer Hallucination Reduction Pipeline for AI-Assisted Science: Production Validation and Prospective Benchmarking
papers.summary: The VaaS pipeline is a systematic approach to reduce hallucinations in AI-generated scientific content, particularly for rare disease gene curations. It demonstrates significant reduction in Type I and II errors through iterative refinement and validation, achieving near-zero error rates with minimal cost per review.

papers.name: Medical AI Scientist
papers.title: Towards a Medical AI Scientist
papers.summary: An autonomous research framework that turns surveyed literature into clinically grounded ideas, implements and runs experiments and drafts manuscripts under three levels of autonomy. Across 171 cases its ideas were rated above those of commercial LLMs and its experiments executed successfully more often.

papers.title: Improving Clinical Diagnosis with Counterfactual Multi-Agent Reasoning
papers.summary: Specialist agents edit clinical findings counterfactually, measure how diagnosis confidence shifts and use these signals to challenge hypotheses in multi-round discussion. Across three diagnostic benchmarks and seven LLMs it improved accuracy over prompting and earlier multi-agent methods, and humans rated its reasoning more interpretable.

papers.title: Collaborative multi-agent conversational artificial intelligence for clinical support in Parkinson disease
papers.summary: The system uses a multi-agent architecture to provide personalized clinical support for Parkinson's disease, employing generation, critique, and synthesis agents. It achieved high accuracy in diagnosing and recommending treatments based on 50 representative clinical queries.

papers.name: PubMed Reasoner
papers.title: PubMed Reasoner: Dynamic Reasoning-based Retrieval for Evidence-Grounded Biomedical Question Answering
papers.summary: PubMed Reasoner is a biomedical question-answering system that iteratively refines PubMed queries and retrieves evidence to generate accurate, evidence-backed responses. It outperforms human experts on the PubMedQA dataset and demonstrates strong performance in clinical relevance and trustworthiness evaluations.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-driven virtual tumor board enhances precision care in myelodysplastic syndromes
papers.summary: The Virtual MDS Panel (VMP) is a multi-agent AI system designed to provide precision care recommendations for myelodysplastic syndromes. It demonstrated superior accuracy and reduced major errors compared to general-purpose LLMs, achieving expert-level ratings in diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment.

papers.name: ClinicalAgents
papers.title: ClinicalAgents: Multi-Agent Orchestration for Clinical Decision Making with Dual-Memory
papers.summary: An orchestrator runs a Monte Carlo tree search over diagnostic hypotheses, verifying evidence and backtracking, supported by a mutable patient-state memory and a retrieved store of guidelines and past cases. It outperformed single-agent and multi-agent baselines on diagnostic accuracy and explainability.

papers.name: SkinGPT-X
papers.title: SkinGPT-X: A Self-Evolving Collaborative Multi-Agent System for Transparent and Trustworthy Dermatological Diagnosis
papers.summary: SkinGPT-X is a collaborative multi-agent system designed for dermatological diagnosis, featuring a self-evolving memory mechanism to enhance adaptability and transparency. The paper demonstrates SkinGPT-X's superior performance in diagnosing both common and rare skin diseases compared to existing large language models.

papers.title: A large language model-based self-learning and critical agent framework for multimodal Alzheimer's disease diagnosis
papers.summary: The system uses a multiagent framework with large language models to simulate team-based diagnosis for Alzheimer's disease, improving interpretability and generalizability. It achieved high accuracy in classifying different stages of cognitive impairment without fine-tuning on specific patient data.

papers.name: Judge Agent
papers.title: A Judge Agent Closes the Reliability Gap in AI-Generated Scientific Simulation
papers.summary: The Judge Agent automates the validation of scientific simulation code generated by large language models, significantly reducing silent failure rates. It introduces a structured specification format and formalizes the boundary for reliable automated error certification.

papers.name: AD-CARE
papers.title: AD-CARE: A Guideline-grounded, Modality-agnostic LLM Agent for Real-world Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis with Multi-cohort Assessment, Fairness Analysis, and Reader Study
papers.summary: AD-CARE is a large language model-based agent designed for real-world Alzheimer's disease diagnosis, capable of generating comprehensive diagnostic reports from incomplete and heterogeneous data. It demonstrated superior accuracy across multiple cohorts and improved decision-making efficiency in a reader study involving neurologists and radiologists.

papers.name: WiseMind
papers.title: WiseMind: a knowledge-guided multi-agent framework for accurate and empathetic psychiatric diagnosis
papers.summary: WiseMind is a multi-agent framework designed for psychiatric diagnosis that integrates logical reasoning and empathetic communication to provide accurate and trustworthy mental health assessments. The system was evaluated using simulated patient interactions and real user sessions, demonstrating high diagnostic accuracy and clinical soundness.

papers.title: Multi-Agent Reasoning with Consistency Verification Improves Uncertainty Calibration in Medical MCQA
papers.summary: The paper introduces a multi-agent framework for medical multiple-choice question answering that uses specialist agents to generate independent diagnoses and Two-Phase Verification to improve uncertainty calibration. The system demonstrates significant improvements in calibration metrics on filtered subsets of MedQA-USMLE and MedMCQA, suggesting enhanced reliability in clinical decision support.

papers.name: MedClarify
papers.title: MedClarify: An information-seeking AI agent for medical diagnosis with case-specific follow-up questions
papers.summary: MedClarify is an AI agent designed to assist in medical diagnosis by iteratively generating follow-up questions based on patient information, aiming to reduce diagnostic uncertainty. The system demonstrates a significant reduction in diagnostic errors compared to standard LLMs through its ability to engage in targeted questioning.

papers.title: Structured retrieval closes the gap between low-cost and frontier clinical language models
papers.summary: The paper evaluates the performance of clinical language models in scoring NIHSS under realistic, noisy conditions and finds that structured retrieval workflows significantly improve accuracy compared to non-agentic baselines. Lower-cost models benefit more from structured retrieval than larger models, suggesting a practical approach for deploying robust clinical decision support systems.

papers.title: Development and Evaluation of an Artificial Intelligence-Simulated Patient Tool for Clinical Training in Family Medicine
papers.summary: The AI-simulated patient tool, powered by GPT-4o and grounded in medical case reports and databases, was developed to enhance clinical training for family medicine. The study showed that the tool is highly rated by participants for its usability, educational value, and ability to provide realistic and evidence-based feedback.

papers.name: RWE-bench
papers.title: Can LLM Agents Generate Real-World Evidence? Evaluating Observational Studies in Medical Databases
papers.summary: The paper introduces RWE-bench, a benchmark for evaluating large language model (LLM) agents in generating real-world evidence from medical databases. It assesses the ability of LLMs to execute observational studies and generate coherent evidence bundles, finding that current models struggle with end-to-end task completion despite some success in individual steps.

papers.name: TogoMCP
papers.title: TogoMCP: Natural Language Querying of Life-Science Knowledge Graphs via Schema-Guided LLMs and the Model Context Protocol
papers.summary: Recasts the LLM as a protocol-driven engine that loads per-database schema metadata files and separates entity resolution through REST APIs from schema-guided SPARQL generation over about 60 aggregated life-science databases. On 50 biologically grounded questions it improved substantially over an unaided LLM, with the schema files contributing most.

papers.title: A Clinical Guideline-Grounded Hybrid Agentic Framework for Holistic Epilepsy Management
papers.summary: The paper introduces a hybrid multi-agent framework for comprehensive epilepsy management, integrating diverse patient data and clinical guidelines to support decision-making. The system demonstrates improved reliability and comprehensiveness in managing epilepsy compared to existing task-specific models.

papers.name: EviSearch
papers.title: EviSearch: Trustworthy Extraction and Synthesis of Clinical Trial Evidence with Agents that Improve with Use
papers.summary: Three tool-using agents extract evidence-table values from trial publications, an attribution verifier confirms each value on its cited page, and agent disagreement routes cells to human review whose feedback updates a curation knowledge base. On a clinician-annotated benchmark it reached 91.7 percent accuracy autonomously and 95.2 percent after reviewing 15.6 percent of cells.

papers.name: GSEM
papers.title: GSEM: Graph-based Self-Evolving Memory for Experience Augmented Clinical Reasoning
papers.summary: GSEM is a clinical decision-making agent that uses a graph-based memory system to store and retrieve past experiences, enhancing its ability to make accurate decisions. The system demonstrated superior performance on the MedR-Bench and MedAgentsBench benchmarks compared to other methods, showcasing its effectiveness in clinical reasoning tasks.

papers.name: Cerebra
papers.title: Cerebra: A Multidisciplinary AI Board for Multimodal Dementia Characterization and Risk Assessment
papers.summary: Cerebra is an interactive multi-agent AI system designed to assist in dementia diagnosis and risk assessment by integrating electronic health records, clinical notes, and medical imaging data. It demonstrated superior performance compared to single-modality models and language model baselines, with significant improvements in accuracy when used by experienced physicians.

papers.title: Agentic Automation of BT-RADS Scoring: End-to-End Multi-Agent System for Standardized Brain Tumor Follow-up Assessment
papers.summary: The system uses a multi-agent architecture to automate BT-RADS scoring for brain tumor follow-up assessments, integrating clinical data extraction and decision logic application. It demonstrated higher accuracy compared to initial clinical assessments, particularly in detecting critical categories like BT-4.

papers.title: From Concept to Clinic: Real World Evidence for Autonomous AI Deployment in Primary Care Telemedicine
papers.summary: Compares a deployed multi-agent LLM intake system's diagnoses and dispositions with those of blinded treating clinicians in 2,379 real primary-care telemedicine visits. Top-1 diagnosis matched in 91.3 percent of cases and 96.3 percent above a safety confidence threshold, with a 2.5 percent disposition error rate.

papers.name: Virtual Study Group
papers.title: Revisiting Gene Ontology Knowledge Discovery with Hierarchical Feature Selection and Virtual Study Group of AI Agents
papers.summary: The Virtual Study Group is an agentic AI framework that uses hierarchical feature selection to identify ageing-related Gene Ontology terms and generate biological knowledge. The system's findings were validated by reviewing existing literature, demonstrating its effectiveness in scientific discovery.

papers.title: Deep reflective reasoning in interdependence constrained structured data extraction from clinical notes for digital health
papers.summary: An LLM agent repeatedly checks its structured outputs against variable dependencies, the source text and retrieved domain knowledge, revising until they converge. In colorectal synoptic reporting, Ewing sarcoma CD99 patterns and lung cancer staging it raised accuracy, for example tumour stage from 0.680 to 0.833.

papers.name: DispatchMAS
papers.title: DispatchMAS: fusing taxonomy and artificial intelligence agents for emergency medical services
papers.summary: DispatchMAS uses AutoGen caller and dispatcher agents grounded in a curated taxonomy of chief complaints and caller identities to simulate emergency medical dispatch calls. Expert clinical assessment and automated metrics were used to evaluate the realism and protocol adherence of the simulations.

papers.title: Chat-Driven Computational (Bio)chemistry: Using LLM Agents to Accelerate Bio- and Chemoinformatics
papers.venue: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: The paper demonstrates the use of large language models (LLMs) to optimize and modernize computational chemistry tools, specifically improving the LEaP program in the AMBER molecular dynamics suite. The LLM was used to implement an optimized unit merge algorithm and 64-bit indexing, significantly reducing parametrization time for mid-sized systems and enabling the handling of multimillion-molecule systems.

papers.name: HARVEST
papers.title: HARVEST: Unlocking the Dark Bioactivity Data of Pharmaceutical Patents via Agentic AI
papers.summary: HARVEST is a multi-agent AI system that autonomously extracts and structures bioactivity data from pharmaceutical patents, significantly expanding the available chemical and biological knowledge. The system's performance was validated through comparison with human-curated databases and revealed limitations in existing models when dealing with novel scaffolds and uncharacterized protein targets.

papers.name: ACP
papers.title: Agentic Cognitive Profiling: Realigning Automated Alzheimer's Disease Detection with Clinical Construct Validity
papers.summary: Agentic Cognitive Profiling (ACP) is an AI framework designed to realign automated Alzheimer's Disease screening with clinical protocol logic, focusing on construct validity. It decomposes standardized assessments into cognitive tasks and uses specialized language model agents for semantic understanding and deterministic function calling for quantification, achieving high accuracy in AD prediction while providing interpretable cognitive profiles.

papers.name: CellVoyager
papers.title: CellVoyager: AI CompBio agent generates new insights by autonomously analyzing biological data
papers.summary: CellVoyager is an LLM agent that autonomously proposes and runs scRNA-seq analyses in Jupyter notebooks. On the 76-study CellBench it beat GPT-4o and o3-mini by up to 23% at predicting authors' analyses, and experts rated its new findings in three case studies as sound.

papers.name: CoNVict
papers.title: CoNVict: An Agentic AI System for Copy Number Variation Prioritization in Rare Disease Diagnosis
papers.summary: CoNVict is an agentic AI system designed to prioritize copy number variations (CNVs) for rare disease diagnosis by integrating patient phenotype data and performing structured reasoning. The study demonstrates that CoNVict outperforms existing computational methods in identifying causal CNVs, particularly in cases involving uncertain or non-coding variants.

papers.name: OmicClaw
papers.title: OmicClaw: executable and reproducible natural-language multi-omics analysis over the unified OmicVerse ecosystem
papers.summary: OmicClaw translates natural-language requests into traceable multi-omics workflows over the OmicVerse ecosystem using a registry-grounded, state-aware execution layer with iterative repair. It was evaluated on a benchmark of bulk, single-cell and spatial analysis tasks.

papers.title: Ablation Study of a Fairness Auditing Agentic System for Bias Mitigation in Early-Onset Colorectal Cancer Detection
papers.summary: The study evaluates an agentic AI system with a two-agent architecture for auditing fairness in machine learning models used to detect early-onset colorectal cancer, focusing on demographic disparities. The results indicate that agents augmented with retrieval capabilities achieve higher semantic similarity to expert-derived statements compared to other configurations, suggesting potential for scaling fairness audits in clinical AI.

papers.name: Samyama
papers.title: Open Biomedical Knowledge Graphs at Scale: Construction, Federation, and AI Agent Access with Samyama Graph Database
papers.summary: The Samyama Graph Database constructs large-scale biomedical knowledge graphs from diverse public data sources, enabling cross-KG federation and AI agent access. It demonstrated high accuracy in answering pharmacology questions compared to standalone LLMs or schema-aware text-to-Cypher approaches.

papers.name: Agent Rosetta
papers.title: Protein Design with Agent Rosetta: A Case Study for Specialized Scientific Agents
papers.summary: Agent Rosetta is an AI agent designed to perform protein design tasks using the Rosetta software, demonstrating its capability in both canonical amino acid designs and non-canonical residue designs where traditional ML methods struggle. The study highlights the importance of environment design for integrating large language models with specialized scientific tools.

papers.name: stMCP
papers.title: stMCP: Spatial Transcriptomics with a Model Context Protocol Server
papers.summary: stMCP is a Model Context Protocol framework that enables natural language-driven spatial transcriptomics analysis, executing tools locally to ensure data privacy and reproducibility. It demonstrates robust performance in biological discovery tasks, reducing the need for bioinformaticians by empowering biologists to independently explore their data.

papers.name: TheraAgent
papers.title: TheraAgent: Multi-Agent Framework with Self-Evolving Memory and Evidence-Calibrated Reasoning for PET Theranostics
papers.summary: TheraAgent is a multi-agent framework designed for PET theranostics in precision oncology, addressing challenges of data scarcity and heterogeneous information integration. It demonstrates improved accuracy in predicting treatment outcomes compared to existing models, highlighting its potential for reliable clinical decision support.

papers.name: EnsAgent
papers.title: EnsAgent: a tool-ensemble multiple Agent system for robust annotation in spatial transcriptomics
papers.summary: EnsAgent is a multi-agent system designed for robust annotation in spatial transcriptomics, decoupling structural partitioning from semantic labeling to ensure reproducibility and accuracy. It demonstrates superior performance by effectively neutralizing batch effects and resolving subtle tumor microenvironment niches missed by single-paradigm approaches.

papers.name: MAESD
papers.title: MAESD: A Unified Multi-Agent Evolutionary Framework for Protein Sequence Design
papers.venue: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: MAESD is a multi-agent framework that uses evolutionary algorithms and large language models to design protein sequences based on natural language instructions. It showed the ability to iteratively refine protein sequences under functional and structural constraints, reducing the need for expert-level biological inputs in traditional computational protein design.

papers.title: A Multi-AI Agent Framework for Interactive Neurosurgical Education and Evaluation: From Vignettes to Virtual Conversations
