papers.summary: The paper describes a multi-AI agent framework for neurosurgical education and evaluation, converting static vignettes into interactive conversations. The system includes specialized AI agents to simulate patient interactions and provide objective clinical data, demonstrating that traditional multiple-choice testing may overestimate LLM capabilities in realistic clinical scenarios.

papers.title: When OpenClaw Meets Hospital: Toward an Agentic Operating System for Dynamic Clinical Workflows
papers.summary: The paper introduces an agentic operating system for hospitals that adapts large language model agents to manage clinical workflows safely and transparently. It evaluates a memory component using manifest-guided retrieval, demonstrating higher precision and efficiency in navigating longitudinal patient records compared to a metadata-filtered RAG baseline.

papers.title: Automated extraction and optimization of protein purification protocols using multi-agent large language models
papers.summary: The system uses multi-agent large language models to automate the creation and optimization of protein purification protocols, reducing manual labor and analysis time. It demonstrated high accuracy in protocol extraction and generated expert-validated optimization recommendations.

papers.name: PULSE
papers.title: Human-AI Co-reasoning for Clinical Diagnosis with Evidence-Integrated Language Agent
papers.summary: Combines a domain-tuned LLM with literature retrieval to propose diagnoses for 82 endocrinology case reports, and tests serial and concurrent collaboration with physicians. It matched senior specialists and beat residents, held accuracy on rare diseases, and helped physicians fix errors while introducing automation bias.

papers.name: ARMS
papers.title: Automated Standardization of Legacy Biomedical Metadata Using an Ontology-Constrained LLM Agent
papers.summary: ARMS is an AI agent that uses large language models to standardize legacy biomedical metadata by dynamically querying authoritative terminology services at runtime. The system demonstrated significant improvements in precision and recall compared to a prompt-based approach, particularly for ontology-constrained fields.

papers.name: MedMASLab
papers.title: MedMASLab: A Unified Orchestration Framework for Benchmarking Multimodal Medical Multi-Agent Systems
papers.summary: Integrates 11 multi-agent architectures under a common communication protocol and evaluates them on 11 clinical benchmarks spanning 473 diseases, using a VLM-based reasoning evaluator. Multi-agent systems reasoned more deeply but were fragile when moving between medical subdomains.

papers.name: FetalAgents
papers.title: FetalAgents: A Multi-Agent System for Fetal Ultrasound Image and Video Analysis
papers.summary: FetalAgents is a multi-agent system designed for fetal ultrasound image and video analysis, dynamically orchestrating specialized vision experts to enhance accuracy in diagnosis, measurement, and segmentation. The system demonstrates superior performance across multiple clinical tasks compared to existing models, providing an auditable solution aligned with clinical workflows.

papers.title: Accelerating Exploratory Clinical Research: An LLM-Powered Framework for Cross-Study Data Harmonization and Natural Language Querying
papers.summary: The paper presents a framework that uses large language models to harmonize clinical trial data across studies, making it interoperable and accessible for exploratory analysis. The system enables natural language querying of the harmonized data, reducing manual effort and improving query accuracy in secondary analysis workflows.

papers.name: Meissa
papers.title: Meissa: Multi-modal Medical Agentic Intelligence
papers.summary: Meissa is a lightweight, multi-modal medical large language model designed for offline deployment in clinical settings. It demonstrates competitive performance with larger models on various medical benchmarks while offering significant advantages in cost and latency.

papers.title: Agentic LLM Workflow for MR Spectroscopy Volume-of-Interest Placements in Brain Tumors
papers.summary: The paper presents an agentic LLM workflow for optimizing the placement of spectroscopy volume-of-interest in brain tumors, enhancing clinical decision-making by generating and selecting from multiple candidate placements. The system demonstrates improved coverage of solid tumors and avoidance of necrosis based on user preferences compared to general expert placements.

papers.name: SELSM
papers.title: Empowering Locally Deployable Medical Agent via State Enhanced Logical Skills for FHIR-based Clinical Tasks
papers.summary: The paper introduces SELSM, a framework that enhances the logical reasoning skills of medical agents to handle clinical tasks in FHIR-based electronic health records without requiring additional training data. It demonstrates significant improvements in task completion rates and success when tested on MedAgentBench.

papers.name: DERM-3R
papers.title: DERM-3R: A Resource-Efficient Multimodal Agents Framework for Dermatologic Diagnosis and Treatment in Real-World Clinical Settings
papers.summary: DERM-3R is a framework of three collaborative agents designed for dermatologic diagnosis and treatment using traditional Chinese medicine, addressing fine-grained lesion recognition, multi-view representation, and holistic clinical reasoning. The system demonstrates strong performance in dermatologic tasks with limited data and computational resources, matching or surpassing larger general-purpose models.

papers.name: MACRO
papers.title: Evolving Medical Imaging Agents via Experience-driven Self-skill Discovery
papers.summary: A medical imaging agent mines its verified execution trajectories for recurring tool sequences, registers them as composite tools, and reinforces their use with an image-feature memory and a GRPO-style training loop. It improved multi-step orchestration accuracy and cross-domain generalization over prior agentic methods across imaging datasets.

papers.name: MedCoRAG
papers.title: MedCoRAG: Interpretable Hepatology Diagnosis via Hybrid Evidence Retrieval and Multispecialty Consensus
papers.summary: MedCoRAG is a framework that uses multi-agent collaboration and retrieval-augmented generation to diagnose hepatic diseases, providing structured reasoning and interpretability. It outperforms existing methods in diagnostic accuracy and interpretability on real-world clinical cases.

papers.title: Formalized scientific methodology enables rigorous AI-conducted research across domains
papers.summary: The paper describes a formalized scientific methodology that enables AI agents to conduct rigorous research across various domains, including population genomics. The approach involves decomposing the research process into procedural workflows and integrity disciplines, which are validated through end-to-end projects and controlled studies demonstrating improved auditability and evidence-backed outputs.

papers.name: Mozi
papers.title: Mozi: Governed Autonomy for Drug Discovery LLM Agents
papers.summary: A control plane enforces role-based tool isolation, constrained action spaces and reflective replanning, while a workflow plane runs drug discovery stages as stateful skill graphs with data contracts and human checkpoints. It outperformed baselines on orchestration accuracy on PharmaBench and was demonstrated in end-to-end therapeutic case studies.

papers.name: RBRA
papers.title: Robust BioReasoning Agent: Enhancing Robust Multi-hop Fact Extraction and Reasoning in Biomedical Large Language Models
papers.summary: The Robust Biomedical Reasoning Agent (RBRA) enhances the robustness and accuracy of large language models in biomedical multi-hop reasoning tasks. It achieves this through hierarchical query decomposition, dynamic context filtering, iterative fact verification, and optimization for robust metrics, demonstrating superior performance on a challenging dataset compared to existing methods.

papers.name: GLEAN
papers.title: Guideline-Grounded Evidence Accumulation for High-Stakes Agent Verification
papers.summary: Compiles expert protocols into step-wise alignment ratings that are accumulated along a diagnostic agent's trajectory and calibrated into correctness probabilities, triggering extra checks when uncertain. On three diseases from MIMIC-IV it beat the best baseline by 12 percent AUROC and halved Brier score, and clinicians judged it useful.

papers.name: EnzySeek
papers.title: EnzySeek: Efficient Exploration of Enzyme Reaction Pathways Using AI Agents
papers.summary: EnzySeek is an AI agent designed to assist in enzyme catalysis simulations by integrating a domain-specific knowledge base and custom Model Context Protocol interfaces. It demonstrates the ability to autonomously execute computational tasks such as molecular docking, MD simulations, and QM/MM calculations while continuously learning from new literature and being validated through human expert review.

papers.title: An agentic AI system enhances clinical detection of immunotherapy toxicities: a multi-phase validation study
papers.summary: The paper describes an agentic AI system designed to detect and grade immune-related adverse events from clinical notes, showing high accuracy in both retrospective and prospective evaluations. The system also demonstrated significant time savings and improved consistency when used by clinical trial staff for annotation tasks.

papers.name: HarmonyCell
papers.title: HarmonyCell: Automating Single-Cell Perturbation Modeling under Semantic and Distribution Shifts
papers.summary: HarmonyCell is an AI agent designed to automate single-cell perturbation modeling by addressing semantic and statistical heterogeneity challenges. It demonstrates high execution rates on heterogeneous datasets and matches or exceeds expert-designed models in out-of-distribution evaluations.

papers.name: ProtRLSearch
papers.title: ProtRLSearch: A Multi-Round Multimodal Protein Search Agent with Large Language Models Trained via Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: ProtRLSearch is a reinforcement learning-trained agent designed to perform multi-round, multimodal protein sequence and text searches for healthcare applications. It demonstrates improved accuracy in reasoning about disease-related variants and protein functions by integrating both textual and sequence data, as validated through the ProtMCQs benchmark.

papers.name: CARE
papers.title: CARE: Towards Clinical Accountability in Multi-Modal Medical Reasoning with an Evidence-Grounded Agentic Framework
papers.summary: CARE is a medical reasoning framework that enhances clinical accountability by decomposing tasks into specialized modules and using explicit evidence, outperforming existing models on standard benchmarks. It demonstrates the benefits of an agentic approach in medical AI for more accurate and trustworthy decision support.

papers.name: ChatSpatial
papers.title: ChatSpatial: Schema-Enforced Agentic Orchestration for Reproducible and Cross-Platform Spatial Transcriptomics
papers.summary: ChatSpatial is a schema-enforced orchestration framework that uses an LLM to select versioned tools and parameters for spatial transcriptomics analyses, ensuring reproducibility and cross-platform compatibility. In cancer case studies, ChatSpatial successfully recovered analytical structures and conclusions from published research with higher execution success and output concordance compared to code generation alternatives.

papers.title: A multiagent large language model-based system to simulate the liver transplant selection committee: a retrospective cohort study
papers.summary: The AI Liver Transplant Selection Committee is a multiagent system using large language models to simulate the decision-making process of a liver transplant selection committee. The study demonstrated high accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity in predicting patient survival post-transplantation and identifying contraindications for transplantation.

papers.name: ChatCLIDS
papers.title: ChatCLIDS: Simulating Persuasive AI Dialogues to Promote Closed-Loop Insulin Adoption in Type 1 Diabetes Care
papers.venue: Proceedings of the ... AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence. AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
papers.summary: ChatCLIDS is a benchmark where LLM nurse agents with evidence-based persuasion strategies hold multi-turn conversations with expert-validated virtual patients who resist closed-loop insulin delivery. Larger reflective models adapted over time, but all models struggled against resistance and social pressure.

papers.name: CIWM
papers.title: Contextual Invertible World Models: A Neuro-Symbolic Agentic Framework for Colorectal Cancer Drug Response
papers.summary: The Contextual Invertible World Model (CIWM) integrates a machine learning emulator with a large language model to predict drug responses in colorectal cancer. It revealed that mutant KRAS has a hierarchical dominance over the APC/Wnt-axis in driving resistance to 5-fluorouracil and identified a paradox where repairing PIK3CA increases chemoresistance.

papers.name: TARSE
papers.title: TARSE: Test-Time Adaptation via Retrieval of Skills and Experience for Reasoning Agents
papers.summary: TARSE is a system designed to enhance clinical decision-making by retrieving and adapting skills and experiences at test time. It demonstrates consistent improvements over existing methods on medical question-answering benchmarks, highlighting the effectiveness of its approach in aligning model reasoning with clinically valid logic.

papers.name: MedCollab
papers.title: MedCollab: IBIS-Guided Multi-Agent Collaboration with Hierarchical Disease Relation Chains for Clinical Diagnosis
papers.summary: MedCollab is a multi-agent framework that uses an Issue-Based Information System (IBIS) protocol and Hierarchical Disease Relation Chains to assist in clinical diagnosis by integrating patient evidence and medical knowledge. The system demonstrates improved diagnostic accuracy, evidence consistency, and clinical reasoning quality compared to existing large language models and baselines.

papers.name: Eubiota
papers.title: Eubiota: Modular Agentic AI for Autonomous Discovery in the Gut Microbiome
papers.summary: Eubiota is an open-source modular agentic framework designed for autonomous discovery in the gut microbiome, using specialized agents for planning, execution, verification, and synthesis. It demonstrated its utility by identifying key DNA repair genes under inflammatory stress, designing a bacterial consortium to attenuate colitis severity, and discovering diet-associated metabolites that suppress NF-kB signaling.

papers.name: OPGAgent
papers.title: OPGAgent: An Agent for Auditable Dental Panoramic X-ray Interpretation
papers.summary: OPGAgent is a multi-tool agentic system designed for interpreting dental panoramic X-rays, combining specialized perception modules and a consensus mechanism to enhance accuracy and versatility. The system outperforms existing vision language models and medical agent frameworks in both structured-report generation and visual question answering tasks.

papers.name: PantheonOS
papers.title: PantheonOS: An Evolvable Multi-Agent Framework for Automatic Genomics Discovery
papers.summary: PantheonOS is a multi-agent framework designed for automatic genomics discovery, enabling the evolution of code and algorithms to achieve super-human performance in tasks such as gene panel selection and batch correction. It demonstrated its capability by uncovering novel biological insights in early mouse embryo development and human fetal heart disease.

papers.title: Bridging the computational-experimental gap: leveraging large language model to prioritize Alzheimer's therapeutics based on comparison of learning models
papers.summary: Candidates for Alzheimer's drug repurposing from three computational predictors were pooled and an LLM agent synthesized literature evidence to filter them using explicit criteria. The prioritized list was checked against patient data, clinical trial registries and pharmacological reviews.

papers.name: CellSwarm
papers.title: CellSwarm: LLM-Driven Cell Agents Recapitulate Tumor Microenvironment Dynamics and Sense Indirect Genetic Perturbations
papers.summary: CELLSWARM uses large language models to drive autonomous cell agents in simulating tumor microenvironment dynamics, achieving performance comparable to traditional rule-based methods. It demonstrates capabilities such as cross-cancer generalization and sensing indirect genetic perturbations that go beyond the limitations of conventional simulation approaches.

papers.name: CXReasonAgent
papers.title: CXReasonAgent: Evidence-Grounded Diagnostic Reasoning Agent for Chest X-rays
papers.summary: CXReasonAgent is a diagnostic reasoning agent designed to interpret chest X-rays by integrating large language models with clinical tools, ensuring evidence-grounded responses. The system demonstrates superior reliability and verifiability compared to vision-language models through evaluations using CXReasonDial, a dialogue benchmark for multi-step diagnostic tasks.

papers.title: Benchmarking LLM-based agents for single-cell omics analysis
papers.summary: The paper presents a benchmarking system for evaluating AI agents in single-cell omics analysis, covering diverse tasks and metrics. It reveals that multi-agent frameworks outperform single-agent approaches by enhancing collaboration and execution efficiency through specialized role division.

papers.title: Care Plan Generation for Underserved Patients Using Multi-Agent Language Models: Applying Nash Game Theory to Optimize Multiple Objectives
papers.summary: Multiple LLM agents with different objectives negotiated Medicaid care plans under a Nash bargaining scheme, compared with compute-matched sequential self-critique. In a pre-registered paired study of 200 patients, Nash orchestration gave a small but significant composite gain in safety, efficiency and equity scores.

papers.title: Performance Comparison of a Neuro-Symbolic Large Language Model System Versus Human Experts in Acute Cholecystitis Management
papers.summary: The paper evaluates LangGraph v1.0, a neuro-symbolic large language model system for managing acute cholecystitis, which outperforms human experts in diagnostic accuracy and treatment recommendations based on the Tokyo Guidelines 2018. The study demonstrates the system's superior performance across various clinical scenarios through automated benchmarking and expert review.

papers.title: What microbes want: exploring microbial substrate preferences with the Web of Microbes Agent
papers.summary: The Web of Microbes (WoM) Agent uses a Bayesian Personalized Ranking model to predict bacterial substrate preferences, integrating it with growth models and large language models for autonomous analysis. It demonstrated accurate predictions in novel medium experiments and correctly identified bacteria enriched in soil metabolite spike-in tests.

papers.name: AgenticSum
papers.title: AgenticSum: An Agentic Inference-Time Framework for Faithful Clinical Text Summarization
papers.summary: Separates clinical summarization into context compression, drafting, detection of weakly grounded spans via attention signals and targeted revision under supervisory control. On two public datasets it beat vanilla LLMs and other baselines under reference metrics, LLM judges and human evaluation.

papers.title: Assessing Risks of Large Language Models in Mental Health Support: A Framework for Automated Clinical AI Red Teaming
papers.summary: Pairs AI therapy agents with simulated alcohol use disorder patients that have dynamic cognitive-affective states, scoring 369 sessions against a care-quality and risk ontology. It found failures such as validating delusions and not de-escalating suicide risk, and stakeholders found the audit dashboard useful.

papers.name: CT-Flow
papers.title: CT-Flow: Orchestrating CT Interpretation Workflow with Model Context Protocol Servers
papers.summary: Decomposes natural-language CT questions into sequences of measurement, radiomics and segmentation tool calls exposed through Model Context Protocol servers, trained on a new 3D CT tool-use benchmark. It improved diagnostic accuracy by 41 percent over baselines with a 95 percent tool invocation success rate.

papers.name: HevaDx
papers.title: Bridging Perception and Reasoning: An Evidence-Based Agentic System for Diagnosis and Treatment Recommendations of Vascular Anomalies
papers.summary: HevaDx is an AI system designed to diagnose and recommend treatments for vascular anomalies, using a multi-agent architecture that separates visual perception from clinical reasoning. The system demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy (94.8%) and treatment recommendation accuracy (83.3%), showcasing its potential in providing reliable support for managing complex medical conditions.

papers.name: GPAS
papers.title: GPAS: an online AI system for rapid and accurate pathogen identification and LLM-based interpretation
papers.summary: GPAS is an AI system that integrates rapid pathogen identification with semantic interpretation using a large language model, aiming to reduce technical barriers in clinical diagnostics. It demonstrated accurate pathogen detection and provided clinically instructive interpretations of immune dysregulation effects on the respiratory microbiome.

papers.title: Agentic Trial Emulation to Learn Health System-specific Drug Effects At Scale
papers.summary: The paper introduces Biomni, an autonomous LLM agent that performs end-to-end trial emulation from electronic health records to support clinical decision-making. It demonstrates Biomni's ability to calibrate EHR-based estimates with RCT results using a Bayesian hierarchical model, significantly reducing discrepancies and improving the reliability of evidence translation.

papers.name: NutriOrion
papers.title: NutriOrion: A Hierarchical Multi-Agent Framework for Personalized Nutrition Intervention Grounded in Clinical Guidelines
papers.summary: NutriOrion is a hierarchical multi-agent framework designed for personalized nutrition intervention in patients with multiple chronic conditions. It decomposes complex nutritional planning into specialized tasks handled by isolated agents, ensuring clinical validity and interoperability, and outperforms existing models in reducing drug-food interactions and improving dietary recommendations.

papers.name: DeepRare
papers.title: An agentic system for rare disease diagnosis with traceable reasoning
papers.summary: DeepRare is a multi-agent LLM system that uses over 40 tools and knowledge sources to rank rare disease diagnoses from phenotypes, free text and genetic results with linked evidence. Across nine datasets it reached 57.18% average Recall@1 on HPO tasks, beat Exomiser on multimodal cases, and experts agreed with most of its reasoning.

papers.name: OpenManus and Manus
papers.title: Benchmarking large language model-based agent systems for clinical decision tasks
papers.summary: The study evaluates two AI agent systems, OpenManus and Manus, for clinical decision tasks using various benchmark datasets. The results show modest performance gains with high computational costs and significant hallucination rates despite advanced tool integration.

papers.name: DAS
papers.title: Beyond Benchmarks: Dynamic, Automatic And Systematic Red-Teaming Agents For Trustworthy Medical Language Models
papers.summary: The DAS red-teaming framework autonomously tests large language models in clinical settings for safety and reliability across various axes, revealing significant discrepancies between static benchmark performance and real-world robustness. This dynamic stress-testing approach highlights the need for continuous evaluation to ensure trustworthy medical AI deployment.

papers.name: KG-Orchestra
papers.title: KG-Orchestra: An Open-Source Multi-Agent Framework for Evidence-Based Biomedical Knowledge Graphs Enrichment
papers.summary: KG-Orchestra is an open-source multi-agent framework that enriches seed biomedical knowledge graphs by autonomously acquiring, validating, and integrating evidence to create specialized, directional BKGs. The system was evaluated in two contexts, demonstrating superior reasoning performance with Qwen 3 variants and enhanced evidence relevance through hybrid retrieval strategies.

papers.name: DAVP
papers.title: Deep Agentic Variant Prioritisation for Expert Level Genetic Diagnosis
papers.summary: DAVP is a hierarchical agentic LLM pipeline that pre-filters genes, writes knowledge-graph-grounded variant reports and runs iterative LLM tournaments to rank variants for rare disease patients. On 709 cases it reached 85.5% top-3 recall, and on a new Turkish cohort it placed the causal variant in the top 3 for 76.2% of patients versus 47.6% for Exomiser.

papers.title: Closing the Loop: A Custom Artificial Intelligence Agent to Improve Detection of Radiologist Follow-Up Recommendations
papers.venue: NEJM catalyst innovations in care delivery
papers.summary: The paper describes an AI agent designed to improve the detection of radiologist follow-up recommendations in electronic health records. The system uses a pretrained large language model to review clinical impressions, extract key details for follow-ups, and integrate these findings into patient outreach workflows, achieving high accuracy and significantly outperforming existing macro-based systems.

papers.title: Agent-based large language model system for extracting structured data from breast cancer synoptic reports: a dual-validation study
papers.summary: A modular pipeline of sequential specialized LLM agents extracts 229 structured fields from breast cancer synoptic pathology reports. Seven LLMs scored 93.8-99.0% on synthetic tests but recall fell to 61.8-87.7% on 90 real reports.

papers.name: MARL-Rad
papers.title: Multi-Modal Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Radiology Report Generation
papers.summary: MARL-Rad is a multi-modal multi-agent reinforcement learning framework designed for generating radiology reports, which optimizes agents within the context of chest X-ray interpretation. The system demonstrates improved clinical efficacy and report accuracy compared to existing methods, as validated by both automated metrics and clinician evaluations.

papers.title: Representation Before Retrieval: Structured Patient Artifacts Reduce Hallucination in Clinical AI Systems
papers.summary: The paper presents a system that compiles patient data into structured artifacts to reduce hallucination in clinical AI systems. It shows that retrieval-augmented generation increases hallucination rates, while structured representation with explicit provenance tracking significantly reduces unsupported claims and improves factual accuracy.

papers.name: LiveMat
papers.title: Reconstructing living materials as a computable design space with multi-agent reasoning
papers.summary: Agents decompose constraints, extract provenance-aware records from literature and check consistency to build a knowledge graph of 34,215 living material records linking cells, matrices, functions and test conditions. In a prospective wound-healing task it prioritized a four-component design with strong in vivo performance.

papers.name: Resp-Agent
papers.title: Resp-Agent: An Agent-Based System for Multimodal Respiratory Sound Generation and Disease Diagnosis
papers.venue: The Fourteenth International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR 2026)
papers.summary: Resp-Agent is an autonomous system designed to generate multimodal respiratory sounds and diagnose diseases by addressing inherent information loss and data scarcity issues. It demonstrates improved diagnostic robustness under challenging conditions through extensive experiments.

papers.name: MAC-AMP
papers.title: MAC-AMP: A Closed-Loop Multi-Agent Collaboration System for Multi-Objective Antimicrobial Peptide Design
papers.summary: MAC-AMP is a multi-agent system designed for the creation of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) that balances multiple objectives such as activity, toxicity, and novelty. The system uses an adaptive reinforcement learning framework to generate AMPs with optimized properties, demonstrating superior performance compared to existing models in terms of antibacterial activity, likelihood of being an AMP, compliance with toxicity standards, and structural reliability.

papers.title: Process-Supervised Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Reliable Clinical Reasoning
papers.summary: This work trains a hierarchical multi-agent system with process-level rewards for gene-disease validity curation, where a supervisor agent calls other agents as tools. On ClinGen data, outcome-only rewards raised accuracy to 0.732 but gave poor process alignment, while adding process rewards improved adherence to valid curation pathways.

papers.title: A Multi-Agent Framework for Medical AI: Leveraging Fine-Tuned GPT, LLaMA, and DeepSeek R1 for Evidence-Based and Bias-Aware Clinical Query Processing
papers.summary: Three fine-tuned LLM families are combined in a pipeline where a reasoning agent explains, a retrieval agent grounds answers in PubMed and a refinement agent improves them, with uncertainty and bias checks. DeepSeek R1 scored best on MedQuAD-derived data and clearly beat BioGPT zero-shot.

papers.name: MAC
papers.title: Do Mixed-Vendor Multi-Agent LLMs Improve Clinical Diagnosis?
papers.summary: The Mixed-Vendor Multi-Agent Conversation (MAC) framework uses agents from different vendors to improve clinical diagnosis, showing better recall and accuracy compared to single-vendor systems. The study reveals that mixed-vendor teams can pool complementary biases to identify diagnoses missed by individual models or homogeneous teams.

papers.name: NeuroWeaver
papers.title: NeuroWeaver: An Autonomous Evolutionary Agent for Exploring the Programmatic Space of EEG Analysis Pipelines
papers.summary: NeuroWeaver is an autonomous evolutionary agent designed to explore and optimize EEG analysis pipelines, incorporating neurophysiological knowledge. It demonstrated superior performance compared to existing methods on various benchmarks, achieving high accuracy with significantly fewer parameters.

papers.name: Vital Trace
papers.title: Vital Trace: Protocol-Constrained Patient-State Reasoning for Longitudinal Clinical Trajectories
papers.summary: Vital Trace is a multi-agent framework designed for clinical reasoning in intensive care units, using a compact patient-state memory and protocol-constrained agents to predict future medical interventions. The system demonstrates improved temporal consistency and predictive performance compared to free-form agent systems.

papers.name: LATCH
papers.title: An LLM-assisted framework for accelerated and verifiable clinical hypothesis testing from electronic health records
papers.summary: LATCH is an LLM-assisted framework that converts natural language clinical hypotheses into structured EHR data analyses, automating cohort construction and statistical analysis. It demonstrated the ability to reproduce findings from published studies efficiently while also enabling new insights through hypothesis modifications.

papers.name: EC2Seq2Sql
papers.title: EC2Seq2Sql: Patient-trial matching with LLM agents
papers.summary: EC2Seq2Sql is a two-stage framework that converts clinical trial eligibility criteria written in natural language into executable SQL queries for patient screening from electronic health records. The system demonstrated high accuracy in generating valid and coherent SQL statements, achieving an exact match accuracy of 0.84 and execution accuracy of 0.91 after normalization.

papers.name: CellMaster
papers.title: CellMaster: Collaborative Cell Type Annotation in Single-Cell Analysis
papers.summary: CellMaster is an AI agent designed to annotate cell types in single-cell RNA sequencing data by leveraging large language models for on-the-fly annotation. It demonstrated significant improvements over existing tools, particularly in identifying rare and novel cell states.

papers.name: scChat
papers.title: scChat: A Large Language Model-Powered Co-Pilot for Contextualized Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Analysis
papers.venue: AIChE journal. American Institute of Chemical Engineers
papers.summary: scChat is a large language model-powered co-pilot designed to enhance the analysis of single-cell RNA sequencing data by integrating research context and supporting hypothesis validation, mechanistic interpretation, and experimental design. The system demonstrates high accuracy in cell type annotation while providing biologically relevant explanations and insights.

papers.name: MedScope
papers.title: MedScope: Incentivizing "Think with Videos" for Clinical Reasoning via Coarse-to-Fine Tool Calling
papers.summary: A video reasoning model interleaves reasoning with coarse-to-fine tool calls that retrieve and verify temporally localized evidence in long surgical and clinical videos, trained with a grounding-aware GRPO variant on a new video suite. It reached state-of-the-art results on in-domain and out-of-domain clinical video benchmarks.

papers.name: BioGuider
papers.title: A multi-agent platform for assessment and improvement of bioinformatics software documentation
papers.summary: BioGuider is a multi-agent platform that evaluates and improves the documentation quality of bioinformatics software, treating documentation as a testable object. It demonstrates robust error detection and correction capabilities and shows a positive correlation between better documentation quality and higher citation frequency among widely used tools.

papers.title: Beyond SMILES: Evaluating Agentic Systems for Drug Discovery
papers.summary: The paper evaluates six agentic systems for drug discovery across 15 task classes, identifying capability gaps such as lack of support for protein language models and peptide-specific predictions. It suggests that the limitations are architectural rather than due to knowledge deficits.

papers.name: DRL
papers.title: Closing Reasoning Gaps in Clinical Agents with Differential Reasoning Learning
papers.summary: The paper introduces Differential Reasoning Learning (DRL), a framework that enhances clinical decision support agents by learning from reasoning discrepancies. DRL uses reference rationales and agent-generated chain-of-thought to improve the reliability of clinical decision-making, as demonstrated through evaluations on medical QA benchmarks and internal clinical data.

papers.name: LingxiDiagBench
papers.title: LingxiDiagBench: A Multi-Agent Framework for Benchmarking LLMs in Chinese Psychiatric Consultation and Diagnosis
papers.summary: LingxiDiagBench is a multi-agent framework that evaluates large language models in Chinese psychiatric consultation and diagnosis, using a dataset of synthetic dialogues. It highlights the limitations of current LLMs in handling complex mental health diagnoses and dynamic consultations.

papers.title: Large Language Model Agent for Modular Task Execution in Drug Discovery
papers.venue: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: The paper introduces a modular framework using large language models (LLMs) to automate tasks in early-stage drug discovery, including data retrieval and molecular generation. The system demonstrated improved accuracy in answering biomedical questions and successfully guided iterative molecular refinement, increasing the number of molecules meeting drug-likeness criteria.

papers.name: ToxMCP
papers.title: ToxMCP: Guardrailed, Auditable Agentic Workflows for Computational Toxicology via the Model Context Protocol
papers.summary: ToxMCP is a set of Model Context Protocol servers that wrap toxicology tools such as CompTox, ADMETlab, AOP services, the QSAR Toolbox and PBPK simulation as typed, auditable tools for LLM agents. The authors show natural-language risk questions compiled into tool calls and outline a protocol for evaluating reproducibility and utility.

papers.name: FHIR-AgentEval
papers.title: FHIR-AgentEval: A Modular Sandbox for Benchmarking Clinical LLM Agents with an Evaluation of Memory-Augmented Configurations
papers.summary: FHIR-AgentEval is a modular evaluation sandbox designed to assess the performance of large language model agents in handling clinical tasks using HL7 FHIR standards. The system demonstrates that memory augmentation significantly improves task success rates and reduces strategic errors, suggesting potential for more reliable clinical applications.

papers.name: CoMMa
papers.title: CoMMa: Contribution-Aware Medical Multi-Agents for Decentralized Oncology Decision Support
papers.summary: Fine-tuned specialist agents each see only their partition of clinical data, and their outputs are combined by a deterministic embedding projection that estimates each agent's marginal contribution. It performed well on tumor board datasets from North American and East Asian hospitals and on public oncology benchmarks.

papers.name: Polaris
papers.title: Perfecting Human-AI Interaction at Clinical Scale. Turning Production Signals into Safer, More Human Conversations
papers.summary: Describes how signals from over 115 million live patient calls and clinician testing are used to train and evaluate an orchestrated patient-facing voice agent system with independent safety checks. Deployed over 10 million calls, it reported a 99.9 percent clinical safety score and halved speech recognition errors.

papers.name: SynthAgent
papers.title: SynthAgent: A Multi-Agent LLM Framework for Realistic Patient Simulation -- A Case Study in Obesity with Mental Health Comorbidities
papers.summary: SynthAgent is a multi-agent system that simulates high-fidelity patient scenarios for complex diseases like obesity with mental health comorbidities. The study shows that GPT-5 and Claude 4.5 Sonnet outperform other models in generating realistic patient simulations, highlighting the potential of SynthAgent for clinical decision support and knowledge discovery.

papers.title: Agentic memory-augmented retrieval and evidence grounding for medical question-answering tasks
papers.summary: The system integrates document retrieval, reranking, and evidence grounding to support multi-step medical reasoning, outperforming standalone language models on several medical question-answering benchmarks. It demonstrates the effectiveness of combining tool-augmented and evidence-grounded strategies for reliable and scalable AI in clinical decision support.

papers.name: PBio-Agent
papers.title: Progressive Multi-Agent Reasoning for Biological Perturbation Prediction
papers.summary: PBio-Agent is a multi-agent framework designed to predict gene regulation responses under complex chemical perturbations in bulk-cell environments, addressing the limitations of existing models. It integrates specialized agents with biological knowledge graphs and iterative refinement processes, outperforming baselines on LINCSQA and PerturbQA benchmarks.

papers.name: BOLE
papers.title: BOLE: A Knowledge-Enhanced Multi-Agent Framework for Intelligent Genomic Breeding
papers.summary: BOLE is a multi-agent AI framework designed to enhance genomic breeding analysis by integrating heterogeneous bioinformatics tools into coherent workflows. It demonstrated the ability to autonomously generate and execute complex analytical workflows, supporting tasks such as genome-wide association studies and heritability estimation, while ensuring reproducibility through artifact-level provenance.

papers.name: MedAgentBrief
papers.title: MedAgentBrief for Hospital Course Summarization: Safety, Use, and Discharge Documentation Burden
papers.summary: MedAgentBrief is an AI system that generates hospital course summaries using a large language model, aiming to reduce clinician documentation burden. The study found that the system was frequently used by physicians with minimal risk of harm and significantly reduced physician burnout.

papers.name: EpiCausalX Agent
papers.title: An AI Agent for Automated Causal Inference in Epidemiology
papers.summary: The EpiCausalX Agent is an AI-powered tool designed to automate causal inference in epidemiology, integrating literature retrieval and causal reasoning. It demonstrated efficient automation of the end-to-end workflow, producing evidence-based conclusions with interactive visualizations accessible via a user-friendly interface.

papers.title: Drug Safety Agents Using Graphs and Ontologies
papers.summary: The system uses a knowledge-grounded framework to analyze drug safety cases, integrating disproportionality analysis and a novel execution planner that minimizes hallucination risk. It demonstrates how combining structured medical knowledge with statistical evidence can support reliable and explainable case assessments.

papers.name: LABBench2
papers.title: LABBench2: An Improved Benchmark for AI Systems Performing Biology Research
papers.summary: LABBench2 is a roughly 1,900-task successor to LAB-Bench measuring what AI systems can do on realistic biology research tasks. Frontier models improved over LAB-Bench but scored 26-46% lower on the harder tasks, leaving a clear gap.

papers.name: MedSAM-Agent
papers.title: MedSAM-Agent: Empowering Interactive Medical Image Segmentation with Multi-turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: MedSAM-Agent is a framework that uses multi-turn agentic reinforcement learning to enhance interactive medical image segmentation, enabling more efficient and accurate decision-making. The system demonstrates state-of-the-art performance across various medical imaging modalities by integrating expert-curated trajectory generation and end-to-end outcome verification.

papers.name: S1-NexusAgent
papers.title: S1-NexusAgent: a Self-Evolving Agent Framework for Multidisciplinary Scientific Research
papers.summary: S1-NexusAgent is a self-evolving agent framework designed for multidisciplinary scientific research, capable of handling complex workflows and large-scale data through hierarchical planning and execution. It demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on authoritative scientific benchmarks involving long-horizon planning and tool orchestration.

papers.title: An AI-Native Biofoundry for Autonomous Enzyme Engineering: Integrating Active Learning with Automated Experimentation
papers.summary: The AI-Native Biofoundry integrates large language models and active learning to autonomously engineer enzymes, bridging the gap between computational design and physical experimentation. In a proof-of-concept study, it successfully evolved a DNA polymerase for improved sequencing accuracy with non-natural nucleotides.

papers.name: RE-MCDF
papers.title: RE-MCDF: Closed-Loop Multi-Expert LLM Reasoning for Knowledge-Grounded Clinical Diagnosis
papers.summary: RE-MCDF is a multi-expert framework designed to enhance clinical diagnosis by integrating logical constraints and medical knowledge. It demonstrates superior performance in complex diagnostic scenarios compared to existing single-agent systems, highlighting the benefits of structured multi-agent reasoning.

papers.title: How do dialysis nurses and AI reason clinically? A scenario-based comparative study
papers.summary: Has 110 dialysis nurses, ChatGPT-4 and the agent-based MAI-DxO system answer four validated hemodialysis scenarios, scored by nephrology nursing experts. The agent system scored highest, especially on structured justification and differential diagnosis, while nurses contributed contextual judgement.

papers.name: SEISMO
papers.title: SEISMO: Explanation-Aware, Trajectory-Conditioned LLM Agents for Sample-Efficient Molecular Optimisation
papers.summary: Conditions each molecular proposal on the task description, the full optimization trajectory and explainability-derived feedback about oracle scores. Across drug-discovery-relevant tasks it was more sample-efficient than existing optimizers and zero-shot LLM generation, and chemists can steer it in natural language.

papers.name: MedTextWeaver
papers.title: MedTextWeaver: Procedural Knowledge Evolution in Agentic Medical Text Editing
papers.summary: Turns sparse expert evaluations into global quality principles and procedural knowledge that guide an LLM agent editing medical texts, without training. Across three clinical text datasets and a real-world test it outperformed LLM baselines and memory-based adaptation methods.

papers.name: VenusRAR
papers.title: Rank-and-Reason: Multi-Agent Collaboration Accelerates Zero-Shot Protein Mutation Prediction
papers.summary: VenusRAR is a two-stage agentic framework that uses multi-agent collaboration to predict protein mutations, improving the efficiency and accuracy of wet-lab validation. The system demonstrated significant improvements in predicting mutation fitness and identified novel mutants with enhanced activity through rigorous evaluation.

papers.name: PABLO
papers.title: Purely Agent-Driven Black-Box Optimization for Biological Design
papers.summary: PABLO is a hierarchical agentic system that uses large language models pretrained on chemistry and biology literature to iteratively refine biological candidates for tasks like molecular design and antimicrobial peptide optimization. It demonstrated state-of-the-art performance in sample efficiency and final objective values, with optimized peptides showing strong activity against drug-resistant pathogens.

papers.name: BioAgent Bench
papers.title: BioAgent Bench: An AI Agent Evaluation Suite for Bioinformatics
papers.summary: BioAgent Bench is an evaluation suite for AI agents in bioinformatics tasks, featuring curated end-to-end tasks and automated assessment. The system reveals that while advanced LLMs can reliably complete complex pipelines, they exhibit vulnerabilities under controlled perturbations.

papers.name: AgentScore
papers.title: Automatic Construction of Clinical Scoring Systems with LLM Agents
papers.summary: LLMs propose candidate binary rules for unit-weighted clinical checklists while a deterministic, data-based loop verifies and selects them under deployability constraints. Across eight prediction tasks it beat existing score-generation methods and on two externally validated tasks exceeded established guideline scores.

papers.name: Planner-Auditor Twin
papers.title: Planner-Auditor Twin: Agentic Discharge Planning with FHIR-Based LLM Planning, Guideline Recall, Optional Caching and Self-Improvement
papers.summary: An LLM planner writes FHIR-based discharge plans with confidence estimates, a rule-based auditor checks coverage and calibration, and failed cases are regenerated or buffered for replay. On MIMIC-IV-on-FHIR the self-improvement loop raised task coverage from 32 to 86 percent and improved calibration.

papers.title: Scaling Medical Reasoning Verification via Tool-Integrated Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Trains medical reasoning verifiers that query external medical corpora repeatedly while judging a reasoning trace, using iterative reinforcement learning with an adaptive curriculum. Across four benchmarks it raised MedQA accuracy by 23.5 percent relative to the base generator with an eightfold smaller sampling budget.

papers.title: An Implantable Device that Converses with Patients and Learns to Co-Manage Epilepsy
papers.summary: An implantable epilepsy platform feeds EEG-derived biomarkers to an LLM agent that converses with patients through a phone app, logs their reports and retrains its detectors. In 13 inpatients, seizure detection precision improved over days without expert programming and patients rated the system usable.

papers.name: PaperSearchQA
papers.title: PaperSearchQA: Learning to Search and Reason over Scientific Papers with RLVR
papers.summary: The authors release a 16-million-abstract biomedical search corpus and a 60k-question factoid dataset, then train search agents with verifiable rewards to reason and retrieve over it. The trained agents beat non-reinforcement retrieval baselines and showed planning and self-verification behavior.

papers.title: Comparative Performance of agentic AI and Physicians in Taking Clinical History across Leading Large Language Models (LLMs)
papers.summary: The paper describes an agentic framework that uses large language models to iteratively prompt patients for a comprehensive clinical history, generating EHR-ready summaries and differential diagnoses. The system was evaluated using case reports and simulated patient interactions, showing high accuracy in capturing relevant history elements and aligning with physician-recommended investigations.

papers.name: ChemCRAFT
papers.title: Agentic reinforcement learning empowers next-generation chemical language models for molecular design and synthesis
papers.summary: ChemCRAFT is a framework that uses agentic reinforcement learning to enable small language models to interact with an external chemical sandbox for precise information retrieval, enhancing their ability in molecular design and synthesis tasks. Evaluations show ChemCRAFT outperforms cloud-based large language models in various drug design aspects while being cost-effective and privacy-preserving.

papers.name: Q4Dx
papers.title: A benchmark for evaluating diagnostic questioning efficiency of LLMs in patient conversations
papers.summary: Q4Dx is a benchmark of synthetic patient cases at different levels of symptom disclosure in which LLM physician agents question simulated patient agents to reach a diagnosis. It measures how efficiently models choose diagnostic questions rather than only final accuracy.

papers.name: SAGE
papers.title: Automated stereotactic radiosurgery planning using a human-in-the-loop reasoning large language model agent
papers.summary: SAGE is an LLM-based planning agent designed for automated stereotactic radiosurgery treatment planning, demonstrating comparable dosimetry to human planners while reducing cochlear dose. It shows systematic reasoning behaviors such as constraint verification and trade-off deliberation when prompted.

papers.name: AgentsEval
papers.title: AgentsEval: Clinically Faithful Evaluation of Medical Imaging Reports via Multi-Agent Reasoning
papers.summary: AgentsEval is a multi-agent framework that evaluates the clinical correctness and reasoning fidelity of automatically generated medical imaging reports by emulating radiologists' collaborative diagnostic workflow. It demonstrates robust evaluation capabilities under various perturbations, ensuring clinically aligned and semantically faithful assessments.

papers.name: SycoEval-EM
papers.title: SycoEval-EM: Sycophancy Evaluation of Large Language Models in Simulated Clinical Encounters for Emergency Care
papers.summary: SycoEval-EM is a simulation framework that evaluates the robustness of large language models in clinical decision support scenarios, particularly under adversarial patient persuasion. The system revealed significant variability among LLMs in adhering to evidence-based guidelines and highlighted the need for multi-turn adversarial testing in AI evaluation.

papers.name: GastroTCM
papers.title: GastroTCM: a large language model assistant for gastroenterology in traditional Chinese medicine
papers.summary: GastroTCM is a specialized large language model assistant for TCM gastroenterology that addresses limitations of general LLMs by incorporating domain-specific knowledge and multi-turn dialogue optimization. It demonstrated superior performance in clinical accuracy and safety compared to baseline models, as validated through expert review.

papers.title: Bayesian Optimization for Biochemical Discovery with LLMs
papers.summary: The authors analyzed how LLMs help or hurt Bayesian optimization on molecular optimization and four-residue protein binding-motif design. They propose an agentic workflow combining chemical tools with statistical BO for molecules, and found reasoning LLMs useful for hypothesis generation in the protein task.

papers.name: SpAgents
papers.title: Early diagnosis of axial spondyloarthritis in primary care using multi-agent systems
papers.summary: SpAgents is a multi-agent system designed to assist primary care physicians in diagnosing axial spondyloarthritis early, integrating large language models and imaging analysis. The study shows that SpAgents significantly improves diagnostic accuracy and sensitivity compared to both junior rheumatologists and primary care providers.

papers.title: Making large language models reliable data science programming copilots for biomedical research
papers.summary: The paper evaluates the accuracy of large language models (LLMs) in generating biomedical data analysis code and finds a low overall accuracy, raising concerns about their reliability. The authors develop an AI agent that iteratively refines analysis plans before generating code, achieving higher accuracy and enabling users to complete over 80% of analysis code for three studies in a user study.

papers.name: DSGym
papers.title: DSGym: A Holistic Framework for Evaluating and Training Data Science Agents
papers.summary: DSGym is a framework for evaluating and training data science agents, addressing limitations of existing benchmarks by providing a standardized, modular architecture. It includes tasks from various domains including bioinformatics and molecular prediction, demonstrating the ability to rigorously measure agents' capabilities in realistic scientific contexts.

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Agentic Rubric Generation for Reliable Medical Response Evaluation
papers.summary: The system automatically generates evaluation rubrics for medical large language models by decomposing retrieved medical evidence into atomic facts and synthesizing them with user interaction constraints. It significantly outperforms baseline methods in evaluating the clinical intent alignment of responses on HealthBench and LLMEval-Med benchmarks, demonstrating its potential to improve patient safety.

papers.name: Medea
papers.title: Medea: An AI agent for therapeutic reasoning across biological contexts
papers.summary: Medea runs multi-step therapeutic analyses with biological tools, machine learning models and literature retrieval while verifying planning, execution and evidence synthesis so biological context is preserved. It was evaluated on 5,673 open-ended analyses covering cell-type-specific target nomination, synthetic lethality and related tasks.

papers.name: MARBLE
papers.title: MARBLE: Multi-Agent Reasoning for Bioinformatics Learning and Evolution
papers.summary: MARBLE is a multi-agent system designed to automate the iterative process of bioinformatics model improvement, including hypothesis formulation and architectural redesign. It demonstrated sustained performance improvements across various bioinformatics tasks while maintaining robust execution stability.

papers.name: AgentEHR
papers.title: AgentEHR: Advancing Autonomous Clinical Decision-Making via Retrospective Summarization
papers.summary: AgentEHR is a benchmark and framework designed to enable autonomous navigation of Electronic Health Records (EHRs) for complex clinical decision-making tasks. It introduces RetroSum, which enhances the performance of agents by preventing information loss through retrospective summarization and maintaining logical coherence in high-noise environments.

papers.name: APOLO
papers.title: Towards Efficient and Robust Linguistic Emotion Diagnosis for Mental Health via Multi-Agent Instruction Refinement
papers.summary: Treats prompt refinement as a partially observable decision process in which planner, teacher, critic, student and target agents iteratively improve instructions for recognizing depression, anxiety and trauma states in text. It improved diagnostic accuracy and robustness across domain-specific and stratified benchmarks.

papers.name: OncoPainBot
papers.title: LLM-driven collaborative framework for knowledge-enhanced cancer pain assessment and management
papers.summary: OncoPainBot uses pain extraction, mechanism reasoning, treatment planning and safety check agents to assess and manage cancer pain. Comparing seven LLMs and three retrieval strategies on 516 real records, Claude-4 with retrieval performed best, and clinicians validated its outputs.

papers.title: Improving the Safety and Trustworthiness of Medical AI via Multi-Agent Evaluation Loops
papers.summary: Two generator models answer clinical queries while two evaluator agents score them against AMA ethics principles and a five-tier safety protocol, looping until responses pass. Over 900 queries the loop cut ethical violations by 89 percent and downgraded risk in 92 percent of cases.

papers.name: PAIR-SAFE
papers.title: PAIR-SAFE: A Paired-Agent Approach for Runtime Auditing and Refining AI-Mediated Mental Health Support
papers.summary: PAIR-SAFE is a paired-agent system designed to audit and refine AI-generated mental health support responses, ensuring they are clinically aligned. The system demonstrates significant improvements in key clinical dimensions of mental health interactions when guided by a supervisory Judge agent.

papers.name: MedConsultBench
papers.title: MedConsultBench: A Full-Cycle, Fine-Grained, Process-Aware Benchmark for Medical Consultation Agents
papers.summary: MedConsultBench is a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating medical consultation agents that covers the entire clinical workflow from history taking to follow-up. It introduces fine-grained metrics and Atomic Information Units to assess information gathering efficiency, diagnostic accuracy, and medication safety, revealing significant gaps between theoretical knowledge and practical application in large language models.

papers.name: ChatInvent
papers.title: Democratising real-world drug discovery through agentic AI
papers.summary: ChatInvent is an agentic AI system developed by AstraZeneca to assist in molecular design and synthesis planning within their drug discovery pipeline. The paper highlights the evolution of ChatInvent from a single-agent proof-of-concept into a multi-agent architecture with a graphical user interface, emphasizing its integration challenges and future potential.

papers.name: ClinAgent
papers.title: ClinAgent: A Five-Layer Architecture for Autonomous Clinical Trial Statistical Programming
papers.summary: ClinAgent is a five-layer architecture that augments any AI coding agent with clinical trial statistical programming capabilities, enabling them to handle SAS datasets and ADaM specifications. The system was validated using artifacts from a real Phase 2 cardiovascular study, demonstrating high accuracy in log analysis and data validation.

papers.name: AutoBinder Agent
papers.title: AutoBinder Agent: An MCP-Based Agent for End-to-End Protein Binder Design
papers.summary: AutoBinder Agent is an agentic framework for end-to-end protein binder design that integrates multiple AI and bioinformatics tools under the coordination of a Large Language Model (LLM) using the Model Context Protocol (MCP). It demonstrated improved reproducibility, reduced manual overhead, and enhanced extensibility in drug design processes.

papers.name: GenomAgent
papers.title: From Single to Multi-Agent Reasoning: Advancing GeneGPT for Genomics QA
papers.summary: GenomAgent is a multi-agent system designed to enhance genomic question answering by coordinating specialized agents for complex queries, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art GeneGPT. It demonstrates improved performance and flexibility across various scientific domains requiring expert knowledge extraction.

papers.name: M^4olGen
papers.title: M^4olGen: Multi-Agent, Multi-Stage Molecular Generation under Precise Multi-Property Constraints
papers.summary: M^4olGen is a multi-stage molecular generation framework that uses a retrieval-augmented, fragment-level approach to generate molecules with precise numeric constraints over multiple physicochemical properties. The system demonstrates superior performance in generating valid and target-constrained molecules compared to existing large language models and graph-based algorithms.

papers.name: ART
papers.title: ART: Action-based Reasoning Task Benchmarking for Medical AI Agents
papers.summary: ART is a benchmark designed to evaluate medical AI agents' performance on complex, multi-step reasoning tasks derived from real electronic health records. It highlights significant gaps in current models' abilities to handle aggregation and conditional logic, indicating the need for improved clinical decision support systems.

papers.name: KT-LLM
papers.title: KT-LLM: an evidence-grounded and sequence text framework for auditable kidney transplant modeling
papers.summary: KT-LLM is a multi-agent system designed to bridge the gap between structured clinical data and text-based rules in kidney transplantation, ensuring decisions are evidence-grounded and auditable. The system demonstrated superior performance in predictive calibration and evidence attribution compared to baselines, while also enabling equitable subgroup analysis among Black recipients.

papers.name: ECR-Agent
papers.title: MedEinst: Benchmarking the Einstellung Effect in Medical LLMs through Counterfactual Differential Diagnosis
papers.summary: ECR-Agent is designed to mitigate the Einstellung Effect in medical LLMs by ensuring evidence-based reasoning through structured causal inference and iterative knowledge refinement. The system demonstrates improved diagnostic accuracy in atypical cases compared to existing models, as evaluated using MedEinst benchmark.

papers.title: An autonomous agentic workflow for clinical detection of cognitive concerns using large language models
papers.summary: The paper presents an autonomous agentic workflow using large language models to detect cognitive concerns from clinical notes, demonstrating its effectiveness in early detection of cognitive impairment. The system showed comparable performance to expert-driven methods and maintained interpretability while offering scalable decision support.

papers.title: Tumor Board-Inspired Multiagent Artificial Intelligence System for Interpreting Oncology Guidelines
papers.summary: A tumor board-style multi-agent system uses a coordinator to choose among 34 ASCO guidelines, specialist agents to extract text, table and figure content, and a reviewer to compose answers. It selected the right guideline 94% of the time and answered 90% of 100 questions correctly, well above single LLMs.

papers.name: EvoMDT
papers.title: EvoMDT: a self-evolving multi-agent system for structured clinical decision-making in multi-cancer
papers.summary: EvoMDT is a self-evolving multi-agent system designed to support structured clinical decision-making in multidisciplinary tumor boards for various cancers. It demonstrated improved guideline adherence and semantic alignment with expert plans, outperforming large language model baselines while maintaining interpretability and traceability.

papers.name: PFUA
papers.title: Interleaved Tool-Call Reasoning for Protein Function Understanding
papers.summary: PFUA is a tool-augmented agent for protein function understanding that decomposes questions, calls biological tools for verifiable intermediate evidence and then answers. Across four benchmarks it outperformed text-only reasoning models, which the authors show mostly amplify keyword patterns.

papers.name: RadDiff
papers.title: RadDiff: Describing Differences in Radiology Image Sets with Natural Language
papers.summary: RadDiff is a multimodal agentic system designed to describe differences between radiology image sets, aiding in clinical insights and AI interpretation. It uses an innovative framework that includes medical knowledge injection, multimodal reasoning, iterative hypothesis refinement, and targeted visual search, achieving significant accuracy on the RadDiffBench benchmark.

papers.title: Vibe Coding Omics Data Analysis Applications
papers.summary: The paper introduces 'vibe coding', an iterative process where AI agents generate executable code in real-time based on natural language prompts, significantly reducing the time and cost of developing custom data analysis platforms. It demonstrates this approach by creating a proteomics data analysis platform capable of performing standard tasks like normalization and differential expression testing within minutes.

papers.title: Can AI Conduct Autonomous Scientific Research? Case Studies on Two Real-World Tasks
papers.summary: The paper evaluates eight AI frameworks on their ability to autonomously conduct scientific research tasks, finding that while the systems can handle conceptual planning and summarization well, they struggle with robust implementation and produce hallucinations. The study highlights the need for human supervision in deploying these AI tools effectively.

papers.name: MedDialogRubrics
papers.title: MedDialogRubrics: A Comprehensive Benchmark and Evaluation Framework for Multi-turn Medical Consultations in Large Language Models
papers.summary: A multi-agent system synthesizes 5,200 patient cases, a fact-limited patient agent with hallucination correction plays them in dialogue, and expert-refined guideline-based rubrics score the doctor model's questioning. Current LLMs showed substantial gaps in information gathering and diagnosis.

papers.title: Hierarchical agent reflection for aligning LLM reasoning with clinical diagnostic processes
papers.summary: The paper introduces a hierarchical agent reflection mechanism to train large language models for medical diagnosis, ensuring the model's reasoning aligns with human clinical practice. The method improves diagnostic transparency and interpretability by generating detailed clinical notes that capture clinicians' step-by-step reasoning processes.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence based resuscitation simulation: a pilot study of a novel approach to team leadership training
papers.summary: Four Claude 3.5 Sonnet agents played ACLS team members following AHA guidelines while an emergency physician led simulated resuscitations for team leadership training. Three blinded emergency specialists rated ten scenario transcripts for completion of recommended steps.

papers.title: Toward Auditable Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning in Pathology: SQL as an Explicit Trace of Evidence
papers.summary: Feature reasoning agents write and execute SQL over tables of interpretable cellular features, and a knowledge comparison agent checks the resulting measurements against pathology knowledge. On two pathology visual question answering datasets this produced executable evidence traces linking measurements to diagnoses.

papers.name: HeurekaBench
papers.title: HeurekaBench: A Benchmarking Framework for AI Co-scientist
papers.summary: HeurekaBench is a benchmarking framework designed to evaluate AI systems acting as co-scientists in biology, focusing on single-cell analysis. It demonstrates the effectiveness of adding critic modules to improve the performance of open-source LLM-based agents.

papers.name: BioTrouble
papers.title: BioTrouble: A Multi-Agent Workflow for Troubleshooting Molecular Biology Techniques
papers.summary: BioTrouble is a multi-agent workflow that uses a troubleshooting knowledge base, small language models and cost-aware model routing to help fix failed PCR, qPCR, cloning and other experiments. Its recommendations were comparable to those of a single state-of-the-art LLM, and user feedback is stored to grow the knowledge base.

papers.name: ggplotAgent
papers.title: ggplotAgent: a self-debugging multi-modal agent for robust and reproducible scientific visualization
papers.summary: Generates ggplot2 code from natural language, fixes execution errors in a loop, and uses a vision-enabled agent to check the rendered figure's appearance for bioinformatics visualization. Against DeepSeek-V3 it raised code executability from 85 to 100 percent and scored higher on publication readiness.

papers.name: MedAgentBench v2
papers.title: MedAgentBench v2: Improving Medical LLM Agent Design
papers.venue: Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing. Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing
papers.summary: MedAgentBench v2 evaluates medical LLM agents on clinical tasks using a FHIR-compliant EHR, introducing improvements such as memory components and enhanced system prompts. The agent demonstrated high success rates with these enhancements, showing adaptability to new tasks without explicit training data.

papers.title: LLM Agent Based Protein Function Prediction
papers.venue: Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing. Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing
papers.summary: An LLM agent refines computational protein function predictions by querying ontology constraints, structured metadata and literature and documenting its evidence. It achieved the lowest Smin on all three Gene Ontology branches and the best Fmax for molecular function and cellular component.

papers.name: Auto-Care
papers.title: An AI-Driven Multimodal Smart Home Platform for Continuous Monitoring and Assistance in Post-Stroke Motor Impairment
papers.venue: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
papers.summary: A smart home platform for post-stroke rehabilitation fuses insole, eye-tracking and ambient sensor data, and an embedded LLM agent issues reminders, adjusts the environment and notifies caregivers. In 20 users, mean satisfaction rose from 3.9 in conventional homes to 8.4 with the full system.

papers.name: MedHopper
papers.title: MedHopper: an agentic RAG-LLM system for multi-hop biomedical QA
papers.venue: Database : the journal of biological databases and curation
papers.summary: MedHopper is a biomedical question-answering system that uses an agentic retrieval and language model pipeline to answer complex, multi-hop questions from a Wikipedia-derived corpus. It demonstrated improved performance on the MedHopQA task with exact match scoring, highlighting the effectiveness of its controlled state machine for routing queries and executing up to three hops of entity extraction.

papers.name: Alvessa
papers.title: An Evidence-Grounded Research Assistant for Functional Genomics and Drug Target Assessment
papers.summary: Alvessa is an evidence-grounded research assistant designed to integrate entity recognition, biological tool orchestration, and data-constrained answer generation with statement-level verification. It improves accuracy in answering functional genomics and drug target assessment questions compared to general-purpose language models while ensuring traceable outputs.

papers.name: MAMA-Memeia
papers.title: MAMA-Memeia! Multi-Aspect Multi-Agent Collaboration for Depressive Symptoms Identification in Memes
papers.summary: Agents discuss memes from several aspects grounded in Cognitive Analytic Therapy competencies to identify depressive symptoms, alongside a new dataset with human-annotated explanations. It improved macro-F1 by 7.55 percent over more than 30 compared methods.

papers.name: ClinDEF
papers.title: ClinDEF: A Dynamic Evaluation Framework for Large Language Models in Clinical Reasoning
papers.summary: Generates patient cases from a disease knowledge graph and runs multi-turn consultations between an LLM doctor and an automated patient agent, scoring accuracy, questioning efficiency and rubric-based quality. It exposed clinical reasoning gaps in current LLMs that static question answering hides.

papers.name: Queryome
papers.title: Queryome: Orchestrating Retrieval, Reasoning, and Synthesis across Biomedical Literature
papers.summary: Queryome is a system of specialized large language model agents designed to perform iterative, evidence-grounded synthesis across biomedical literature. It demonstrated superior performance on the MIRAGE benchmark and excelled in constructing review articles compared to other systems.

papers.name: Prompt-to-Pill
papers.title: Prompt-to-Pill: Multi-Agent Drug Discovery and Clinical Simulation Pipeline
papers.summary: Prompt-to-Pill is a multi-agent system that integrates various large language models to automate drug discovery and clinical trial simulation from target identification to virtual patient recruitment. The study demonstrates the pipeline's capability by applying it to Dipeptidyl Peptidase 4 (DPP4), showcasing its potential for operationalizing drug development workflows in silico.

papers.name: MolAct
papers.title: MolAct: An Agentic RL Framework for Molecular Editing and Property Optimization
papers.summary: Trains LLM agents with reinforcement learning to edit and optimize molecules over multiple turns, calling tools for validity, property and similarity checks and using their feedback. MolEditAgent-7B made nearly all requested edits validly, and MolOptAgent-7B beat the best closed reasoning model on LogP.

papers.name: HARMON-E
papers.title: HARMON-E: Hierarchical Agentic Reasoning for Multimodal Oncology Notes to Extract Structured Data
papers.summary: HARMON-E is a hierarchical agentic reasoning framework that uses large language models to extract structured clinical data from unstructured oncology notes. It demonstrated high accuracy in extracting over 100 oncology-specific variables, with critical variables achieving F1-scores above 0.95 on a dataset of 400,000 real-world clinical notes.

papers.title: An Agentic AI Framework for Training General Practitioner Student Skills
papers.summary: The paper presents an agentic AI framework for training general practitioner student skills, which includes evidence-based vignette generation, persona-driven patient dialogue, and standards-based assessment. The system was evaluated with medical students who reported realistic dialogues, appropriate difficulty levels, stable personality signals, useful feedback, and high usability.

papers.title: Autonomous Analysis of Curated Patient Data Using a Large Language Model-Based Multiagent Framework
papers.summary: The paper presents a multiagent AI framework for automating medical data analysis workflows, which outperforms nonagent-based approaches using large language models. The system successfully replicated primary outcomes from bone marrow transplantation studies with higher accuracy and fewer errors.

papers.name: AIPatient
papers.title: Simulated patient systems powered by large language model-based AI agents offer potential for transforming medical education
papers.summary: AIPatient is a simulated patient system powered by large language model-based AI agents and a knowledge graph, designed to enhance medical education through realistic clinical interactions. The study demonstrates AIPatient's high accuracy in electronic health record-based question answering, robustness, and positive user feedback from medical students.

papers.name: Moremi Bio Agent
papers.title: Moremi Bio Agent: Using Neisseria meningitidis Reference Data For The Double Blinded Validation of A General Purpose Biology-Trained Reasoning Model for Pathogen and Antigen Discovery
papers.summary: Moremi Bio Nano, an agentic reasoning LLM, was given only the heavy and light chain sequences of an anonymized monoclonal antibody and asked to hypothesize, rank and check its antigen and pathogen targets. Four of ten blinded runs completed and three of those identified the antigen confirmed by wet-lab data.

papers.name: SAGE
papers.title: Biosecurity-Aware AI: Agentic Risk Auditing of Soft Prompt Attacks on ESM-Based Variant Predictors
papers.summary: SAGE is an agentic auditing loop that injects soft prompt perturbations into genomic models such as ESM2, tracks behavior across checkpoints, computes risk metrics and writes narrative reports. It showed that variant effect prediction degrades measurably under targeted embedding-space attacks.

papers.name: MedEduChat
papers.title: Personalizing prostate cancer education for patients using an EHR-Integrated LLM agent
papers.summary: MedEduChat is an EHR-integrated LLM agent designed to provide personalized prostate cancer education for patients. The study demonstrated that MedEduChat significantly enhances patient health confidence and receives high usability scores, indicating its potential in improving patient engagement and educational outcomes.

papers.name: CliniKiosk
papers.title: CLINIKIOSK-An innovative technology to expand health care access
papers.summary: A router, planner, executor and manager architecture with speech input and retrieval from PubMed, trial registries and guideline sources delivers multilingual patient guidance in a kiosk. It is benchmarked on 500 clinician-verified simulated cases against GPT-4o, Claude 3 Opus, Mixtral and Gemma for accuracy, empathy and explainability.

papers.title: A self-correcting Agentic Graph RAG for clinical decision support in hepatology
papers.summary: Agents generate, validate and iteratively refine search strategies over a clinically verified hepatology knowledge graph in a retrieve-evaluate-refine loop before an LLM answers. On custom clinical questions it beat GPT-4, standard RAG and graph RAG on faithfulness, context recall and answer relevancy.

papers.title: AI-Orchestrated Active Learning for Insulin Delivery Material Discovery
papers.summary: The paper describes an AI-driven platform for discovering materials used in insulin delivery patches, which uses active learning and integrates literature mining, polymer SMILES generation, and molecular dynamics simulations. The system demonstrates the potential of large language models to orchestrate complex scientific workflows, accelerating material discovery in biomedical applications.

papers.title: Multi-Agent Medical Decision Consensus Matrix System: An Intelligent Collaborative Framework for Oncology MDT Consultations
papers.summary: The Multi-Agent Medical Decision Consensus Matrix System uses seven specialized large language model agents to simulate realistic multidisciplinary team workflows in oncology, improving clinical decision-making quality and efficiency. The system demonstrates substantial gains over existing approaches with high accuracy and consensus rates, as well as strong ratings from expert reviewers for clinical appropriateness.

papers.name: TxAgent
papers.title: MedAI: Evaluating TxAgent's Therapeutic Agentic Reasoning in the NeurIPS CURE-Bench Competition
papers.summary: TxAgent is an AI system designed to assist in therapeutic decision-making by iteratively retrieving and executing biomedical functions. It demonstrated improved performance in the NeurIPS CURE-Bench competition through enhanced tool-retrieval strategies, highlighting the importance of accurate reasoning and tool usage for clinical decision support.

papers.name: CP-Env
papers.title: CP-Env: Evaluating Large Language Models on Clinical Pathways in a Controllable Hospital Environment
papers.summary: CP-Env is a simulated hospital environment that evaluates large language models on complex clinical pathways, including patient care transitions and multidisciplinary team interactions. The system reveals that most models struggle with pathway complexity and exhibit issues like hallucinations and loss of diagnostic details.

papers.title: Development of an Agentic AI Model for NGS Downstream Analysis Targeting Researchers with Limited Biological Background
papers.summary: The Agentic AI Model for NGS Downstream Analysis automates the interpretation and analysis of Next-Generation Sequencing data, providing biological insights and advanced analytical recommendations.
