It demonstrated its utility by identifying significant differentially expressed genes in a cancer dataset and linking them to clinical outcomes through literature-based validation.

papers.name: INFORM-CT
papers.title: INFORM-CT: INtegrating LLMs and VLMs FOR Incidental Findings Management in Abdominal CT
papers.summary: INFORM-CT is a framework that integrates large language models and vision-language models to automate the detection, classification, and reporting of incidental findings in abdominal CT scans. The system demonstrates improved accuracy and efficiency compared to existing approaches.

papers.name: HopeAI
papers.title: AI for evidence-based treatment recommendation in oncology: a blinded evaluation of large language models and agentic workflows
papers.summary: HopeAI is an agentic workflow-based system designed to provide evidence-based treatment recommendations in oncology. The study showed that HopeAI outperformed other LLMs and RAG systems in terms of accuracy, relevance, and comprehensiveness for clinical scenarios related to multiple myeloma.

papers.name: MoMA
papers.title: MoMA: a mixture-of-multimodal-agents architecture for enhancing clinical prediction modelling
papers.summary: MoMA is a multi-agent architecture that uses specialized language model agents to convert non-textual medical data into structured text, which is then aggregated and used for clinical predictions. The system demonstrated superior performance in clinical prediction tasks compared to existing methods using private datasets.

papers.title: Multi-Agent Intelligence for Multidisciplinary Decision-Making in Gastrointestinal Oncology
papers.summary: A hierarchical team of agents mirrors a multidisciplinary tumor board, interpreting endoscopy, radiology and lab data separately before combining them. Expert raters scored it 4.60 of 5, above a single multimodal model, especially for reasoning logic and medical accuracy.

papers.name: MOSAIC
papers.title: An Agentic AI System for Multi-Framework Communication Coding
papers.summary: Plan, update, annotation and verification agents select codebooks, maintain retrieval databases, annotate transcripts with retrieval-guided prompting and check consistency. On 50 rheumatology and OB/GYN transcripts it reached an F1 of 0.928 against trained human coders.

papers.name: CASSIA
papers.title: CASSIA: a multi-agent large language model for automated and interpretable cell annotation
papers.summary: CASSIA is a multi-agent LLM system that annotates cell types in single-cell RNA-seq data with reasoning, quality scoring and confidence calibration. Across 970 cell types it improved annotation accuracy, including on complex and rare populations.

papers.name: SigSpace
papers.title: SigSpace: an LLM-based agent for drug response signature interpretation
papers.summary: An LLM agent system processes differential expression signatures from the Tahoe-100M drug perturbation atlas and writes short summaries of each drug response. Blinded summaries were matched to their drug or mechanism of action better than chance, with results depending on the LLM and signature score.

papers.name: gffutilsAI
papers.title: gffutilsAI: an AI-agent for interactive genomic feature exploration in GFF files
papers.summary: A command-line agent built on gffutils and the Strands agent framework turns natural-language questions into executable queries over GFF genome annotations, using local or cloud LLMs. It supports coordinate and attribute queries, GO searches, hierarchy traversal, summaries and export without coding.

papers.name: MS4MS
papers.title: MS4MS: LLMs-driven Multi-agent System for Small-molecule Identification via LC-MS/MS
papers.summary: MS4MS is a multi-agent LLM system that runs LC-MS/MS small-molecule identification from raw spectra to annotated compounds, aimed at complex mixtures such as traditional Chinese medicine. It achieved the best molecular formula prediction on a public benchmark and identified compounds and isomers in herbal extracts.

papers.name: CognAlign
papers.title: CognAlign: A Multi-Agent Cognitive-Alignment Framework for Transparent, Bias-Aware Medical Triage Using Small Language Models
papers.summary: CognAlign is a multi-agent system designed to enhance transparency and bias-awareness in medical triage using small language models. It demonstrated improved clinical accuracy, reduced errors by 24%, eliminated patient safety violations, and increased transparency compared to baseline systems.

papers.name: MCP-AI
papers.title: MCP-AI: Protocol-Driven Intelligence Framework for Autonomous Reasoning in Healthcare
papers.summary: MCP-AI is a protocol-driven framework for autonomous reasoning in healthcare that integrates Model Context Protocol (MCP) to enable secure, long-term state management and collaboration among AI agents. It was validated through clinical use cases involving Fragile X Syndrome with comorbid depression and remote coordination for Type 2 Diabetes and hypertension, demonstrating its capability to streamline clinical processes while ensuring regulatory compliance.

papers.name: GRASP
papers.title: GRASP: Graph Reasoning Agents for Systems Pharmacology with Human-in-the-Loop
papers.summary: GRASP is a multi-agent framework that uses graph reasoning to develop quantitative systems pharmacology models, making the process more accessible and rigorous for domain experts. It outperforms traditional methods in terms of biological plausibility, mathematical correctness, structural fidelity, and code quality when evaluated by human judges.

papers.name: MOA
papers.title: Multimodal Oncology Agent for IDH1 Mutation Prediction in Low-Grade Glioma
papers.summary: The Multimodal Oncology Agent predicts IDH1 mutation in low-grade glioma by combining a TITAN-based histology tool with reasoning over clinical and genomic inputs and searches of PubMed and OncoKB. On 488 TCGA-LGG patients it reached an F1 of 0.912 with histology fused in, above histology and clinical baselines.

papers.name: CureAgent
papers.title: CureAgent: A Training-Free Executor-Analyst Framework for Clinical Reasoning
papers.summary: CureAgent is a modular framework that uses specialized TxAgents for executing tasks and long-context foundation models for clinical reasoning, addressing the limitations of monolithic models. It demonstrates improved performance on CURE-Bench without requiring expensive end-to-end fine-tuning.

papers.name: ClinTutor-R1
papers.title: ClinTutor-R1: Advancing Scalable and Robust One-to-Many Alignment in Clinical Socratic Education
papers.summary: ClinTutor-R1 is a multi-agent system designed to facilitate one-to-many clinical education, addressing the challenge of balancing individual and collective learning. The system demonstrates improved performance over baseline models in maintaining instructional quality across diverse student groups through comprehensive evaluation methods.

papers.title: A multi-agent approach to neurological clinical reasoning
papers.summary: The paper introduces a multi-agent system designed to address the unique challenges of neurological clinical reasoning, demonstrating its effectiveness through comprehensive benchmarking against various large language models. The system significantly outperforms individual LLMs and retrieval-enhanced models on complex neurological questions, showcasing the potential for structured AI approaches in specialized medical domains.

papers.name: Radiologist Copilot
papers.title: Radiologist Copilot: An Agentic Framework Orchestrating Specialized Tools for Reliable Radiology Reporting
papers.summary: Radiologist Copilot is an AI system designed to assist radiologists in the complex task of creating accurate and standardized reports for medical images. It autonomously orchestrates various specialized tools to handle image localization, interpretation, template selection, report composition, and quality control, demonstrating superior performance compared to existing methods.

papers.name: UCAgents
papers.title: UCAgents: Unidirectional Convergence for Visual Evidence Anchored Multi-Agent Medical Decision-Making
papers.summary: Agents are barred from changing positions and interact only through targeted verification of visual evidence, with one inquiry round to expose image-text mismatch. On four medical VQA benchmarks it reached 71.3 percent on PathVQA, six points above prior work, with 87.7 percent fewer tokens.

papers.title: Many-to-One Adversarial Consensus: Exposing Multi-Agent Collusion Risks in AI-Based Healthcare
papers.summary: Sets up doctor agents advised by assistant agents, some of which collude adversarially, plus a verifier agent checking decisions against clinical guidelines. Collusion pushed harmful recommendation rates up to 100 percent, and the verifier restored full accuracy on 50 clinical questions.

papers.name: SelfAI
papers.title: SelfAI: A self-directed framework for long-horizon scientific discovery
papers.summary: SelfAI turns a research intent into executable experiments, reasons over accumulated experiment trajectories to pick the next move and stops unproductive branches under explicit efficiency-diversity trade-offs. On real tasks from machine learning to drug discovery it found good solutions with fewer redundant trials than classical optimization and other LLM baselines.

papers.title: Auditable Context-Aware HFMD Forecasting with Structured LLM Agents
papers.summary: The paper introduces a two-agent neuro-symbolic framework for forecasting HFMD cases, which integrates contextual information through an LLM-based Event Interpreter and generates probabilistic forecasts with a Forecast Generator. The system demonstrates competitive point accuracy and robust interval coverage while providing interpretable explanations of forecast changes.

papers.title: Swarms of Large Language Model Agents for Protein Sequence Design with Experimental Validation
papers.summary: The paper introduces a swarm intelligence framework using multiple large language model agents for de novo protein design, which iteratively proposes mutations to achieve tailored properties without fine-tuning or specialized training. The system's effectiveness is demonstrated through experimental validation on proteins with alpha helix and coil structures, showing efficient navigation of the protein fitness landscape.

papers.title: Byzantine Fault-Tolerant Multi-Agent System for Healthcare: A Gossip Protocol Approach to Secure Medical Message Propagation
papers.summary: The paper introduces a Byzantine fault-tolerant multi-agent system for healthcare that uses gossip protocols and cryptographic validation to ensure secure message propagation in adversarial environments. The system successfully maintains consensus accuracy even with up to 33% Byzantine nodes, demonstrating its capability to support collaborative medical decision-making securely.

papers.name: kai
papers.title: Notebook-based alignment of human and agentic reasoning in single-cell biology
papers.summary: kai is an agent that iteratively writes and runs single-cell analyses in computational notebooks so that human scientists can follow and critique its reasoning. Compared with one-shot generation it was more robust to code errors and sycophancy on cell type annotation problems.

papers.title: A Multi-Agent Approach to Generating Context-Rich Gene Sets
papers.summary: Open-source LLM agents read PubMed abstracts to confirm evidence for genes already in a gene set and to propose missing genes, producing context-specific sets. Applied to reconstructing Human Phenotype Ontology gene sets, it recovered and extended their membership from literature evidence.

papers.name: PathReasoning
papers.title: PathReasoning: A multimodal reasoning agent for query-based ROI navigation on whole-slide images
papers.summary: PathReasoning is a multimodal reasoning agent designed to navigate whole-slide images for cancer diagnosis and prognosis, focusing on tumor microenvironment analysis. It demonstrates superior performance in selecting relevant regions of interest compared to existing methods, enhancing the accuracy of diagnostic reports.

papers.name: MTBBench
papers.title: MTBBench: A Multimodal Sequential Clinical Decision-Making Benchmark in Oncology
papers.summary: MTBBench is a benchmark designed to evaluate the performance of multimodal large language models in simulating clinical decision-making processes within oncology, specifically focusing on Molecular Tumor Boards. The system highlights the limitations of current LLMs in handling complex, longitudinal, and multimodal data and demonstrates improvements through an agentic framework that enhances reasoning capabilities.

papers.name: Genie-CAT
papers.title: Beyond Protein Language Models: An Agentic LLM Framework for Mechanistic Enzyme Design
papers.summary: Genie-CAT is an AI system that integrates large language models with domain-specific tools to accelerate hypothesis generation in protein design, focusing on metalloproteins. It demonstrates the ability to autonomously identify residue-level modifications affecting redox properties, reproducing expert hypotheses more efficiently.

papers.name: MedSAM-3
papers.title: MedSAM3: Delving into Segment Anything with Medical Concepts
papers.summary: MedSAM-3 is a medical image segmentation model that fine-tunes the Segment Anything Model (SAM) on annotated medical images to enable precise anatomical structure segmentation via text prompts. The system demonstrates superior performance across various imaging modalities compared to existing models, showcasing its potential for biomedical discovery.

papers.name: BioSage
papers.title: Cross-Disciplinary Knowledge Retrieval and Synthesis: A Compound AI Architecture for Scientific Discovery
papers.summary: BioSage orchestrates retrieval agents with query planning, cross-disciplinary translation agents and reasoning agents over biomedical, biosecurity, AI and data science literature with citations. On LitQA2, GPQA, WMDP and HLE-Bio plus a new cross-modal benchmark it beat plain and retrieval-augmented baselines by 13-21%.

papers.name: LongevityLLM
papers.title: LongevityLLM: A Function-Driven AI Agent for End-to-End Protein and Aging Research
papers.summary: LongevityLLM is an AI agent designed to perform real, reproducible analyses in aging biology and structural bioinformatics by mapping natural language queries to deterministic bioinformatics pipelines. It demonstrated its capability to retrieve scientific information from databases and literature, integrate multiple epigenetic clocks, predict the impact of mutations on protein structure, and conduct phylogenetic analysis.

papers.name: KOM
papers.title: KOM: A Multi-Agent Artificial Intelligence System for Precision Management of Knee Osteoarthritis (KOA)
papers.summary: KOM is a multi-agent system that handles knee osteoarthritis evaluation, risk prediction and treatment prescription. It beat general LLMs on imaging analysis and prescription benchmarks, and a randomized simulation showed clinician-KOM collaboration reduced workload.

papers.name: OpenBioLLM
papers.title: Beyond GeneGPT: A Multi-Agent Architecture with Open-Source LLMs for Enhanced Genomic Question Answering
papers.summary: OpenBioLLM reproduces and extends GeneGPT with open-source models and separate agents for tool routing, query generation and response validation over genomic databases. It matched or beat GeneGPT on over 90% of tasks, scoring 0.849 on GeneTuring and 0.830 on GeneHop.

papers.name: ClinPreAI
papers.title: CLINPREAI: AN AGENTIC AI SYSTEM FOR EARLY POSTPARTUM DEPRESSION RISK PREDICTION FROM MULTIMODAL EHR DATA
papers.summary: ClinPreAI is an autonomous AI system designed to predict early postpartum depression risk using multimodal electronic health record data. It demonstrated superior performance compared to traditional AutoML and commercial solutions, showcasing the potential of agentic AI in clinical settings for democratizing sophisticated predictive modeling.

papers.name: MedBench v4
papers.title: MedBench v4: A Robust and Scalable Benchmark for Evaluating Chinese Medical Language Models, Multimodal Models, and Intelligent Agents
papers.summary: A cloud benchmark of over 700,000 clinician-reviewed tasks across 24 specialties with separate tracks for LLMs, multimodal models and agents. Agents built on the same backbones scored a mean of 79.8 of 100, far above base LLMs at 54.1, with large gains on safety tasks.

papers.name: KOSMOS
papers.title: When AI Does Science: Evaluating the Autonomous AI Scientist KOSMOS in Radiation Biology
papers.summary: Checks three KOSMOS-generated radiation biology hypotheses on public expression datasets against random-gene null models. One hypothesis was well supported, one uncertain and one false, showing the need for rigorous auditing.

papers.name: MedDCR
papers.title: MedDCR: Learning to Design Agentic Workflows for Medical Coding
papers.summary: A designer agent proposes coding workflows, a coder executes them on clinical notes, and a reflector critiques results while a memory archive stores prior designs for reuse. It outperformed earlier agentic and non-agentic baselines on medical coding benchmarks.

papers.name: GHAR
papers.title: Grounded by Experience: Generative Healthcare Prediction Augmented with Hierarchical Agentic Retrieval
papers.summary: GHAR is a hierarchical agentic retrieval framework designed to enhance healthcare predictions by addressing when and how to retrieve external knowledge. It demonstrates superior performance over existing methods in clinical decision support tasks, showcasing the potential of its dual-agent architecture.

papers.title: Multi-agent Self-triage System with Medical Flowcharts
papers.summary: The paper presents a multi-agent system that uses clinically validated flowcharts to guide patients through medical decision-making, ensuring accuracy and transparency. The system was evaluated using synthetic datasets and achieved high performance in both flowchart retrieval and navigation tasks.

papers.name: Agentic Lab
papers.title: Agentic Lab: An Agentic-physical AI system for cell and organoid experimentation and manufacturing
papers.summary: Agentic Lab is an AI platform that integrates large language models and vision-language models to assist in cell and organoid experimentation, enabling real-time protocol design, data analysis, and error detection. It demonstrates its capability by autonomously managing the differentiation of human pluripotent stem cells into organoids, providing context-aware instructions and improving experimental efficiency through continuous learning.

papers.title: Enhancing Large Language Models With AI Agents for Chronic Gastritis Management: Comprehensive Comparative Study
papers.summary: The paper describes an AI agent framework for managing chronic gastritis that integrates large language models with retrieval-augmented generation and a search engine tool. The study demonstrates the superior performance of this AI agent in addressing complex clinical questions compared to standard LLMs, highlighting its potential for enhancing patient self-management and reducing physician workload.

papers.name: BioVerge Agent
papers.title: BioVerge: A Comprehensive Benchmark and Study of Self-Evaluating Agents for Biomedical Hypothesis Generation
papers.summary: BioVerge Agent is an LLM-based framework designed for biomedical hypothesis generation, utilizing a ReAct approach with iterative generation and evaluation modules. The study demonstrates that structured and textual data sources enhance the quality of generated hypotheses, while self-evaluation improves their novelty and relevance.

papers.name: EasyMED
papers.title: Human or LLM as Standardized Patients? A Comparative Study for Medical Education
papers.summary: EasyMED is a multi-agent framework designed to simulate standardized patients for medical education, offering stable and inquiry-conditioned patient behavior. The system was evaluated against human-standardized patients using SPBench, demonstrating superior performance in case consistency and controlled disclosure.

papers.title: Using secure artificial intelligence agents integrated within the electronic medical record for the evaluation of blood culture appropriateness-Northern California, 2025
papers.summary: The paper evaluates the use of large language model agents integrated into electronic medical records to assess the appropriateness of blood cultures. The study highlights high sensitivity but low specificity in performance, influenced by prompt phrasing and other factors, indicating both potential benefits and limitations for clinical decision support systems.

papers.name: Bio AI Agent
papers.title: Bio AI Agent: A Multi-Agent Artificial Intelligence System for Autonomous CAR-T Cell Therapy Development with Integrated Target Discovery, Toxicity Prediction, and Rational Molecular Design
papers.summary: Bio AI Agent is a multi-agent system designed to streamline CAR-T cell therapy development by integrating target discovery, toxicity prediction, and molecular design. The system demonstrated its capability in identifying high-risk targets and patent infringement risks, showcasing potential for accelerating the translation of immunotherapies from discovery to clinical use.

papers.name: MADD
papers.title: MADD: Multi-Agent Drug Discovery Orchestra
papers.summary: MADD is a multi-agent system designed for drug discovery that builds and executes customized hit identification pipelines from natural language queries. It demonstrates superior performance compared to existing large language model-based solutions, pioneering AI-first drug design for several biological targets.

papers.title: Can Lightweight LLM Agents Improve Spatial Transcriptomics Annotation?
papers.summary: The paper explores the use of lightweight LLM agents to improve automated annotation in spatial transcriptomics, integrating rule-based heuristics and multirole reasoning. Results show that these models match or slightly exceed deterministic baselines in cluster recovery while providing more spatially consistent predictions.

papers.name: Coated-LLM
papers.title: Multi agent large language models for biomedical hypothesis generation in drug combination discovery
papers.summary: Coated-LLM has researcher, reviewer and moderator LLM agents generate and evaluate hypotheses about effective drug combinations for Alzheimer's disease. It outperformed knowledge-based methods (accuracy 0.74 vs 0.52), and one predicted combination reduced amyloid aggregation in vitro.

papers.name: VISA
papers.title: Voice-Interactive Surgical Agent for Multimodal Patient Data Control
papers.summary: The Voice-Interactive Surgical Agent (VISA) is a hierarchical multi-agent system designed to assist surgeons in accessing and manipulating patient data during robotic surgery through voice commands. VISA demonstrates high accuracy and robustness in executing tasks such as retrieving clinical information and navigating 3D anatomical models, enhancing surgical workflow without interruptions.

papers.name: FLEX
papers.title: FLEX: Continuous Agent Evolution via Forward Learning from Experience
papers.summary: FLEX is an autonomous agent that uses a gradient-free learning paradigm to continuously evolve its capabilities through experience, improving performance in tasks like chemical retrosynthesis and protein fitness prediction. The system demonstrates scalable continuous evolution and inheritable improvements across different agents, showing significant performance gains on benchmark datasets.

papers.name: CyteType
papers.title: Multi-agent AI enables evidence-based cell annotation in single-cell transcriptomics
papers.summary: Agents generate competing cell type hypotheses from full expression data and study context, check them against external databases and iteratively self-evaluate. It outperformed reference-based and LLM-based annotators, and its confidence scores identified reliable annotations.

papers.name: MSK-MATCH
papers.title: AI-assisted workflow enables rapid, high-fidelity breast cancer clinical trial eligibility prescreening
papers.summary: Combines an LLM with a curated oncology trial knowledge base and retrieval to screen patients for trial eligibility with source-grounded explanations, sending uncertain cases to human reviewers. On 731 breast cancer patients it resolved 61.9 percent automatically, reached 98.6 percent accuracy, and cut review time per case from 20 minutes to 43 seconds.

papers.name: RADAR
papers.title: Learning to reason about rare diseases through retrieval-augmented agents
papers.summary: Agents search embedded case reports and literature for evidence relevant to unfamiliar brain MRI findings and use it to reason about rare diagnoses without additional training. On the NOVA dataset of 280 rare diseases it improved several LLMs by up to 10.2 percent.

papers.name: UORCA
papers.title: Uncovering biological patterns across studies through automated large-scale reanalyses of public transcriptomic data
papers.summary: UORCA is a tool that uses large language models and multi-agent systems to automate the reanalysis of public transcriptomic datasets, identifying differentially expressed genes. It demonstrated its utility by uncovering biological patterns not initially described in the literature and generating hypotheses relevant for drug design.

papers.name: IMMUNIA
papers.title: IMMUNIA: A Multi-LLM Reasoning Agent for Immunoregulatory Surfaceome Discovery
papers.summary: Scores candidate surfaceome genes across immunotherapy, inflammation and NF-kB contexts with structured prompting and takes consensus across three LLMs, checked with positive and negative control genes. It prioritized eight candidates and highlighted PTPRS, VCAN and MXRA5 as previously unrecognized stromal checkpoint-like regulators.

papers.name: MDAT
papers.title: Multidisciplinary large language model agent teams for precision oncology enhance complex gynecologic oncology decision support
papers.summary: The MDAT framework uses multiple large language models to simulate a multidisciplinary tumor board, enhancing clinical decision-making in complex oncology cases. The study shows that fixed-size MDATs outperform single-agent approaches and are particularly effective for high-complexity questions.

papers.name: OpenMedicine AI
papers.title: Toward Accurate and Actionable Differential Diagnosis with Lean LLM Orchestration
papers.summary: OpenMedicine AI is an LLM-powered diagnostic agent that generates ranked differential diagnoses for complex medical cases. The system demonstrated superior accuracy and actionability compared to both AMIE and human physicians, significantly reducing diagnostic errors in high-complexity clinical scenarios.

papers.name: MedRaC
papers.title: From Scores to Steps: Diagnosing and Improving LLM Performance in Evidence-Based Medical Calculations
papers.venue: Proceedings of the Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing. Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
papers.summary: The authors cleaned MedCalc-Bench, built a stepwise evaluation of formula selection, entity extraction and arithmetic, and an automatic error attribution checked against experts. Their MedRaC pipeline, combining retrieval with Python code execution, raised LLM accuracy on medical calculations from 16.35% to as much as 53.19% without fine-tuning.

papers.name: MarIA
papers.title: Assessing the User Experience of an LLM-Based Conversational Assistant in Diabetes Mellitus Care
papers.summary: MarIA is a GPT-3.5-powered conversational assistant designed to support patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, demonstrating increased user engagement and richer contextual understanding through personalized interactions. The study highlights the importance of comprehensive patient profiling and safety mechanisms in AI-supported chronic care.

papers.name: LIDDiA
papers.title: LIDDIA: Language-based Intelligent Drug Discovery Agent
papers.venue: Proceedings of the Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing. Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
papers.summary: LIDDiA is an autonomous AI agent designed to navigate the drug discovery process, leveraging large language models for reasoning and molecule generation. It demonstrated its capability by generating molecules that meet pharmaceutical criteria for over 70% of clinically relevant targets and identified a promising candidate for treating prostate and breast cancers.

papers.title: Agentic Generative Artificial Intelligence System for Classification of Pathology-Confirmed Primary Progressive Aphasia Variants
papers.summary: A multi-agent generative AI system processed clinical notes, neuropsychological tests and MRI to classify primary progressive aphasia by syndrome and underlying pathology. It was evaluated on 54 autopsy-confirmed cases at UCSF in open-ended and constrained diagnosis settings.

papers.name: QSP-Copilot
papers.title: QSP-Copilot: An AI-Augmented Platform for Accelerating Quantitative Systems Pharmacology Model Development
papers.summary: QSP-Copilot is an AI-augmented platform that accelerates the development of Quantitative Systems Pharmacology (QSP) models by automating tasks such as literature extraction and model structuring. It demonstrated high precision in extracting biological interaction pairs from peer-reviewed articles, significantly reducing manual curation efforts.

papers.name: FT-ARM
papers.title: FT-ARM: Fine-Tuned Agentic Reflection Multimodal Language Model for Pressure Ulcer Severity Classification with Reasoning
papers.summary: A fine-tuned multimodal LLM reassesses its own pressure ulcer stage prediction by reasoning over image features and encoded clinical knowledge before settling on an answer, with natural-language justifications. On a public pressure injury dataset it reached 85 percent accuracy, four points above earlier convolutional models, and was tested under live inference.

papers.name: DiagAgent
papers.title: Evolving Interactive Diagnostic Agents in a Virtual Clinical Environment
papers.summary: Trains an interactive diagnostic agent with multi-turn reinforcement learning inside a learned diagnostics world model built from electronic records, alongside a multi-center benchmark with physician rubrics. It beat 11 LLMs and two prompted agents, gaining 11.2 percent diagnostic accuracy and 17.6 points of examination recommendation F1.

papers.name: AgentMD
papers.title: AgentMD: Empowering language agents for risk prediction with large-scale clinical tool learning
papers.summary: AgentMD is a language-based system that curates and applies clinical calculators to predict medical risks, demonstrating superior accuracy compared to GPT-4. It also provides population-level risk insights for institutional management.

papers.name: EBMChat
papers.title: Augmenting Large Language Models and Retrieval-Augmented Generation with an Evidence-Based Medicine-Enabled Agent System
papers.summary: EBMChat is a large language model-based agent designed to support clinical decision-making by integrating Evidence-Based Medicine principles and contextual conversation capabilities. The system demonstrated superior performance in retrieving high-quality evidence and maintaining context during multi-turn dialogues compared to existing methods.

papers.name: BRAINCELL-AID
papers.title: BRAINCELL-AID: An Agentic AI Created Brain Cell Type Resource for Community Annotation
papers.summary: BRAINCELL-AID is a multi-agent system that annotates brain cell gene sets by combining free-text descriptions with ontology labels and refining predictions using retrieved PubMed literature. It produced correct annotations for 77% of mouse gene sets among its top predictions.

papers.title: Clinical Agents Don’t Care
papers.summary: The study evaluates the ability of clinical agents to detect inconsistencies in patient identity across electronic health records. It finds that these agents often fail to notice such discrepancies, highlighting a critical risk for misbinding and emphasizing the need for explicit verification mechanisms before deployment.

papers.name: SPI-WSI
papers.title: Agent SPI-WSI: In context learning for computationally spatial pathway inferring on whole slide histopathology images conditioned on bulk RNA sequencing using pathologist in the loop
papers.summary: SPI-WSI iteratively generates, critiques with PubMed evidence and refines text prompts that a vision-language model uses to localize bulk RNA-seq pathway activity on whole-slide images, with pathologist guidance. Among the LLMs tested, Claude 4.0 gave the highest image-prompt similarity.

papers.name: TriAgent
papers.title: TriAgent: Automated Biomarker Discovery with Deep Research Grounding for Triage in Acute Care by LLM-Based Multi-Agent Collaboration
papers.summary: TriAgent pairs automated biomarker discovery for emergency triage with a supervisor research agent that delegates literature queries to sub-agents for grounding and novelty checks. Candidate biomarkers are classified as already supported or novel with transparent justification for acute care risk stratification.

papers.name: TEAM-PHI
papers.title: Towards Automatic Evaluation and Selection of PHI De-identification Models via Multi-Agent Collaboration
papers.summary: TEAM-PHI is a multi-agent framework that uses large language models to automatically evaluate and select the best PHI de-identification model, reducing reliance on expert annotations. It demonstrates consistent and accurate rankings of de-identification models through independent evaluations by multiple agents followed by LLM-based majority voting.

papers.name: MolAgent
papers.title: MolAgent: Biomolecular Property Estimation in the Agentic Era
papers.venue: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: MolAgent is an agentic AI framework designed for high-fidelity modeling of molecular properties in early-stage drug discovery. It autonomously implements expert-level pipelines for property estimation, ensuring optimal accuracy and model robustness through automated feature engineering and comprehensive validation frameworks.

papers.name: MedTrust-RAG
papers.title: MedTrust-RAG: Evidence Verification and Trust Alignment for Biomedical Question Answering
papers.summary: MedTrust-RAG requires every biomedical answer to cite retrieved documents and runs an iterative loop where a verification agent judges evidence sufficiency and rewrites queries after a medical gap analysis. It is designed to cut hallucinations caused by noisy retrieval in medical question answering.

papers.name: GenCellAgent
papers.title: GenCellAgent: Generalizable, Training-Free Cellular Image Segmentation via Large Language Model Agents
papers.summary: GenCellAgent routes cellular images to specialist segmenters or vision-language models through a planner-executor-evaluator loop with long-term memory and text-guided segmentation of uncovered organelles. Across seven benchmarks with 4,718 images it matched or beat the best single tool on every dataset and did markedly better on out-of-distribution organelles.

papers.name: MedKGEval
papers.title: MedKGEval: A Knowledge Graph-Based Multi-Turn Evaluation Framework for Open-Ended Patient Interactions with Clinical LLMs
papers.summary: MedKGEval is a framework that evaluates large language models in clinical settings through multi-turn patient interactions, using a knowledge graph to simulate realistic conversations. It demonstrates the ability to identify subtle flaws and safety risks in LLMs' responses by assessing each turn with fine-grained metrics.

papers.name: MedARC
papers.title: MedARC: Adaptive multi-agent refinement and collaboration for enhanced medical reasoning in large language models
papers.summary: MedARC is a multi-agent framework designed to enhance medical question answering by facilitating structured debates among LLM agents, improving accuracy and factual consistency. The system demonstrates significant performance gains over baseline methods in various medical QA tasks through automated benchmarks and human evaluations.

papers.name: OpenPFx
papers.title: OpenPFx: Evaluating the Ability of LLMs to Create Patient-Friendly Explanations of Radiological Incidental Findings
papers.summary: OpenPFx compared zero-shot, few-shot, multiple few-shot and agentic LLM workflows for writing patient-friendly explanations of incidental MRI findings. Over 407 outputs per workflow, the agentic workflow gave the highest ICD-10 accuracy and reached a sixth-grade reading level.

papers.name: ChatMyopia
papers.title: ChatMyopia: An AI agent for myopia-related consultation in primary eye care settings
papers.summary: Answers text and image questions about myopia by calling an image classifier and retrieving from a knowledge base of literature, expert consensus and guidelines. It graded myopic maculopathy accurately and, in a randomized trial, raised patient satisfaction and education quality over printed leaflets.

papers.title: Zero-Shot Large Language Model Agents for Fully Automated Radiotherapy Treatment Planning
papers.summary: The paper introduces a large language model (LLM) agent that performs automated radiotherapy treatment planning for IMRT without any prior training or fine-tuning. The LLM-generated plans were evaluated against clinical manual plans and showed comparable organ-at-risk sparing while improving hot spot control and conformity.

papers.name: MedCoAct
papers.title: MedCoAct: Confidence-Aware Multi-Agent Collaboration for Complete Clinical Decision
papers.summary: Confidence-aware doctor and pharmacist agents cross-check each other to connect diagnosis with medication decisions, evaluated on a new DrugCareQA benchmark. It reached 67.58 percent accuracy on both diagnosis and medication, about seven points above a single agent.

papers.name: Traj-CoA
papers.title: Traj-CoA: Patient Trajectory Modeling via Chain-of-Agents for Lung Cancer Risk Prediction
papers.summary: Worker agents read long EHR histories chunk by chunk, writing key events into a shared memory, and a manager agent uses the summaries and timeline to predict risk. In zero-shot one-year lung cancer prediction from five years of records it beat four classes of baselines.

papers.name: VivaBench
papers.title: Simulating Viva Voce Examinations to Evaluate Clinical Reasoning in Large Language Models
papers.summary: Turns 1,762 physician-curated vignettes into interactive scenarios where agents must request history, examination findings and investigations before diagnosing. LLMs that diagnose well from full vignettes degraded sharply, showing anchoring, poor test ordering, premature closure and missed critical conditions.

papers.name: MedAgentAudit
papers.title: Auditing medical multi-agent AI reveals risks of false consensus
papers.summary: Derives an expert-validated taxonomy of ten collaboration failures from 3,600 execution logs and applies automated probes to 14,400 cases across six multi-agent architectures and six datasets. Agents repeated their initial views in 98 percent of discussions, left unsupported observations in 16.6 percent of cases and showed authority bias in 28.8 percent.

papers.title: An Agentic System for Natural Language Querying of The Cancer Genome Atlas Clinical Data
papers.summary: The paper introduces an agentic system that allows natural language querying of TCGA clinical data, combining rule-based extraction and large language model capabilities. The system successfully handles a range of queries from simple patient lookups to complex cohort analyses across ten cancer types.

papers.name: AI-HOPE-PM
papers.title: Conversational Artificial Intelligence for Integrating Social Determinants, Genomics, and Clinical Data in Precision Medicine: Development and Implementation Study of the AI-HOPE-PM System
papers.summary: AI-HOPE-PM converts natural-language queries into Python statistical workflows that join genomic, clinical and social determinants of health data for cancer analysis. It was assessed on colorectal cancer cohorts from TCGA and cBioPortal for query interpretation accuracy and runtime.

papers.title: Rapid Development of Omics Data Analysis Applications through Vibe Coding
papers.summary: Vibe coding is an iterative process where users describe their goals in natural language and AI agents generate, test, and refine executable code for omics data analysis applications. The paper demonstrates the rapid development of a proteomics data analysis website using vibe coding, showcasing its potential to democratize computational biology software development.

papers.name: Council of AIs
papers.title: Collaborative intelligence in AI: Evaluating the performance of a council of AIs on the USMLE
papers.summary: The paper presents a multi-agent framework called the 'Council of AIs' that enhances Large Language Models (LLMs) performance on knowledge assessments by facilitating collaborative decision-making among multiple GPT-4 instances. The Council achieved high consensus accuracy rates across different stages of the USMLE, demonstrating the potential for AI collaboration to improve consistency and correctness in clinical decision support.

papers.name: Cascade Framework
papers.title: Large Language Model Agent for Managing Patients With Suspected Hypertension
papers.summary: The Cascade Framework is an LLM agent built on the Dify platform for hypertension education and clinical decision support. Adding it to GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini and DeepSeek-V3 improved rated accuracy and comprehensiveness, and it was externally validated in patients with suspected hypertension.

papers.name: DeepEvolve
papers.title: Scientific Algorithm Discovery by Augmenting AlphaEvolve with Deep Research
papers.summary: DeepEvolve is an AI agent that integrates deep research with algorithm evolution to discover new scientific algorithms. It demonstrates consistent improvement in generating executable and validated algorithms across various complex domains, showcasing its capability to bridge the gap between unguided evolution and theoretical research.

papers.title: LLM-based multi-agent system for neuro-ophthalmic diagnosis and personalized treatment planning
papers.summary: An information collection agent normalizes clinical text and optional fundus or OCT images, and a diagnosis agent ensembles several LLMs and a CNN with uncertainty-aware fusion for neuro-ophthalmic screening. It was more robust than single-model baselines on a curated corpus.

papers.title: Bridging Clinical Narratives and ACR Appropriateness Guidelines: A Multi-Agent RAG System for Medical Imaging Decisions
papers.summary: The paper presents a multi-agent system that translates unstructured clinical narratives into structured imaging recommendations based on ACR Appropriateness Criteria. The system uses a fine-tuned dense retrieval model and LLM-based agents to achieve high accuracy in matching guidelines, demonstrating significant improvement over standalone models.

papers.name: M-Reason
papers.title: Biomedical reasoning in action: Multi-agent System for Auditable Biomedical Evidence Synthesis
papers.summary: M-Reason assigns each agent to one biomedical evidence stream so retrieval, appraisal and synthesis run in parallel with full traceability from source to conclusion, focused on cancer research. An interactive interface lets researchers inspect the workflow, and evaluation showed gains in efficiency and output consistency.

papers.name: MedPAO
papers.title: MedPAO: A Protocol-Driven Agent for Structuring Medical Reports
papers.venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science, vol 16147, 2025. Springer, Cham
papers.summary: MedPAO is a protocol-driven agent designed to structure medical reports accurately by following established clinical protocols, ensuring verifiable reasoning and reducing hallucinations. The system demonstrated high reliability with an F1-score of 0.96 for concept categorization and received an average score of 4.52 out of 5 from expert radiologists and clinicians.

papers.name: Doctor-R1
papers.title: Doctor-R1: Mastering Clinical Inquiry with Experiential Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Doctor-R1 is an AI agent designed to excel in clinical decision-making and patient consultation, trained using a multi-agent interactive environment with a two-tiered reward system. It surpasses existing models on benchmarks like HealthBench and MAQuE, demonstrating superior performance in communication quality, user experience, and task accuracy.

papers.name: GraphMed-LT
papers.title: GraphMed-LT: Patient-Specific Graph Memory with Latent Clinical Thought Refinement for Multi-Turn Medical Conversations
papers.summary: GraphMed-LT is a system designed to enhance multi-turn medical conversations by maintaining a patient-specific graph memory that captures clinical evidence across conversation turns. It demonstrates improved performance in generating answerable follow-up questions and providing accurate final answers compared to existing methods.

papers.name: MetaboT
papers.title: MetaboT: An LLM-based Multi-Agent Frameworkfor Interactive Analysis of Mass SpectrometryMetabolomics Knowledge Graphs
papers.venue: 33rd annual international conference on Intelligent Systems for Molecular Biology (ISMB 2025) / 24th Annual Conference of the European Conference on Computational Biology (ECCB 2025), Jul 2025, Liverpool, United Kingdom
papers.summary: Specialised agents validate scope, resolve entities against authoritative resources, generate schema-aware SPARQL, refine failed queries and interpret results over mass spectrometry metabolomics knowledge graphs. It was validated on an expert-authored benchmark of natural-language questions about plant metabolites and bioactivities.

papers.name: Qimai
papers.title: Qimai: a multi-agent framework for zero-shot DNA-protein interaction prediction
papers.summary: Qimai is a multi-agent framework that predicts DNA-protein interactions by integrating deep learning predictions with biological evidence using an LLM as the reasoning engine. It demonstrated superior performance on unseen proteins compared to standalone models, highlighting its capability in generalizing across diverse datasets.

papers.name: LabscriptAI
papers.title: Execution-aware agent harness for accessible and responsible synthetic biology automation
papers.summary: LabscriptAI is an execution-aware agent framework that translates natural-language instructions into robot scripts for laboratory automation, addressing biosecurity and community standards. It demonstrated high accuracy in a liquid-handling benchmark and was used to screen sequences, characterize GFP designs, engineer enzymes with enhanced functionality, and prepare genetic parts for distribution.

papers.name: BioinfoMCP
papers.title: BioinfoMCP: A Unified Platform Enabling MCP Interfaces in Agentic Bioinformatics
papers.summary: BioinfoMCP is a platform that converts bioinformatics tools into Model Context Protocol (MCP) compliant servers, enabling seamless integration with AI agents. The system was validated across diverse computational tasks and showed high reliability and versatility in executing complex workflows.

papers.name: CLARITY
papers.title: CLARITY: Clinical Assistant for Routing, Inference, and Triage
papers.summary: CLARITY is an AI-driven platform that uses a hybrid architecture to facilitate patient-to-specialist routing and clinical consultations. It surpasses human-level performance in first-attempt routing precision and significantly reduces consultation duration compared to human interaction.

papers.name: LDPR
papers.title: Combination AI-Machine Learning to Diagnose Pulmonary Hypertension: A Real-World Evidence Cohort Study
papers.summary: Three task-specific LLM agents extracted unstructured right heart catheterization variables across a 12-hospital network, cross-validated by two pulmonary hypertension experts, with machine learning filling missing pressure values. The resulting data supported automated detection of pulmonary hypertension.

papers.name: EMR-AGENT
papers.title: EMR-AGENT: Automating Cohort and Feature Extraction from EMR Databases
papers.summary: EMR-AGENT is an automated framework that uses language models to dynamically extract and standardize clinical data from EMRs, replacing manual rule writing for cohort selection and feature extraction. The system demonstrates strong performance across multiple EMR databases, showing the potential of automating complex tasks previously requiring expert-driven design.

papers.name: DrugPilot
papers.title: DrugPilot: LLM-based Parameterized Reasoning Agent for Drug Discovery
papers.summary: Combines structured tool use with a parameterized memory pool that standardizes heterogeneous drug data across multi-turn workflows, trained on a new drug instruction dataset. It completed 98.0, 93.5 and 64.0 percent of simple, multi-tool and multi-turn tasks, ahead of ReAct and LoT.

papers.name: RadOnc-GPT
papers.title: RadOnc-GPT: An Autonomous LLM Agent for Real-Time Patient Outcomes Labeling at Scale
papers.summary: An LLM agent retrieves patient-specific structured and unstructured data, assesses the evidence iteratively and returns structured outcome labels. It was validated on treatment-detail retrieval and on labeling osteoradionecrosis and cancer recurrence in prostate and head-and-neck cohorts.

papers.name: MAQuE
papers.title: The Dialogue That Heals: A Comprehensive Evaluation of Doctor Agents' Inquiry Capability
papers.summary: Provides 3,000 simulated patient agents with varied language, cognitive limits, emotions and reluctance to disclose, scored on task success, inquiry skill, dialogue quality, efficiency and patient experience. Leading LLMs left substantial room for improvement and were sensitive to realistic patient behavior.

papers.name: MedMMV
papers.title: MedMMV: A Controllable Multimodal Multi-Agent Framework for Reliable and Verifiable Clinical Reasoning
papers.summary: MedMMV is a controllable multimodal multi-agent framework designed to enhance the reliability and verifiability of clinical reasoning. It stabilizes reasoning processes, grounds intermediate steps in structured evidence, and aggregates candidate paths to improve accuracy by up to 12.7% on medical benchmarks while ensuring truthfulness as confirmed by blind physician evaluations.

papers.name: TusoAI
papers.title: TusoAI: Agentic Optimization for Scientific Methods
papers.summary: Given a task description and evaluation function, the agent organizes domain knowledge into a tree and iteratively diagnoses and improves candidate computational methods. It beat expert methods and other scientific agents on tasks including single-cell RNA-seq denoising, and on two genetics problems uncovered new associations.

papers.name: EHR-ChatQA
papers.title: From Conversation to Query Execution: Benchmarking User and Tool Interactions for EHR Database Agents
papers.summary: EHR-ChatQA is a benchmark designed to evaluate the performance of large language model-powered agents in handling Electronic Health Record data access, focusing on query clarification and value resolution. The study reveals that while top-performing agents achieve high accuracy rates under certain conditions, they struggle with consistency across multiple trials, highlighting the need for more robust agent development.

papers.name: AMANDA
papers.title: AMANDA: Agentic Medical Knowledge Augmentation for Data-Efficient Medical Visual Question Answering
papers.summary: AMANDA is a training-free framework that uses large language model agents to augment medical knowledge for visual question answering tasks in low-resource settings. It demonstrates substantial improvements over existing models across multiple benchmarks, showing its effectiveness in both zero-shot and few-shot scenarios.

papers.title: Lightweight Structured Multimodal Reasoning for Clinical Scene Understanding in Robotics
papers.summary: Pairs a small VLM with a SmolAgent orchestration layer that invokes tools, fuses speech and vision, builds scene graphs and uses hybrid retrieval for clinical video understanding in robotics. It was competitive with larger VLMs on Video-MME and more robust on a custom clinical dataset.

papers.name: RCA
papers.title: Rethinking Explainable Disease Prediction: Synergizing Accuracy and Reliability via Reflective Cognitive Architecture
papers.summary: An LLM learns rules from tabular patient data by revising them after prediction errors and checking them against global data distributions. Across medical datasets, including a catheter-related thrombosis cohort, it matched or beat over 20 baselines while producing evidence-based explanations.

papers.name: TissueLab
papers.title: A co-evolving agentic AI system for medical imaging analysis
papers.summary: TissueLab is an agentic AI system designed for medical imaging analysis that integrates various tools and allows real-time expert feedback to refine analyses. It demonstrates state-of-the-art performance in clinical tasks, such as staging and prognosis, by continuously learning from clinicians.

papers.title: Scan-do Attitude: Towards Autonomous CT Protocol Management using a Large Language Model Agent
papers.summary: An LLM agent interprets natural-language or structured requests and uses tool calls to retrieve and modify CT acquisition, reconstruction and post-processing protocol elements. It generated device-compatible protocol files and implemented requests faithfully, though validity suffered without a unified device API and on ambiguous requests.

papers.name: MACD
papers.title: MACD: Multi-Agent Clinical Diagnosis with Self-Learned Knowledge for LLM
papers.summary: MACD is a multi-agent framework that enables large language models to self-learn clinical knowledge through iterative consultations, improving diagnostic accuracy. The system demonstrates significant improvements in primary diagnostic accuracy and shows the potential for human-AI collaboration in clinical decision support.

papers.title: LLMs for Bayesian Optimization in Scientific Domains: Are We There Yet?
papers.summary: Evaluates open and closed LLM agents on iterative design of genetic perturbation and molecular property experiments against bandit and Gaussian process baselines. The agents ignored experimental feedback, performing the same with permuted labels, and a simple LLM-prior nearest-neighbour hybrid did better.

papers.name: NBA
papers.title: Nano Bio-Agents (NBA): Small Language Model Agents for Genomics
papers.summary: The Nano Bio-Agent (NBA) framework uses small language models to address genomics questions, integrating task decomposition and API access for efficient performance. It demonstrates superior accuracy compared to larger models on the GeneTuring benchmark while significantly reducing computational costs.

papers.title: A Virtual Patients Ensemble Approach for Predicting Surgical Complications
papers.summary: The paper introduces an AI agent using a Virtual Patients Ensemble (VPE) approach to predict specific surgical complications from individual patient profiles, outperforming baseline methods. The system generates plausible variations of the original case to capture uncertainty and provides interpretable predictions for clinical decision-making.

papers.name: Medical AI Consensus
papers.title: Medical AI Consensus: A Multi-Agent Framework for Radiology Report Generation and Evaluation
papers.summary: The Medical AI Consensus framework uses a multi-agent reinforcement learning approach to generate and evaluate radiology reports, integrating large language models and vision models. It demonstrates the potential for fine-grained assessment of clinical reliability in automated report generation through iterative human-in-the-loop evaluation.

papers.name: EHR-MCP
papers.title: EHR-MCP: Real-world Evaluation of Clinical Information Retrieval by Large Language Models via Model Context Protocol
papers.summary: EHR-MCP is a framework that integrates large language models with hospital electronic health record databases to retrieve clinically relevant information. The system demonstrated near-perfect accuracy in simple tasks but faced challenges in more complex scenarios requiring time-dependent calculations.

papers.name: OpenLens AI
papers.title: OpenLens AI: Fully Autonomous Research Agent for Health Infomatics
papers.summary: OpenLens AI is a multi-agent system designed for health informatics research, automating tasks such as literature review, data analysis, and manuscript preparation. It demonstrates the ability to generate publication-ready manuscripts with transparent workflows while incorporating medical visualization interpretation and quality control.

papers.name: KAMAC
papers.title: A Knowledge-driven Adaptive Collaboration of LLMs for Enhancing Medical Decision-making
papers.summary: KAMAC is a framework that uses large language models to dynamically form and expand expert teams for medical decision-making, addressing the limitations of static multi-agent systems. It demonstrates significant improvements over single-agent and advanced multi-agent methods in real-world medical benchmarks, particularly in complex clinical scenarios.

papers.name: DELPHAI
papers.title: DELPHAI, AI Agent for Predicting Drug Response and Resistance
papers.summary: DELPHAI is an AI agent designed to predict drug responses and resistance mechanisms in patient-derived organoids, particularly for glioblastoma. It successfully identified the mechanism of action for temozolomide and suggested combination therapies that align with clinical trial outcomes, demonstrating its potential in precision medicine.

papers.name: BCI-Agent
papers.title: An AI Agent for cell-type specific brain computer interfaces
papers.summary: BCI-Agent repurposes vision-language models as few-shot classifiers of neuronal cell types from electrophysiological features and wraps this in an agent that tracks neurons, validates calls against molecular atlases and synthesizes literature. It was tested against optogenetically tagged datasets for subtype inference.

papers.title: Privacy-, linguistic-, and information-preserving synthesis of clinical documentation through generative agents
papers.summary: The paper presents a protocol for generating synthetic clinical documentation using multiple generative agents that are context-aware and role-specific, aiming to preserve privacy, linguistic accuracy, and information integrity. The authors developed an automated evaluation framework to compare synthetic EHRs with real ones, demonstrating the potential of this approach in advancing learning health systems.

papers.name: Dr. CaBot
papers.title: Teaching large language models to reason like expert diagnosticians
papers.summary: Dr. CaBot is an AI system designed to emulate expert diagnostic reasoning by generating detailed case presentations from initial patient descriptions, demonstrating its ability to solve complex medical cases and outperform existing models in a benchmark based on real clinical scenarios. In evaluations, physicians were unable to distinguish between diagnoses generated by Dr. CaBot and those written by human experts.

papers.name: MedicalOS
papers.title: MedicalOS: An LLM Agent based Operating System for Digital Healthcare
papers.summary: Translates clinician instructions into guideline-constrained commands such as history retrieval, exam ordering, report writing, referral and treatment planning, implemented as Python, API and MCP tools. On 214 cases across 22 specialties it achieved high diagnostic accuracy and clinically sound exam requests.

papers.title: Designing and Evaluating a Conversational Agent for Early Diagnosis of Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias
papers.summary: Voice-based LLM agents systematically question patients and informants to collect narratives relevant to Alzheimer's disease and related dementias. In 30 adults with suspected dementia, agent-detected symptoms agreed well with blinded specialist interviews and users valued its patient questioning.

papers.name: CARENLI
papers.title: Compartmentalised Agentic Reasoning for Clinical NLI
papers.summary: Routes each clinical premise-statement pair to one of four reasoning families and applies a specialised solver followed by explicit verification and targeted refinement. On a 200-item clinical trial NLI benchmark it raised mean accuracy from about 23 to 57 percent across four backbones.

papers.name: FHIR-AgentBench
papers.title: FHIR-AgentBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Realistic Interoperable EHR Question Answering
papers.summary: FHIR-AgentBench is a benchmark designed to evaluate large language model agents on real-world clinical questions grounded in the HL7 FHIR standard, assessing their ability to retrieve and reason over complex health data. The benchmark highlights challenges such as intricate data retrieval from FHIR resources and reasoning difficulties, underscoring the need for robust LLMs in clinical applications.

papers.name: MAVeRiC-AD
papers.title: MAVeRiC-AD: Mixture-of-experts Agentic Vision-Language Ensemble for Robust MRI Classification of Alzheimer’s Disease
papers.summary: MAVeRiC-AD is an agentic framework that dynamically selects the best model for classifying Alzheimer's disease from MRI images, improving robustness across different imaging protocols and demographics. It demonstrates enhanced performance by integrating a mixture-of-experts vision-language model with demographic information, achieving higher ROC-AUC scores compared to single-model approaches.

papers.name: HypoGeneAgent
papers.title: HypoGeneAgent: A Hypothesis Language Agent for Gene-Set Cluster Resolution Selection Using Perturb-seq Datasets
papers.summary: HypoGeneAgent is a large language model-driven framework that uses gene-set analysis and hypothesis generation to optimize the resolution selection and functional annotation of clusters in single-cell Perturb-seq datasets. The system demonstrated improved cluster resolution and functional annotation compared to traditional metrics, highlighting its potential for automated interpretation pipelines in multi-omics studies.

papers.title: BioLab: End-to-End Autonomous Life Sciences Research with Multi-Agents System Integrating Biological Foundation Models
papers.summary: This paper presents BioLab, a multi agent system that integrates domain specific foundation models and computational tools to automate end to end biological research. BioLab outperforms leading large language models on biomedical reasoning benchmarks and autonomously executes complex pipelines, including de novo antibody design with experimental validation. The results demonstrate that AI native multi agent frameworks can tightly couple computation and experimentation to drive scalable scientific discovery.

papers.name: AI co-scientist
papers.title: AI mirrors experimental science to uncover a mechanism of gene transfer crucial to bacterial evolution
papers.summary: The AI co-scientist platform generated hypotheses about the mechanism of gene transfer in bacteria, which were experimentally validated. The study demonstrates that AI can effectively generate and test high-level scientific hypotheses, potentially accelerating discovery in biological research.

papers.name: CancerGUIDE
papers.title: CancerGUIDE: Cancer Guideline Understanding via Internal Disagreement Estimation
papers.summary: CancerGUIDE is an AI system that uses large language models to generate guideline-concordant treatment trajectories for non-small cell lung cancer patients, reducing the time and expertise required. It demonstrates high correlation with expert-annotated benchmarks and includes a meta-classifier for verifying prediction accuracy.

papers.title: A multimodal LLM-agent framework for personalized clinical decision-making in hepatocellular carcinoma
papers.summary: The DeepSeek-R1 framework integrates radiomics, deep learning models, and large language model-based agents to generate personalized treatment recommendations for hepatocellular carcinoma. The system demonstrated improved prediction accuracy for critical pathological markers like microvascular invasion and capsule presence, with clinical relevance scores indicating its potential in precision oncology.

papers.name: Paper2Agent
papers.title: Paper2Agent: Reimagining Research Papers As Interactive and Reliable AI Agents
papers.summary: Paper2Agent converts research papers into interactive AI agents that can interpret genomic variants and perform single-cell and spatial transcriptomics analyses, demonstrating its ability to reproduce original results and answer novel queries. It showcases the potential of transforming static scientific literature into dynamic tools for knowledge discovery and exploration.

papers.name: HAO
papers.title: Demo: Healthcare Agent Orchestrator (HAO) for Patient Summarization in Molecular Tumor Boards
papers.summary: The Healthcare Agent Orchestrator (HAO) is a multi-agent system that uses large language models to generate comprehensive patient summaries for molecular tumor boards, aiding in clinical decision-making. It demonstrates high accuracy and completeness in capturing critical patient information through the TBFact evaluation framework.

papers.name: BioML-bench
papers.title: BioML-bench: Evaluation of AI Agents for End-to-End Biomedical ML
papers.summary: BioML-bench evaluates AI agents on end-to-end biomedical machine learning tasks in protein engineering, single-cell omics, imaging and drug discovery, graded by standard metrics. Four open-source agents, including STELLA and Biomni, were tested and generally fell short of human baselines.

papers.name: Code Like Humans
papers.title: Code Like Humans: A Multi-Agent Solution for Medical Coding
papers.summary: Code Like Humans is a framework that uses large language models to map unstructured clinical notes to ICD-10 codes, supporting over 70K labels. It demonstrates superior performance in coding rare diagnosis codes compared to existing methods.

papers.title: Optimizing Order Sets With a Large Language Model-Powered Multiagent System
papers.summary: A multi-agent LLM system with critique, search, knowledge retrieval, medication verification and summarization agents suggests improvements to hospital order sets at Vanderbilt. Physicians rated 735 suggestions, and an LLM-as-a-judge filter was developed to align outputs with expert preferences.

papers.title: Towards Agents That Know When They Don't Know: Uncertainty as a Control Signal for Structured Reasoning
papers.summary: An agent for query-conditioned multi-table summarization uses entropy over table-selection rollouts and summary self-consistency as control signals, both in reinforcement learning and at inference. On multi-omics benchmarks it roughly tripled correct useful claims per summary and raised downstream survival prediction C-index from 0.32 to 0.63.

papers.name: AuraGenome
papers.title: AuraGenome: An LLM-Powered Framework for On-the-Fly Reusable and Scalable Circular Genome Visualizations
papers.summary: AuraGenome is an LLM-powered framework that generates multilayered circular genome visualizations, combining a semantic-driven multiagent workflow with interactive visual analytics. The system was validated through case studies and user evaluations, demonstrating its effectiveness in rapid, reusable, and scalable visualization of genomic data.

papers.name: RDguru
papers.title: RDguru: A Conversational Intelligent Agent for Rare Diseases
papers.venue: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: RDguru is a conversational intelligent agent designed to assist in the diagnosis and management of rare diseases by integrating multiple knowledge sources and diagnostic tools. It demonstrates improved diagnostic accuracy compared to existing methods, as well as effective elicitation of relevant patient information through iterative questioning.

papers.name: AI-HOPE-TP53
papers.title: AI-HOPE-TP53: A Conversational Artificial Intelligence Agent for Pathway-Centric Analysis of TP53-Driven Molecular Alterations in Early-Onset Colorectal Cancer
papers.summary: This version of AI-HOPE-TP53 pairs a fine-tuned LLaMA 3 model with harmonized cBioPortal cohorts to translate questions into mutation, survival and odds ratio analyses of TP53 alterations in early-onset colorectal cancer. It reproduced known associations and reported subgroup differences by treatment and population.

papers.name: DR. INFO
papers.title: OpenAIs HealthBench in Action: Evaluating an LLM-Based Medical Assistant on Realistic Clinical Queries
papers.summary: DR. INFO is an LLM-based medical assistant that uses the RAG architecture to provide situationally aware answers to clinical questions, outperforming other leading models on a complex benchmark called HealthBench. The system demonstrates strengths in communication and accuracy but shows areas for improvement in context awareness and response completeness.

papers.title: Automated Clinical Problem Detection from SOAP Notes using a Collaborative Multi-Agent LLM Architecture
papers.summary: A manager agent assembles specialist agents that debate hierarchically over the subjective and objective sections of SOAP notes to identify clinical problems. On 420 MIMIC-III notes it beat a single agent for heart failure, acute kidney injury and sepsis, though debates sometimes showed groupthink.

papers.name: PHA
papers.title: The Anatomy of a Personal Health Agent
papers.summary: The Personal Health Agent (PHA) is a multi-agent system designed to provide personalized health recommendations by analyzing multimodal data from consumer wellness devices and personal health records. The PHA framework includes sub-agents for data analysis, expert insights generation, and user guidance, which were evaluated through both automated benchmarks and human-in-the-loop assessments involving extensive annotations and expert reviews.

papers.name: MATRIX
papers.title: MATRIX: Multi-Agent simulaTion fRamework for safe Interactions and conteXtual clinical conversational evaluation
papers.summary: Combines a safety taxonomy of clinical scenarios and failure modes, an LLM hazard-detecting evaluator and a simulated patient agent to stress-test clinical dialogue agents. Its evaluator matched expert hazard detection with an F1 of 0.96 and the framework benchmarked five agents over 2,100 dialogues across 14 hazard scenarios.

papers.name: TrustEHRAgent
papers.title: Trustworthy Agents for Electronic Health Records through Confidence Estimation
papers.summary: An EHR agent estimates confidence at each reasoning step so it can answer or abstain, evaluated with a new metric of accuracy under hallucination control. On MIMIC-III and eICU it improved accuracy at a 70 percent reliability threshold by 44 and 25 points where baselines failed.

papers.name: AT-CXR
papers.title: AT-CXR: Uncertainty-Aware Agentic Triage for Chest X-rays
papers.summary: AT-CXR is an uncertainty-aware agent designed for chest X-ray triage, which decides when to issue a decision or defer to human intervention based on per-case confidence and distributional fit. The system outperforms existing models in terms of accuracy and selective prediction performance while maintaining lower latency suitable for clinical use.

papers.title: Proof of concept for voice based MRI scanner control using large language models in real time guided interventions
papers.summary: A voice interface uses collaborating LLM agents to run MRI scanner functions such as sequence execution, parameter changes and table positioning during interventions. In 90 tests of 18 tasks in a real scanner room it completed 93.3% of tasks with 5-10 second response times on a laptop.

papers.name: CARE-AD
papers.title: CARE-AD: a multi-agent large language model framework for Alzheimer's disease prediction using longitudinal clinical notes
papers.summary: Specialised LLM agents extract Alzheimer's-relevant signs and symptoms from longitudinal EHR notes and evaluate them by domain before a combined risk judgement. Predicting risk ten years before the first diagnosis code, it reached 0.53 accuracy versus 0.26 to 0.45 for single-model baselines.

papers.title: Orchestrated multi agents sustain accuracy under clinical-scale workloads compared to a single agent
papers.summary: The study evaluates the performance of a multi-agent system versus a single agent in handling clinical-scale workloads, demonstrating that the multi-agent setup maintains higher accuracy and efficiency under load. The research highlights the benefits of task isolation and reduced context interference in large language models for clinical applications.

papers.title: Evaluating Large Language Model Diagnostic Performance on JAMA Clinical Challenges via a Multi-Agent Conversational Framework
papers.summary: JAMA Clinical Challenge cases were converted into multi-turn dialogues in which a clinical LLM questions a patient agent and a system agent holding exam, lab and imaging data. Diagnostic accuracy of O1, GPT-4o, LLaMA-3-70B and a DeepSeek distillate dropped in this conversational format compared with the original vignettes.

papers.name: Moremi Bio Agent
papers.title: Moremi Bio Agent: Leveraging Agentic Large Language Model for the Discovery of Broad-Spectrum Antibiotics for Enterobacteriaceae
papers.summary: Moremi Bio Agent is an AI system designed to autonomously discover broad-spectrum antibiotics targeting Enterobacteriaceae. It demonstrated the feasibility of using dual-target strategies for antibiotic design, generating and evaluating over a thousand candidate molecules with promising drug-like properties.

papers.name: Deep-DxSearch
papers.title: End-to-End Agentic RAG System Training for Traceable Diagnostic Reasoning
papers.summary: Trains an LLM end to end with reinforcement learning to query guideline-derived disease profiles, patient records and biomedical literature, evaluate evidence and refine searches until the diagnosis is supported. It beat GPT-4o, DeepSeek-R1 and medical frameworks by 22.7 percent on average and raised physicians' accuracy from 45.6 to 69.1 percent on 150 real cases.

papers.name: SciToolAgent
papers.title: SciToolAgent: a knowledge-graph-driven scientific agent for multitool integration
papers.summary: SciToolAgent is a scientific agent that integrates and orchestrates hundreds of computational tools across various domains using a knowledge graph, enabling both experts and nonexperts to automate complex workflows. The system demonstrates its effectiveness in handling tasks like protein engineering and chemical synthesis through extensive evaluations and case studies.

papers.name: MedResearcher-R1
papers.title: MedResearcher-R1: Expert-Level Medical Deep Researcher via A Knowledge-Informed Trajectory Synthesis Framework
papers.summary: MedResearcher-R1 is a medical deep research agent designed to address the limitations of general-purpose LLMs in clinical reasoning tasks. It uses a knowledge-informed trajectory synthesis framework and integrates specialized retrieval tools, demonstrating superior performance on complex medical benchmarks.

papers.name: PRINCE
papers.title: From data silos to insights: the PRINCE multi-agent knowledge engine for preclinical drug development
papers.summary: PRINCE is a cloud-hosted data integration platform that uses a multi-agent architecture to integrate and analyze safety study reports for preclinical drug development. It evolved from a simple search tool into a sophisticated research assistant capable of drafting regulatory documents, demonstrating the potential of AI in enhancing data accessibility and research efficiency while maintaining human accountability.

papers.title: LLM-Powered Virtual Patient Agents for Interactive Clinical Skills Training with Automated Feedback
papers.summary: The paper introduces a framework that enhances large language model-based virtual patients for medical training by enabling non-textual interactions and providing real-time feedback. The system was evaluated with medical experts who found the simulated patient behaviors natural and coherent, and the feedback from virtual tutors useful and appropriate.

papers.name: EMRC
papers.title: Expertise-aware Multi-LLM Recruitment and Collaboration for Medical Decision-Making
papers.summary: The EMRC framework uses multiple LLMs to enhance medical decision-making by dynamically selecting the best agents based on their expertise and integrating their responses through confidence scores and adversarial validation. The system demonstrates superior diagnostic performance compared to single-LLM approaches, showcasing its effectiveness in leveraging diverse expert capabilities.

papers.title: Improving Automated Deep Phenotyping Through Large Language Models Using Retrieval Augmented Generation
papers.summary: This paper introduces RAG-HPO, a retrieval-augmented generation tool that improves automatic extraction and assignment of Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) terms from clinical text. By combining LLM-based phrase extraction with real-time retrieval from a large vector database of phenotype–HPO mappings, RAG-HPO reduces hallucinations and avoids costly fine-tuning. Evaluated on 112 rare-disease case reports, it significantly outperforms existing HPO extraction tools in precision, recall, and F1 score, with most false positives being clinically relevant ancestor terms rather than hallucinations. The results demonstrate that RAG-based grounding enables accurate, reliable phenotype extraction for clinical genomics and rare disease diagnosis.

papers.name: ADAM-1
papers.title: ADAM-1: An AI Reasoning and Bioinformatics Model for Alzheimer's Disease Detection and Microbiome-Clinical Data Integration
papers.venue: IEEE access : practical innovations, open solutions
papers.summary: ADAM-1 is a multi-agent LLM framework that integrates microbiome profiles, clinical data and literature to classify Alzheimer's disease. Compared with XGBoost, it achieved a higher mean F1 score with lower variance.

papers.name: CardAIc-Agents
papers.title: CardAIc-Agents: A Multimodal Framework with Hierarchical Adaptation for Cardiac Care Support
papers.summary: CardAIc-Agents is a multimodal framework that uses adaptive reasoning and external tools to support cardiac care tasks, generating task-aware plans and delivering decisions based on clinical data. The system demonstrated efficiency in handling complex cardiac cases compared to existing vision-language models and agentic systems.

papers.title: Standardization of Neuromuscular Reflex Analysis -- Role of Fine-Tuned Vision-Language Model Consortium and OpenAI gpt-oss Reasoning LLM Enabled Decision Support System
papers.summary: The system uses a consortium of fine-tuned vision-language models and an OpenAI reasoning LLM to provide decision support for the analysis of H-reflex EMG waveforms, demonstrating improved accuracy and standardization in neuromuscular diagnostics compared to traditional methods.

papers.name: Gregory
papers.title: AI vs Human Performance in Conversational Hospital-Based Neurological Diagnosis
papers.summary: Gregory is a multi-agent system designed to assist in neurological diagnosis, demonstrating superior diagnostic accuracy and efficiency compared to human neurologists and base LLMs. The DiagnosticXchange platform used for evaluation revealed that Gregory employs targeted testing strategies, significantly reducing costs and time without compromising thoroughness.
