papers.title: Self-Explained Thinking Agent for Autonomous Microscopy Restoration
papers.summary: The paper introduces a self-explained thinking agent that uses multimodal large language models to identify image degradation in microscopy and select restoration strategies. The system demonstrates high accuracy and explainability, outperforming human-level performance across various scenarios.

papers.name: FROGENT
papers.title: FROGENT: An End-to-End Full-process Drug Design Multi-Agent System
papers.summary: FROGENT is a multi-agent system designed for full-process drug design, integrating target identification, small-molecule generation, peptide optimization, and retrosynthetic planning. It demonstrates superior performance across various benchmarks compared to existing methods, showcasing the potential of large language model-based systems in automating complex drug discovery pipelines.

papers.title: CART-GPT: A T Cell-Informed AI Linguistic Framework for Interpreting Neurotoxicity and Therapeutic Outcomes in CAR-T Therapy
papers.summary: This paper introduces CART-GPT, a transformer-based model trained on over one million CAR-T single-cell RNA-seq profiles to predict patient-specific treatment response and neurotoxicity risk in CAR-T therapy. The model achieves strong predictive performance while providing interpretable insights showing that outcomes are driven by coordinated subsets of T cell states rather than single cell types. By linking single-cell predictions to patient-level outcomes and releasing a large annotated atlas, the study demonstrates the value of foundation models for precision CAR-T treatment planning.

papers.name: BioScientist Agent
papers.title: BioScientist Agent: Designing LLM-Biomedical Agents with KG-Augmented RL Reasoning Modules for Drug Repurposing and Mechanistic of Action Elucidation
papers.summary: BioScientist Agent is a framework that integrates a large biomedical knowledge graph with machine learning modules to facilitate drug repurposing and elucidate the mechanism of action for drug-disease pairs. The system surpasses existing methods in various metrics, providing mechanistic explanations consistent with literature.

papers.title: Conversational AI agent for precision oncology: AI-HOPE-WNT integrates clinical and genomic data to investigate WNT pathway dysregulation in colorectal cancer
papers.summary: AI-HOPE-WNT is a conversational AI agent designed to enable natural-language, WNT-focused analysis of integrated clinical and genomic colorectal cancer data. The system accurately reproduces published findings on WNT pathway alterations while uncovering new associations related to survival, treatment response, mutation co-occurrence, and population-specific risk. By automating complex bioinformatics workflows, AI-HOPE-WNT lowers technical barriers and establishes a pathway-specific paradigm for precision oncology research.

papers.name: TeamMedAgents
papers.title: TeamMedAgents: Pareto-Efficient Multi-Agent Medical Reasoning Through Teamwork Theory
papers.summary: Implements shared mental models, leadership, trust networks and mutual monitoring as coordination mechanisms so small language models can do multi-step clinical reasoning. Across eight medical benchmarks it matched the accuracy of MDAgents, MedAgents, DyLAN and ReConcile at one to two orders of magnitude lower token cost, with the lowest cross-dataset variance.

papers.name: miRKatAI
papers.title: miRKatAI: An Integrated Database and Multi-agent AI system for microRNA Research
papers.summary: miRKatAI is a multi-agent system that integrates and analyzes microRNA-target interactions using a comprehensive database (miRKatDB) and large language models. It provides researchers with an intuitive interface for querying complex biological data, enhancing exploratory analysis and hypothesis generation in miRNA research.

papers.name: K-Dense Analyst
papers.title: K-Dense Analyst: Towards Fully Automated Scientific Analysis
papers.summary: K-Dense Analyst is a hierarchical multi-agent system that plans bioinformatics analyses and executes verified tasks in secure environments through a dual-loop design. On the open-ended BixBench it reached 29.2% accuracy, 6.3 points above GPT-5.

papers.title: AI-driven Toolset for IPF and Aging Research Associates Lung Fibrosis with Accelerated Aging
papers.summary: This study applies AI to uncover aging-related mechanisms underlying idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis by combining a pathway-aware proteomic aging clock with a domain-specific language model, ipf-P3GPT. The aging clock shows strong predictive performance and links accelerated aging to severe COVID-19, while molecular analyses reveal that IPF reflects dysregulated aging pathways rather than simple aging acceleration. These results highlight new connections between aging biology and IPF and demonstrate the value of AI-guided strategies for studying age-related diseases.

papers.name: MedOrch
papers.title: Mediator-Guided Multi-Agent Collaboration among Open-Source Models for Medical Decision-Making
papers.summary: An LLM mediator lets several open-source general and medical VLM agents exchange and reflect on each other's answers to medical image questions. On five medical VQA benchmarks the collaboration outperformed every individual model without any training.

papers.name: LLM-DTR
papers.title: Are Large Language Models Dynamic Treatment Planners? An In Silico Study from a Prior Knowledge Injection Angle
papers.summary: The paper evaluates large language models as dynamic treatment planners for insulin dosing in Type 1 diabetes, showing that smaller LLMs can match or outperform small neural network-based agents with zero-shot prompts. However, the study also highlights significant limitations of LLMs in handling complex clinical scenarios and underscores the need for careful prompt engineering and hybrid approaches.

papers.title: An Auditable Agent Platform For Automated Molecular Optimisation
papers.summary: The paper describes a hierarchical agent framework for automated molecular optimization in drug discovery, where agents collaborate to generate and optimize molecules. The study demonstrates that multi-agent systems excel at focused binding optimization compared to single-agent or unguided LLM approaches.

papers.name: Tree-of-Reasoning (ToR)
papers.title: Tree-of-Reasoning: Towards Complex Medical Diagnosis via Multi-Agent Reasoning with Evidence Tree
papers.summary: Tree-of-Reasoning is a multi-agent framework designed to enhance complex medical diagnosis by recording reasoning paths and clinical evidence in a tree structure, improving the consistency of decision-making through cross-validation. The system outperforms existing methods on real-world medical data, demonstrating its effectiveness in handling intricate diagnostic tasks.

papers.name: ICARE
papers.title: Clinically Grounded Agent-based Report Evaluation: An Interpretable Metric for Radiology Report Generation
papers.summary: ICARE is an evaluation framework for radiology report generation that uses large language model agents to generate clinically meaningful questions and assess the consistency of findings in generated reports. The system demonstrates significant alignment with expert judgment, providing a transparent and interpretable assessment method.

papers.name: SNOW
papers.title: Scaling Clinician-Grade Feature Generation from Clinical Notes with Multi-Agent Language Models
papers.summary: SNOW is a multi-agent language model system designed to generate clinical features from unstructured EHR notes, mimicking the iterative reasoning and validation workflow of human clinicians. The study shows that SNOW can achieve performance comparable to manual feature generation by experts and outperform other methods in predicting cancer recurrence and heart failure mortality.

papers.name: BioDisco
papers.title: BioDisco: Multi-agent hypothesis generation with dual-mode evidence, iterative feedback and temporal evaluation
papers.summary: BioDisco is a multi-agent system designed to generate novel scientific hypotheses by integrating language model reasoning with dual-mode evidence retrieval from biomedical knowledge graphs and literature. The system demonstrates superior hypothesis novelty and significance through rigorous temporal evaluation methods, outperforming both ablated configurations and generalist agents.

papers.name: BioRAGent
papers.title: BioRAGent: natural language biomedical querying with retrieval-augmented multiagent systems
papers.summary: BioRAGent is a biomedical assistant that uses retrieval-augmented generation and a multiagent system to facilitate natural language queries about genes, phenotypes, diseases, and their interrelationships. It demonstrates superior performance in handling complex multi-hop queries compared to existing models through automated benchmarks and user evaluations.

papers.name: CellAtria
papers.title: An Agentic AI Framework for Ingestion and Standardization of Single-Cell RNA-seq Data Analysis
papers.summary: CellAtria is an agentic AI framework that automates the process of ingesting and standardizing single-cell RNA-seq data analysis through a chatbot interface. It demonstrated efficient and accessible data reuse by integrating large language models with tool-execution capabilities to handle metadata extraction, dataset retrieval, and downstream analysis.

papers.title: CRISPR-GPT for agentic automation of gene-editing experiments
papers.summary: This work presents CRISPR-GPT, an LLM-based agent system designed to support end-to-end CRISPR gene-editing experiment design and data analysis. By integrating domain knowledge, retrieval, external tools, and a fine-tuned model, CRISPR-GPT assists with experimental planning, guide RNA design, protocol drafting, and result interpretation. Experimental validations demonstrate its effectiveness as an AI co-pilot for genome engineering across different CRISPR modalities.

papers.name: PrimeGen
papers.title: Accelerating primer design for amplicon sequencing using large language model-powered agents
papers.summary: PrimeGen is a multi-agent system that uses large language models to streamline primer design for targeted next-generation sequencing, reducing labor and improving efficiency. The system demonstrates high amplification uniformity and minimizes dimer formation across various applications.

papers.name: Virtual Lab
papers.title: The Virtual Lab of AI agents designs new SARS-CoV-2 nanobodies
papers.summary: An LLM principal investigator agent runs research meetings with specialist LLM agents under light human direction, here building a nanobody design pipeline around a protein language model, AlphaFold-Multimer and Rosetta. The 92 designed nanobodies included functional binders, two with improved binding to recent variants while retaining ancestral spike binding.

papers.name: GeneAgent
papers.title: GeneAgent: self-verification language agent for gene-set analysis using domain databases
papers.summary: GeneAgent is an AI agent designed to analyze gene sets by generating functional descriptions and verifying them against biological databases, thereby reducing inaccuracies. It was shown to be more accurate than GPT-4 in analyzing diverse gene sets and provided valuable insights into gene functions when applied to novel datasets.

papers.name: GenoMAS
papers.title: GenoMAS: Guided Multi-Agent Programming for Scientific Discovery from Genomic Data
papers.summary: GenoMAS runs a team of programming agents that decompose gene expression analysis guidelines into action units and can advance, revise, bypass or backtrack while passing typed messages. On GenoTEX it reached 89.13% preprocessing composite score and 60.48% F1 for trait-associated gene identification, above prior systems.

papers.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Replication of Guideline-Based PGx Recommendations
papers.summary: This study assesses how well large language models can generate clinically accurate pharmacogenomic (PGx) recommendations aligned with CPIC guidelines. Using 599 curated gene–drug–phenotype scenarios and a novel expert-validated semantic metric (LLM Score), the authors show that general-purpose LLMs often produce incomplete or unsafe recommendations. In contrast, a domain-adapted, fine-tuned model achieves substantially better accuracy (LLM Score = 0.92) and faster inference. The results emphasize that fine-tuning and structured prompting are more critical than model scale alone for safe, effective AI-driven personalized medicine.

papers.title: Development and evaluation of an agentic LLM based RAG framework for evidence-based patient education
papers.summary: The paper describes the development and evaluation of an agentic retrieval augmented generation (ARAG) framework using open-source large language models for generating evidence-based Arabic patient education materials. The ARAG framework significantly improved the quality of generated patient education materials, especially when used with larger, context-aware models like AceGPT-v2-32B.

papers.name: Q4Dx
papers.title: Asking the Right Questions: Evaluating Diagnostic Dialogue with Q4Dx
papers.summary: This Q4Dx benchmark uses synthetic patient narratives and simulated physician-patient dialogues to measure how efficiently LLMs choose diagnostic questions. It scores whether models reach the right diagnosis while keeping questions few and short.

papers.name: GPT-RadPlan
papers.title: Automated radiotherapy treatment planning guided by GPT-4Vision
papers.summary: GPT-RadPlan is an automated radiotherapy treatment planning system that uses GPT-4Vision to iteratively refine treatment plans based on textual feedback, aiming to balance multiple objectives. It demonstrated superior performance compared to human-generated clinical plans in prostate and head & neck cancer cases, showing better target coverage and reduced organ-at-risk doses.

papers.name: ReasonAgent
papers.title: Multimodal reasoning agent for enhanced ophthalmic decision-making: a preliminary real-world clinical validation
papers.venue: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: ReasonAgent combines a multimodal image analysis module, knowledge retrieval and a diagnostic reasoning module for ophthalmic diagnosis and treatment planning. On 30 real cases its diagnostic accuracy was comparable to residents and its treatment plans were better than GPT-4o and residents.

papers.name: AgentMRI
papers.title: AgentMRI: A Vison Language Model-Powered AI System for Self-regulating MRI Reconstruction with Multiple Degradations
papers.venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
papers.summary: AgentMRI is an autonomous AI system that uses vision language models to detect and correct MRI image degradations, selecting the appropriate deep learning model for reconstruction without human intervention. It demonstrated high accuracy in both zero-shot and fine-tuned settings on a brain MRI dataset, showcasing its potential for scalable and intelligent MR image processing.

papers.name: P-MedAgent
papers.title: P-MedAgent:Medical diagnostics based on LLM programmable CoT
papers.summary: P-MedAgent is a specialized AI agent designed for medical data analysis tasks, transforming them into code generation problems to predict and classify outcomes. The system demonstrates high accuracy in various medical diagnostic tasks, achieving performance levels comparable to human experts.

papers.name: AURA
papers.title: AURA: A Multi-Modal Medical Agent for Understanding, Reasoning & Annotation
papers.summary: A Qwen-32B agent calls segmentation, counterfactual image generation and evaluation tools to analyse, explain and test hypotheses about medical images interactively. The work demonstrates the system as an explainability agent for chest imaging rather than reporting a large benchmark.

papers.title: Comparison of the Performance of Five Generative Artificial Intelligence Models on a Medical Molecular Biology Examination
papers.summary: This study compares the performance of five Chinese generative AI models on a medical molecular biology exam. Results show that several models outperform undergraduate students, while underscoring the need for critical evaluation and domain-specific AI systems in education.

papers.title: LLM-based approaches for automated vocabulary mapping between SIGTAP and OMOP CDM concepts
papers.summary: Compares an embedding-plus-retrieval pipeline with LLM agents that follow predefined mapping protocols and refine their queries, mapping Brazilian SIGTAP procedure and medicine codes to OMOP CDM concepts. Both reached similar F1, with the agent pipeline achieving better recall through dynamic query refinement.

papers.name: AtlasAgent
papers.title: AtlasAgent: Vision language model and Agent-guided Framework for Evaluation of Atlas-scale Single-cell Integration
papers.summary: AtlasAgent is a vision-language model and AI agent framework designed to evaluate large-scale single-cell data integration efficiently. It uses chain-of-thought reasoning and prompting strategies to assess batch correction quality, biological signal preservation, and overcorrection risks, significantly reducing evaluation time from hours to seconds while maintaining accuracy.

papers.name: Doctronic
papers.title: Toward the Autonomous AI Doctor: Quantitative Benchmarking of an Autonomous Agentic AI Versus Board-Certified Clinicians in a Real World Setting
papers.summary: Doctronic is a multi-agent AI system designed to autonomously function as an AI doctor in urgent care settings. The study shows that Doctronic achieves high diagnostic and treatment plan concordance with human clinicians, indicating its potential to address healthcare workforce shortages.

papers.name: Transplant-Agents
papers.title: Transplant-Agents : A Multi-Agent Artificial Intelligence Framework for Reproducibility Assessment of Post-Transplant Risk Prediction and Rejection Biomarkers
papers.summary: Transplant-Agents combines LLM agents with machine learning in rule-governed iterative dialogue to select reproducible biomarkers and predict transplant rejection risk. On 683 kidney, liver and heart transplant patients from ImmPort it reached AUROCs of 0.93, 0.88 and 0.88.

papers.name: ARMOA
papers.title: Agentic RAG-Driven Multi-Omics Analysis for PI3K/AKT Pathway Deregulation in Precision Medicine
papers.summary: ARMOA is an autonomous system that integrates retrieval-augmented generation, large language models, and agentic AI to analyze multi-omics data for the PI3K/AKT pathway. It demonstrated high accuracy in predicting therapeutic outcomes and identifying drug repurposing candidates through external testing and cross-validation.

papers.name: Infherno
papers.title: Infherno: End-to-end Agent-based FHIR Resource Synthesis from Free-form Clinical Notes
papers.summary: Infherno is an end-to-end framework that uses large language model agents to convert free-form clinical notes into structured FHIR resources, enhancing interoperability in healthcare. The system demonstrates strong performance on synthetic and real clinical datasets compared to human baselines.

papers.name: Dr.Copilot
papers.title: Dr.Copilot: A Multi-Agent Prompt Optimized Assistant for Improving Patient-Doctor Communication in Romanian
papers.summary: Dr. Copilot is a multi-agent system designed to improve the quality of written medical advice given by Romanian-speaking doctors, providing feedback on 17 communication-related axes. The system has been deployed in real-world telemedicine settings and shown measurable improvements in user reviews and response quality.

papers.title: Lessons Learned from Evaluation of LLM based Multi-agents in Safer Therapy Recommendation
papers.summary: The study evaluates the use of a Large Language Model (LLM)-based multi-agent system for safer therapy recommendations in patients with multimorbidity, comparing its performance to single-agent approaches and real-world benchmarks. The results indicate that while LLM-based systems can provide correct recommendations addressing clinical goals, they often produce incomplete advice or unnecessary medications leading to potential conflicts.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Adaptation of Large Language Models for Protein-Protein Interaction Analysis
papers.summary: This study introduces an uncertainty-aware framework for protein–protein interaction prediction using fine-tuned large language models. By integrating LoRA ensembles and Bayesian LoRA for uncertainty quantification, the approach improves the reliability and reproducibility of LLM-based PPI analysis across multiple disease contexts. The results highlight the importance of confidence-aware modeling for trustworthy applications of LLMs in precision medicine and computational biology.

papers.name: RDMA
papers.title: RDMA: Cost Effective Agent-Driven Rare Disease Mining from Electronic Health Records
papers.summary: RDMA is an agentic framework that uses smaller quantized language models to mine rare diseases from unstructured clinical notes, resolving abbreviations and grounding phenotypes against Orphanet and HPO ontologies. It outperforms baselines without task-specific training, significantly reducing inference costs and expert annotation burden.

papers.name: NAMD-Agent
papers.title: Automating MD simulations for Proteins using Large language Models: NAMD-Agent
papers.summary: NAMD-Agent is an automated pipeline that uses large language models and Python scripting to prepare, run, and analyze molecular dynamics simulations for proteins. It was evaluated across various biomolecular systems, demonstrating its ability to reproduce key metrics from published benchmarks while differing in efficiency and cost among different LLM orchestrators.

papers.name: DrugMCTS
papers.title: DrugMCTS: a drug repurposing framework combining multi-agent, RAG and Monte Carlo Tree Search
papers.summary: DrugMCTS combines retrieval, five specialized agents for molecular and protein evidence, and Monte Carlo tree search to reason about drug repositioning. On DrugBank and KIBA it achieved higher recall and robustness than general LLMs and deep learning baselines.

papers.name: DocCHA
papers.title: DocCHA: Towards LLM-Augmented Interactive Online diagnosis System
papers.summary: DocCHA is a modular framework that uses large language models to assist in clinical diagnosis through iterative dialogue, improving accuracy and symptom recall. It outperforms existing prompting-based LLMs on real-world datasets by refining reasoning links and prioritizing informative clarifications.

papers.name: PromptBio
papers.title: PromptBio: A Multi-Agent AI Platform for Bioinformatics Data Analysis
papers.summary: PromptBio is a modular AI platform that uses multi-agent systems to facilitate scalable and reproducible bioinformatics analysis, supporting both human-in-the-loop workflows and automated large-scale omics analysis. The system demonstrates its capability through the integration of specialized agents for data management, pipeline execution, and interactive summarization, alongside tools for machine learning and statistical interpretation.

papers.name: MedScrubCrew
papers.title: <i>MedScrubCrew</i>: A Medical Multi-Agent Framework for Automating Appointment Scheduling Based on Patient-Provider Profile Resource Matching
papers.summary: MedScrubCrew is a medical multi-agent framework that automates appointment scheduling and triage classification in healthcare settings. The system integrates the Gale-Shapley stable matching algorithm, knowledge graphs, and large language model-based agents to enhance operational efficiency and contextual relevance.

papers.title: Architecting Clinical Collaboration: Multi-Agent Reasoning Systems for Multimodal Medical VQA
papers.summary: Compares seven vision-language models under baseline, fine-tuned, multi-model consultation and literature-retrieval configurations for telemedicine dermatology questions. Fine-tuning often hurt, while the consultation and retrieval architectures reached up to 70 percent accuracy and held up on unseen data.

papers.name: openCHA
papers.title: Conversational health agents: a personalized large language model-powered agent framework
papers.summary: The paper introduces openCHA, an open-source framework for developing conversational health agents (CHAs) that leverage large language models. The system demonstrates its effectiveness in various healthcare tasks such as diabetic patient management and mental health chatbot evaluation, outperforming other LLMs like GPT-4.

papers.name: STELLA
papers.title: STELLA: Towards a Biomedical World Model with Self-Evolving Multimodal Agents
papers.summary: Manager, developer, critic and tool-creation agents update reasoning templates and grow their own tool collection, extending to robotic execution via vision-language-action models. It scored 4.01 of 5 on its tool-creation benchmark above GPT-5 and Biomni, identified BTN3A1 as a negative regulator of NK cell function confirmed by CRISPR knockout, and found an enzyme variant with doubled activity.

papers.name: AI-VaxGuide
papers.title: AI-VaxGuide: An Agentic RAG-Based LLM for Vaccination Decisions
papers.summary: A multilingual question-answering system applies agent-based multi-step retrieval over national and WHO vaccination guidelines and is delivered as a point-of-care mobile app. Agentic retrieval outperformed standard RAG, especially on multi-step or ambiguous questions.

papers.name: MESHAgents
papers.title: Multi-Agent Reasoning for Cardiovascular Imaging Phenotype Analysis
papers.summary: LLM agents acting as a multidisciplinary team iteratively propose, debate and settle on phenotypes and confounders for phenome-wide association analysis of heart and aorta imaging data. Its autonomously chosen phenotypes matched expert-selected ones on disease classification, with mean AUC differences near zero and better recall for six of nine diseases.

papers.name: KERAP
papers.title: KERAP: A Knowledge-Enhanced Reasoning Approach for Accurate Zero-shot Diagnosis Prediction Using Multi-agent LLMs
papers.venue: American Medical Informatics Association (AMIA) 2025 Annual Symposium, Oral
papers.summary: KERAP is a multi-agent system that uses knowledge graphs to enhance large language models for accurate zero-shot medical diagnosis prediction. It demonstrates improved diagnostic reliability and scalability compared to traditional LLMs by iteratively refining predictions through structured knowledge extraction.

papers.name: BioMARS
papers.title: BioMARS: A Multi-Agent Robotic System for Autonomous Biological Experiments
papers.summary: BioMARS is a multi-agent robotic system that integrates large language and vision models to autonomously design, plan, and execute biological experiments. It demonstrated the ability to match or exceed manual performance in cell culture tasks and supported context-aware optimization for differentiating retinal pigment epithelial cells.

papers.name: SciGym
papers.title: Measuring Scientific Capabilities of Language Models with a Systems Biology Dry Lab
papers.summary: SciGym is a dry-lab benchmark where LLMs iteratively design perturbation experiments on systems biology models encoded in SBML and interpret the simulated results. Six frontier models were tested on 137 systems, and all degraded sharply as system complexity grew.

papers.title: An LLM-Powered Agent for Physiological Data Analysis: A Case Study on PPG-based Heart Rate Estimation
papers.venue: Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. Annual International Conference
papers.summary: The LLM-Powered Agent is designed to analyze physiological time-series data, specifically for heart rate estimation from PPG signals. It demonstrates superior performance compared to benchmark models by integrating user interaction and analytical tools, achieving lower error rates in HR estimation.

papers.title: Towards Intelligent Agents for Radiotherapy: Integrating Exploration-Exploitation with Foundation Models
papers.venue: Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. Annual International Conference
papers.summary: The paper presents an automated radiotherapy treatment planning system that uses a reinforcement-learning framework with GPT-4V to optimize beam angles for better dose distribution. The study demonstrates the system's superior performance in prostate cancer cases compared to random selection and deep reinforcement learning baselines.

papers.name: Bio-Copilot
papers.title: A data-intelligence-intensive bioinformatics copilot system for large-scale omics research and scientific insights
papers.summary: Bio-Copilot is a multi-agent bioinformatics system with agent group management, human-agent interaction, a shared knowledge base and continual learning for large omics studies. It outperformed GPT-4o and other agents across bioinformatics tasks and reproduced and extended a human lung cell atlas.

papers.name: AI-HOPE
papers.title: AI-HOPE: an AI-driven conversational agent for enhanced clinical and genomic data integration in precision medicine research
papers.summary: AI-HOPE is an AI-driven conversational agent that integrates clinical and genomic data to support precision medicine research through natural language interactions. It demonstrated its utility by identifying significant genetic associations in colorectal cancer data, aligning with established literature.

papers.name: STELLA
papers.title: STELLA: Self-Evolving LLM Agent for Biomedical Research
papers.summary: STELLA is a self-evolving AI agent designed for biomedical research that uses a multi-agent architecture to autonomously improve its capabilities. It demonstrated superior performance on several biomedical benchmarks and showed significant improvement in accuracy with increased trials, indicating its potential for dynamic scaling of expertise.

papers.title: AutoPM3: Enhancing Variant Interpretation via LLM-driven PM3 Evidence Extraction from Scientific Literature
papers.summary: This paper introduces AutoPM3, an automated framework that extracts ACMG/AMP PM3 variant evidence from biomedical literature to support rare disease diagnosis. Using open-source LLMs combined with a Text2SQL-based variant extractor and a retrieval-augmented generation module, AutoPM3 efficiently processes both text and tables. Evaluated on the newly curated PM3-Bench dataset, the method achieves high accuracy and recall, outperforming approaches that rely on larger models. The results show that open-source LLMs can provide fast, cost-effective, and scalable solutions for literature-based variant interpretation.

papers.title: GOLF: A Generative AI Framework for Pathogenicity Prediction of Myocilin OLF Variants
papers.summary: This work introduces GOLF, a generative AI framework for predicting and interpreting the pathogenicity of MYOC OLF domain variants associated with glaucoma. By combining generative models with sparse autoencoders, the framework achieves accurate classification while revealing underlying biochemical features driving predictions.

papers.name: AgentDistill
papers.title: AgentDistill: Training-Free Agent Distillation with Generalizable MCP Boxes
papers.summary: AgentDistill is a framework for distilling knowledge from large language model-based agents to smaller models without training, using reusable task-solving modules called MCP boxes. The system demonstrates its effectiveness in biomedical and mathematical tasks by achieving performance comparable to advanced systems with minimal supervision.

papers.name: LA-CDM
papers.title: Language Agents for Hypothesis-driven Clinical Decision Making with Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: LA-CDM is a language agent designed to support clinical decision-making by iteratively requesting and interpreting relevant tests to converge towards an accurate diagnosis. The system demonstrates improved diagnostic performance and efficiency through a hybrid training paradigm that combines supervised and reinforcement learning.

papers.name: INSPIRE
papers.title: Agent-guided AI-powered interpretation and reporting of nerve conduction studies and EMG (INSPIRE)
papers.venue: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: Three agents consult reference tables and a long-context neuromuscular textbook to integrate patient history, complaints and electrodiagnostic findings into standardized reports. It classified tests as normal or abnormal with 92.2 percent accuracy versus 62.6 percent for one-shot LLM inference.

papers.title: Enhancing hepatopathy clinical trial efficiency: a secure, large language model-powered pre-screening pipeline
papers.summary: The paper presents a pre-screening pipeline for clinical trials involving complex liver diseases, using large language models to interpret semantically complex criteria from electronic health records. The system demonstrates high precision and good recall in patient recruitment, with different pathways excelling in specific aspects of reasoning and data extraction.

papers.name: DeepSeq
papers.title: DeepSeq: High-Throughput Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Data Labeling via Web Search-Augmented Agentic Generative AI Foundation Models
papers.venue: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML). Workshop on Multi-modal Foundation Models and Large Language Models for Life Sciences (FM4LS), July 2025
papers.summary: DeepSeq is an AI system that uses web search and generative models to automatically label single-cell RNA sequencing data, achieving high accuracy. It demonstrates the potential of agentic foundation models in overcoming bottlenecks in biological data annotation by reducing reliance on manual curation.

papers.title: Tiered Agentic Oversight: A Hierarchical Multi-Agent System for Healthcare Safety
papers.summary: Tiered Agentic Oversight (TAO) is a hierarchical multi-agent system designed to enhance AI safety in clinical settings by routing tasks to specialized agents based on complexity. The system was shown to outperform single-agent and other multi-agent systems across multiple healthcare safety benchmarks, with human validation confirming its effectiveness in improving medical triage accuracy.

papers.title: Exploring the Potential of AI-powered Applications for Clinical Decision-making in Gynecologic Oncology
papers.summary: This study evaluates GPT-4 for automated therapy recommendations by comparing its suggestions with multidisciplinary tumor board decisions for gynecologic and breast cancer cases. GPT-4 generated coherent and clinically reasonable recommendations, though limitations in accuracy and completeness remained, particularly in surgical and systemic treatment choices. Iterative prompting substantially improved concordance with expert decisions, indicating that GPT-4 may serve as a supportive tool in clinical decision making rather than a replacement for physicians.

papers.name: MCP-FHIR
papers.title: Enhancing Clinical Decision Support and EHR Insights through LLMs and the Model Context Protocol: An Open-Source MCP-FHIR Framework
papers.summary: The MCP-FHIR framework integrates large language models with HL7 FHIR data to enhance clinical decision support and EHR insights, enabling real-time summarization and personalized communication. It is evaluated using synthetic EHR data from SMART Health IT sandbox for privacy and reproducibility.

papers.title: Importance of Prior Patient Interactions With the Healthcare System to Engaging With Pretest Cancer Genetic Services via Digital Health Tools Among Unaffected Primary Care Patients: Findings From the BRIDGE Trial
papers.summary: This randomized trial examined factors associated with opening patient portal messages about cancer genetic services and initiating pretest genetic care. Engagement was strongly driven by prior interaction with the healthcare system, such as frequent portal use and primary care visits, while sociodemographic and clinical characteristics showed no significant effects. The findings suggest that improving access to healthcare and digital tools may be key to increasing uptake of cancer genetic services.

papers.title: Multi-agent AI System for High Quality Metadata Curation at Scale
papers.summary: The paper introduces a multi-agent AI system that uses large language models to curate high-quality metadata from biomedical datasets and associated publications, achieving both precision and scalability. The system outperforms existing automated methods in terms of recall on key metadata fields, demonstrating its potential for downstream applications like classifier model development.

papers.name: NordDRG-AI-Benchmark
papers.title: The NordDRG AI Benchmark for Large Language Models
papers.summary: NordDRG-AI-Benchmark is a public benchmark designed to evaluate large language models' ability to perform Diagnosis-Related Group (DRG) reasoning, which is crucial for clinical decision support and hospital funding. The benchmark includes logic and grouper tasks that assess the models' capability in DRG coding and full grouper emulation with strict exact-match scoring.

papers.name: PhenoGraph
papers.title: PhenoGraph: A Multi-Agent Framework for Phenotype-driven Discovery in Spatial Transcriptomics Data Augmented with Knowledge Graphs
papers.summary: PhenoGraph is a multi-agent LLM system that finds phenotype-annotated cohorts, aligns them with spatial transcriptomics data, and selects, runs and corrects analysis pipelines with knowledge graph support. It was demonstrated across several tumor microenvironment datasets and phenotype classes.

papers.name: MedChat
papers.title: MedChat: A Multi-Agent Framework for Multimodal Diagnosis with Large Language Models
papers.venue: Proc. 2025 IEEE 8th International Conference on Multimedia Information Processing and Retrieval (MIPR), pp. 456-462, 2025
papers.summary: A director agent coordinates glaucoma detection models and several role-specific LLM agents to produce diagnostic reports through an interface for clinical review and teaching. The authors report that the multi-agent design improves reliability and reduces hallucination compared with a single generalist agent.

papers.name: HEAL-KGGen
papers.title: HEAL-KGGen: A Hierarchical Multi-Agent LLM Framework with Knowledge Graph Enhancement for Genetic Biomarker-Based Medical Diagnosis
papers.summary: HEAL-KGGen routes genetic biomarker questions from a general practitioner agent to genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics and clinical specialist agents grounded in an automatically built ontology-aligned knowledge graph. It improved question-answering accuracy across several LLMs, by up to 43.75% for Claude 3.5 Sonnet.

papers.name: OriGene
papers.title: OriGene: A Self-Evolving Virtual Disease Biologist Automating Therapeutic Target Discovery
papers.summary: OriGene is a self-evolving multi-agent system that integrates over 600 specialized tools to identify therapeutic targets by reasoning across diverse data modalities. It demonstrated superior performance in accuracy and robustness compared to human experts and other AI models, and nominated previously underexplored therapeutic targets for liver and colorectal cancer with significant anti-tumor activity.

papers.title: Development and validation of an autonomous artificial intelligence agent for clinical decision-making in oncology
papers.summary: A GPT-4 agent combines vision transformers for MSI and KRAS/BRAF detection, MedSAM segmentation and searches of OncoKB, PubMed and Google for oncology decisions. On 20 multimodal cases it selected tools correctly 87.5% of the time and raised decision accuracy from 30.3% for GPT-4 alone to 87.2%.

papers.name: ChatMyopia
papers.title: ChatMyopia: An AI Agent for Pre-consultation Education in Primary Eye Care Settings
papers.summary: ChatMyopia is an AI agent designed to provide personalized education and information about myopia, integrating image classification and a knowledge base. It demonstrated high accuracy and patient satisfaction in clinical settings compared to traditional educational materials.

papers.name: Agentomics-ML
papers.title: Agentomics-ML: Autonomous Machine Learning Experimentation Agent for Genomic and Transcriptomic Data
papers.summary: Agentomics-ML autonomously builds classification models for genomic and transcriptomic datasets by working through predefined machine learning steps via shell commands and reflecting on validation metrics. It produces the trained model plus files needed for reproducible training and inference.

papers.name: AutoCT
papers.title: AUTOCT: Automating Interpretable Clinical Trial Prediction with LLM Agents
papers.summary: AutoCT is a framework that uses large language models to predict clinical trial outcomes, combining reasoning capabilities with explainability through iterative refinement. It demonstrates superior or comparable performance to state-of-the-art methods while maintaining interpretability and cost-efficiency.

papers.name: MedAgentGym
papers.title: MedAgentGym: A Scalable Agentic Training Environment for Code-Centric Reasoning in Biomedical Data Science
papers.summary: MedAgentGym is a training environment of 72,413 coding tasks from 12 real biomedical data science scenarios in executable sandboxes with verifiable answers and trajectory generation. Benchmarking 29 LLMs showed large gaps, and its Med-Copilot gained over 43% from offline and online reinforcement learning.

papers.title: AI Agents for Conversational Patient Triage: Preliminary Simulation-Based Evaluation with Real-World EHR Data
papers.summary: The paper describes a Patient Simulator that uses real-world EHR data to create realistic patient scenarios for training and testing AI agents in clinical decision support. The simulator was validated by expert clinicians who found it consistent with actual patient encounters, demonstrating its potential as an evaluation tool for conversational AI agents.

papers.name: MoodAngels
papers.title: MoodAngels: A Retrieval-augmented Multi-agent Framework for Psychiatry Diagnosis
papers.summary: Agents analyse clinical assessment items in detail, retrieve similar cases and pass conclusions through a structured verification step to diagnose mood disorders, alongside a released synthetic dataset of 1,173 cases. Its baseline agent beat GPT-4o by 12.3 percent on real cases and the full multi-agent system improved further.

papers.title: Biomni: A General-Purpose Biomedical AI Agent
papers.summary: This paper introduces Biomni, a general purpose biomedical AI agent designed to autonomously execute complex research tasks across diverse biomedical domains. By integrating large language model reasoning with retrieval augmented planning and code based execution, Biomni demonstrates strong generalization across tasks such as gene prioritization, drug repurposing, and rare disease diagnosis without task specific tuning. The results suggest that agentic AI systems can substantially enhance biomedical research productivity and support human scientists in complex discovery workflows.

papers.title: MEGA-GPT: Artificial Intelligence Guidance and Building Analytical Protocols Using MEGA Software
papers.summary: This study introduces MEGA-GPT, a retrieval-augmented, AI-driven assistant designed to help users navigate the increasingly complex functionalities of the MEGA evolutionary genetics software through natural language queries. By integrating MEGA documentation and version-specific resources, MEGA-GPT provides step-by-step guidance, clarifies analytical settings, and recommends optimal workflows while significantly reducing hallucinations compared with standard ChatGPT. The tool improves usability for both novice and experienced users and demonstrates how customized RAG-based assistants can enhance complex scientific software.

papers.name: KODA
papers.title: KODA: An Agentic Framework for KEGG Orthology-Driven Discovery of Antimicrobial Drug Targets in Gut Microbiome
papers.summary: KODA is an agentic framework that uses large language models and knowledge graphs to discover antimicrobial drug targets in the gut microbiome. It demonstrates its efficacy by identifying conserved essential genes as potential drug targets, thereby providing actionable insights for antimicrobial research.

papers.name: CHATCBD
papers.title: Taming Unleashed Large Language Models With Blockchain for Massive Personalized Reliable Healthcare
papers.venue: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: The CHATCBD system uses blockchain technology to enhance the reliability of large language models in personalized healthcare, addressing issues like hallucinations and ensuring patient safety. It includes a controllable AI agent framework and a self-audit mechanism that improves decision-making and audit professionalism.

papers.name: MMedAgent-RL
papers.title: MMedAgent-RL: Optimizing Multi-Agent Collaboration for Multimodal Medical Reasoning
papers.summary: Trains a triage agent to route cases to specialty agents and an attending agent to integrate their opinions, using curriculum-guided reinforcement learning on Qwen2.5-VL. On five medical VQA benchmarks it gained 23.6 percent on average over strong baselines.

papers.name: Potato Knowledge Hub
papers.title: An AI-powered Knowledge Hub for Potato Functional Genomics
papers.summary: The Potato Knowledge Hub is a platform that uses large language models and curated research papers to provide accurate gene information and specialized knowledge about potatoes. It includes a functional gene database and a retrieval-augmented generation knowledge base, which mitigates LLM hallucination by providing literature citations for answers.

papers.name: MedOrch
papers.title: MedOrch: Medical Diagnosis with Tool-Augmented Reasoning Agents for Flexible Extensibility
papers.summary: An agent-based architecture plugs in domain-specific tools and keeps traceable intermediate reasoning for diagnosis across modalities. It reached 93.26 percent accuracy on Alzheimer's diagnosis, over four points above the prior best, and was also evaluated on chest X-rays and multimodal question answering.

papers.title: Large Language Model-Based Agents for Automated Research Reproducibility: An Exploratory Study in Alzheimer's Disease
papers.summary: A simulated team of GPT-4o agents was asked to write and run code reproducing findings from five highly cited Alzheimer's studies using the NACC dataset, given only abstracts, methods and the data dictionary. The agents approximately reproduced 53.2% of the 35 extracted findings, often differing in numeric values and statistical choices.

papers.name: Consensus Mechanism
papers.title: Second Opinion Matters: Towards Adaptive Clinical AI via the Consensus of Expert Model Ensemble
papers.summary: The Consensus Mechanism is a clinical decision support system that uses an ensemble of specialized medical expert agents to improve accuracy and robustness. It demonstrated superior performance compared to single-model systems across multiple benchmarks, including differential diagnosis tasks.

papers.name: CDR-Agent
papers.title: CDR-Agent: Intelligent Selection and Execution of Clinical Decision Rules Using Large Language Model Agents
papers.summary: CDR-Agent is a large language model-based system that autonomously selects and applies the most appropriate clinical decision rules based on unstructured clinical notes to enhance emergency department decision-making. The system demonstrated significant improvements in accuracy and efficiency compared to standalone LLMs, reducing unnecessary medical interventions while effectively identifying positively diagnosed cases.

papers.title: Integrating large language model-based agents into a virtual patient chatbot for clinical anamnesis training
papers.summary: The Virtual Patient Chatbot integrates large language model-based agents to simulate patient interactions for clinical anamnesis training, offering a flexible and scalable solution. Evaluations demonstrated its effectiveness in providing consistent and plausible responses, with high usability scores indicating its potential as a valuable educational tool.

papers.name: GeneBreaker
papers.title: GeneBreaker: Jailbreak Attacks against DNA Language Models with Pathogenicity Guidance
papers.summary: A safety-evaluation framework in which an LLM agent with bioinformatics tools probes whether DNA generative models can be steered past their safety behaviour, scored automatically against a reference database. The audit found current models are vulnerable and that larger models carry greater dual-use risk, motivating stronger safety alignment and provenance tracing.

papers.name: PerTurboAgent
papers.title: PerTurboAgent: A Self-Planning Agent for Boosting Sequential Perturb-seq Experiments
papers.summary: An LLM agent analyses Perturb-seq data, retrieves prior knowledge, runs statistical and predictive tools and proposes the gene panel for the next experimental round. It supports iterative screen design by prioritising perturbations under a fixed experimental budget.

papers.name: Catfish Agent
papers.title: Silence is Not Consensus: Disrupting Agreement Bias in Multi-Agent LLMs via Catfish Agent for Clinical Decision Making
papers.summary: Adds a role-specialised agent that challenges an emerging diagnosis, modulating how strongly it intervenes by case complexity and calibrating its tone. Across nine medical question answering and three medical VQA benchmarks it beat single- and multi-agent frameworks including GPT-4o and DeepSeek-R1.

papers.name: FUAS-Agents
papers.title: FUAS-Agents: Autonomous Multi-Modal LLM Agents for Treatment Planning in Focused Ultrasound Ablation Surgery
papers.summary: FUAS-Agents is an autonomous system that uses large language models to assist in treatment planning for focused ultrasound ablation surgery, integrating patient data and MRI images with specialized medical tools. The system was evaluated by clinical experts who rated its generated plans highly in terms of completeness, accuracy, fluency, and compliance.

papers.name: MT-Mol
papers.title: MT-Mol:Multi Agent System with Tool-based Reasoning for Molecular Optimization
papers.summary: MT-Mol is a multi-agent system designed for molecular optimization that integrates large language models with RDKit tools to enhance structured reasoning and interpretability. The system demonstrates superior performance on the PMO-1K benchmark, showcasing its effectiveness in generating high-quality molecules through collaborative interactions between specialized agents.

papers.name: AI-HOPE-PI3K
papers.title: From Mutation to Prognosis: AI-HOPE-PI3K Enables Artificial Intelligence-Agent Driven Integration of PI3K Pathway Data in Colorectal Cancer Precision Medicine
papers.summary: A fine-tuned LLaMA 3 system turns natural-language questions into executable statistical pipelines over cBioPortal colorectal cancer data, building cohorts and running survival and mutation analyses. It reproduced known PI3K pathway associations in early-onset colorectal cancer and compared well with existing platforms.

papers.name: AI-HOPE-TP53
papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Agent: AI-HOPE-TP53 Enables Pathway-Centric Analysis of TP53-Driven Molecular Alterations in Colorectal Cancer Precision Oncology
papers.summary: AI-HOPE-TP53 is a conversational agent that turns natural-language questions into executable cBioPortal analyses of TP53 pathway alterations in colorectal cancer. It supports stratification by age, ancestry, MSI status, treatment and stage with mutation, co-mutation, survival and odds ratio analyses.

papers.name: MRGAgents
papers.title: MRGAgents: A Multi-Agent Framework for Improved Medical Report Generation with Med-LVLMs
papers.summary: MRGAgents is a multi-agent framework designed to improve medical report generation by fine-tuning specialized agents for different disease categories, addressing the limitations of existing models that often overlook critical abnormalities. The system demonstrates improved comprehensiveness and diagnostic utility in generated reports compared to state-of-the-art methods.

papers.name: Moremi Bio Agent
papers.title: Can Large Language Models Design Biological Weapons? Evaluating Moremi Bio
papers.summary: The authors prompted the Moremi Bio biodesign agent with its safety guardrails removed and examined the toxicity of what it produced, finding generated proteins computationally resembling known toxins. They use this dual-use assessment to argue for layered safeguards in LLM-enabled biodesign pipelines.

papers.name: AI-HOPE-TGFbeta
papers.title: AI-HOPE-TGFbeta: A Conversational AI Agent for Integrative Clinical and Genomic Analysis of TGF-β Pathway Alterations in Colorectal Cancer to Advance Precision Medicine
papers.summary: AI-HOPE-TGFbeta couples an LLM, a natural-language-to-code interpreter and a bioinformatics backend to analyze TGF-beta pathway alterations in colorectal cancer using harmonized clinical and genomic data. It enables cohort stratification and hypothesis testing aimed at underrepresented populations.

papers.name: BehaveAgent
papers.title: An autonomous AI agent for universal behavior analysis
papers.summary: BehaveAgent is an autonomous AI agent designed to analyze behavior from video inputs across various species without the need for retraining or manual intervention. It demonstrates its capability by autonomously identifying behavioral paradigms, tracking subjects and objects, executing targeted analysis, and generating comprehensive research reports.

papers.name: MedBrowseComp
papers.title: MedBrowseComp: Benchmarking Medical Deep Research and Computer Use
papers.summary: Over 1,000 human-curated questions require agents to retrieve and reconcile multi-hop facts from live medical knowledge bases on trials, studies, regulation and cost. Frontier agentic systems scored as low as ten percent on some subsets.

papers.name: MedAgentBoard
papers.title: MedAgentBoard: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Collaboration with Conventional Methods for Diverse Medical Tasks
papers.summary: Compares multi-agent collaboration with single LLMs and conventional models on medical QA and VQA, lay summaries, EHR prediction and clinical workflow automation. Multi-agent setups helped task completeness in workflow automation but did not consistently beat strong single LLMs or specialized conventional methods.

papers.name: LITERAS
papers.title: LITERAS: Biomedical literature review and citation retrieval agents
papers.summary: Agents search MEDLINE through the PubMed API and communicate bidirectionally to draft literature reviews with verifiable citations across five medical fields. Citation accuracy was 99.82 percent, similar to Perplexity Sonar, and referencing accuracy was higher at 96.81 percent.

papers.title: Case Study of Using AI as Co-Pilot in Biotech Research: Functional Network Analysis of Invasive Cancer
papers.summary: The study uses AI tools like ChatGPT and GitHub Copilot to assist in the analysis of functional protein networks in invasive colorectal cancer, showing that while these systems can improve efficiency, they require human oversight for complex tasks. The research highlights the limitations of current AI in fully automating biotech studies due to issues with data accuracy and system stability.

papers.title: A Multimodal Multi-Agent Framework for Radiology Report Generation
papers.summary: Task-specific agents handle retrieval, draft writing, visual analysis, refinement and synthesis in sequence to generate radiology reports. It outperformed a strong baseline on automatic metrics and LLM-based evaluation.

papers.name: Intelliscope
papers.title: Automating AI Discovery for Biomedicine Through Knowledge Graphs And LLM Agents
papers.summary: Intelliscope integrates knowledge graphs with large language models to facilitate biomedical discovery by identifying relevant pathways between entities and designing AI predictors for these pathways. The system also proposes wet-lab experiments for validation, demonstrating its capability in accelerating scientific discoveries across various therapeutic areas.

papers.name: PhenoAssistant
papers.title: PhenoAssistant: A Conversational Multi-Agent AI System for Automated Plant Phenotyping
papers.summary: PhenoAssistant uses an LLM to orchestrate a curated toolkit for plant phenotype extraction, visualization and model training through natural language. It was validated on representative case studies and a set of evaluation tasks.

papers.name: CellTypeAgent
papers.title: CellTypeAgent: Trustworthy cell type annotation with Large Language Models
papers.summary: CellTypeAgent is an LLM agent that annotates cell types and verifies its calls against marker databases to limit hallucinated labels. It was tested on nine datasets covering 303 cell types from 36 tissues and was more accurate than existing methods.

papers.name: SAMIRA
papers.title: Towards user-centered interactive medical image segmentation in VR with an assistive AI agent
papers.summary: SAMIRA is an AI agent designed for medical image segmentation in virtual reality, assisting users with tasks such as localization and visualization of 3D medical concepts through speech-based interaction. The system was evaluated in a user study where it demonstrated high usability and potential for training radiologists in complex segmentation tasks.

papers.title: SleepBert: An Intelligent Clinical Encyclopaedia for Sleep Disorders Using Large Language Models
papers.summary: This paper introduces SleepBert, a retrieval augmented model that integrates structured polysomnography features with unstructured clinical narratives for comprehensive sleep disorder analysis. By fine tuning ClinicalBERT and incorporating real time medical literature retrieval, SleepBert achieves substantially higher diagnostic accuracy than existing baselines. The system supports scalable and evidence based interpretation of complex sleep data to assist clinical decision making and research.

papers.title: Performance of single-agent and multi-agent language models in Spanish language medical competency exams
papers.summary: Tests GPT-4o on 1,062 Chilean licensure questions under single-agent prompting strategies and multi-agent strategies including voting, MedAgents and MDAgents. MDAgents scored highest at about 90 percent, though simpler strategies sufficed for many questions.

papers.title: Assessing large language model performance related to aging in genetic conditions
papers.summary: This study evaluates whether large language models (Llama-2-70B-chat and GPT-3.5) can generate plausible clinical vignettes, clinician–patient dialogues, and management plans for pediatric and adult presentations across 282 genetic conditions. Clinician grading showed that both models generally produced age-appropriate descriptions with good correctness and completeness for disease presentation, including for neonatal-onset metabolic disorders. However, both models performed substantially worse when generating management plans, with only moderate correctness and completeness. These findings suggest that while LLMs can capture age-dependent clinical features, their reliability for clinical decision-making and management remains limited.

papers.name: ARIEL
papers.title: Advancing AI Research Assistants with Expert-Involved Learning
papers.summary: ARIEL is an evaluation and optimization framework that uses expert-vetted tasks to assess the capabilities of AI models in biomedical research, focusing on summarization and figure interpretation. The system demonstrates improvements through prompt engineering and fine-tuning, showing potential for generating testable hypotheses by integrating textual and visual information.

papers.title: Automatic Biomarker Discovery and Enrichment with BRAD
papers.summary: Integrating large language models with biomedical research tools raises challenges in transparency, reproducibility, and data provenance. This work introduces BRAD, an agent-based system that combines LLMs with external tools and databases to automate research workflows while maintaining transparent and reliable protocols. Applied to biomarker discovery and other tasks, BRAD enables contextualized interpretation and automation that exceed conventional bioinformatics tools.

papers.name: mAIstro
papers.title: mAIstro: an open-source multi-agentic system for automated end-to-end development of radiomics and deep learning models for medical imaging
papers.summary: mAIstro is an open-source, multi-agentic system that automates the end-to-end development of medical AI models using a natural language interface. It successfully executed various tasks across diverse datasets and imaging modalities, demonstrating its capability to unify data analysis, model development, and inference in healthcare applications.

papers.title: Knowledge-Driven Agentic Scientific Corpus Distillation Framework for Biomedical Large Language Models Training
papers.summary: The paper introduces a multi-agent framework for distilling high-quality biomedical data from scientific literature, enhancing the training of large language models in biomedicine. The system demonstrates significant improvements in question-answering tasks compared to existing models and baselines.

papers.name: Deep Thought
papers.title: Can AI Agents Design and Implement Drug Discovery Pipelines?
papers.summary: The paper introduces the DO Challenge, a benchmark for evaluating AI agents' decision-making in drug discovery. The Deep Thought multi-agent system was developed to participate in this challenge and showed strong performance but still fell short of expert-designed solutions, highlighting both potential and limitations of AI-driven methodologies in molecular drug design.

papers.title: Comprehensive molecular analyses of an autoimmune-related gene predictive model and immune infiltrations using machine learning methods in intracranial aneurysma
papers.summary: This study investigates the genetic links between autoimmune processes and intracranial aneurysm (IA) by integrating transcriptomic data, functional enrichment analyses, and multiple machine-learning approaches. Two key autoimmune-related diagnostic genes, ADIPOQ and IL21R, were identified and used to build a neural-network model with strong predictive performance (AUC = 0.944). The results highlight immune infiltration and gene–miRNA–drug regulatory networks as important contributors to IA pathogenesis, suggesting potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Learning to Be A Doctor: Searching for Effective Medical Agent Architectures
papers.summary: The paper presents a framework for the automated design of medical agent architectures using large language models, aiming to improve diagnostic accuracy in clinical settings. The proposed method demonstrates effectiveness in evolving workflow structures and enhancing diagnostic performance through iterative self-improvement guided by feedback.

papers.name: MD2GPS
papers.title: An LLM-Driven Multi-Agent Debate System for Mendelian Diseases
papers.summary: MD2GPS is a multi-agent debate system that uses language models to enhance the accuracy of diagnosing Mendelian diseases by integrating data-driven and knowledge-driven approaches. The system was evaluated on multiple datasets, demonstrating improved diagnostic accuracy and reduced time for identifying potential pathogenic genes.

papers.title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics
papers.summary: This work presents a comprehensive map of human subcellular architecture by integrating biophysical interaction data and immunofluorescence imaging for over 5,100 proteins. Using self-supervised multimodal learning and large language model–assisted annotation, the study identifies hundreds of molecular assemblies, reveals new protein functions, decodes cancer-associated alterations, and provides a public platform for structural and functional cell biology research.

papers.title: Change of Heart: Can Artificial Intelligence Transform Infective Endocarditis Management?
papers.summary: This review summarizes how artificial intelligence is increasingly applied to the diagnosis and management of infective endocarditis, a clinically complex and high-morbidity disease. Machine learning models and AI-enhanced imaging and microbiological techniques show improved accuracy in diagnosis, risk stratification, pathogen identification, and outcome prediction compared with traditional approaches. Despite these promising results, challenges remain in data availability, interpretability, ethics, and clinical validation. The authors conclude that carefully integrated and validated AI, including generative AI as decision-support tools, could substantially improve patient outcomes and safety in infective endocarditis care.

papers.name: P3GPT
papers.title: LLMs and AI Life Models for Traditional Chinese Medicine-derived Geroprotector Formulation
papers.summary: The paper introduces P3GPT, an AI agent-driven framework that integrates a multi-omics transformer model with TCM compound-target interaction databases to identify potential geroprotectors from traditional Chinese medicine. It demonstrates the system's ability to bridge ancient therapeutic knowledge with modern pharmacology by identifying promising TCM formulations for age-related diseases.

papers.name: TxGemma
papers.title: TxGemma: Efficient and Agentic LLMs for Therapeutics
papers.summary: TxGemma is a suite of large language models fine-tuned for therapeutic development tasks, demonstrating superior performance in predicting properties and adverse events compared to existing models. It also includes conversational agents that provide mechanistic reasoning and engage in scientific discussions, enhancing its utility in drug discovery.

papers.name: Fleming
papers.title: Fleming: An AI Agent for Antibiotic Design for Mycobacterium tuberculosis
papers.summary: Fleming is an agent for tuberculosis antibiotic lead discovery that combines trained inhibition classifiers, generative models, molecular optimization, ADMET prediction and literature search. It separated known Mtb leads from others better than a generic LLM agent and its predicted inhibitors showed an 83% in vitro hit rate.

papers.name: scAgent
papers.title: scAgent: Universal Single-Cell Annotation via a LLM Agent
papers.summary: scAgent is a large language model-based framework designed to annotate and discover novel cell types from single-cell RNA-seq data across various tissues. The system demonstrates superior performance in general cell-type annotation, novel cell discovery, and extensibility to new cell types compared to existing methods.

papers.title: SpatialAgent: An Autonomous AI Agent for Spatial Biology
papers.summary: This paper introduces SpatialAgent, a fully autonomous AI agent designed to support end to end spatial biology research by integrating large language models with adaptive reasoning and dynamic tool use. Evaluated on large scale human and mouse spatial datasets, SpatialAgent outperforms existing computational methods and matches or exceeds human performance on key tasks. The study demonstrates a new paradigm for scalable and collaborative AI driven discovery in spatial biology.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics AI agent charts hPSC-pancreas maturation in vivo
papers.summary: This work introduces STAgent, an autonomous multimodal AI agent that integrates large language models with specialized computational tools to automate complex spatial transcriptomics analyses. Applied to human stem cell–derived pancreatic tissues, STAgent rapidly uncovers spatial maturation patterns, cell–cell interactions, and underlying biological mechanisms while contextualizing findings with relevant literature. The results demonstrate a new agentic paradigm that dramatically reduces analysis time and expertise barriers in spatial biology research.

papers.name: OLAF
papers.title: OLAF: An Open Life Science Analysis Framework for Conversational Bioinformatics Powered by Large Language Models
papers.summary: OLAF is an open-source platform that uses large language models to enable researchers to perform bioinformatics analyses through natural language commands. It demonstrated the ability to execute complex bioinformatics workflows, including single-cell RNA-seq analysis and gene annotation, making computational biology more accessible to non-programmers.

papers.title: PCMR: A Comprehensive Precancerous Molecular Resource
papers.summary: This study introduces the PreCancerous Molecular Resource (PCMR), a large integrated database compiling multi-omics molecular profiles of precancerous lesions across diverse cancer types and tissues. By combining differential analysis with ChatGPT-based text mining, PCMR systematically identifies precancer–gene associations and validates their biological and clinical relevance. The resource provides a comprehensive foundation for studying early carcinogenesis and advancing precancer research and intervention.

papers.name: GeneWhisperer
papers.title: GeneWhisperer: Enhancing manual genome annotation with large language models
papers.summary: GeneWhisperer is a system that uses large language models to assist in the manual annotation of gene functions, aiming to enhance human expertise and efficiency. It demonstrates improved accuracy and speed in genome annotation tasks through its conversational interface and integration with relevant bioinformatics tools.

papers.name: AI-HOPE-PM
papers.title: Conversational Artificial Intelligence for Translational Precision Medicine: Integrating Social Determinants of Health, Genomics, and Clinical Data with AI-HOPE-PM
papers.summary: AI-HOPE-PM is a conversational AI platform that integrates genomic, clinical, and social determinants of health data to enable users to conduct multi-dimensional cancer analyses through natural language interaction. The system successfully demonstrated its capability by identifying significant differences in survival outcomes influenced by genetic mutations and socio-economic factors.

papers.name: PharmAgents
papers.title: PharmAgents: Building a Virtual Pharma with Large Language Model Agents
papers.summary: PharmAgents is a virtual pharmaceutical ecosystem that uses large language model agents to streamline and accelerate the drug discovery process, from target identification to preclinical evaluation. The system demonstrates its potential by identifying therapeutic targets, discovering lead compounds, and conducting in silico analyses for toxicity and synthetic feasibility.

papers.name: MedAgentSim
papers.title: Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Simulations for Realistic Clinical Interactions
papers.summary: MedAgentSim is a simulated clinical environment that evaluates and enhances large language models' performance in dynamic diagnostic settings through multi-agent interactions. It demonstrates the effectiveness of its approach by showing improved diagnostic strategies and context-aware interaction abilities in various simulated scenarios.

papers.title: Exploring new drug treatment targets for immune related bone diseases using a multi omics joint analysis strategy
papers.summary: This study applies an integrated multi-omic Mendelian randomization framework to identify causal plasma protein targets for immune-related bone diseases. By combining MR, SMR, Bayesian colocalization, LDSC, and downstream network and drug analyses, the authors systematically uncover disease-specific therapeutic targets across rheumatoid arthritis, multiple sclerosis, psoriatic arthritis, and Crohn’s disease–related arthritis. The results provide robust genetic evidence for key proteins underlying disease pathogenesis and offer a strong foundation for precision drug discovery in immune-associated bone disorders.

papers.name: MedAgent-Pro
papers.title: MedAgent-Pro: Towards Evidence-Based Multi-Modal Medical Diagnosis via Reasoning Agentic Workflow
papers.summary: MedAgent-Pro is a hierarchical reasoning system that uses multi-modal inputs and clinical criteria to generate reliable diagnostic plans for medical conditions. It demonstrates superior performance in both 2D and 3D medical diagnosis tasks, providing precise and explainable diagnoses.

papers.name: DEMENTIA-PLAN
papers.title: DEMENTIA-PLAN: An Agent-Based Framework for Multi-Knowledge Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Dementia Care
papers.summary: DEMENTIA-PLAN is a retrieval-augmented generation framework that uses large language models and multiple knowledge graphs to provide conversational support for dementia patients, addressing memory loss and emotional instability. The system includes a self-reflection planning agent that coordinates knowledge retrieval and integration across different types of knowledge graphs to optimize response generation.

papers.name: TAMA
papers.title: TAMA: A Human-AI Collaborative Thematic Analysis Framework Using Multi-Agent LLMs for Clinical Interviews
papers.summary: Agents conduct structured conversations to generate, refine and evaluate themes from interview transcripts, with cardiac experts giving feedback during the process. On interviews with parents of children with a rare coronary anomaly it achieved higher hit rate, coverage and distinctiveness than single-agent analysis.

papers.name: CompBioAgent
papers.title: CompBioAgent : An LLM-powered agent for single-cell RNA-seq data exploration
papers.summary: Converts scientific questions into structured queries against the CellDepot single-cell repository and drives a visualization platform to return violin plots, UMAP embeddings and heatmaps. It gives researchers without programming skills access to gene expression exploration across diseases, cell types and conditions.

papers.title: Chatbot for the Return of Positive Genetic Screening Results for Hereditary Cancer Syndromes: A Prompt Engineering Project
papers.summary: This study designs and evaluates a GPT-4 powered chatbot to support the return of positive population wide genomic screening results in a large public health program. Expert evaluation shows that the chatbot provides clear, user friendly, and contextually appropriate communication, performing well in tone, usability, and boundary management, though program specific accuracy requires improvement. The findings demonstrate the feasibility of LLM based chatbots to augment genetic counseling services and improve the accessibility of genomic health care.

papers.name: GPT-Plan
papers.title: A feasibility study of automating radiotherapy planning with large language model agents
papers.summary: GPT-Plan uses GPT-4 agents acting as dosimetrist and physicist to iteratively adjust and evaluate radiotherapy plans, supported by retrieval of historical plans. On 12 lung IMRT and 5 cervical VMAT cases its plans were comparable to or better than ECHO auto-planning and a senior physicist.

papers.name: DOLA
papers.title: Autonomous Radiotherapy Treatment Planning Using DOLA: A Privacy-Preserving, LLM-Based Optimization Agent
papers.summary: A locally hosted LLaMA agent adjusts optimization objectives inside a commercial treatment planning system over repeated iterations, using retrieval of past attempts and reinforcement learning. On 18 prostate cancer patients the 70B model scored 16.4 percent higher than the 8B model and retrieval improved scores by 19.8 percent.

papers.title: Empowering Medical Multi-Agents with Clinical Consultation Flow for Dynamic Diagnosis
papers.summary: The Consultation Flow Multi-Agent Framework uses a multi-agent system to simulate clinical consultations, integrating multiple modalities of medical data for dynamic diagnosis. The framework demonstrates improved diagnostic accuracy and decision-making persistence compared to existing methods on a public benchmark.

papers.title: Large language model agents can use tools to perform clinical calculations
papers.summary: The study evaluates the performance of large language models in performing medical calculations and finds that they are prone to errors. It demonstrates that integrating these models with task-specific calculation tools significantly improves their accuracy, suggesting a potential pathway for their safe integration into clinical workflows.

papers.name: MMA
papers.title: Integration of Multi-Source Medical Data for Medical Diagnosis Question Answering
papers.summary: The MMA system is designed to integrate multi-source medical data for answering questions related to medical diagnosis, enhancing clinical decision-making. The system uses a multi-agent architecture tailored to handle various modalities of medical data and demonstrates improved performance in handling complex diagnostic tasks compared to existing methods.

papers.name: Agentographer
papers.title: A CT Operation Agent "Agentographer" built on Multimodal Large Language Model versus Radiographer in Chest CT Lung Cancer Screening
papers.summary: Agentographer is a CT operation agent designed to autonomously perform chest CT lung cancer screenings, reducing the workload and error risk for radiographers. In a clinical trial involving 500 subjects, Agentographer successfully completed 95.2% of cases independently, demonstrating significant improvements in efficiency and radiation dose reduction.

papers.name: TxAgent
papers.title: TxAgent: An AI Agent for Therapeutic Reasoning Across a Universe of Tools
papers.summary: TxAgent is an AI agent designed to generate personalized treatment recommendations by leveraging multi-step reasoning and real-time biomedical knowledge retrieval across a wide range of tools. It outperforms existing models in drug reasoning tasks, achieving high accuracy while ensuring that treatment recommendations align with clinical guidelines.

papers.name: MAC
papers.title: Enhancing diagnostic capability with multi-agents conversational large language models
papers.summary: The MAC framework uses multiple conversational agents to enhance disease diagnosis in complex medical scenarios, outperforming single LLMs and other methods. It demonstrates higher diagnostic accuracy and consistency through evaluations on rare disease cases.

papers.name: SurgRAW
papers.title: SurgRAW: Multi-Agent Workflow with Chain of Thought Reasoning for Robotic Surgical Video Analysis
papers.venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters, 2026, pp. 1-8
papers.summary: SurgRAW is a multi-agent system designed for zero-shot reasoning in robotic surgical video analysis, addressing the need for unified scene understanding and interpretability. The system demonstrates superior performance compared to existing vision-language models and supervised approaches through extensive experiments on SurgCoTBench.

papers.name: Talk2Biomodels
papers.title: Talk2Biomodels: AI agent-based open-source LLM initiative for kinetic biological models
papers.summary: An agentic platform lets users explore, simulate and analyse SBML kinetic models from the BioModels database through natural language instead of a fixed interface. Use cases cover precision medicine, epidemiology and emergent network properties for users without computational biology training.

papers.name: Enzyme Co-Scientist
papers.title: Enzyme Co-Scientist: Harnessing Large Language Models for Enzyme Kinetic Data Extraction from Literature
